declaration.title: Four-dimensional real extended super-Poincare algebra
declaration.design_state: Draft authored for aqft-susy-math-foundations; full statement, dependencies, and source qualifications are in the item carrier.
declaration.statement:
Use the complex field $\mathbb C$ with conjugation $z\mapsto\overline z$. Fix an integer $N\ge1$. Let $S=\mathbb C^2$ and let $\dot S=\overline S$ be its conjugate vector space, with dotted basis labels. In the chosen bases put $\epsilon_{12}=\epsilon_{\dot1\dot2}=1$ and $\epsilon_{21}=\epsilon_{\dot2\dot1}=-1$, with zero diagonal. Write $\mathfrak{sl}(S)$ and $\mathfrak{sl}(\dot S)$ for the traceless complex $2\times2$ matrices. The complex even space is

$$\mathfrak g_{\bar0}=\bigl(\mathfrak{sl}(S)\oplus\mathfrak{sl}(\dot S)\bigr)\oplus V\oplus C_N,\qquad V=S\otimes\dot S,\qquad C_N=\Lambda^2\mathbb C^N\oplus\overline{\Lambda^2\mathbb C^N}.$$

Write $T_{\alpha\dot\beta}$ for the basis of $V$. The central space $C_N$ has generators $Z^{IJ}$ and $\bar Z_{IJ}$ for $1\le I<J\le N$, extended by antisymmetry in the flavor indices and with zero diagonal. The complex odd space is

$$\mathfrak g_{\bar1}=(S\otimes\mathbb C^N)\oplus(\dot S\otimes(\mathbb C^N)^*),$$

with basis $Q^I_\alpha$ and $\bar Q_{\dot\alpha I}$. A homogeneous vector has parity $|x|\in\{0,1\}$. The bracket is complex-bilinear, preserves parity, and obeys $[x,y]=-(-1)^{|x||y|}[y,x]$. Its complete nonzero table, apart from the graded-skew consequences, is

$$[ (A,B),(A',B') ]=([A,A'],[B,B']),\qquad [(A,B),T]= (A\otimes I+I\otimes B)T,$$

$$[(A,B),Q^I_\alpha]=A_\alpha{}^\gamma Q^I_\gamma,\qquad [(A,B),\bar Q_{\dot\alpha I}]=B_{\dot\alpha}{}^{\dot\gamma}\bar Q_{\dot\gamma I},$$

$$\{Q^I_\alpha,\bar Q_{\dot\beta J}\}=-2\delta^I{}_J T_{\alpha\dot\beta},\qquad \{Q^I_\alpha,Q^J_\beta\}=2\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}Z^{IJ},\qquad \{\bar Q_{\dot\alpha I},\bar Q_{\dot\beta J}\}=2\epsilon_{\dot\alpha\dot\beta}\bar Z_{IJ}.$$

All other brackets vanish: $V$ and $C_N$ are abelian, $C_N$ is central, and $V$ brackets trivially with the odd space. The two antisymmetric factors in each equal-chirality odd bracket make that bracket symmetric in the combined spinor-flavor labels. The Lie-superalgebra and real-form properties are established by the local Jacobi result.

Define a conjugate-linear involution $*$ on the generators by

$$ (A,B)^*=(-\overline B,-\overline A),\quad Q^I_\alpha{}^*=\bar Q_{\dot\alpha I},\quad \bar Q_{\dot\alpha I}{}^*=Q^I_\alpha,\quad T_{\alpha\dot\beta}^*=T_{\beta\dot\alpha},\quad (Z^{IJ})^*=\bar Z_{IJ},\quad (\bar Z_{IJ})^*=Z^{IJ}.$$

It uses the operator-adjoint convention $[x,y]^*=-(-1)^{|x||y|}[x^*,y^*]$. The associated real Lie superalgebra is the fixed space of the conjugate-linear map $\tau(x)=-x^*$ on even elements and $\tau(x)=i x^*$ on odd elements. Its real Lorentz algebra is the fixed diagonal copy of $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb C)$; its real translation generators are the $\tau$-fixed skew-Hermitian bispinors. Hermitian physical momenta are obtained by multiplying those real translation generators by $-i$ in a unitary representation.

For the metric convention $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, put $\sigma^0=I_2$ and

$$\sigma^1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma^2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma^3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad \bar\sigma^0=I_2,\qquad \bar\sigma^j=-\sigma^j.$$

They obey

$$\sigma^\mu\bar\sigma^\nu+\sigma^\nu\bar\sigma^\mu=-2\eta^{\mu\nu}I_2.$$

Identify the Hermitian bispinor momentum matrix by $T_{\alpha\dot\beta}=\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}P_\mu$, where $P_\mu=\eta_{\mu\nu}P^\nu$. This fixes the mixed relation as $\{Q^I_\alpha,\bar Q_{\dot\beta J}\}=-2\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}P_\mu\delta^I{}_J$. In a massive rest fiber $P^\mu=(M,0,0,0)$, so $P_0=-M$ and the mixed anticommutator is $2M\delta_{\alpha\dot\beta}\delta^I{}_J$. Here $N$ counts left Weyl spinors; the scalar central-charge matrix is antisymmetric and therefore vanishes for $N=1$. Tensorial or topological extensions are outside this scalar-central-charge algebra. The convention uses natural units $\hbar=c=1$; translation and central-charge generators have mass dimension one and supercharges have mass dimension one-half.

declaration.title: Positive unitary super-Poincare representation with spectral-domain covariance
declaration.design_state: Draft authored for aqft-susy-math-foundations; full statement, dependencies, and source qualifications are in the item carrier.
declaration.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Use the complex Hilbert-space convention that the inner product is linear in its first variable and conjugate-linear in its second. Let $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $\sigma^0=I_2$, $\sigma^1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma^2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix}$, and $\sigma^3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$. Define $\operatorname{Herm}_2(\mathbb C)=\{H\in M_2(\mathbb C):H^\dagger=H\}$ and $\Phi:\mathbb R^{1,3}\to\operatorname{Herm}_2(\mathbb C)$ by $\Phi(x)=-\sigma^\mu x_\mu$. For $g\in\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C)=\{g\in M_2(\mathbb C):\det g=1\}$, define $\Lambda_g$ by $\Phi(\Lambda_gx)=g\Phi(x)g^\dagger$; the real-linear map $\Phi$ is an isomorphism because $I_2,\sigma^1,\sigma^2,\sigma^3$ form a basis of $\operatorname{Herm}_2(\mathbb C)$, and $\det\Phi(x)=-\eta_{\mu\nu}x^\mu x^\nu$ is preserved. Congruence by $g$ preserves positive-semidefinite Hermitian matrices, so $\Lambda_g$ preserves the chosen future cone. Let $\Lambda_g^\vee$ be the dual action on covectors, $(\Lambda_g^\vee p)(x)=p(\Lambda_g^{-1}x)$. The spin-cover Poincare group is $\mathcal P=\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C)\ltimes_\Lambda\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with product $(g,a)(h,b)=(gh,a+\Lambda_gb)$.

A **positive unitary super-Poincare representation** in this item is the following data. It includes a nonzero complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, a bounded self-adjoint grading $\Gamma$ with $\Gamma^2=I$, and a strongly continuous unitary representation $U$ of $\mathcal P$ commuting with $\Gamma$. It also includes a regular projection-valued measure $E$ on the Borel subsets of the covector space $(\mathbb R^{1,3})^*$ such that

$$U(1,a)=\Phi_E(p\mapsto e^{i p(a)}),\qquad U(g,0)E(B)U(g,0)^*=E(\Lambda_g^\vee B),\qquad E(\mathcal C_+^*)=I,$$

where $\Phi_E$ is the bounded Borel PVM integral, $\mathcal C_+^*=\{p:p^0=-p_0\ge |\vec p|\}$ is the closed future cone in covector coordinates, and $p(a)=p_\mu a^\mu$. The PVM functional calculus makes every translation unitary commute with every $E(B)$. For each coordinate define the self-adjoint translation generator

$$P_\mu=p_\mu(E),\qquad D(P_\mu)=\left\{\psi\in\mathcal H:\int |p_\mu|^2\,dE_\psi(p)<\infty\right\},\qquad E_\psi(B)=\langle E(B)\psi,\psi\rangle.$$

Here $p_\mu(E)$ is the unbounded PVM integral with its truncation domain; the real-valued integral is self-adjoint under Countable Choice. Thus $P^0=\eta^{0\nu}P_\nu$ is nonnegative. The joint PVM is part of the representation data; no joint spectral measure is inferred from formal commutators on a dense domain.

For each $I,\alpha$, the supercharge $Q^I_\alpha$ is a closed densely defined operator on $\mathcal H$ and $\bar Q_{\dot\alpha I}=(Q^I_\alpha)^*$ is its actual Hilbert adjoint, with exactly the adjoint domain. The central generators $Z^{IJ}$ and $\bar Z_{IJ}$ are represented by closed densely defined operators with $\bar Z_{IJ}=(Z^{IJ})^*$ as an actual Hilbert adjoint. On a common dense graded linear domain $\mathcal D$, contained in the domains of every generator product in the bracket table, the operator supercommutator is the displayed algebra bracket. In particular,

$$\{Q^I_\alpha,\bar Q_{\dot\beta J}\}=-2\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}P_\mu\delta^I{}_J,\qquad \{Q^I_\alpha,Q^J_\beta\}=2\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}Z^{IJ},\qquad \{\bar Q_{\dot\alpha I},\bar Q_{\dot\beta J}\}=2\epsilon_{\dot\alpha\dot\beta}\bar Z_{IJ}.$$

The domain $\mathcal D$ is invariant under those generators and under $U(\mathcal P)$. The even group acts on the charge domains exactly: for every $g\in\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C)$, conjugation by $U(g,0)$ sends each closed charge to the corresponding fundamental or dotted spinor transform as an equality of operators, including equality of domains. The central generators transform as Lorentz scalars, commute with translations, and commute on $\mathcal D$ with all supercharges; these relations also include their domain invariance.

For every Borel set $B\subseteq(\mathbb R^{1,3})^*$ and every charge $Q$ or $Q^*$, require the reducing-projection/domain conditions

$$E(B)D(Q)\subseteq D(Q),\qquad Q E(B)\psi=E(B)Q\psi\quad(\psi\in D(Q)),$$

and the same conditions with $Q^*$ in place of $Q$. Require also $\Gamma E(B)=E(B)\Gamma$ for every Borel $B$. In particular this supplies integrated translation covariance with domain invariance; a relation $[P_\mu,Q]=0$ on a common core alone is not substituted for it. A closed graded subspace $K$ is invariant when $U(g,a)K=K$ for all $(g,a)\in\mathcal P$ and each charge and adjoint maps $D(Q)\cap K$ into $K$, with those intersections dense in $K$. The representation is irreducible when its only such invariant subspaces are $\{0\}$ and $\mathcal H$.

declaration.title: Mass is constant on an irreducible positive super-Poincare representation
declaration.design_state: Draft authored for aqft-susy-math-foundations; full statement, dependencies, and source qualifications are in the item carrier.
declaration.statement:
Let $\mathcal H$ carry an irreducible positive unitary super-Poincare representation with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, future-cone support and the charge-domain reduction conditions stated in its definition. Let $\mathcal C_+^*$ be the closed future cone from the representation definition and define $s:\mathcal C_+^*	o[0,\infty)$ by $s(p)=-\eta^{\mu
u}p_\mu p_
u$. For Borel $A\subseteq[0,\infty)$ define $F(A)=E(\{p\in\mathcal C_+^*:s(p)\in A\})$. Then every supercharge and its adjoint reduce each mass-squared spectral subspace: if $\psi\in D(Q)\cap\operatorname{ran}F(A)$ then $Q\psi\in\operatorname{ran}F(A)$, and the same holds for $Q^*$. Moreover there is a unique $m^2\ge0$ such that $F(A)=I$ when $m^2\in A$ and $F(A)=0$ when $m^2
otin A$. Thus the nonnegative mass $m=\sqrt{m^2}$ is constant throughout the irreducible multiplet. Use natural units $\hbar=c=1$, so $m$ has mass dimension one and $m^2$ has mass dimension two. For a nonzero supercharge image, the source and image lie in the same mass spectral sector. No sharp-momentum eigenvector or rest frame is assumed in the full Hilbert space. If an additional group acts unitarily and commutes with the supercharges on their invariant domains, each supercharge also intertwines that group action; no gauge-charge conclusion is asserted without this extra hypothesis.

declaration.title: Positive central-charge bounds on a massive rest representation fiber
declaration.design_state: Draft authored for aqft-susy-math-foundations; full statement, dependencies, and source qualifications are in the item carrier.
declaration.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $N\ge2$. A fixed massive rest representation fiber consists here of a nonzero complex Hilbert space $\mathcal K$, a number $M>0$ with $P^0=MI$ and $P^j=0$, and scalar central charges $Z^{IJ}=z^{IJ}I$, where $Z=(z^{IJ})$ is the complex antisymmetric $N\times N$ matrix in the four-dimensional algebra with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $\epsilon_{12}=1$. Suppose the charge operators and their actual Hilbert adjoints have a common dense invariant domain $\mathcal D$ on the fiber and every product in the expanded anticommutators is defined there. Use natural units $\hbar=c=1$, so $M$ and each $z^{IJ}$ have mass dimension one. For $v=(v_1,\ldots,v_N)\in\mathbb C^N$ define $\|v\|_2^2=\sum_I|v_I|^2$ and for $u,v\in\mathbb C^N$ put $u^*Zv=\sum_{I,J}\bar u_Iz^{IJ}v_J$. Define

$$\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sup_{\|v\|_2=1}\|Zv\|_2.$$

Then $M\ge\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. For $N=2$, write $z=z^{12}$, so $Z=\begin{pmatrix}0&z\\-z&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}=|z|$. If $z=e^{i\phi}|z|$ (with any $\phi$ when $z=0$), define on $\mathcal D$

$$A:=Q^1_1-e^{i\phi}(Q^2_2)^*,\qquad A^\sharp:=(Q^1_1)^*-e^{-i\phi}Q^2_2.$$

The algebraic anticommutator $AA^\sharp+A^\sharp A$ equals $4(M-|z|)I$ on $\mathcal D$. Here $A^\sharp$ is the displayed combination of the individual actual adjoints; it is not asserted to be the adjoint of an unbounded sum on its maximal domain. If $\mathcal K$ is finite-dimensional, all charge domains equal $\mathcal K$ and $A^\sharp=A^*$, so the formula is the ordinary operator anticommutator. At saturation $M=|z|$, for every $\psi\in\mathcal D$ one has $A\psi=A^\sharp\psi=0$. This is a representation-theoretic fiber statement: it does not assert that the fixed-momentum fiber is a normalizable subspace of the full Hilbert space, or that a state with specified charge exists or is stable.

declaration.title: Four-dimensional N=1 superspace Grassmann algebra and Berezin integration
declaration.design_state: Draft authored for aqft-susy-math-foundations; full statement, dependencies, and source qualifications are in the item carrier.
declaration.statement:
Let $\mathcal A=\mathcal A_{\bar0}\oplus\mathcal A_{\bar1}$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Z_2$-graded complex algebra whose homogeneous elements satisfy $ab=(-1)^{|a||b|}ba$, equipped with a conjugate-linear parity-preserving involutive anti-automorphism $a\mapsto a^*$ extending complex conjugation on $\mathbb C$. For the ordered index set $J=\{1,2,3,4\}$, let $\Lambda_4$ be the complex vector space with specified basis $(e_S)_{S\subseteq J}$, including $e_\varnothing=1$. Define
$$ \nu(S,T)=|\{(s,t)\in S\times T:s>t\}|,\qquad e_Se_T=\begin{cases}0,&S\cap T\ne\varnothing,\\(-1)^{\nu(S,T)}e_{S\cup T},&S\cap T=\varnothing.\end{cases} $$
Put $\xi_1=\theta^1=e_{\{1\}}$, $\xi_2=\theta^2=e_{\{2\}}$, $\xi_3=\bar\theta^{\dot1}=e_{\{3\}}$, and $\xi_4=\bar\theta^{\dot2}=e_{\{4\}}$. Then each $\xi_i$ is odd, $\xi_i^2=0$, and $\xi_i\xi_j=-\xi_j\xi_i$ for $i\ne j$. Give $\Lambda_4$ the grading $|e_S|=|S|\bmod2$. The superspace coefficient vector space is $\mathcal A\otimes_\mathbb C\Lambda_4$ with total parity and graded-tensor multiplication
$$ (a\otimes e_S)(b\otimes e_T)=(-1)^{|S||b|}(ab)\otimes(e_Se_T) $$
for homogeneous $a,b$. On the basis, the left derivative removes $i$ with sign $(-1)^{|\{s\in S:s<i\}|}$ and the right derivative removes $i$ with sign $(-1)^{|\{s\in S:s>i\}|}$ when $i\in S$, and both give zero when $i\notin S$. On a coefficient-left homogeneous tensor $a\otimes e_S$, define $\partial^L_{\xi_i}(a\otimes e_S)=(-1)^{|a|}a\otimes\partial^L_{\xi_i}e_S$ and $\partial^R_{\xi_i}(a\otimes e_S)=a\otimes\partial^R_{\xi_i}e_S$; in particular both vanish on $a\otimes1$. The algebra axioms and derivative rules below are verified in the local well-definedness result. Complex conjugation on this coefficient algebra extends the given operation on $\mathcal A$ by $i^*=-i$, $(\theta^\alpha)^*=\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}$, $(\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha})^*=\theta^\alpha$, and $(uv)^*=v^*u^*$. In the coefficient-left tensor notation this means $(a\otimes e_S)^*=(-1)^{|a||S|}a^*\otimes e_S^*$, where $e_S^*$ is obtained by reversing the ordered generator word for $e_S$ and applying the stated generator conjugation.

For each $i\in J$, the left derivative $\partial^L_{\xi_i}$ is the unique odd derivation of the graded tensor algebra that vanishes on $\mathcal A$ and has $\partial^L_{\xi_i}\xi_j=\delta_{ij}$; on homogeneous $u,v$ it obeys
$$ \partial^L_{\xi_i}(uv)=(\partial^L_{\xi_i}u)v+(-1)^{|u|}u(\partial^L_{\xi_i}v). $$
The right derivative $\partial^R_{\xi_i}$ is the unique right odd derivation vanishing on $\mathcal A$ with $\partial^R_{\xi_i}\xi_j=\delta_{ij}$ and
$$ \partial^R_{\xi_i}(uv)=(-1)^{|v|}(\partial^R_{\xi_i}u)v+u(\partial^R_{\xi_i}v). $$
For one generator, write a polynomial uniquely with that generator on the left as $f=f_0+\xi_i f_1$, with $f_0,f_1$ independent of $\xi_i$, and define its Berezin integral by the complex-linear coefficient-extraction rule $\int d\xi_i\,f=f_1$. Thus $\int d\xi_i\,1=0$ and $\int d\xi_i\,\xi_i=1$. Fix the ordered measures
$$ \int d^2\theta:=\int d\theta^2\,d\theta^1,\qquad \int d^2\bar\theta:=\int d\bar\theta^{\dot2}\,d\bar\theta^{\dot1},\qquad \int d^4\theta:=\int d\bar\theta^{\dot2}\,d\bar\theta^{\dot1}\,d\theta^2\,d\theta^1. $$
With this order, $\int d^4\theta$ extracts the coefficient of $\theta^1\theta^2\bar\theta^{\dot1}\bar\theta^{\dot2}$. For superspace coordinates $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)\in\mathbb R^{1,3}$ in natural units $\hbar=c=1$, assign mass dimensions $[x^\mu]=-1$, $[\theta^\alpha]=[\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}]=-\tfrac12$, $[d\theta^\alpha]=[d\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}]=\tfrac12$, and hence $[d^2\theta]=[d^2\bar\theta]=1$ and $[d^4\theta]=2$. These are formal engineering dimensions; no physical model or empirical unit convention is asserted.

declaration.title: Four-dimensional N=1 chiral superfield on flat superspace
declaration.design_state: Draft authored for aqft-susy-math-foundations; full statement, dependencies, and source qualifications are in the item carrier.
declaration.statement:
Let $\mathcal A=\mathcal A_{\bar0}\oplus\mathcal A_{\bar1}$ be the finite-dimensional supercommutative complex coefficient algebra, and let $\Lambda_4$ have ordered generators $\theta^1,\theta^2,\bar\theta^{\dot1},\bar\theta^{\dot2}$ and the product, parity, derivatives and conjugation specified in the four-dimensional superspace Grassmann algebra. Let $\mathscr S=C^\infty(\mathbb R^{1,3},\mathcal A\otimes\Lambda_4)$ be the space of smooth coefficient functions; $\partial_\mu$ differentiates the real coordinate $x^\mu$ and acts trivially on the finite Grassmann basis. Use the mostly-plus metric and the matrices $\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\alpha}$ specified by the four-dimensional super-Poincare algebra. A **chiral superfield** is an even element $\Phi\in\mathscr S$ satisfying the two equations

$$\bar D_{\dot\alpha}\Phi=0,\qquad \bar D_{\dot\alpha}:=-\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}}-i\sum_{\alpha,\mu}\theta^\alpha\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\alpha}\partial_\mu,\quad \dot\alpha\in\{\dot1,\dot2\}.$$

Define the nilpotent coordinate shift $\Delta y^\mu=i\sum_{\alpha,\dot\alpha}\theta^\alpha\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\alpha}\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}$ and $y^\mu=x^\mu+\Delta y^\mu$. For a smooth coefficient function $f$, $f(y)$ means the finite Taylor substitution $\sum_{k=0}^{2}(\Delta y^{\mu_1}\cdots\Delta y^{\mu_k}/k!)\,\partial_{\mu_1}\cdots\partial_{\mu_k}f(x)$, with the $k=0$ term equal to $f(x)$ and repeated spacetime indices summed; higher terms vanish in $\Lambda_4$. The chiral components are the unique smooth coefficient functions $A,F\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^{1,3},\mathcal A_{\bar0})$ and $\psi_1,\psi_2\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^{1,3},\mathcal A_{\bar1})$ in

$$\Phi(y,\theta)=A(y)+\theta^1\psi_1(y)+\theta^2\psi_2(y)+\theta^1\theta^2F(y).$$

The total parity of every term is even. Define the supersymmetry generators on $\mathscr S$ by

$$Q_\alpha=\partial^L_{\theta^\alpha}-i\sum_{\mu,\dot\alpha}\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\alpha}\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}\partial_\mu,\qquad \bar Q_{\dot\alpha}=-\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}}+i\sum_{\mu,\alpha}\theta^\alpha\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\alpha}\partial_\mu.$$

For external odd constant parameters $\epsilon^\alpha,\bar\epsilon^{\dot\alpha}$ that anticommute with the odd generators and coefficient algebra, set $\delta_{\epsilon,\bar\epsilon}\Phi=\sum_\alpha\epsilon^\alpha Q_\alpha\Phi+\sum_{\dot\alpha}\bar\epsilon^{\dot\alpha}\bar Q_{\dot\alpha}\Phi$. The component transformation is, by definition, the unique ordered-basis coefficient tuple of this transformed superfield in the displayed $y,\theta$ expansion. The space of fields is classical and smooth, so these differential operations have common domain $\mathscr S$; no quantum-field operator domain or field equation is assumed. In natural units $[x^\mu]=-1$ and $[\theta]=[\bar\theta]=-\tfrac12$. If $[\Phi]=d$ is assigned, the formal component dimensions are $[A]=d$, $[\psi_\alpha]=d+\tfrac12$, and $[F]=d+1$; no value of $d$ is fixed. In the same natural-unit convention, $D_\alpha$, $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}$, $Q_\alpha$ and $\bar Q_{\dot\alpha}$ have mass dimension $+\tfrac12$, while $[\epsilon^\alpha]=[\bar\epsilon^{\dot\alpha}]=-\tfrac12$, so $\delta_{\epsilon,\bar\epsilon}$ is dimensionless.

declaration.title: Positive-energy eigenspaces pair under an odd self-adjoint supercharge
declaration.design_state: Locally added prerequisite lemma; proves positive-energy parity pairing from the actual self-adjoint supercharge and its domain.
declaration.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal H=\mathcal H^+\oplus\mathcal H^-$ be a complex Hilbert space with grading operator $\Gamma=+I$ on $\mathcal H^+$ and $\Gamma=-I$ on $\mathcal H^-$. Let $Q$ be a densely defined self-adjoint operator with domain invariant under $\Gamma$ and $Q\Gamma\psi=-\Gamma Q\psi$ for every $\psi\in D(Q)$. Set $H=Q^2$ on the composition domain $D(H)=\{\psi\in D(Q):Q\psi\in D(Q)\}$. For each $\lambda>0$, let $E_\lambda=\{\psi\in D(H):H\psi=\lambda\psi\}$ be finite-dimensional, and put $E_\lambda^\pm=E_\lambda\cap\mathcal H^\pm$. Then $Q$ maps $E_\lambda$ into itself, and

$$U_\lambda:=(Q/\sqrt{\lambda})|_{E_\lambda^+}:E_\lambda^+\longrightarrow E_\lambda^-$$

is a unitary isomorphism, with inverse $(Q/\sqrt{\lambda})|_{E_\lambda^-}$. In particular $\dim E_\lambda^+=\dim E_\lambda^-$. Also $Q\psi=0$ for every zero-energy vector $\psi\in\ker H$. No discrete spectrum or finite-multiplicity assumption is made about energies other than the selected $\lambda$.

declaration.title: Pure-point graded trace-class index data
declaration.design_state: Draft authored for aqft-susy-math-foundations; full statement, dependencies, and source qualifications are in the item carrier.
declaration.statement:
A **pure-point graded trace-class index datum** consists of a complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H=\mathcal H^+\oplus\mathcal H^-$, its grading operator $\Gamma$ equal to $+I$ on $\mathcal H^+$ and $-I$ on $\mathcal H^-$, and a densely defined self-adjoint operator $Q$ such that $D(Q)$ is invariant under $\Gamma$ and $Q\Gamma\psi=-\Gamma Q\psi$ for every $\psi\in D(Q)$. Set $H=Q^2$ on $D(H)=\{\psi\in D(Q):Q\psi\in D(Q)\}$ and require this composition operator to be nonnegative and self-adjoint. Assume $H$ has the orthogonal pure-point decomposition

$$\mathcal H=\mathcal H_0^+\oplus\mathcal H_0^-\oplus\widehat{\bigoplus}_{\lambda\in\Sigma}(\mathcal H_\lambda^+\oplus\mathcal H_\lambda^-),$$

where $\Sigma\subset(0,\infty)$ is a supplied countable set of distinct eigenvalues, $\mathcal H_0^\pm=\ker H\cap\mathcal H^\pm$ are finite-dimensional, and $\mathcal H_\lambda^\pm=\ker(H-\lambda I)\cap\mathcal H^\pm$ are finite-dimensional eigenspaces contained in $D(H)$. Supply orthonormal bases of these subspaces whose union $E=E^+\sqcup E^-$ is a Hilbert basis of $\mathcal H$ compatible with energy and parity. Assume Countable Choice as used by the imported Hilbert-space, adjoint and trace-class definitions. The local positive-energy-pairing lemma derives, rather than assumes, the unitary map $Q/\sqrt\lambda:\mathcal H_\lambda^+\to\mathcal H_\lambda^-$ and equality of their finite dimensions.

For each real $\beta>0$, a bounded diagonal operator $T_\beta$ is supplied as part of the data, with $T_\beta e=e^{-\beta\lambda}e$ on $E_\lambda^+\cup E_\lambda^-$ and $T_\beta e=e$ on $E_0^+\cup E_0^-$. Require $T_\beta$ to be trace class for every $\beta>0$; it is denoted $e^{-\beta H}$. Its graded heat supertrace, called the **Witten index at parameter $\beta$** in this data class, is

$$W(\beta):=\sum_{e\in E^+}\langle T_\beta e,e\rangle-\sum_{e\in E^-}\langle T_\beta e,e\rangle,$$

where each family sum is in the finite-subset sense for absolutely summable scalar families. The supplied trace-class Hilbert-basis definition makes these sums absolutely convergent. Here $\beta$ is only a positive real mathematical parameter and has no assigned physical units or temperature interpretation. The index datum is discrete: it contains no continuous spectral subspace or continuum regularization prescription, and makes no physical model identification.

declaration.title: Equivariant elliptic-complex index and character
declaration.statement:
Let $T$ be a compact torus and $M$ a compact smooth manifold without boundary. A smooth left $T$-action is a jointly smooth map $a:T\times M\to M$ with $a(e,x)=x$ and $a(st,x)=a(s,a(t,x))$. Let $E^0,\ldots,E^N$ be finite-rank complex vector bundles on $M$. For each $j<N$, let $d_j:C^\infty(M,E^j)\to C^\infty(M,E^{j+1})$ be a linear differential operator of finite order, and put $d_{-1}=d_N=0$. The sequence is a complex when $d_{j+1}d_j=0$ for every $j$. It is **elliptic** when, for every $x\in M$ and every nonzero real cotangent vector $\xi\in T_x^*M$, the sequence of principal-symbol maps

$$0\longrightarrow E_x^0\xrightarrow{\sigma(d_0)(x,\xi)}E_x^1\xrightarrow{\sigma(d_1)(x,\xi)}\cdots\xrightarrow{\sigma(d_{N-1})(x,\xi)}E_x^N\longrightarrow0$$

is exact. Suppose each bundle has a smooth $T$-linearization $\rho_t^j:E_x^j\to E_{t\cdot x}^j$, satisfying the group-action law, and the induced section maps

$$ (U_t^j s)(x):=\rho_t^j\bigl(s(t^{-1}\cdot x)\bigr) $$

commute with $d_j$. Require the cohomology spaces $H^j(E^\bullet):=\ker d_j/\operatorname{im}d_{j-1}$ to be finite-dimensional. The representation ring $R(T)$ is the Grothendieck ring of finite-dimensional continuous complex representations of $T$. Define

$$\operatorname{Ind}_T(E^\bullet):=\sum_{j=0}^N(-1)^j[H^j(E^\bullet)]\in R(T),\qquad \chi_{E^\bullet}(t):=\sum_{j=0}^N(-1)^j\operatorname{tr}\!\left(U_t^j\bigm|_{H^j(E^\bullet)}\right).$$

For a two-term complex $0\to C^\infty(M,E^+)\xrightarrow{D^+}C^\infty(M,E^-)\to0$, this gives $[\ker D^+]-[\operatorname{coker}D^+]$. This definition concerns elliptic complexes, not transversally elliptic operators.

Let $P$ be a smooth second-order differential operator with positive-frequency principal symbol $p(x,\xi)$, a Hermitian matrix satisfying $p(x,\xi)\ge c|\xi|^2I$ for some $c>0$. Assume its nonnegative selfadjoint realization has a complete orthonormal basis of smooth eigensections and a smooth heat kernel $K_t(y,z):E_z\to E_y$ relative to Riemannian volume. $$k_x(w)=(2\pi)^{-n}\int_{\mathbb R^n}e^{iw\cdot\xi}e^{-p(x,\xi)}\,d\xi.$$

$$t^{n/2}K_t(\exp_x(\sqrt t\,a),\exp_x(\sqrt t\,b))\longrightarrow k_x(a-b).$$

For every integer $L>n$ there is $C_L$ such that

$$\|K_t(y,z)\|\le C_Lt^{-n/2}(1+d(y,z)/\sqrt t)^{-L}\qquad(0<t\le1).$$

In dimension zero the corresponding assertion is the finite-dimensional limit $K_t(x,x)\to I$ and zero kernel between distinct points.

Assume the principal-symbol sequence is exact for every nonzero real cotangent vector. Suppose smooth unitary bundle maps $\rho_t^j:E_x^j\to E_{t\cdot x}^j$ satisfy $\rho_e^j=I$ and $\rho_{st}^j|_{E_x^j}=\rho_s^j|_{E_{t\cdot x}^j}\circ\rho_t^j|_{E_x^j}$, and commute with all $d_j$; on sections set $(U_t^j s)(y)=\rho_t^j(s(t^{-1}\cdot y))$. Put $d_{-1}=d_N=0$, $E^{\mathrm{ev}}=\bigoplus_{j\text{ even}}E^j$, $E^{\mathrm{odd}}=\bigoplus_{j\text{ odd}}E^j$, $d=\bigoplus_jd_j$, and $\Delta=(d+d^*)^2$, where $d^*$ is the formal adjoint for the chosen metrics and Riemannian volume. For the nonnegative selfadjoint Hodge realization on $L^2$, assume that $\Delta$ has discrete spectrum, smooth eigensections, a trace-class heat operator $e^{-t\Delta}$ with smooth kernel for every $t>0$, finite-dimensional cohomology, and a harmonic representative for each cohomology class. For $g\in T$, let $M^g=\{x\in M:g\cdot x=x\}$, and suppose each $x\in M^g$ is simple, meaning $I-dg_x:T_xM\to T_xM$ is invertible. Then

$$\lim_{t\downarrow0}\operatorname{Str}(U_g e^{-t\Delta})=\sum_{x\in M^g}\frac{\sum_{j=0}^N(-1)^j\operatorname{tr}(\rho_g^j|_{E_x^j})}{|\det_{\mathbb R}(I-dg_x)|}.$$

Here $\operatorname{Str}$ is the trace on $E^{\mathrm{ev}}$ minus the trace on $E^{\mathrm{odd}}$. The simplicity condition makes $M^g$ a finite set; the determinant is the normal Jacobian at that isolated fixed point.

declaration.title: Equivariant elliptic-complex index character at simple fixed points
declaration.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let $T$ be a compact torus acting smoothly by isometries on a compact smooth manifold $M$ without boundary. Let $E^0,\ldots,E^N$ be finite-rank Hermitian bundles, set $E^{-1}=E^{N+1}=0$ and $d_{-1}=d_N=0$, and for $0\le j<N$ let $d_j:C^\infty(M,E^j)\to C^\infty(M,E^{j+1})$ be first-order differential maps with $d_{j+1}d_j=0$. Assume the principal-symbol sequence is exact for every nonzero real cotangent vector. Suppose smooth unitary bundle maps $\rho_t^j:E_x^j\to E_{t\cdot x}^j$ satisfy $\rho_e^j=I$ and $\rho_{st}^j|_{E_x^j}=\rho_s^j|_{E_{t\cdot x}^j}\circ\rho_t^j|_{E_x^j}$, and commute with all $d_j$. Let $H^j=\ker d_j/\operatorname{im}d_{j-1}$ be finite-dimensional, use $T$-invariant Hermitian metrics and Riemannian volume to form the formal adjoint $d^*$ and $\Delta=(d+d^*)^2$, and, for its nonnegative selfadjoint Hodge realization on $L^2$, assume $\Delta$ has discrete spectrum, trace-class heat operators with smooth kernels for $t>0$, and zero eigenspace canonically isomorphic to $\bigoplus_jH^j$. Put $\operatorname{Ind}_T(E^\bullet)=\sum_j(-1)^j[H^j]\in R(T)$, where $R(T)$ is the Grothendieck ring of finite-dimensional continuous complex representations of $T$, and let $\chi_{\operatorname{Ind}_T(E^\bullet)}(g)$ be the alternating trace on these cohomology representations. For $g\in T$, suppose every fixed point $x\in M^g=\{y:g\cdot y=y\}$ is simple, meaning $I-dg_x:T_xM\to T_xM$ is invertible. Then

$$\chi_{\operatorname{Ind}_T(E^\bullet)}(g)=\sum_{x\in M^g}\frac{\sum_{j=0}^N(-1)^j\operatorname{tr}(\rho_g^j|_{E_x^j})}{|\det_{\mathbb R}(I-dg_x)|}.$$

The numerator is the fiber character $\sum_j(-1)^j\operatorname{tr}(\rho_g^j|_{E_x^j})$, equivalently the degree-zero equivariant Chern character of the virtual fiber $\sum_j(-1)^jE_x^j$; the denominator is the isolated fixed point's real normal Jacobian. The formula is asserted only at group elements with simple fixed points.

declaration.title: A nontrivial virtual character on a two-point manifold
declaration.statement: Let $T=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ and let $M=\{p,q\}$ be a two-point smooth $0$-manifold with trivial $T$-action. For $k\in\mathbb Z$, let $\mathbb C_k$ be the one-dimensional representation $[s]\mapsto e^{2\pi i k s}$. Take the zero-differential complex whose fibers are $E_p^0=\mathbb C_0\oplus\mathbb C_1$, $E_p^1=\mathbb C_2$, $E_q^0=\mathbb C_1$, and $E_q^1=\mathbb C_0$, with all other fibers zero. Its equivariant index is $2[\mathbb C_1]-[\mathbb C_2]$, with character $2z-z^2$ at $z=e^{2\pi i s}$. Every point is fixed, the tangent determinant is the empty determinant $1$, and the fixed-point sum is also $2z-z^2$.

declaration.statement: Assume countable choice. Give $S^2=\{(x,y,z)\in\mathbb R^3:x^2+y^2+z^2=1\}$ its outward orientation and the de Rham complex. declaration.title: Finite-Dimensional Q-Exact Localization Data
declaration.statement:
Let $M$ be an oriented smooth manifold of finite dimension $n$, with a chosen integration cycle and a smooth positive volume form $\mu$. Its parity-reversed tangent bundle $\Pi TM$ has even base coordinates $x^1,\ldots,x^n$ and odd fiber coordinates $\theta^1,\ldots,\theta^n$, which transform as the coordinate one-forms $dx^i$. Smooth functions on $\Pi TM$ are identified with inhomogeneous complex differential forms $\mathcal A=\Omega^\bullet(M;\mathbb C)$; the parity of a form is its degree modulo two. The Berezin convention is $\int d\theta^n\cdots d\theta^1\,\theta^1\cdots\theta^n=1$. For $F\in\mathcal A$, write $F_{[n]}=f_F\mu$ for its degree-$n$ component and define the graded integral by $I_\Gamma(F):=\int_M f_F\,d\mu=\int_M F_{[n]}$, equivalently by Berezin integration over the odd fibers followed by integration over the body $M$ with the chosen orientation.

A supercharge $Q$ is a smooth odd derivation of $\mathcal A$, so for homogeneous forms $\alpha,\beta$ it satisfies $Q(\alpha\wedge\beta)=Q\alpha\wedge\beta+(-1)^{|\alpha|}\alpha\wedge Q\beta$. Its square $Q^2:=Q\circ Q$ is an even derivation. The measure and cycle are $Q$-invariant on an admissible class of integrands when $I_\Gamma(QF)=0$ for every $F$ in that class. The associated Berezinian density on $\Pi TM$ has local expression $dx^1\cdots dx^n\,d\theta^n\cdots d\theta^1$ in oriented coordinates. In that coordinate description, zero divergence means $\mathcal L_Q\boldsymbol\mu_\Pi=(\operatorname{div}_{\boldsymbol\mu_\Pi}Q)\boldsymbol\mu_\Pi=0$, together with vanishing boundary flux. Compact support in the interior or explicit decay may impose the boundary condition on a noncompact or bounded cycle.

An admissible finite-dimensional $Q$-exact deformation consists of even smooth forms $S,O\in\mathcal A$, an odd smooth form $V\in\mathcal A$, and an open interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ such that $QS=QO=0$. The even form $QV$ is the $Q$-exact deformation, $S_t:=S+tQV$, and $E_t:=e^{-S_t}$, with the exponential defined by the usual pointwise exponential of its degree-zero part and the finite exterior-degree expansion of its positive-degree part. Require $(Q^2V)E_t=0$ for every $t\in J$; the stronger condition $Q^2V=0$ is sufficient. Require $O E_t$ and $O V E_t$ to be admissible integrands, with no boundary flux in $I_\Gamma(Q(O V E_t))$.

Write $(O E_t)_{[n]}=f_t\mu$. The deformation data are analytically admissible when $f_t$ is integrable for every $t\in J$, $t\mapsto f_t(x)$ is differentiable for almost every $x$, $\partial_t f_t$ is measurable, and for every compact $K\subset J$ there is a single nonnegative $g_K\in L^1(M,\mu)$ such that $|f_t(x)|\le g_K(x)$ and $|\partial_t f_t(x)|\le g_K(x)$ for every $t\in K$ outside one $\mu$-null set. The underlying manifold is finite-dimensional; its smooth-function algebra need not be finite-dimensional as a vector space.

declaration.title: Finite-Dimensional Q-Exact Deformation Invariance
declaration.statement:
Let $M$ be an oriented smooth manifold of finite dimension $n$, with integration cycle $M$, smooth positive volume form $\mu$, graded algebra $\mathcal A=\Omega^\bullet(M;\mathbb C)$, and integral $I_\Gamma(F)=\int_M F_{[n]}$ of the degree-$n$ part. Let $Q$ be a smooth odd derivation of $\mathcal A$, let $S,O$ be smooth even forms, let $V$ be a smooth odd form, and let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval. Suppose $QS=QO=0$, $(Q^2V)e^{-S-tQV}=0$ for every $t\in J$, and $I_\Gamma(Q(O V e^{-S-tQV}))=0$ for every $t\in J$, including the zero-boundary-flux condition. Write $(Oe^{-S-tQV})_{[n]}=f_t\mu$. Suppose that $f_t$ is integrable for each $t\in J$, is differentiable in $t$ almost everywhere with measurable derivative, and that for every compact $K\subset J$ one integrable majorant $g_K$ bounds both $|f_t|$ and $|\partial_t f_t|$ for all $t\in K$, outside one null set. Then

$$Z(t):=I_\Gamma(Oe^{-S-tQV})=\int_M f_t\,d\mu$$

is constant on $J$, and for every $t\in J$,

$$Z'(t)=-I_\Gamma(O(QV)e^{-S-tQV})=-I_\Gamma(Q(O V e^{-S-tQV}))=0.$$

In particular, the conclusion is finite-dimensional and applies only at finite parameter values in $J$; it gives no $t\to\infty$ saddle-point limit and no identity for an infinite-dimensional continuum functional integral.

declaration.title: A nonzero Q-exact deformation on the four-torus
declaration.statement: Let $T^4=(\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z)^4$ have global angular coordinates $x^1,\ldots,x^4$ and orientation $\omega=dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\wedge dx^4$. declaration.title: Framed U(N) Instanton Moduli and ADHM Data
declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $N\geq 2$ and let $S^4=\mathbb R^4\cup\{\infty\}$ be the one-point compactification, oriented so the coordinates $x^1,x^2,x^3,x^4$ on $\mathbb R^4$ have $dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\wedge dx^4>0$. Give $S^4$ a smooth round metric in the conformal class of the Euclidean metric on $\mathbb R^4$. A framed $U(N)$ connection is a smooth unitary connection $A$ on a Hermitian rank-$N$ vector bundle $E\to S^4$, together with a chosen unitary frame $\Phi:E_\infty\to\mathbb C^N$ of its fiber at $\infty$. Gauge transformations are smooth unitary bundle automorphisms that equal the identity in this frame at $\infty$. The curvature is $F_A$, and the Hodge operator is defined by $\alpha\wedge *_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,d\mathrm{vol}_g$ on two-forms. Set $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2$ and $F_A^-=(F_A-*_gF_A)/2$; the anti-self-dual condition is $F_A^+=0$, and the self-dual condition is $F_A^-=0$.

Let $\mathfrak u(N)$ be the anti-Hermitian matrices and put $B_N(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_N(XY)$. In the trace convention of the library, the charge of $A$ is $q_N(A)=(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}B_N(F_A\wedge F_A)$, and the positive anti-self-dual instanton number is $k(A)=-q_N(A)$. For $k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}$, the framed anti-self-dual charge-$k$ moduli set $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ consists of framed pairs $(E,A)$ with $F_A^+=0$ and $k(A)=k$, modulo the stated based gauge transformations. The integer-charge condition is part of the selected bundle sector; no analytic existence or uniqueness assertion is included in this definition. The trace and Hodge conventions agree with the supplied compact-four-manifold definition of $q_B$; its special $SU(2)$ integrality clause is not used to assert $U(N)$ integrality.

For $k\geq0$, take Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$. The ADHM data are
$$B_1,B_2\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V),\qquad I\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(W,V),\qquad J\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(V,W).$$
Their data space is $\mathcal R_{k,N}=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)^2\oplus\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(W,V)\oplus\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(V,W)$, and their complex and real moment-map expressions are
$$\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V),\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V).$$
Here $[X,Y]=XY-YX$, and $\dagger$ is the Hermitian adjoint. The two displayed formulas define maps $\mu_{\mathbb C}:\mathcal R_{k,N}\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ and $\mu_{\mathbb R}:\mathcal R_{k,N}\to\operatorname{Herm}(V)$, where $\mathcal R_{k,N}$ is the stated product of four Hom spaces and $\operatorname{Herm}(V)$ is the real vector space of Hermitian endomorphisms. They are the complex and real ADHM moment-map expressions, with these formulas fixing their normalization. A datum is stable when
$$\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w):m\geq0,\ i_j\in\{1,2\},\ w\in W\}=V,$$
where the word of length zero is the identity. Equivalently, no proper $B_1,B_2$-invariant subspace of $V$ contains $\operatorname{im}I$. The group $GL(V)$ consists of invertible complex-linear endomorphisms, and $U(V)$ is its subgroup preserving the chosen Hermitian inner product. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. For $\zeta>0$, the stable complex ADHM quotient $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{GIT},\zeta}_{k,N}$ is the geometric quotient of $\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \text{stable}\}$ by $GL(V)$ in the positive stability chamber; $\zeta$ labels that chamber and is not an additional coordinate on the complex equation set.

For a real parameter $\zeta\geq0$, the real moment-map presentation is the quotient of $\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta\,\mathrm{id}_V,\ \text{stable}\}$ by $U(V)$. At $\zeta>0$ this is called the resolved or positive-FI ADHM quotient; at $\zeta=0$ its affine completion includes the small-instanton locus. The equations and quotient are definitions; this item does not assert that the real moment-map quotient is isomorphic to the stable complex quotient or to an instanton moduli space.

Write $\mathbb{CP}^2$ for the complex projective plane, $\ell_\infty=\{[0:z_1:z_2]\}$ for its line at infinity, and $\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}$ for the sheaf of holomorphic functions on that line. The affine chart $\mathbb{CP}^2\setminus\ell_\infty$ is $\mathbb C^2$; projective compactification adds the whole line $\ell_\infty$, unlike the one-point compactification $S^4$. Let $\mathcal O(1)$ be the hyperplane line bundle and $\mathcal O(m)=\mathcal O(1)^{\otimes m}$ for $m\geq0$. A coherent sheaf is a sheaf of $\mathcal O_{\mathbb{CP}^2}$-modules that is locally finitely presented; it is torsion-free when no nonzero local section is annihilated by a nonzero local function. Its rank is the dimension of its generic fiber over the function field. Define its Hilbert polynomial by $P_E(m)=\sum_{i=0}^2(-1)^i\dim_{\mathbb C}H^i(\mathbb{CP}^2,E\otimes\mathcal O(m))$ for all sufficiently large integers $m$. The framed Gieseker moduli space $\mathcal G_{k,N}$ is the moduli of pairs $(E,\Phi)$ with $E$ a rank-$N$ torsion-free coherent sheaf, $P_E(m)=N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$, and $\Phi:E|_{\ell_\infty}\cong\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}^{\oplus N}$. Its locally-free locus is distinguished from the boundary of non-locally-free sheaves. The Uhlenbeck set-theoretic compactification is the disjoint union of strata $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k-\ell,N}\times\operatorname{Sym}^{\ell}(\mathbb R^4)$ for $0\leq\ell\leq k$, where $\operatorname{Sym}^{\ell}(\mathbb R^4)=(\mathbb R^4)^\ell/S_\ell$ records ideal point defects. The Gieseker space and the Uhlenbeck space are distinct: the former retains torsion-free sheaf data at the small-instanton boundary, while the latter records only ideal points. No compactness of either full space is asserted here.

Write $z_1=x^1+ix^2$ and $z_2=x^3+ix^4$. The compact torus $T=(S^1)^2\times T_G$, with $T_G\subset U(W)$ the diagonal framing torus, acts on ADHM data by
$$(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ).$$
This convention makes $\mu_{\mathbb C}$ transform with character $t_1t_2$ and leaves $\mu_{\mathbb R}$ invariant. Let $e_\alpha$ denote the character of the dual of the $\alpha$th framing line, so the framing representation has character $\mathbf W=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha$. For the rotation characters write $t_1,t_2$, and write $\epsilon_i=c_1^T(t_i)$ and $a_\alpha=c_1^T(e_\alpha)$ for their additive equivariant weights.

declaration.title: Stable ADHM partition fixed points and tangent character
declaration.statement:
Assume full AC. Fix integers $N\geq1$ and $k\geq0$ and a positive real stability parameter $\zeta$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ have their standard Hermitian structures. Define $\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N}$ to be the geometric quotient by $GL(V)$ of data $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I\in\operatorname{Hom}(W,V)$, $J\in\operatorname{Hom}(V,W)$, $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$, and $\operatorname{span}\{B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w):m\geq0,\ w\in W\}=V$. The positive parameter $\zeta$ specifies the positive-FI stability chamber. Let $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$, with rotation characters $t_1,t_2$ and dual framing characters $e_1,\ldots,e_N$. Thus $W$ has character $\mathbf W=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and $W^\vee$ has character $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$, where $h$ acts on $W$ with weights $e_\alpha^{-1}$. Work over the rational function field $K=\mathbb Q(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,a_1,\ldots,a_N)$ in algebraically independent variables. For $\chi=t_1^{m_1}t_2^{m_2}\prod_\alpha e_\alpha^{n_\alpha}$ set $u_\chi=m_1\epsilon_1+m_2\epsilon_2+\sum_\alpha n_\alpha a_\alpha$.

For a partition $Y$, a Young diagram means a finite downward-closed subset of $\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^2$; write $|Y|$ for its number of boxes. declaration.title: ADHM Fixed Points and the Equivariant Instanton Count
declaration.statement:
Fix integers $N\geq1$ and $k\geq0$ and a positive real stability parameter $\zeta$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ have their standard Hermitian structures. Define $\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N}$ to be the geometric quotient by $GL(V)$ of data $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I\in\operatorname{Hom}(W,V)$, $J\in\operatorname{Hom}(V,W)$, $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$, and $\operatorname{span}\{B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w):m\geq0,\ w\in W\}=V$. The positive parameter $\zeta$ specifies the positive-FI stability chamber. Let $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$, with rotation characters $t_1,t_2$ and dual framing characters $e_1,\ldots,e_N$. Thus $W$ has character $\mathbf W=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and $W^\vee$ has character $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$, where $h$ acts on $W$ with weights $e_\alpha^{-1}$. Complexify the characters and work over the rational function field $K=\mathbb Q(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,a_1,\ldots,a_N)$, where $\epsilon_i=c_1^T(t_i)$ and $a_\alpha=c_1^T(e_\alpha)$.

For a partition $Y$, a Young diagram means a finite downward-closed subset of $\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^2$; write $|Y|$ for its number of boxes. For an $N$-tuple $\vec Y=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_N)$ set $|\vec Y|=\sum_\alpha|Y_\alpha|$, $\mathbf W=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$, $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$, and
$$\mathbf V_{\vec Y}=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha\sum_{(i,j)\in Y_\alpha}t_1^it_2^j.$$
Then $\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N}$ is smooth of complex dimension $2kN$, and its $T$-fixed points are isolated and in bijection with the $N$-tuples of partitions of total size $k$. At the fixed point $\vec Y$, the tangent character is
$$\operatorname{ch}_T(T_{\vec Y}\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N})=\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf V_{\vec Y}(t_1+t_2-1-t_1t_2)+\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf W^\vee+t_1t_2\mathbf W\mathbf V_{\vec Y}.$$
For each character $\chi$, let $u_\chi=c_1^T(\chi)$. Let $E_{\vec Y}$ be the product of $u_\chi$ over the tangent weights counted with multiplicity; the fixed points are isolated, so none of these weights is zero. Define the fixed-point series by
$$Z^{\mathrm{fp}}_N(q)=\sum_{k\geq0}q^k\sum_{|\vec Y|=k}E_{\vec Y}^{-1}\in K\langle\!\langle q\rangle\!\rangle.$$
Each coefficient is a finite sum, and the series is formal; no analytic convergence is asserted.

Assume full AC as inherited from the supplied instanton-charge convention. If a $T$-equivariant isomorphism from the positive-FI quotient to the moduli of framed rank-$N$ torsion-free coherent sheaves on $\mathbb{CP}^2$ with Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$ is supplied, it transfers the fixed-point classification and tangent characters to that Gieseker space. The ordinary framed anti-self-dual moduli space is a separate zero-FI regular locus: identifying that locus with the regular ADHM quotient uses the separate ordinary dictionary below, and no fixed-point count or equality of series is asserted for it. If a separately proved noncompact equivariant pushforward for $\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N}$ has a localization identity with these isolated fixed points and tangent Euler classes, then its value on the unit is the coefficient displayed above. The compact ABBV formula alone does not establish such an identity: $\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N}$ is noncompact for $k>0$. This theorem makes no identification with an ordinary continuum gauge-theory path integral.

declaration.title: Finite 2-group background cochains
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; current readiness is recorded in the run-local Step-1 receipt.
declaration.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group with identity $e$, let $A$ be a finite abelian group written additively, and let $\rho:G\to\operatorname{Aut}(A)$ be a left action, so $\rho_{gh}=\rho_g\rho_h$ and $\rho_e=\operatorname{id}_A$. A group $2$-cochain is a function $c:G^2\to A$; it is normalized when it vanishes if either input is $e$. Its coboundary is

$$
(\delta_\rho c)(g,h,k)=\rho_g c(h,k)-c(gh,k)+c(g,hk)-c(g,h).
$$

A normalized group $3$-cocycle is a function $\beta:G^3\to A$ that vanishes whenever any argument is $e$ and satisfies

$$
\rho_g\beta(h,k,l)-\beta(gh,k,l)+\beta(g,hk,l)-\beta(g,h,kl)+\beta(g,h,k)=0
$$

for all $g,h,k,l\in G$. Two normalized $3$-cocycles represent the same class when their difference is $\delta_\rho c$ for a normalized $2$-cochain $c$; this is an equivalence relation by additivity of $\delta_\rho$. The class $[\beta]$ is the Postnikov class in this skeletal model.

The corresponding skeletal categorical $2$-group has objects $g\in G$ and, for each $g$, one automorphism labelled by each $u\in A$; there are no morphisms between distinct objects. Composition of automorphisms adds their labels, tensor product is

$$
(g,u)\otimes(h,v)=(gh,u+\rho_gv),
$$

and the associator from $(gh)k$ to $g(hk)$ has label $\beta(g,h,k)$. The two pentagon path labels are $\beta(gh,k,l)+\beta(g,h,kl)$ and $\rho_g\beta(h,k,l)+\beta(g,hk,l)+\beta(g,h,k)$; equality of these labels is exactly the displayed $3$-cocycle equation.

A finite ordered simplicial complex $K$ is a finite vertex set with a total order and a collection of nonempty finite vertex subsets, called simplices, closed under taking nonempty subsets. Write each simplex in increasing order. A $q$-cochain with values in a local coefficient system assigns an element to each ordered $q$-simplex at its first vertex. A flat $G$-valued edge cochain is a family $a_{ij}\in G$ for each edge $i<j$ such that $a_{ij}a_{jk}=a_{ik}$ on every triangle. It defines the local coefficient system with fiber $A$ at each vertex and transport $\rho_{a_{ij}}$ from vertex $j$ to vertex $i$.

For each integer $q\geq0$ and local-coefficient $q$-cochain $c$, define the twisted coboundary on each ordered $(q+1)$-simplex by

$$
(\delta_a c)_{i_0\ldots i_{q+1}}=\rho_{a_{i_0i_1}}c_{i_1\ldots i_{q+1}}+\sum_{r=1}^{q+1}(-1)^r c_{i_0\ldots\widehat{i_r}\ldots i_{q+1}}.
$$

In particular, for an $A$-valued $2$-cochain $B$,

$$
(\delta_aB)_{ijkl}=\rho_{a_{ij}}B_{jkl}-B_{ikl}+B_{ijl}-B_{ijk},\qquad (a^*\beta)_{ijkl}=\beta(a_{ij},a_{jk},a_{kl}).
$$

A finite $2$-group background on $K$ is a flat edge cochain $a$ and an $A$-valued $2$-cochain $B$ satisfying $\delta_aB=a^*\beta$ on every ordered tetrahedron. This fixes the cochain representative, local coefficient action, and sign convention.

A $1$-gauge transformation consists of vertex labels $g_i\in G$ and edge labels $\lambda_{ij}\in A$ at vertex $i$. Define

$$
a^g_{ij}=g_i a_{ij}g_j^{-1},
$$

$$
\zeta^g_{ijk}=-\beta(g_i,a_{ij},a_{jk})+\beta(a^g_{ij},g_j,a_{jk})-\beta(a^g_{ij},a^g_{jk},g_k),
$$

$$
B^{g,\lambda}_{ijk}=\rho_{g_i}B_{ijk}+\zeta^g_{ijk}+(\delta_{a^g}\lambda)_{ijk},\qquad (\delta_{a^g}\lambda)_{ijk}=\rho_{a^g_{ij}}\lambda_{jk}-\lambda_{ik}+\lambda_{ij}.
$$

Changing the chosen representative to $\beta'=\beta+\delta_\rho c$ for a normalized $2$-cochain $c$ and simultaneously replacing $B$ by $B+a^*c$ changes the cochain presentation but preserves the background equation: on every tetrahedron, flatness gives

$$
(\delta_a(a^*c))_{ijkl}=\rho_{a_{ij}}c(a_{jk},a_{kl})-c(a_{ik},a_{kl})+c(a_{ij},a_{jl})-c(a_{ij},a_{jk})=(\delta_\rho c)(a_{ij},a_{jk},a_{kl}).
$$

This finite mathematical model makes no assertion that a physical theory realizes the symmetry or has an anomaly.

declaration.statement:
Let $K$ be a finite ordered simplicial complex; let $G$ be a finite group, $A$ a finite abelian group written additively, $\rho:G\to\operatorname{Aut}(A)$ a left action, and $\beta:G^3\to A$ a normalized group $3$-cocycle with the convention that its associator is directed from $(gh)k$ to $g(hk)$. Let $a_{ij}\in G$ be flat on every ordered triangle, let $B_{ijk}\in A$ be an $A$-valued $2$-cochain at the first vertex, and assume on every ordered tetrahedron that

$$
\rho_{a_{ij}}B_{jkl}-B_{ikl}+B_{ijl}-B_{ijk}=\beta(a_{ij},a_{jk},a_{kl}).
$$

For arbitrary vertex labels $g_i\in G$ and edge labels $\lambda_{ij}\in A$, put $a'_{ij}=g_i a_{ij}g_j^{-1}$ and

$$
\zeta_{ijk}=-\beta(g_i,a_{ij},a_{jk})+\beta(a'_{ij},g_j,a_{jk})-\beta(a'_{ij},a'_{jk},g_k).
$$

$$
B'_{ijk}=\rho_{g_i}B_{ijk}+\zeta_{ijk}+\rho_{a'_{ij}}\lambda_{jk}-\lambda_{ik}+\lambda_{ij}.
$$

Then $a'$ is flat and $(a',B')$ satisfies the same twisted tetrahedron equation. If $(g,\lambda)$ is followed by $(h,\mu)$, with $a''_{ij}=h_i a'_{ij}h_j^{-1}$, their composite is $(hg,\nu)$ where

$$
\nu_{ij}=\beta(h_i,g_i,a_{ij})+\rho_{h_i}\lambda_{ij}-\beta(h_i,a'_{ij},g_j)+\mu_{ij}+\beta(a''_{ij},h_j,g_j).
$$

Each transformation is invertible: for a fixed source background, put $h_i=g_i^{-1}$ and

$$
\mu_{ij}=-\beta(h_i,g_i,a_{ij})-\rho_{h_i}\lambda_{ij}+\beta(h_i,a'_{ij},g_j)-\beta(a_{ij},h_j,g_j);
$$

then its composite has $\nu_{ij}=0$. Treating a gauge arrow as its induced map on background cochains, sequential maps compose associatively, and the displayed formula gives a representative for each composite. This is a mathematical consistency result and does not assert a physical anomaly theorem.

declaration.statement:
Fix a finite ordered simplicial complex $K$, a finite group $G$, a finite abelian group $A$ in additive notation, a left action $\rho:G\to\operatorname{Aut}(A)$, and a normalized inhomogeneous $3$-cocycle $\beta:G^3\to A$. A background $x=(a,B)$ has flat edge labels $a_{ij}a_{jk}=a_{ik}$ and satisfies $\delta_aB=a^*\beta$, with coefficients at the first vertex. Here $(\delta_a t)_{ij}=\rho_{a_{ij}}t_j-t_i$ for a vertex cochain, $(\delta_a\lambda)_{ijk}=\rho_{a_{ij}}\lambda_{jk}-\lambda_{ik}+\lambda_{ij}$ for an edge cochain, and $(\delta_aB)_{ijkl}=\rho_{a_{ij}}B_{jkl}-B_{ikl}+B_{ijl}-B_{ijk}$. The cocycle convention is

$$
D(s,t,r,q):=\rho_s\beta(t,r,q)-\beta(st,r,q)+\beta(s,tr,q)-\beta(s,t,rq)+\beta(s,t,r)=0.
$$

The **background gauge 2-groupoid** $\mathcal B(K)$ has these backgrounds as objects. A $1$-arrow $f:x\to y$ is a raw pair $(g,\lambda)$ of vertex $G$-labels and edge $A$-labels with target $y=(b,C)$ given by

$$
b_{ij}=g_i a_{ij}g_j^{-1},\qquad \zeta^g_{ijk}(a)=-\beta(g_i,a_{ij},a_{jk})+\beta(b_{ij},g_j,a_{jk})-\beta(b_{ij},b_{jk},g_k),\qquad C=\rho_gB+\zeta^g(a)+\delta_b\lambda.
$$

Raw pairs remain distinct even when their induced functions on backgrounds coincide. For fixed $g$ and target edge labels $b$, a $2$-arrow $t:(g,\lambda)\Rightarrow(g,\lambda')$ is a vertex $A$-cochain satisfying $\lambda'-\lambda=\delta_b t$. There are no $2$-arrows between different vertex labels $g$. Vertical composition adds vertex cochains; the identity $2$-arrow is zero.

For consecutive $1$-arrows $(g,\lambda):x\to y$ and $(h,\mu):y\to z$, write $a,b,c$ for the successive edge labels. Their composite is $(hg,\nu)$, where

$$
\nu_{ij}=\rho_{h_i}\lambda_{ij}+\mu_{ij}+\tau(h,g;a)_{ij},\qquad \tau(h,g;a)_{ij}=\beta(h_i,g_i,a_{ij})-\beta(h_i,b_{ij},g_j)+\beta(c_{ij},h_j,g_j).
$$

Horizontal composition of $t$ on the first arrow and $s$ on the second is $s+\rho_h t$. Identity $1$-arrows have all vertex labels $e$ and edge labels zero. For three consecutive arrows $g,h,k$, the associator from $((k\circ h)\circ g)$ to $k\circ(h\circ g)$ is the vertex cochain $\sigma_i=\beta(k_i,h_i,g_i)$. Unit constraints are identity $2$-arrows.

A $2$-groupoid here means these data form a bicategory: each pair of objects has a category of $1$-arrows and $2$-arrows; horizontal composition preserves identities and vertical composition; associators are natural and obey the pentagon; units obey the triangle identity; all $2$-arrows are invertible and every $1$-arrow has a reverse up to invertible $2$-arrows. Finiteness means all three sets of labels are finite. Coherence of the displayed data is a separate theorem.

Write $\pi_0\mathcal B(K)$ for the equivalence classes of objects under $1$-arrows. For an object $x$, let $\pi_1(\mathcal B(K),x)$ be the group of $2$-isomorphism classes of $1$-automorphisms of $x$, and let $\pi_2(\mathcal B(K),x)$ be the abelian group of $2$-automorphisms of its identity $1$-arrow. In particular, $\pi_2$ retains vertex cochains with $\delta_a t=0$ rather than discarding them. For a subcomplex $L\subseteq K$ and fixed background $s$ on $L$, the **relative background 2-groupoid** has objects restricting exactly to $s$, $1$-arrows with $g=e$ on vertices of $L$ and $\lambda=0$ on edges of $L$, and $2$-arrows with $t=0$ on vertices of $L$.

declaration.title: Finite background groupoid and cocycle-weighted gauging data
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; conditional two-group prerequisite status and current readiness are recorded in the batch notes and Step-1 receipt.
declaration.statement:
Let $K$ be a finite ordered simplicial complex. A **finite background field groupoid** $\mathcal F(K)$ is a small category of declared fields and invertible gauge equivalences, with finitely many isomorphism classes and finite automorphism groups. Its automorphisms retain the multiplicities declared by the field model. A **cocycle/action weight** is a function $W_K:\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal F(K)\to U(1)$ constant on every gauge arrow. Its normalized gauging sum is

$$
Z_K(W_K)=\sum_{[x]\in\pi_0\mathcal F(K)}\frac{W_K(x)}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal F(K)}(x)|}.
$$

For the finite $2$-group specialization, fix finite $(G,A,\rho,\beta)$ and let $\mathcal B(K)$ be the explicit background gauge $2$-groupoid: objects are flat $G$-edge cochains and $A$-face cochains satisfying $\delta_aB=a^*\beta$; $1$-arrows retain raw vertex/edge parameters $(g,\lambda)$, and $2$-arrows are vertex cochains $t$ with $\lambda'-\lambda=\delta_{a^g}t$, for fixed $g$. The raw $1$-composition is the displayed $\tau$-corrected composition; its associator is $\beta(k_i,h_i,g_i)$. Write $\pi_0$ for object equivalence classes, $\pi_1(\mathcal B(K),x)$ for $2$-isomorphism classes of $1$-automorphisms, and $\pi_2(\mathcal B(K),x)$ for $2$-automorphisms of the identity $1$-arrow. For a phase weight $W_K$ constant on all $1$-arrows, define the higher normalized gauging sum

$$
Z^{(2)}_K(W_K)=\sum_{[x]\in\pi_0\mathcal B(K)}W_K(x)\frac{|\pi_2(\mathcal B(K),x)|}{|\pi_1(\mathcal B(K),x)|}.
$$

Distinct raw gauge labels are not identified by equality of their effects on fields. The higher sum retains $\pi_2$; it is not ordinary groupoid integration of the $1$-truncation. In particular a point has higher weight $|A|/|G|$ for unit action, whereas an ordinary field groupoid $BG$ has weight $1/|G|$.

For a subcomplex $L\subseteq K$ and fixed field $s$ on $L$, relative fields and arrows use exact restriction to $s$, identity vertex gauge labels on $L$, zero edge gauge labels on $L$, and zero vertex $2$-gauge labels on $L$. Their higher sum uses the same $\pi_2/\pi_1$ prescription. Ordinary groupoids are included as $2$-groupoids with only identity $2$-arrows, so this prescription reduces to the preceding ordinary sum. A higher cocycle supplies an admissible scalar action only after its evaluated weight is proved invariant; nontrivial boundary line-bundle actions require their own transgression data and are not silently treated as scalar functions.

declaration.title: Finite cocycle-weighted groupoid gauging and gluing
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; conditional two-group prerequisite status and current readiness are recorded in the batch notes and Step-1 receipt.
declaration.statement:
Let $K=K_1\cup_\Sigma K_2$ be a finite ordered simplicial complex written as a union of two finite subcomplexes with common subcomplex $\Sigma$. Let $\mathcal F$, $\mathcal F_1$, $\mathcal F_2$, and $\mathcal S$ be finite background field groupoids for $K$, $K_1$, $K_2$, and $\Sigma$, with restriction functors $r_i:\mathcal F_i\to\mathcal S$. The homotopy pullback $\mathcal H=\mathcal F_2\times^h_{\mathcal S}\mathcal F_1$ has objects $(x_2,x_1,\alpha)$ with $\alpha:r_2(x_2)\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow}r_1(x_1)$ and morphisms $(u_2,u_1)$ satisfying $r_1(u_1)\circ\alpha=\alpha'\circ r_2(u_2)$.

Assume that restriction induces an equivalence $J:\mathcal F\to\mathcal H$. Let $W,W_1,W_2$ be $U(1)$-valued cocycle/action weights on these groupoids, and assume that under $J$ the weight factors as $W(x_2,x_1,\alpha)=W_2(x_2)W_1(x_1)$. For each object $s$ of $\mathcal S$, define the homotopy fiber $(\mathcal F_i)_s$ to have objects $(x_i,\eta_i:r_i(x_i)\overset{\cong}{\longrightarrow}s)$ and morphisms $u_i$ satisfying $\eta'_i\circ r_i(u_i)=\eta_i$, and put

$$ Z_i(s):=\sum_{[(x_i,\eta_i)]\in\pi_0((\mathcal F_i)_s)} \frac{W_i(x_i)}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{(\mathcal F_i)_s}(x_i,\eta_i)|}. $$

Then the normalized gauging sums are finite, are invariant under replacement of a field by a gauge-isomorphic field, and satisfy

$$ Z_K(W)= \sum_{[s]\in\pi_0(\mathcal S)} \frac{Z_2(s)Z_1(s)}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal S}(s)|}. $$

This is a finite groupoid theorem. A finite cocycle action is covered only when its evaluated weights obey the stated arrow-invariance and gluing-factorization hypotheses.

declaration.statement:
Fix a finite group $G$, finite abelian group $A$, action $\rho$, normalized $3$-cocycle $\beta$, and a finite ordered simplicial complex $K$. Let $\mathcal B(K)$ be the full background gauge $2$-groupoid, retaining its vertex $2$-gauge transformations, and let $W_K:\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal B(K)\to U(1)$ be constant on $1$-arrows. Let $V_K,E_K$ be the numbers of vertices and edges and define

$$
c(K)=\frac{|A|^{V_K-E_K}}{|G|^{V_K}}.
$$

Then its higher gauging sum satisfies

$$
Z_K^{(2)}(W_K)=\sum_{[x]}W_K(x)\frac{|\pi_2(\mathcal B(K),x)|}{|\pi_1(\mathcal B(K),x)|}=c(K)\sum_{x\in\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal B(K)}W_K(x).
$$

For any subcomplex $L$ and fixed field $s$ on $L$, the higher sum over the relative $2$-groupoid is

$$
Z_{K,L}^{(2)}(s)=\frac{c(K)}{c(L)}\sum_{x|_L=s}W_K(x).
$$

In particular let $K=K_1\cup_\Sigma K_2$, where the intersection is the subcomplex $\Sigma$ and all orders are induced. Assume invariant weights $W_i$ and $W_K$ obey $W_K(x)=W_2(x|_{K_2})W_1(x|_{K_1})$. Put $Z_i(s)=Z_{K_i,\Sigma}^{(2)}(s)$. These boundary functions are invariant on $1$-arrows of $\mathcal B(\Sigma)$ and obey the actual finite $2$-group gluing law

$$
Z_K^{(2)}(W_K)=\sum_{[s]\in\pi_0\mathcal B(\Sigma)}Z_2(s)Z_1(s)\frac{|\pi_2(\mathcal B(\Sigma),s)|}{|\pi_1(\mathcal B(\Sigma),s)|}.
$$

The empty complex has $c=1$ and one empty field. For a point and unit weight the sum is $|A|/|G|$. When $A$ is trivial these formulas reduce to ordinary finite flat $G$-connection normalization. The theorem assumes scalar invariant weights and their stated factorization; it does not assert that an arbitrary higher cocycle defines such boundary scalar data.

declaration.title: Finite semisimple fusion data for non-invertible defects
declaration.design_state: Planned exact finite semisimple fusion-category and higher-category definition; draft authored with explicit coherence and physical-realization boundary.
declaration.statement:
Fix a field $k$. In the ordinary categorical case, a **finite semisimple fusion category over $k$** is a finite semisimple tensor category in the sense of the earlier fusion-and-multifusion definition. Concretely, it is a locally small category whose Hom spaces are $k$-vector spaces and whose composition maps are $k$-bilinear. It is abelian: finite biproducts, kernels, and cokernels exist, every monomorphism is a kernel, and every epimorphism is a cokernel. Each Hom space is finite-dimensional, and every object has finite length, meaning a finite composition series with simple quotients. A simple object is nonzero with no subobject except zero and itself; every object is a finite direct sum of simple objects, and only finitely many simple isomorphism classes occur. It has a $k$-bilinear tensor bifunctor, a tensor unit $\mathbf 1$ with $\operatorname{End}(\mathbf 1)\cong k$, and a natural associator $\alpha_{X,Y,Z}:(X\otimes Y)\otimes Z\to X\otimes(Y\otimes Z)$ and left and right unitors satisfying the pentagon and triangle axioms. It is rigid: every object has left and right duals with evaluation and coevaluation morphisms satisfying the corresponding two snake identities.

Choose representatives $i\in I$ of the finitely many simple-object isomorphism classes, with $0\in I$ representing $\mathbf 1$. For each $i,j\in I$, the **fusion multiplicity** $N_{ij}^{\ell}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$ is the multiplicity of the simple object $\ell$ in a semisimple decomposition of $i\otimes j$, so $i\otimes j\cong\bigoplus_{\ell\in I}N_{ij}^{\ell}\ell$. Choose left and right duals $i^L,i^R$ with their evaluation and coevaluation maps. The fusion datum includes the actual associator, unitors, and duality maps, not just the integers $N_{ij}^{\ell}$. In chosen direct-sum decompositions the associator induces invertible maps between the corresponding multiplicity spaces; these maps must obey the pentagon, and the unitors must obey the triangle. The evaluation and coevaluation maps must obey both snake identities.

A **tensor-invertible object** $D$ is an object for which some object $E$ satisfies $D\otimes E\cong\mathbf 1$ and $E\otimes D\cong\mathbf 1$. An object with no such two-sided inverse is **non-invertible**. Simplicity and tensor-invertibility are separate properties: an object can be simple and non-invertible, or a direct sum of invertible simple objects and non-invertible as a whole.

For the **finite semisimple fusion 2-category** convention, assume that $k$ is algebraically closed of characteristic zero. A strict $k$-linear 2-category has objects, a $k$-linear Hom category for each ordered pair of objects, 1-morphisms as objects of those Hom categories, 2-morphisms as their morphisms, and strictly associative and unital horizontal composition satisfying interchange. A 1-morphism is **adjointable** when it has left and right adjoint 1-morphisms with unit and counit 2-morphisms satisfying the two triangle identities. A 1-morphism $f:A\to B$ is fully faithful when, for every object $X$, postcomposition with $f$ gives a fully faithful functor $\operatorname{Hom}(X,A)\to\operatorname{Hom}(X,B)$. A zero object $0$ is an object for which each Hom category $\operatorname{Hom}(X,0)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(0,X)$ is equivalent to the category with one object and one morphism; a zero subobject is a fully faithful 1-morphism whose domain is equivalent to a zero object. Two objects are equivalent when there are 1-morphisms in both directions whose composites are 2-isomorphic to the respective identity 1-morphisms. A nonzero object is **simple** when every fully faithful subobject of it is either zero or an equivalence.

A 2-category is **finite semisimple** when each Hom category is a finite semisimple $k$-linear category, every 1-morphism is adjointable, the 2-category is additive, every separable monad splits, and there are finitely many equivalence classes of simple objects. Additive means that zero objects and finite direct sums of objects exist and each Hom category is additive. Here a monad is a 1-endomorphism $E:B\to B$ with unit and multiplication 2-morphisms $\eta:\operatorname{id}_B\Rightarrow E$ and $m:E\circ E\Rightarrow E$ satisfying the unit and associativity laws. It is separable when $m$ has a section $c:E\Rightarrow E\circ E$ that respects the left and right $E$-actions and satisfies $m\circ c=\operatorname{id}_E$. A separable splitting is a separable adjunction $\iota:A\rightleftarrows B:\rho$ for which $E\cong\iota\circ\rho$ as monads; separability of the adjunction means that its counit has a 2-morphism section.

Use the following semistrict monoidal 2-category convention (a Gray monoid). It adds a unit object $I$, strict $k$-linear 2-functors $L_A=A\otimes-$ and $R_A=-\otimes A$ for every object $A$, and for every pair of 1-morphisms $f:A\to A'$ and $g:B\to B'$ an invertible interchanger
$$\phi_{f,g}:(f\otimes B')\circ(A\otimes g)\Rightarrow(A'\otimes g)\circ(f\otimes B).$$
Write $A\otimes B=L_A(B)=R_B(A)$. The tensor is strictly unital and associative: $L_I=R_I=\operatorname{id}$, $L_A L_B=L_{A\otimes B}$, $R_B R_A=R_{A\otimes B}$, and $L_A R_B=R_B L_A$. The interchanger is the identity when either 1-morphism is an identity, is natural in both 2-morphisms, is compatible with composition in each 1-morphism variable, and is compatible with tensoring by an object in either variable. These are coherence axioms on the data, not consequences of a fusion table.

An object $A^\#$ is a right dual of $A$ when there are evaluation and coevaluation 1-morphisms $e:A\otimes A^\#\to I$ and $i:I\to A^\#\otimes A$ and invertible 2-morphisms exhibiting $(e\otimes A)\circ(A\otimes i)\cong\operatorname{id}_A$ and $(A^\#\otimes e)\circ(i\otimes A^\#)\cong\operatorname{id}_{A^\#}$; left duals use the reversed order. A **fusion 2-category** in this convention is a finite semisimple monoidal 2-category in which every object has left and right duals and the monoidal unit is simple.

Neither finite semisimplicity nor either categorical definition asserts unitarity: a dagger structure, positivity, and any unitary coherence are additional hypotheses and data. These are abstract mathematical structures. They do not construct defect operators or junctions in a quantum field theory, specify spacetime support, or prove topological invariance; a physical realization requires a separately specified model and its own construction and proof.

The ordinary associator pentagon below displays the two composites that the axiom requires to agree. This diagram records that axiom; no proof or example verification relies on the drawing.

```tikzcd
& (((W\otimes X)\otimes Y)\otimes Z) \arrow[rr,"\alpha_{W\otimes X,Y,Z}"] \arrow[dl,"\alpha_{W,X,Y}\otimes 1_Z"'] & & (W\otimes X)\otimes(Y\otimes Z) \arrow[dr,"\alpha_{W,X,Y\otimes Z}"] & \\
(W\otimes(X\otimes Y))\otimes Z \arrow[rr,"\alpha_{W,X\otimes Y,Z}"'] & & W\otimes((X\otimes Y)\otimes Z) \arrow[ur,"1_W\otimes\alpha_{X,Y,Z}"'] & & W\otimes(X\otimes(Y\otimes Z))
```

Let $\mathbf 1$ be the trivial representation and let $\varepsilon$ be the one-dimensional sign representation, with $\varepsilon(r)=1$ and $\varepsilon(s)=-1$. In the finite-dimensional complex representation category with the tensor product action $g\cdot(x\otimes y)=(g\cdot x)\otimes(g\cdot y)$, these objects satisfy

declaration.title: A non-invertible direct sum in Vec_Z2
declaration.design_state: B-page algebraic example distinguishing non-invertibility of a direct sum from simple non-invertibility.
declaration.statement:
Let $G=\mathbb Z_2=\{0,1\}$ with addition modulo $2$. Let $\operatorname{Vec}_G$ be the category of finite-dimensional complex $G$-graded vector spaces $W=W_0\oplus W_1$, with grade-preserving linear maps and tensor product
$$(W\otimes U)_c=\bigoplus_{a+b=c}W_a\otimes_{\mathbb C}U_b.$$
Its tensor unit is $\delta_0=\mathbb C$ in grade $0$; write $\delta_1=\mathbb C$ in grade $1$. The simple objects are $\delta_0,\delta_1$, with $\delta_a\otimes\delta_b\cong\delta_{a+b}$. The object $D=\delta_0\oplus\delta_1$ satisfies
$$D\otimes D\cong 2\delta_0\oplus2\delta_1.$$
Thus $D$ is non-invertible although each of its two simple summands is tensor-invertible. The object $D$ is reducible; this example does not assert the existence of a non-invertible simple object or a physical defect realization.

declaration.title: A Z2 fusion datum with a nontrivial associator scalar
declaration.design_state: B-page algebraic example checking normalized cocycle coherence and separating fusion multiplicities from associator data.
declaration.statement:
Let $G=\mathbb Z_2=\{0,1\}$ with addition modulo $2$, and define $\omega:G^3\to\mathbb C^\times$ by $\omega(a,b,c)=(-1)^{abc}$. Let $\operatorname{Vec}_{G}^{\omega}$ have as objects finite-dimensional complex $G$-graded vector spaces, as morphisms grade-preserving linear maps, tensor product
$$(W\otimes U)_c=\bigoplus_{a+b=c}W_a\otimes_{\mathbb C}U_b,$$
and unit $\delta_0$, the one-dimensional line in grade $0$. Write $\delta_a$ for the one-dimensional line in grade $a$. On homogeneous lines take the associator
$$\alpha_{\delta_a,\delta_b,\delta_c}=\omega(a,b,c)\operatorname{id}_{\delta_{a+b+c}},$$
and extend it linearly to direct sums. Since $\omega$ is a normalized $3$-cocycle, this defines a finite semisimple fusion category with $\delta_a\otimes\delta_b\cong\delta_{a+b}$. In particular, $\delta_1\otimes\delta_1\cong\delta_0$, while $\alpha_{\delta_1,\delta_1,\delta_1}=-\operatorname{id}_{\delta_1}$. The untwisted choice $\omega\equiv1$ has the same fusion multiplicities but associator $+\operatorname{id}_{\delta_1}$ on that triple. Thus the fusion multiplicities alone do not record the specified associator component; no claim about monoidal inequivalence of these two categories is made.

declaration.title: Finite renormalization schemes and Wilson coefficient vectors
declaration.design_state: Defines a fixed-weight complex quotient coefficient interface and supplied truncated RG data; no QFT beta function or omitted-term estimate is asserted.
declaration.statement:
Work in four spacetime dimensions and natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Fix an
engineering weight $d\in\mathbb Q$ and take as input a finite-dimensional
complex quotient $V=\mathcal Q_d$ of local operators at that fixed weight, with
an ordered basis of representatives $O_1,\ldots,O_N$ and $N=\dim_{\mathbb C}V\ge1$.
The quotient and its declared relations are supplied data; this definition does
not assert that every relation relevant to an EFT, observable, or infinite
operator tower has been included. Each $O_i$ has the same engineering weight
$d$. For a fixed cutoff $\Lambda>0$ of mass dimension one, a coefficient vector
$C=(C_1,\ldots,C_N)\in\mathbb C^N$ determines the formal coefficient
expression in $V$
$$\sum_{i=1}^N\frac{C_i O_i}{\Lambda^{d-4}}.$$
Each $C_i$ is dimensionless, and each summand has mass dimension four. This is
a formal expression in the supplied quotient, not a constructed action. No
Hermiticity or reality condition is imposed; a real-action condition is
additional conjugation data.

A finite scheme record consists of a nonempty set $B$ of input labels, an open
interval $J\subset(0,\infty)$ of renormalization scales, and supplied
coefficient-coordinate maps
$$\mathcal R_\mu:B\longrightarrow\mathbb C^N\qquad(\mu\in J).$$
The maps encode the chosen subtraction and normalization convention and are
not constructed here. For $b\in B$, the scale-dependent Wilson coefficient
vector is $C_{\mathcal R}(\mu;b):=\mathcal R_\mu(b)$. The scale $\mu$ and
cutoff $\Lambda$ are distinct inputs. Choose a reference scale $\mu_0\in J$
and set
$$t:=\log(\mu/\mu_0),\qquad I:=\{\log(\mu/\mu_0):\mu\in J\};$$
then $t$ is dimensionless and $I$ is an open interval containing $0$.

Use the Euclidean norm $\|C\|_2^2=\sum_{i=1}^N|C_i|^2$ on $\mathbb C^N$.
Define the realification $\rho_N:\mathbb C^N\to\mathbb R^{2N}$ by
$$\rho_N(C_1,\ldots,C_N)=(\operatorname{Re}C_1,\operatorname{Im}C_1,\ldots,\operatorname{Re}C_N,\operatorname{Im}C_N).$$
With the Euclidean norm on $\mathbb R^{2N}$, $\rho_N$ is a real-linear
isometry. A supplied finite-dimensional truncated RG datum for this scheme
is an open set $\Omega\subset I\times\mathbb R^{2N}$ and a supplied
continuous map $\beta:\Omega\to\mathbb R^{2N}$. A truncated RG trajectory is
a continuously differentiable curve $C:I'\to\mathbb C^N$, on an interval
$I'\subset I$ for which $(t,\rho_N(C(t)))\in\Omega$, satisfying
$$\frac{d}{dt}\rho_N(C(t))=\beta(t,\rho_N(C(t))).$$
The components of $\beta$ are the beta functions under this logarithmic-scale
convention. If the supplied flow is complex-linear, with a supplied matrix
function $\Gamma:I'\to\mathbb C^{N\times N}$, its equation can be written
$C'=\Gamma(t)C$, where the real-coordinate vector field is
$\beta(t,\rho_N(C))=\rho_N(\Gamma(t)C)$. In this column-vector convention,
$\Gamma$ is called the anomalous-dimension matrix. A scheme record does not
assert that its coefficient-coordinate maps solve a supplied RG equation; that
relation, the entries of $\beta$, and any matching map are separate inputs.
This definition calculates no QFT beta function and supplies no bound on
omitted perturbative or higher-dimension terms.
