declaration.title: Gapped identical-scalar forward-amplitude data
declaration.design_state: Exact conditional input package for a gapped identical-scalar forward amplitude, including crossing, pole subtraction, real analyticity, growth, and spectral-sign assumptions.
declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. An external scalar datum consists of a spin-zero species assigned a mass $m>0$ and elastic two-particle threshold $s=4m^2$. This is a mathematical input package; it does not construct a one-particle scattering state or a scattering matrix. For real on-shell momenta $p_1,p_2$ incoming and $p_3,p_4$ outgoing, with $p_j^2=-m^2$ and $p_1+p_2=p_3+p_4$, define

$$s=-(p_1+p_2)^2,\qquad t=-(p_1-p_3)^2,\qquad u=-(p_1-p_4)^2.$$

Then $s+t+u=4m^2$. The forward slice is the complex-valued function $A(s)=\mathcal A(s,0,4m^2-s)$ obtained by analytically continuing the identical-scalar $2\to2$ amplitude to $t=0$. The crossing action on this slice is $s\mapsto4m^2-s$, which exchanges $s$ and $u$. Assume $A(s)=A(4m^2-s)$ wherever both sides are defined.

For context, when a full $t$-dependent amplitude is supplied, use the partial-wave normalization

$$\mathcal A(s,t,u)=16\pi\sqrt{\frac{s}{s-4m^2}}\sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty}(2\ell+1)P_\ell\!\left(1+\frac{2t}{s-4m^2}\right)a_\ell(s),\qquad P_\ell(1)=1,$$

where $\ell$ is a nonnegative integer and $P_\ell$ is the Legendre polynomial. The forward result below uses only the optical-theorem sign $\operatorname{Im}A(s+i0)\ge0$ for $s>4m^2$; a full partial-wave realization is not inferred from this definition. In the displayed normalization, this sign follows when the forward partial-wave sum converges and the supplied partial waves obey $\operatorname{Im}a_\ell(s)\ge|a_\ell(s)|^2\ge0$.

Put $\nu_0=2m^2$ and $v=s-2m^2$, so $u-2m^2=-v$. Choose finitely many real numbers $p_j\in(0,4m^2)\setminus\{2m^2\}$ and real residues $r_j$, and set

$$P(s)=\sum_j\left(\frac{r_j}{s-p_j}+\frac{r_j}{4m^2-p_j-s}\right).$$

Each summand pair is the real simple-pole principal part at $s=p_j$ and its $s\leftrightarrow u$ crossing partner; hence $P(4m^2-s)=P(s)$. These poles lie off the two-particle cuts. Define the pole-subtracted forward function $B(v)=A(2m^2+v)-P(2m^2+v)$. Assume $B$ is holomorphic on

$$\Omega_{\nu_0}=\mathbb C\setminus\bigl((-\infty,-\nu_0]\cup[\nu_0,\infty)\bigr),$$

real analytic there, meaning $B(\overline v)=\overline{B(v)}$, and has finite upper and lower boundary values on both cuts except at their endpoints. Here the two-particle gap is the open interval $(-\nu_0,\nu_0)$ in the $v$ variable; no massless pole or cut reaches the forward point $t=0$.

Require additionally that $B$ extends continuously from each open half-plane onto every compact segment of either real cut bank avoiding $\pm\nu_0$. This is an extra admissibility assumption on the supplied data, not a consequence of finite pointwise boundary values or a claim about every quantum field theory. 

Assume the exact high-energy condition $B(w)=o(|w|^2)$ uniformly as $|w|\to\infty$ in the closed upper half-plane, including upper cut-bank limits. In particular this holds on the large upper semicircles after any fixed bounded horizontal translation. For $\nu\ge\nu_0$, define the absorptive density $\rho(\nu)=\operatorname{Im}B(\nu+i0)$. Require $\rho$ to be nonnegative and Riemann integrable on every compact subinterval of $[\nu_0,\infty)$, and require $\int_{\nu_0}^{\infty}\rho(\nu)\nu^{-3}\,d\nu$ to converge as a finite improper Riemann integral. For every real $v$ with $|v|<\nu_0$, require the integrals along both sides of the two cuts of $[B(x)-B(0)]/[x^2(x-v)]$, with boundary values taken from the upper and lower half-planes, to exist as finite improper Riemann limits. Require also that the small endpoint arcs at $\pm\nu_0$ for this integrand vanish in the contour limit. Since $P$ is real off its poles, $\rho(\nu)=\operatorname{Im}A(2m^2+\nu+i0)$ for $\nu>\nu_0$ on the right cut.

The normalized forward Taylor coefficients are $c_n=B^{(2n)}(0)/(2n)!$ for integers $n\ge1$. They have units $(\text{mass})^{-4n}$; $\nu_0$ has units $(\text{mass})^2$. No sign is assigned here to a generic off-shell Lagrangian coefficient.

declaration.title: Finite truncated forward-amplitude bootstrap data
declaration.design_state: Exact finite normalized on-shell coefficient vector and three stated families of necessary quadratic positivity tests.
declaration.statement:
Let $B(v)$ and the positive gap scale $\nu_0$ be the pole-subtracted forward-amplitude data with $B$ even and holomorphic near $v=0$. Fix an integer truncation order $N\ge1$. For $n\ge1$ define the Taylor coefficient $c_n=B^{(2n)}(0)/(2n)!$ and the dimensionless forward on-shell coefficient $b_k=\nu_0^{2k+2}c_{k+1}$ for $0\le k\le N$. Since $v$ and $\nu_0$ have units $(\text{mass})^2$, $c_n$ has units $(\text{mass})^{-4n}$ and $b_k$ is dimensionless. Here “Wilson coefficient” refers only to this normalized on-shell amplitude coordinate; it does not identify a generic coefficient of an off-shell Lagrangian operator basis.

For each integer $r\ge0$ with $2r\le N$, form the quadratic constraint

$$\sum_{i,j=0}^{r}a_i a_j b_{i+j}\ge0\qquad\text{for every }(a_0,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb R^{r+1}.$$

For each integer $r\ge0$ with $2r+1\le N$, form the two additional quadratic constraints

$$\sum_{i,j=0}^{r}a_i a_j b_{i+j+1}\ge0,\qquad \sum_{i,j=0}^{r}a_i a_j\bigl(b_{i+j}-b_{i+j+1}\bigr)\ge0\qquad\text{for every }(a_0,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb R^{r+1}.$$

The **finite order-$N$ forward-amplitude bootstrap feasible set** $\mathcal K_N$ is the subset of $\mathbb R^{N+1}$ consisting of vectors $(b_0,\ldots,b_N)$ that satisfy every applicable constraint above. The finite truncated bootstrap problem is to determine whether a supplied coefficient vector belongs to $\mathcal K_N$. Passing this finite test is a necessary condition supplied by forward positivity; it is not defined to be sufficient for the existence of a full amplitude-data package as defined above.

declaration.title: Quartic scalar contact jets descend through verified operator relations
declaration.design_state: Explicit bounded quartic polarization map on the verified-relation image of the existing finite operator quotient; contact coefficient and exact-remainder interface, not arbitrary quantum matching.
declaration.statement:
Fix $m>0$, $\Lambda>0$, integers $r\ge1$, $D\ge4$ and $N\ge1$, and the metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Use the finite-jet operator quotient $\mathcal Q_D=V_D/R_D$ for one commuting scalar $\phi$ of weight one, field-degree cutoff four, derivative cutoff $r$, and complex orthogonal spacetime-index action preserving $\eta$. Let $U_D\subset V_D$ be the subspace of degree-exactly-four scalar polynomials whose indices are contracted using $\eta$ only, and let $Q_D^{(4)}$ be its image in $\mathcal Q_D$. Thus $Q_D^{(4)}=U_D/(U_D\cap R_D)$; operators outside this image are not assigned a contact map.

Require the following certificate for the actual declared relations: every $H\in U_D\cap R_D$ is a finite sum of identically zero jet polynomials, total divergences $\partial_\mu J^\mu$ with $J$ quartic, and $F(\Box-m^2)\phi$ with $F$ cubic, where $\Box=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu$. The summands may use a larger finite jet space and different engineering weights; their polynomial sum must equal $H$ before any on-shell substitution. This is an additional restriction on the selected $R_D$, not a claim about an arbitrary relation subspace or its completeness.

For $O\in U_D$ introduce commuting indeterminates $z_1,\ldots,z_4$ and complex four-vectors $k_1,\ldots,k_4$. Its polarized Fourier vertex is

$$T_O(k_1,k_2,k_3,k_4)=[z_1z_2z_3z_4]\,O\!\left(\partial_{\mu_1}\cdots\partial_{\mu_a}\phi\mapsto\sum_{j=1}^4 z_j i^a k_{j,\mu_1}\cdots k_{j,\mu_a}\right).$$

The coefficient convention contains no $1/4!$. Impose $\sum_jk_j=0$, $k_j^2=-m^2$, and set $s=-(k_1+k_2)^2$, $t=-(k_1+k_3)^2$, $u=-(k_1+k_4)^2$. Replace contracted products by $k_j^2=-m^2$, $k_1\cdot k_2=k_3\cdot k_4=m^2-s/2$, $k_1\cdot k_3=k_2\cdot k_4=m^2-t/2$, and $k_1\cdot k_4=k_2\cdot k_3=m^2-u/2$. Put $t=0$, $s=2m^2+v$, $u=2m^2-v$, obtaining a polynomial $t_O(v)$. Define $\nu_0=2m^2$ and the linear contact-jet map

$$M_{D,N}([O])_k=\nu_0^{2k+2}\Lambda^{4-D}[v^{2k+2}]t_O(v),\qquad 0\le k\le N.$$

Then this map $Q_D^{(4)}\to\mathbb C^{N+1}$ is well-defined, $t_O$ is even, and it takes real operator classes to real vectors. For $D=8$, $O_8=(\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi)^2$ satisfies

$$t_{O_8}(v)=8m^4+4v^2,\qquad M_{8,N}([C_8O_8])=(4\nu_0^2C_8/\Lambda^4,0,\ldots,0).$$

In particular the coefficient $[v^2]\Lambda^{-4}t_{C_8O_8}=4C_8/\Lambda^4$ is invariant under the certified relations. The target has precisely the normalized coordinate convention of the finite forward-amplitude problem. This algebraic map describes one quartic contact insertion about the free massive scalar quadratic action. It does not equate the contact polynomial to an exact full amplitude, discard loop or other-operator contributions, or infer positivity of a perturbative term from positivity of a full amplitude.

declaration.design_state: Step 1 authoring and scoped checks complete; readiness is recorded in the native per-item Step 1 record.
declaration.statement:
Each instance of the adopted classical pure Yang–Mills model has spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$,
coordinates $x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3$ of length, orientation
$dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, time orientation of increasing
$x^0$, and Lorentz metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Use
$c=\hbar=1$, so $x^0=t$, the coordinate and spacetime lengths have unit
$\mathrm m$, and the natural action $S/\hbar$ is dimensionless.

Fix the global structure group $G=SU(2)$, not its quotient $SO(3)$. Each
instance selects a smooth right principal $SU(2)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$ and
admits only its bundle sector $\Sigma=\{[P]\}$. The matter-representation label set
is empty, so there are no matter fields or current source. The Lie algebra is
$\mathfrak{su}(2)$ with basis $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$ and positive
$\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant form
$\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$, normalized by
$\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$. The positive coupling $g_{\mathrm{YM}}$ is a
fixed dimensionless model parameter.

A smooth right principal bundle here has a free and transitive smooth right
$SU(2)$ action on each fibre and equivariant local trivializations; a global
section is not part of the datum. The sector $[P]$ is the class of bundles
smoothly isomorphic to $P$ by equivariant diffeomorphisms over
$\operatorname{id}_M$. The gauge group $\mathcal G(P)$ consists of smooth
diffeomorphisms $\Phi:P\to P$ with $\pi\circ\Phi=\pi$ and
$\Phi(pg)=\Phi(p)g$. A gauge function $U_i\to SU(2)$ is only a local
description unless a global trivialization has been specified.

A principal connection is a smooth right-invariant horizontal complement
$TP=VP\oplus H$. A gauge field is its connection form $\omega$ with
$\omega(Z_P)=Z$ and $R_g^*\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}}\omega$, where
$R_g(p)=pg$ and
$Z_P(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0}p\exp_{SU(2)}(tZ)$. In a local
section $s_i:U_i\to P$, let $A_i=s_i^*\omega$ and let
$F_i=dA_i+\frac12[A_i\wedge A_i]$ be its curvature. Here the bracket is the
alternating-form extension of the Lie bracket, and the local forms on
overlaps satisfy the right-action transition convention
$A_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{ij}^{-1}}A_i+g_{ij}^{-1}dg_{ij}$ and
$F_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{ij}^{-1}}F_i$ when $s_j=s_i g_{ij}$. Thus
$F_i$ represents one global $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued two-form in the
associated adjoint bundle; the invariant form $\kappa$ makes
$\kappa(F_i\wedge *_\eta F_i)$ a global scalar four-form.

$$
\mathcal L_{\mathrm{YM}}(A_i)\,d^4x=-\frac{1}{2g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}\,\kappa(F_i\wedge *_\eta F_i),\qquad [A_i]=\mathrm m^{-1},\quad [F_i]=\mathrm m^{-2}.
$$

action is its integral. On all of $M$, the action is defined when that
integral converges. Local stationarity is tested through relative action
differences under smooth compactly supported adjoint-bundle-valued
one-form variations; these differences have compact support and are finite.
No boundary values are imposed at infinity. On a finite region, admissible
variations vanish near its boundary. This is an adopted classical model and
normalization, not a theorem, measured law, or claim that a quantum

declaration.design_state: Step 1 authoring and scoped checks complete; readiness is recorded in the native per-item Step 1 record.
declaration.statement:

$dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$ and metric

$\pi\circ\Phi=\pi$ and $\Phi(pg)=\Phi(p)g$, let $\Phi_*H=d\Phi(H)$ be its
action on a principal connection $H$. Then the local curvature density is
unchanged in every section, so every defined local action and every
convergent global action are invariant under $H\mapsto\Phi_*H$. More

$v_i:U_i\to SU(2)$ by
$\Phi^{-1}\circ s_i=s_i v_i$. The transformed curvature components satisfy
$F_i^{\Phi}=\operatorname{Ad}_{v_i^{-1}}F_i$. Each $v_i$ is local data; the
statement assumes no global map $M\to SU(2)$ for a possibly nontrivial
bundle.

declaration.statement:

$A_i=s_i^*\omega$,

local trivialization.

$D_{A_i}(*_\eta F_i)=0$ in every local section. The local equations transform
by the adjoint action on overlaps and therefore define the global,
source-free Yang–Mills equation on the selected bundle sector. This
equivalence is a conditional classical deduction from the adopted action

declaration.title: Non-Abelian gauge data and bundle sectors
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
declaration.statement:
Assume the axiom of countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. A **non-Abelian gauge datum on $M$** consists of the following specified objects.

First choose a finite-dimensional real Lie group $G$ that is compact in its manifold topology (every open cover has a finite subcover) and noncommutative (there are $g,h\in G$ with $gh\ne hg$). The actual group $G$, including its global form, is part of the datum. Its Lie algebra is $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)=T_eG$ with the bracket transported from left-invariant smooth vector fields.

Choose a smooth right principal $G$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$: the projection and right action are smooth, the action is free and transitive on each fibre, and there are local trivializations $\pi^{-1}(U)\cong U\times G$ that are equivariant diffeomorphisms over each open $U\subseteq M$.

Choose a specified set $I$ of representation labels and, for each $a\in I$, a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V_a$, a positive-definite Hermitian form $h_a$, and a smooth group homomorphism $\rho_a:G\to U(V_a,h_a)$. Here $U(V_a,h_a)$ is the group of complex-linear isometries of $h_a$, and a representation is the corresponding finite-dimensional group action. Its associated vector bundle is the quotient $E_a=P\times_{\rho_a}V_a$ with relation $[pg,v]=[p,\rho_a(g)v]$.

Two smooth right principal $G$-bundles over $M$ are isomorphic over $M$ when a smooth diffeomorphism between their total spaces covers $\operatorname{id}_M$ and commutes with the right $G$-actions. A **bundle sector** is one equivalence class under this relation. The datum specifies a set $\Sigma$ of admitted bundle sectors and requires $[P]\in\Sigma$; a model may take $\Sigma=\{[P]\}$. The Lie algebra alone does not replace the chosen group or sector. This definition does not choose a connection, an action functional, or a quantum theory.

declaration.title: Principal connection 1-form from a horizontal distribution
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
declaration.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, and let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle for a finite-dimensional real Lie group $G$, with $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)=T_eG$. A supplied principal connection is a smooth, right-invariant complement $TP=VP\oplus H$, where $VP=\ker d\pi$; write $v:TP\to VP$ for the projection along $H$, and let $K_H(X,Y)=-v([hX,hY])$ be its vertical-valued curvature. For $Z\in\mathfrak g$ and $p\in P$, define the fundamental vertical vector $Z_P(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0}p\exp_G(tZ)$. The orbit differential $\zeta_p: \mathfrak g\to V_pP$, $Z\mapsto Z_P(p)$, is a linear isomorphism, as proved below. Define the **principal connection 1-form** by

$$\omega_p(X):=\zeta_p^{-1}(v_pX),\qquad X\in T_pP.$$

Then $\omega$ is a smooth $\mathfrak g$-valued 1-form satisfying $\omega(Z_P)=Z$, $\ker\omega=H$, and $R_g^*\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}}\omega$ for every fixed $g\in G$. Conversely, a smooth $\mathfrak g$-valued 1-form with the reproduction and equivariance properties determines the principal connection $H=\ker\omega$. The converted vertical curvature $\kappa_H:=\omega\circ K_H$ is a $\mathfrak g$-valued alternating 2-form; its equality with the Cartan curvature is established in the curvature lemma.

declaration.title: Graded bracket of Lie-algebra-valued differential forms
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; authorized inventory expansion recorded; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
declaration.statement:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and $\mathfrak g$ a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra. For homogeneous $\alpha\in\Omega^p(M,\mathfrak g)$ and $\beta\in\Omega^q(M,\mathfrak g)$, define their **graded bracket** by

$$[\alpha\wedge\beta](X_1,\ldots,X_{p+q}) := \frac{1}{p!q!}\sum_{\sigma\in S_{p+q}}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)[\alpha(X_{\sigma(1)},\ldots,X_{\sigma(p)}),\beta(X_{\sigma(p+1)},\ldots,X_{\sigma(p+q)})].$$

Here $\Omega^p(M,\mathfrak g)$ is the space of smooth alternating $p$-linear forms with values in $\mathfrak g$, the inner bracket is the Lie-algebra bracket, and the sum is over all permutations. This is a smooth $\mathfrak g$-valued $(p+q)$-form. It obeys graded skew-symmetry $[\alpha\wedge\beta]=-(-1)^{pq}[\beta\wedge\alpha]$, graded Jacobi

$$\left[\alpha\wedge\left[\beta\wedge\gamma\right]\right]=\left[\left[\alpha\wedge\beta\right]\wedge\gamma\right]+(-1)^{pq}\left[\beta\wedge\left[\alpha\wedge\gamma\right]\right],$$

and the exterior-derivative rule

$$d[\alpha\wedge\beta]=[d\alpha\wedge\beta]+(-1)^p[\alpha\wedge d\beta].$$

In particular, for $\mathfrak g$-valued 1-forms $A,B$, $[A\wedge B](X,Y)=[A(X),B(Y)]-[A(Y),B(X)]$, so $\tfrac12[A\wedge A](X,Y)=[A(X),A(Y)]$. This fixes the normalization used by the Cartan curvature formula.

declaration.title: Covariant derivative on an associated representation bundle
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
declaration.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional smooth manifold, $G$ a finite-dimensional real Lie group, $\pi:P\to M$ a smooth right principal $G$-bundle, and $\omega$ the principal connection 1-form of a supplied horizontal distribution. Fix a finite-dimensional complex representation $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ that is smooth, and let $E=P\times_\rho V$ be its associated vector bundle with relation $[pg,v]=[p,\rho(g)v]$. Define $\rho_*:=d\rho_e:\mathfrak g\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, where the differential is taken after viewing $\rho$ as a smooth matrix-valued map. For any open cover with smooth local sections $s_i:U_i\to P$, write $A_i=s_i^*\omega$. A smooth section $\sigma$ of $E$ has unique local components $\psi_i:U_i\to V$ given by $\sigma(x)=[s_i(x),\psi_i(x)]$. Define the **associated covariant derivative** $\nabla^\omega\sigma$ by its local components

$$
(\nabla^\omega\sigma)_i=d\psi_i+\rho_*(A_i)\psi_i,
$$

where $(\rho_*(A_i)\psi_i)(X)=\rho_*(A_i(X))\psi_i$ for $X\in TU_i$. These expressions patch to a smooth $E$-valued 1-form on $M$, independently of the chosen local sections, and satisfy $\nabla^\omega(f\sigma)=df\otimes\sigma+f\nabla^\omega\sigma$ for every smooth scalar function $f$ on $M$.

declaration.title: Compact non-Abelian Lie-group structure of SU(2)
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored as a local mathematical prerequisite; readiness follows scoped checks.
declaration.statement:
Assume the axiom of countable choice. Let

$$SU(2):=\{U\in M_2(\mathbb C):U^*U=I_2,\ \det U=1\}$$

with matrix multiplication and the topology induced by the eight real and imaginary matrix-entry coordinates. Equip it with its standard real Lie-group structure as the special unitary matrix group. Then $SU(2)$ is a compact Hausdorff non-Abelian finite-dimensional real Lie group. Its defining representation is the map $\rho_2:SU(2)\to U(2)$, $\rho_2(V)=V$, acting on $\mathbb C^2$ with the standard Hermitian form $h(v,w)=v^*w$; it is a smooth unitary group homomorphism.

Every $V\in SU(2)$ has the form $V=\begin{pmatrix}\alpha&\beta\\-\overline{\beta}&\overline{\alpha}\end{pmatrix}$ with $|\alpha|^2+|\beta|^2=1$; consequently $\tfrac12\operatorname{ReTr}_2V=\operatorname{Re}\alpha\in[-1,1]$.

declaration.statement:
Assume full AC and use the finite non-Abelian lattice-data interface with global group $SU(2)$ and its smooth defining unitary representation on standard $\mathbb C^2$. Let $N_s,N_t\geq3$ be finite integers and let $a>0$, $\beta>0$. Use the finite periodic Euclidean lattice $\Lambda=(\mathbb Z/N_s\mathbb Z)^3\times(\mathbb Z/N_t\mathbb Z)$, with its finite oriented two-complex of vertices, positive spatial edges $(x,i,t)$, temporal edges $(x,t)$, and oriented plaquette boundary words. On every positive edge put an independent matrix in the compact Hausdorff Lie group

$$SU(2)=\{U\in M_2(\mathbb C):U^*U=I_2,\ \det U=1\},$$

and assign its inverse to reverse traversal. A vertex function $\Omega:\Lambda\to SU(2)$ acts on an oriented link $U_{vw}$ by $U_{vw}\mapsto\Omega_vU_{vw}\Omega_w^{-1}$. For each oriented plaquette $p$, let $U_p$ be the ordered product of its four boundary links, using inverse matrices for reverse traversals. Put

$$S_\Lambda(U)=\beta\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_\Lambda}\left(1-\tfrac12\operatorname{ReTr}_2U_p\right).$$

Let $dU$ be the unique normalized left Haar Borel probability measure on $SU(2)$, which is also right invariant, and use it as the bi-invariant link measure in the finite lattice-data interface. Let $d\mu_\Lambda$ be its finite product over all positive links, formed by the finite-product measure theorem. Define

$$Z_\Lambda=\int e^{-S_\Lambda(U)}\,d\mu_\Lambda(U).$$

For every bounded measurable function $O$ on the finite link configuration space, the integral $\int Oe^{-S_\Lambda}\,d\mu_\Lambda$ is finite; moreover $0<Z_\Lambda\leq1$, so its normalized expectation is defined.

For a spatial slice $u=(U_{x,i})$, define the spatial plaquette action $S_s(u)$ by restricting the displayed action to spatial plaquettes. For two adjacent slices $u',u$ and temporal links $\eta_x$, define $S_t(u',u;\eta)$ by summing the same plaquette term over $\eta_xU'_{x,i}\eta_{x+\hat i}^{-1}U_{x,i}^{-1}$. Let $d\mu_s,d\mu_V$ be the corresponding finite product Haar probabilities, let $\mathcal H_{\rm kin}=L^2(SU(2)^{E_s},d\mu_s)$, and for $h\in SU(2)^{V_s}$ set $(\mathcal U(h)\psi)(u)=\psi(h^{-1}\cdot u)$, with equality in $L^2$. Define $\mathcal H_{\rm phys}=\{\psi\in\mathcal H_{\rm kin}:\mathcal U(h)\psi=\psi\text{ for every }h\in SU(2)^{V_s}\}$.

$$K(u',u)=e^{-\frac12S_s(u')-\frac12S_s(u)}\int e^{-S_t(u',u;\eta)}\,d\mu_V(\eta),\qquad (T\psi)(u')=\int K(u',u)\psi(u)\,d\mu_s(u).$$

Then $\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$ is closed and contains the nonzero constant function. $T$ is a bounded operator on $\mathcal H_{\rm kin}$ with $\|T\|\leq1$ and maps $\mathcal H_{\rm kin}$ into $\mathcal H_{\rm phys}$. The cyclic product of $N_t$ kernels integrates to $Z_\Lambda$; insertion of any bounded slice observable gives the corresponding finite-volume unnormalized expectation. No self-adjointness, positivity as a quadratic form, Hamiltonian limit, or continuum statement is asserted.

declaration.title: Compact Non-Abelian Finite-Lattice Regulator
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored conditionally on the actual batch-6 finite-lattice-data interface; current upstream readiness records are verified.
declaration.statement:
Adopt the following pure-gauge Euclidean regulator. Assume full AC for normalized Haar-probability existence and for the L² transfer-operator framework. Let $N_s,N_t\geq3$ be integers, $a>0$ a common lattice spacing, and $g_0>0$ a dimensionless bare coupling. Use natural units $\hbar=c=1$. The finite periodic lattice is

$$\Lambda=(\mathbb Z/N_s\mathbb Z)^3\times(\mathbb Z/N_t\mathbb Z),$$

with spatial extent $L_s=N_sa$ in each spatial direction and Euclidean time extent $L_t=N_ta$. The global gauge group supplied by the finite non-Abelian lattice datum is

$$SU(2)=\{U\in M_2(\mathbb C):U^*U=I_2,\ \det U=1\},$$

the compact Hausdorff non-Abelian Lie group established in the preceding local lemma, with its smooth defining two-dimensional unitary representation. Use that representation; $U^*$ denotes conjugate transpose and $\operatorname{Tr}_2$ its matrix trace. All link variables are dimensionless.

For each positive spatial direction $i\in\{1,2,3\}$, assign a link matrix $U_{x,i,t}\in SU(2)$ from $(x,t)$ to $(x+\hat i,t)$. Assign a temporal link matrix $\eta_{x,t}\in SU(2)$ from $(x,t)$ to $(x,t+1)$, with time understood modulo $N_t$. A reversed link carries the inverse matrix. Vertex gauge transformations are all functions $\Omega:\Lambda\to SU(2)$, acting by

$$U_{x,i,t}\mapsto \Omega_{x,t}U_{x,i,t}\Omega_{x+\hat i,t}^{-1},\qquad \eta_{x,t}\mapsto\Omega_{x,t}\eta_{x,t}\Omega_{x,t+1}^{-1}.$$

For $i<j$, define the spatial plaquette product

$$U_{x,ij,t}=U_{x,i,t}U_{x+\hat i,j,t}U_{x+\hat j,i,t}^{-1}U_{x,j,t}^{-1},$$

and define the temporal-spatial plaquette product

$$Q_{x,i,t}=\eta_{x,t}U_{x,i,t+1}\eta_{x+\hat i,t}^{-1}U_{x,i,t}^{-1}.$$

Set $\beta=4/g_0^2$, a positive dimensionless parameter. For a spatial slice $u=(U_{x,i})$, set

$$S_s(u)=\beta\sum_{x,\ i<j}\left(1-\tfrac12\operatorname{ReTr}_2 U_{x,ij}\right),$$

and for adjacent slices $u',u$ and temporal links $\eta=(\eta_x)$, set

$$S_t(u',u;\eta)=\beta\sum_{x,\ i}\left(1-\tfrac12\operatorname{ReTr}_2(\eta_xU'_{x,i}\eta_{x+\hat i}^{-1}U_{x,i}^{-1})\right).$$

The adopted Wilson action is $S_\Lambda=\sum_{t=0}^{N_t-1}\big(S_s(u_t)+S_t(u_{t+1},u_t;\eta_t)\big)$, with $u_{N_t}=u_0$. The compact Hausdorff group $SU(2)$ has the unique normalized left Haar probability measure $dU$, which is also right invariant under the assumed Axiom of Choice. On each positively oriented link use this measure; $d\mu_\Lambda$ is its finite product over the link set. The exact finite-volume partition function and observable expectation for every bounded gauge-invariant function $O$ are

$$Z_\Lambda=\int e^{-S_\Lambda}\,d\mu_\Lambda,\qquad \langle O\rangle_\Lambda=Z_\Lambda^{-1}\int Oe^{-S_\Lambda}\,d\mu_\Lambda.$$

For the transfer convention, let $\mathcal H_{\rm kin}=L^2(SU(2)^{E_s},d\mu_s)$, where $E_s$ is the finite set of positive spatial links in one slice and $d\mu_s$ is product normalized Haar probability. Define $\mathcal H_{\rm phys}=\{\psi\in\mathcal H_{\rm kin}:\mathcal U(h)\psi=\psi\text{ for every }h\in SU(2)^{V_s}\}$, where $V_s$ is the finite vertex set of the slice and $\mathcal U(h)\psi(u)=\psi(h^{-1}\!\cdot u)$ in $L^2$. The finite-lattice well-definedness result establishes that this fixed subspace is closed. It is the group-invariant finite-slice Gauss sector. Define

$$K(u',u)=e^{-\frac12S_s(u')-\frac12S_s(u)}\int_{SU(2)^{V_s}}e^{-S_t(u',u;\eta)}\,d\mu_V(\eta),\qquad (T\psi)(u')=\int K(u',u)\psi(u)\,d\mu_s(u).$$

The finite Euclidean time direction is assembled by iterating this one-step transfer operator, with the periodic boundary identification stated above. This is a Euclidean transfer convention only: no self-adjoint or positive-spectrum claim for $T$, no Lorentzian Hamiltonian identification, and no continuum or infinite-volume limit are postulated. The model has no dynamical matter fields, so it makes no matter-screening, confinement, or string-breaking claim. The regulator is adopted, not derived from a continuum theory or empirical evidence.

The quantities $a,L_s,L_t$ have units of length; $g_0,\beta,U_{x,i,t},\eta_{x,t},S_\Lambda,Z_\Lambda$ are dimensionless in the stated natural-unit convention. No measured parameter is supplied.

declaration.statement:

T_{C_2}(T_{C_1}f)(x)=T_{C_1+C_2}f(x)\qquad(x\in\mathbb R^d)

e^{-(V_{C_1})_{C_2}(x)}=e^{-V_{C_1+C_2}(x)}.

The Gaussian measures are normalized probabilities, so no determinant or vacuum constant appears. This is a finite-regulator composition identity; it asserts no derivative equation along a covariance path and no continuum limit.

Use four-dimensional Minkowski space $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$, coordinates $x^0=ct$ and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and natural units $c=\hbar=1$ for mass-dimension counting. A **physical EFT operator contract** is a record of the following selected model data; none of the selections is inferred from an operator's name.

Here an EFT is an adopted low-energy model whose local Lagrangian is organized by specified fields, symmetries, coefficients, and a finite retained order; this definition implies no ultraviolet completion or physical realization. First choose a finite set $I$ of field species. For each $i\in I$, specify a finite-dimensional complex graded space $\Phi_i=\Phi_i^{\bar 0}\oplus\Phi_i^{\bar 1}$, its bosonic or fermionic parity, its smooth field domain on $M$, any reality condition, and its assigned rational engineering weight $\Delta_i$. Even fields are smooth maps $M\to\Phi_i^{\bar 0}$; odd field components take values in a fixed Grassmann algebra with smooth coefficient functions. A spurion is a fixed, non-dynamical parameter assigned a representation and engineering weight, used to record a declared symmetry-breaking insertion. The proper orthochronous Lorentz group is $SO^+(1,3)=\{L\in GL_4(\mathbb R):L^T\eta L=\eta,\ \det L=1,\ L^0{}_0\ge1\}$; specify its finite-dimensional action on all spacetime indices and require each Lagrangian density to be a Lorentz scalar. State the full gauge and flavor actions on every field, index, and spurion. A flavor symmetry that is absent is recorded as trivial; an approximate or explicitly broken symmetry requires its breaking spurions and weights to be listed.

For a non-Abelian gauge sector, specify the compact real gauge group with its actual global form, smooth right principal bundle, admitted bundle sectors, unitary representations, and a smooth principal connection. The connection is a Lie-algebra-valued one-form reproducing fundamental vertical vectors and transforming by the adjoint action; its local curvature is $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$, and the covariant derivative in a representation $\rho$ is $D_\mu\psi=\partial_\mu\psi+\rho_*(A_\mu)\psi$. The field and connection data must include their regularity and spacetime and internal index representations. These formulas use the right-principal-bundle convention fixed by the supplied gauge-geometry definitions.

The local operator algebra uses a separate finite-dimensional rational representation of a complex reductive affine algebraic group $G_{\mathrm{alg}}$ on the finite jet generators. A contract must supply the maps and representations relating $G_{\mathrm{alg}}$ to the selected compact gauge group and flavor group. It must either verify, on each retained finite jet space, that the algebraic invariant subspace is exactly the intended physical invariant space, or label the quotient as a formal algebraic selection only. Compactness of a real gauge group alone does not identify its invariant polynomials with those of an algebraic complexification.

Choose nonnegative integer cutoffs $r$ and $q$, a coefficient field (here $\mathbb C$) and its conjugation data, and a finite rational maximum engineering dimension $D_{\max}$. With derivatives assigned weight one, the local field-jet definition supplies the supercommutative polynomial module $P_r=\operatorname{Sym}(J_{r,\bar 0}^*)\otimes\Lambda(J_{r,\bar 1}^*)$ and its fixed-weight subspaces. For each weight $D$, let $W_D$ be the finite raw polynomial space, $V_D=W_D^{G_{\mathrm{alg}}}$ its invariant scalar subspace, and $\widetilde R_D$ the explicitly declared $G_{\mathrm{alg}}$-stable linear relation subspace. The selected operator quotient is $\mathcal Q_D=V_D/(\widetilde R_D\cap V_D)$: it identifies exactly the declared relations and makes no completeness claim about all EFT redundancies. For each retained $D$, choose a vector-space basis of $\mathcal Q_D$ and one representative $\mathcal O_\alpha\in V_D$ of each basis class; write $\mathcal I_{\mathrm{op}}$ for the resulting finite set of representative labels and $\Delta_\alpha$ for the weight of $\mathcal O_\alpha$. The finite jet, field-degree, and dimension cutoffs give a finite-dimensional retained space, and the fixed-cutoff monomial set gives finitely many retained weights and representatives.

For each $\widetilde R_D$, record each generator as a polynomial or Fierz identity, a total divergence under compact-support or stated boundary conditions, or a leading-equation or field-redefinition relation tied to an explicit base action and retained order. An equation-of-motion entry records its variational derivative and field multiplier; a field-redefinition entry records the local map, its inverse through the retained order, and all induced higher-order terms. The quotient is a definition of the declared relation space; its existence alone does not establish action, off-shell Green-function, quantum-measure, or scattering equivalence.

Choose the canonical-dimension power-counting scheme, coefficient truncation, and a nonnegative integer loop order $L_{\max}$. The formal loop label $\zeta$ is dimensionless bookkeeping and is not a convergence claim. If $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}>0$ is the coefficient-suppression scale, the retained local Lagrangian has the convention

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{tr}}=\sum_{\substack{\alpha\in\mathcal I_{\mathrm{op}}\\\Delta_\alpha\le D_{\max}}}\sum_{\ell=0}^{L_{\max}}\zeta^\ell C_{\alpha,\ell}(\mu_W)\frac{\mathcal O_\alpha}{\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}^{\Delta_\alpha-4}},$$

where each $\mathcal O_\alpha$ has engineering weight $\Delta_\alpha$, each $C_{\alpha,\ell}$ is dimensionless in the stated natural units, and the chosen reality conditions make $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{tr}}$ real. This is canonical-dimension counting for the selected linear EFT; HEFT chiral counting and multi-scale SCET counting are different schemes and are not implied. A truncation order is not a numerical error bound, a coefficient prediction, or a derived renormalization-group flow.

If the same application also uses a finite-regulator data record, retain its graph variables, measure, Wilsonian scale $\mu_W$, heavy mass $M$, external-energy bound $E$, and regulator cutoff $\Lambda$ with their supplied meanings. The operator-suppression scale $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$, regulator cutoff $\Lambda$, $M$, $E$, and $\mu_W$ are distinct parameters unless an additional model input identifies them. Let $\phi\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ be a real, Grassmann-even (commuting) scalar field of engineering dimension one, with a stable one-particle state of pole mass $m>0$; here stable means an isolated real mass pole with zero decay width. Stability and the existence of this state are physical input data; no construction of a state is asserted. An effective field theory (EFT) here is the selected local low-energy representative organized in powers of its cutoff; its exact amplitude is separate supplied model data. For the finite-jet local-operator convention, use the complexification for the finite-jet algebra and impose the usual reality condition on $\phi$. Take one field species, maximum jet order $r=1$, polynomial degree at most $q=4$, weight $D=8$, trivial internal group, and the standard Lorentz tensor action with contractions formed using $\eta$. The real operator $\mathcal O_8=(\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi)^2$ is then a local scalar of engineering dimension eight. Its coefficient in a chosen local representative is written

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{EFT}}=-\frac12\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi-\frac12m^2\phi^2+\frac{C_8(\mu_*)}{\Lambda^4}\mathcal O_8+\cdots,$$

where $\Lambda>2m$ is the positive energy cutoff of the EFT description, $0<\mu_*<\Lambda$ is the chosen scale at which the coefficient and matching identity are specified, and $C_8(\mu_*)\in\mathbb R$ is dimensionless in the fixed coefficient convention and local representative. No basis-independence under field redefinitions, equations of motion, or integration by parts is asserted for $C_8$ itself.

The amplitude data consist of an identical-scalar $2\to2$ amplitude $\mathcal A(s,t,u)$ and real on-shell momenta $p_j$ with $p_j^2=-m^2$, $p_1+p_2=p_3+p_4$, and

$$s=-(p_1+p_2)^2,\qquad t=-(p_1-p_3)^2,\qquad u=-(p_1-p_4)^2,\qquad s+t+u=4m^2.$$

The forward slice is $A(s)=\mathcal A(s,0,4m^2-s)$ and assume $A(s)=A(4m^2-s)$ wherever both sides are defined. When the full $t$-dependent amplitude is supplied, use the partial-wave normalization

$$\mathcal A(s,t,u)=16\pi\sqrt{\frac{s}{s-4m^2}}\sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty}(2\ell+1)P_\ell\!\left(1+\frac{2t}{s-4m^2}\right)a_\ell(s),\qquad P_\ell(1)=1.$$

Here $\ell=0,1,2,\ldots$, $P_\ell$ is the Legendre polynomial, and $a_\ell(s)$ is the partial-wave coefficient. The formula is a normalization convention when a full amplitude is supplied; it does not assert convergence or unitarity by itself.

The $S$-matrix convention is $S=1+i(2\pi)^4\delta^4(p_{\mathrm{out}}-p_{\mathrm{in}})\mathcal A+\cdots$. The channel adopts the forward optical-theorem input $\operatorname{Im}A(s+i0)\ge0$ for $s>4m^2$ in this normalization. This sign is an assumption on the supplied amplitude data, not a deduction from the EFT truncation.

Put $\nu_0=2m^2$ and $v=s-2m^2$, so $u-2m^2=-v$. Let the specified finite list contain every isolated variable simple pole in the subthreshold interval, with real locations $p_j\in(0,4m^2)\setminus\{2m^2\}$ and real residues $r_j$. For the dimensionless amplitude convention above, $r_j$ has mass dimension two. Define the crossing-symmetric pole subtraction

$$P(s)=\sum_j\left(\frac{r_j}{s-p_j}+\frac{r_j}{4m^2-p_j-s}\right),\qquad B(v)=A(2m^2+v)-P(2m^2+v).$$

The exact amplitude data are required to be crossing even and real analytic, with $B(-v)=B(v)$, $B(\overline v)=\overline{B(v)}$, and $B$ holomorphic on

$$\Omega_{\nu_0}=\mathbb C\setminus\bigl(( -\infty,-\nu_0]\cup[\nu_0,\infty)\bigr).$$

There is no massless pole or cut at the forward point $t=0$. Require finite upper and lower cut-boundary values except at $\pm\nu_0$. Also require $B$ to extend continuously from each open half-plane onto every compact segment of either real cut bank avoiding $\pm\nu_0$. This is an extra admissibility assumption on the supplied data, not a consequence of finite pointwise boundary values or a claim about every quantum field theory. Require the uniform high-energy condition $B(w)=o(|w|^2)$ as $|w|\to\infty$ in the closed upper half-plane including upper cut-bank limits, and vanishing endpoint arcs for the cut integrals. For $\nu>\nu_0$, let $\rho(\nu)=\operatorname{Im}B(\nu+i0)$ and assign $\rho(\nu_0)=0$ by convention, without asserting a threshold boundary limit; changing this one endpoint value changes no Riemann integral; require $\rho\ge0$, local Riemann integrability on every compact subinterval of $[\nu_0,\infty)$, and finite convergence of $\int_{\nu_0}^{\infty}\rho(\nu)\nu^{-3}\,d\nu$. For every real $|v|<\nu_0$, the upper- and lower-bank integrals of $[B(x)-B(0)]/[x^2(x-v)]$ are required to exist as finite improper Riemann limits. The positive gap $m>0$ and these analytic and spectral assumptions are IR and UV input conditions; they are not derived from a finite regulator.

Define the first nonconstant even forward coefficient by $c_1=B''(0)/2!$, of mass dimension $-4$. Exact matching at $\mu_*$ is a supplied datum of the form

declaration.title: N=2 central-charge saturation is equivalent to annihilation by the null supercharge pair
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft with complete conditional argument or definition; current prerequisite interfaces and page inventories reconciled in the owner resolution evidence. Root records readiness separately.
declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Use the four-dimensional rigid N=2 super-Poincare convention with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $\epsilon_{12}=1$, and natural units $\hbar=c=1$. Let $\mathcal K\ne\{0\}$ be a positive Hilbert rest-fiber representation with $P^\mu=(M,0,0,0)$, $M>0$, scalar central charges $Z^{12}=zI$ and $Z^{21}=-zI$, and a common dense invariant domain $\mathcal D$ on which the supercharges, their actual Hilbert adjoints, and every product below are defined. Thus $P_0=-M$, each supercharge has mass dimension one-half, and $M,z$ have mass dimension one. Choose $\phi\in\mathbb R$ so that $e^{-i\phi}z=|z|$, with arbitrary $\phi$ when $z=0$, and on $\mathcal D$ put

$$q=Q^1_1,\qquad r=Q^2_2,\qquad A=q-e^{i\phi}r^*,\qquad A^\sharp=q^*-e^{-i\phi}r.$$

For every $\psi\in\mathcal D$,

$$\langle(AA^\sharp+A^\sharp A)\psi,\psi\rangle=\|A\psi\|^2+\|A^\sharp\psi\|^2=4(M-|z|)\|\psi\|^2.$$

Consequently, for every nonzero $\psi\in\mathcal D$, $M=|z|$ if and only if $A\psi=A^\sharp\psi=0$. The operator $A^\sharp$ is the displayed sum of the individual charge adjoints; for unbounded charges it is not asserted to be the maximal-domain adjoint of the sum $A$. This conditional statement neither asserts that such a vector or representation occurs in a physical model nor proves its dynamical stability.

declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and use natural units $\hbar=c=1$. A **BPS-saturated state** in this item is a nonzero vector $\psi\in\mathcal D$ in a specified massive rest fiber for which $M=\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. This term records algebraic saturation only; it does not assert that any specified charge is represented by a state, or that a saturating state exists, is stable, or occurs in a physical spectrum.

For $N=2$, write $z=z^{12}$, so $Z=\begin{pmatrix}0&z\\-z&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}=|z|$. In this $N=2$ case, a nonzero domain vector saturates the bound if and only if both displayed combinations annihilate it. For unbounded charges, $A^\sharp$ denotes the displayed sum of individual adjoints and is not assumed to be the maximal-domain adjoint of $A$.

declaration.title: Finite-dimensional gauge slices and Faddeev–Popov operators
declaration.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; item readiness is recorded separately. The planned Singer theorem has no carrier and remains explicitly escalated in batch evidence.
declaration.statement:
Assume the axiom of countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. Fix a compact noncommutative finite-dimensional real Lie group $G$, whose Lie algebra is $\mathfrak g=T_eG$ with bracket transported from left-invariant vector fields. Let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth right principal bundle: the right action is smooth, free and transitive on each fibre, and each point has a local equivariant principal chart. Let $H\subset TP$ be a supplied smooth right-invariant horizontal complement to $VP=\ker(d\pi)$, and write $v$ for projection onto $VP$ along $H$. For $Z\in\mathfrak g$, the fundamental vertical vector is $Z_P(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0}p\exp_G(tZ)$. The principal connection form $\omega$ is a smooth $\mathfrak g$-valued one-form satisfying $\omega(Z_P)=Z$, $\ker\omega=H$, and $R_g^*\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}}\omega$, where $\operatorname{Ad}_g=d(C_g)_e$ and $C_g(h)=ghg^{-1}$. In a local section $s:U\to P$ (a smooth map with $\pi\circ s=\operatorname{id}_U$), the potential $A=s^*\omega$ changes under a section change $s'=su$, for smooth $u:U\to G$, by $A'=\operatorname{Ad}_{u^{-1}}A+\theta_L(u)$, where $\theta_L(u)=u^*\theta_L$, $(\theta_L)_g=d(L_{g^{-1}})_g$, and $L_g(h)=gh$. The full gauge group consists of smooth diffeomorphisms $\Phi:P\to P$ satisfying $\pi\circ\Phi=\pi$ and $\Phi(pg)=\Phi(p)g$; this definition gives it no finite-dimensional Lie-group structure.

A **finite-dimensional regulated gauge-slice datum** consists of integers $1\le k\le n$; a finite-dimensional Lie group $K$ of dimension $k$, with Lie algebra $\mathfrak k:=T_eK$ and bracket transported from left-invariant vector fields; a chosen smooth positive left-invariant density $\mu_K$, meaning $(L_h^K)^*\mu_K=\mu_K$ for $L_h^K(g)=hg$; a finite-dimensional smooth manifold $X$ of dimension $n$ with a chosen smooth positive density $\mu_X$; and a smooth right action $\alpha:X\times K\to X$, written $x\cdot g$, with $x\cdot e=x$ and $(x\cdot g)\cdot h=x\cdot(gh)$. A smooth positive density on an $m$-manifold has coordinate form $\rho(x)|dx^1\cdots dx^m|$ with smooth $\rho>0$, and transforms by the absolute coordinate Jacobian. The group $K$ and its action on $X$ are separate regulator data. They are not identified with the full gauge group or the full space of connections unless a particular finite model explicitly constructs such an action and verifies that it preserves $X$.

Choose an embedded smooth submanifold $S\subset X$ of codimension $k$, a smooth positive density $\mu_S$, and an open neighborhood $U\subset X$ of a point $s\in S$. Embedded means that near each point of $S$, a smooth chart on $X$ identifies $S$ with $\mathbb R^{n-k}\times\{0\}$. A **gauge condition** on $U$ is a smooth map $\chi:U\to\mathbb R^k$ such that $U\cap S=\chi^{-1}(0)$ and, for every $s'\in U\cap S$, $d\chi_{s'}$ is surjective with kernel $T_{s'}S$. For every $x\in U$, the **infinitesimal orbit map** is $R_x:=d(\alpha_x)_e:\mathfrak k\to T_xX$, where $\alpha_x(g)=x\cdot g$; call its kernel the infinitesimal stabilizer at $x$. The **Faddeev–Popov operator** at $x$ is the ordinary linear map $M_x:=d\chi_x\circ R_x:\mathfrak k\to\mathbb R^k$. At a slice point $s'\in U\cap S$, call the condition **transverse** when $M_{s'}$ is an isomorphism. Choose a positive density $\nu$ on $\mathfrak k$ equal to $(\mu_K)_e$, and the standard positive density $\lambda$ on $\mathbb R^k$. For every $x\in U$, the finite-dimensional Faddeev–Popov Jacobian $\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}(x)$ is the nonnegative density ratio defined by $M_x^*\lambda=\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}(x)\nu$; in chosen bases it is $|\det M_x|$, and it is zero when $M_x$ is singular.

This datum defines only finite-dimensional Jacobians and local coordinate slices. It neither defines a determinant of an infinite-dimensional operator nor constructs a functional measure or a continuum path integral. A finite-mode or lattice application must supply the regulator manifold $X$, the finite-dimensional group $K$, their smooth action, and the domains and densities above.

where $\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}$ uses the density $(\mu_K)_e$ and the standard density on $\mathbb R^k$. $$
\int_O f\,d\mu_X=\int_{V\times W}(f\circ\Psi)J_\Psi\,d\mu_K\,d\mu_S.
$$

For the exact multiplicity statement, fix $x\in X$ and a relatively compact open set $\Gamma\subset K$ such that $x\cdot\overline{\Gamma}\subset U$. Let $F_x(g)=\chi(x\cdot g)$. Let $r\ge 0$ be finite, and suppose $F_x$ has exactly $r$ zeros $g_1,\ldots,g_r$ in the support of a smooth function $\varphi$ compactly supported in $\Gamma$, each $M_{x\cdot g_i}$ is invertible, and the slice points $s_i=x\cdot g_i$ are distinct. $$

$$

declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a nonempty compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, let $N\ge2$, and let $P\to M$ be any smooth right principal $SU(N)$-bundle. Write $SU(N)=\{g\in M_N(\mathbb C):g^*g=I,\det g=1\}$ and $\mathfrak{su}(N)=\{X\in M_N(\mathbb C):X^*=-X,\operatorname{tr}X=0\}$. Then there exists a smooth $\mathfrak{su}(N)$-valued one-form $\omega$ on $P$ such that, for every $X\in\mathfrak{su}(N)$, its fundamental vertical vector is $X_P(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0}p\exp(tX)$, and
$$
\omega(X_P)=X,\qquad R_h^*\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{h^{-1}}\omega\quad(h\in SU(N)),
$$
where $R_h(p)=ph$ and $\operatorname{Ad}_h(X)=hXh^{-1}$. Such a one-form is a smooth principal connection form; the conclusion does not assert a global trivialization of $P$.

declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $r\in\{3,4\}$, let $N\ge2$, and let $P\to S^r$ be any smooth principal right $SU(N)$-bundle, with the standard round metric and orientation on $S^r$. Here $S^r=\{x\in\mathbb R^{r+1}:\|x\|=1\}$, and $SU(N)=\{U\in M_N(\mathbb C):U^*U=I,\det U=1\}$. A principal right bundle means a smooth surjective bundle with free right $SU(N)$ action, locally equivariantly diffeomorphic to $U\times SU(N)$. Write $\mathfrak{su}(N)$ for its Lie algebra, set $\operatorname{ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}\mathfrak{su}(N)$ and $\operatorname{Ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}SU(N)$, using $[pg,z]=[p,gzg^{-1}]$ and $\operatorname{Ad}_g z=gzg^{-1}$. A smooth principal connection is a smooth $\mathfrak{su}(N)$-valued one-form $\omega$ on $P$ with $\omega(\xi_P)=\xi$ for each fundamental vertical vector $\xi_P(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0}p\exp(t\xi)$ and $R_g^*\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}}\omega$, where $R_g(p)=pg$. Let $\mathcal A^\infty(P)$ be the affine space of these connections, modeled on $\Omega^1(S^r;\operatorname{ad}P)$, with the $C^\infty$ section topology generated by all derivative seminorms in a fixed finite bundle atlas. Let $\mathcal G^\infty(P)=\Gamma^\infty(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ be the smooth gauge group with pointwise multiplication and its $C^\infty$ section topology. For the Sobolev intermediary choose a smooth reference connection $A_0$ (its existence is also exhibited in the proof), fix any integer $k>r/2+1$, and use $\mathcal A_k(P)=A_0+H^k(T^*S^r\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and $\mathcal G_{k+1}(P)=H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$, where these Sobolev spaces are completions in the finite-atlas norms from square-integrable derivatives through the indicated order.

Fix $m\in S^r$ and a frame $p_m\in P_m$. Parallel transport around piecewise smooth loops based at $m$, expressed in this frame, gives the holonomy subgroup $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)\subseteq SU(N)$. A connection is **irreducible** when this subgroup leaves no nonzero proper complex subspace of $\mathbb C^N$ invariant; this condition is unchanged by conjugating the chosen frame. Write $\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)\subseteq\mathcal A^\infty(P)$ for this locus. In local sections the right gauge action is $A^u=u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$.

Let $Z_N=\{\zeta I_N:\zeta^N=1\}$ be the central subgroup of constant gauge sections and let $\overline{\mathcal G}^\infty(P)=\mathcal G^\infty(P)/Z_N$ with its quotient topology. Give every orbit space below its quotient topology, and define
$$
q_*:\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)\longrightarrow\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)/\overline{\mathcal G}^\infty(P),\qquad q:\mathcal A^\infty(P)\longrightarrow\mathcal A^\infty(P)/\mathcal G^\infty(P)
$$
to be the reduced and full orbit projections. A continuous section of either projection is a continuous right inverse. The natural square

```tikz
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P) \arrow[r,hook,"j"] \arrow[d,"q_*"'] & \mathcal A^\infty(P) \arrow[d,"q"] \\
\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P)/\overline{\mathcal G}^\infty(P) \arrow[r,"\iota"'] & \mathcal A^\infty(P)/\mathcal G^\infty(P)
\end{tikzcd}
```

commutes, where $j$ is inclusion and $\iota$ sends a reduced orbit to its full orbit. The map $\iota$ identifies its domain with the open subset $q(\mathcal A^{\infty,*}(P))$ of the full orbit space.

Neither $q_*$ nor $q$ has a continuous section. Both conclusions hold for every bundle sector, including nontrivial bundles; irreducibility here does not mean that the holonomy equals all of $SU(N)$.

declaration.statement:
Take $M=\{\star\}$, $G=SU(2)$ as the noncommutative group of unit quaternions, $P=SU(2)\to M$ with right multiplication, $H=0$, and connection form $\omega=q^{-1}dq$. $$
(x,y)\cdot R_\theta=(x\cos\theta+y\sin\theta,\,-x\sin\theta+y\cos\theta).
$$

For a fixed orbit point $x_0=(r,0)$, $r>0$, the gauge function is $F_{x_0}(R_\theta)=-r\sin\theta$. At the origin the full group stabilizes the point, $M_{(0,0)}=0$, and $F_{(0,0)}$ vanishes on all of $SO(2)$; the theorem's isolated transverse-zero hypotheses fail there.

declaration.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer. Give $\mathbb C^n$ the Euclidean topology transported from $\mathbb R^{2n}$ by the real coordinates $z^i=x^i+i y^i$, where $x^i,y^i\in\mathbb R$. Let $U\subseteq\mathbb C^n$ be open in this topology and contain $0$. Each complex number has its unique real decomposition $a+ib$ with $a,b\in\mathbb R$; write $\overline{a+ib}=a-ib$. A function on $U$ is smooth if all of its partial derivatives of every finite order in the real coordinates $(x^1,y^1,\ldots,x^n,y^n)$ exist and are continuous. Define the Wirtinger derivatives by $\partial_i=\tfrac12(\partial_{x^i}-i\partial_{y^i})$ and $\partial_{\bar i}=\tfrac12(\partial_{x^i}+i\partial_{y^i})$.

A **Kähler coordinate-patch datum** is such a pair $(U,K)$ with a smooth real-valued function $K:U\to\mathbb R$ for which the matrix $g_{i\bar j}(z,\bar z):=\partial_i\partial_{\bar j}K(z,\bar z)$ satisfies $g_{i\bar j}=\overline{g_{j\bar i}}$ and is positive definite: for every $z\in U$ and every nonzero $v=(v^1,\ldots,v^n)\in\mathbb C^n$, $\bar v^{\bar j}g_{i\bar j}(z,\bar z)v^i>0$. This smooth Hermitian matrix is the Kähler metric specified by the potential $K$. In natural units $\hbar=c=1$, mass dimensions are powers of mass; assign $[z^i]=1$, $[K]=2$, and $[g_{i\bar j}]=0$.

declaration.title: Kähler-metric F-term scalar potential in the rigid N=1 model
declaration.design_state: Step 1 carrier authored from the exact planned contract; current inputs and open page-level readiness edges are recorded in batch-30 notes.
declaration.statement:

The simple sum is specific to that metric; for a noncanonical Kähler metric the inverse matrix in the displayed formula is required. This statement concerns the classical F-term sector only and does not include gauge D-terms or quantum corrections.

Use natural units $\hbar=c=1$, so $[x^\mu]=-1$, $[g_{\mathrm{YM}}]=0$, $[A_\mu]=1$, and $[F_{A,\mu\nu}]=2$. Let $g=g_{\mathrm{YM}}$.

The matter covariant derivative is $D_\mu\phi^a=\partial_\mu\phi^a+\rho_{a*}(A_\mu)\phi^a=\partial_\mu\phi^a-ig B_\mu^b t_{b,a}\phi^a$, where $t_{b,a}=i\rho_{a*}(T_b)$ and $T_b=-i\sigma_b/2$. declaration.statement: Let $\mathscr R$ be the commutative ring of even smooth chiral superfields on the specified flat superspace, with the supercommutative complex coefficient algebra of the superspace definition. Let $\Phi_1,\Phi_2,\Phi_3$ be traceless $2\times2$ matrices over $\mathscr R$. Use $[X,Y]=XY-YX$ and the complex-bilinear trace form $\kappa_{\mathbb C}(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$, where $\operatorname{Tr}_2 A=\sum_{j=1}^2 A_{jj}$. Suppose a supplied invertible even chiral matrix $U\in GL_2(\mathscr R)$ acts simultaneously by $\Phi_i'=U\Phi_iU^{-1}$. Then the even chiral cubic polynomial $\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\Phi_1,[\Phi_2,\Phi_3])$ and every constant multiple are invariant. This includes the substitution $U=e^{i\Lambda}$ whenever the given even chiral parameter defines that invertible chiral matrix. The trace form restricts to the real form $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$ on the explicitly defined real Lie algebra of anti-Hermitian traceless complex $2\times2$ matrices. No physical model, gauge measure or extended-supersymmetry premise is used.
declaration.physical_scope: Pure matrix algebra over the even chiral coefficient ring with a specified conjugation action and trace form; no physical premise is used.

declaration.title: Four-dimensional N=2 SU(2) vector and hypermultiplet model
declaration.design_state: Step 1 ready; all current formulation/model suppliers match the stated normalization; eight-supercharge invariance remains an adopted premise.
declaration.statement:
Use the physical action brackets $[U]_D=-I_D(U)/4$ and $[Y]_F=I_F(Y)/2$ from [[def-qftx-physical-superspace-normalization]], with raw mathematical coefficient integrals $I_D,I_F$ unchanged. Physical chiral components obey $\psi_{\mathrm{raw}}=\sqrt2\psi$ and $F_{\mathrm{raw}}=2F$. All physical action and coupling formulas below use these brackets and physical component names; adding Hermitian conjugation applies only to the F action and occurs once.

Adopt a classical rigid four-dimensional model on the oriented, time-oriented Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with coordinates $x^\mu$ of length, orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, time orientation of increasing $x^0$, and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Use $c=\hbar=1$. Fix the global gauge group $G=SU(2)$, not its quotient $SO(3)$. The adjoint action is $\operatorname{Ad}_uX=uXu^{-1}$; choose one smooth right principal bundle $\pi:P\to M$ in the single sector $\Sigma=\{[P]\}$, where $[P]$ means smooth bundle isomorphism over $\operatorname{id}_M$. In the anti-Hermitian basis $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$, use $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$, so $\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$, and a fixed dimensionless coupling $g=g_{\mathrm{YM}}>0$. Use $\sigma^0=I_2$, the Pauli matrices $\sigma^j$, $\bar\sigma^0=I_2$, $\bar\sigma^j=-\sigma^j$, and $\epsilon_{12}=1$; there is no theta term in this selected model.

Use the N=1 superspace algebra with even coordinates $x^\mu$ and odd coordinates $\theta^\alpha,\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}$, the left derivatives and Berezin measures specified in the superspace definitions, and $D_\alpha=\partial^L_{\theta^\alpha}+i\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}\bar\theta^{\dot\beta}\partial_\mu$, $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}=-\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}}-i\theta^\beta\sigma^\mu_{\beta\dot\alpha}\partial_\mu$. A chiral field obeys $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}\Phi=0$. In each representation $R$, the dimensionless real vector prepotential $V_R$ transforms by $e^{2gV_R}\mapsto e^{i\Lambda_R^\dagger}e^{2gV_R}e^{-i\Lambda_R}$ and a chiral matter field transforms by $Q_R\mapsto e^{i\Lambda_R}Q_R$, where $\Lambda_R$ is a chiral gauge-parameter superfield. Its represented matrix curvature is $\mathscr C_{\alpha,R}=-\tfrac14\bar D^{\dot\beta}\bar D_{\dot\beta}(e^{-2gV_R}D_\alpha e^{2gV_R})$. The connection-normalized vector multiplet consists on shell of the connection $A_\mu$, one complex adjoint scalar $\phi$, and two adjoint Weyl fermions; its N=1 decomposition is one vector superfield $V_{\mathrm{ad}}$ and one adjoint chiral superfield $\Phi$. The canonical scalar is $\phi_{\mathrm{can}}=\phi/g$. Here “on shell” means after eliminating algebraic auxiliary fields and imposing the field equations; the full vector superfield also contains the real auxiliary adjoint field $D$.

Choose one finite-dimensional complex Hermitian space $V_R$ and smooth unitary representation $\rho_R:SU(2)\to U(V_R)$. The hypermultiplet consists of chiral superfields $Q$ and $\widetilde Q$ whose scalar components are smooth sections of $P\times_{\rho_R}V_R$ and its dual; the dual action is $\rho_{R^*}(u)\ell=\ell\circ\rho_R(u^{-1})$. Each chiral N=1 hypermultiplet field has one complex scalar, one Weyl fermion, and one auxiliary field; hence the pair has two complex scalars and two Weyl fermions, which form one Dirac fermion on shell. Write $\mathfrak{su}(2)_{\mathbb C}=\mathfrak{su}(2)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$ and let $\kappa_{\mathbb C}$ be the complex-bilinear extension of $\kappa$. This form is nondegenerate and invariant under the complexified adjoint action, so for $R=\mathrm{ad}$ it identifies the dual with the adjoint. Use the Hermitian form $h_R(X,Y)=\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\overline X,Y)$ on the complexified adjoint, where conjugation is with respect to the real Lie algebra. The local invariant pairing is $\widetilde Q Q$, and $\widetilde Q\Phi Q$ means $\widetilde Q\,\rho_{R*}(\Phi)Q$. Under a chiral supergauge transformation $U_R=e^{i\Lambda_R}$, use $Q\mapsto U_RQ$, $\widetilde Q\mapsto\widetilde Q U_R^{-1}$, and $M_R:=\rho_{R*}(\Phi)\mapsto U_RM_RU_R^{-1}$; the associated mass and cubic bilinears are gauge invariant. The hypermultiplet is canonically normalized, while $\Phi$ is in the connection normalization above. “Holomorphic” means complex analytic in the adjoint coordinates $\Phi^a$ on $\mathfrak{su}(2)_{\mathbb C}$. The microscopic vector prepotential is the holomorphic, gauge-invariant quadratic function

$$\mathcal F_{\mathrm{UV}}(\Phi)=\frac{i}{2g^2}\,\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\Phi,\Phi),\qquad \operatorname{Im}(\mathcal F_{ab})=\frac{1}{g^2}\kappa_{ab}>0.$$

Here $\mathcal F_{ab}=\partial_a\partial_b\mathcal F_{\mathrm{UV}}$ in the basis $T_a$. With the normalized physical action brackets, its N=1 vector action is

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{vec}}=\frac{1}{4g^2}\left([\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal W^\alpha,\mathcal W_\alpha)]_F+\mathrm{h.c.}\right)+\frac{1}{g^2}[\kappa_H(\bar\Phi,e^{2gV_{\mathrm{ad}}}\Phi)]_D,$$

where $\mathcal W_\alpha$ is the abstract connection-normalized Lie-algebra-valued chiral curvature, with $\rho_{R*}(\mathcal W_\alpha)=\mathscr C_{\alpha,R}/(2i)$; hence its gauge F-term coefficient also equals $\operatorname{Tr}_2(\mathscr C^\alpha\mathscr C_\alpha)/(8g^2)$ in the defining representation, before adding its Hermitian conjugate, and $\kappa_H(\bar X,Y)=\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\bar X,Y)$. For a superspace expression $X$, $[X]_F=I_F(X)/2$ and $[X]_D=-I_D(X)/4$, using the raw generator order with the normalized physical brackets. Thus the vector kinetic term has exactly the connection-normalized Yang-Mills coefficient $-\kappa(F\wedge *_\eta F)/(2g^2)$.

The adopted renormalizable one-hypermultiplet action is

$$\mathcal L_{N=2}=\mathcal L_{\mathrm{vec}}+[Q^\dagger e^{2gV_R}Q+\widetilde Q^\dagger e^{2gV_{R^*}}\widetilde Q]_D+\left([\sqrt2\,\widetilde Q\Phi Q+m\widetilde Q Q]_F+\mathrm{h.c.}\right),$$

with complex mass parameter $m$ of dimension $\mathrm m^{-1}$. In canonical normalization $\Phi_{\mathrm{can}}=\Phi/g$, the cubic coefficient is $\sqrt2g$, the same gauge coupling that appears in the covariant derivative. The ultraviolet prepotential above is quadratic; a low-energy effective prepotential may instead be non-polynomial and valid only on a specified electric/magnetic patch. This postulate adopts no such low-energy solution or duality claim.

The model includes rigid four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ supersymmetry: “rigid” means its spinor parameters are constant in spacetime, and $\mathcal N=2$ means two independent left-Weyl supercharges, hence eight real components. Its invariance is an adopted model premise, not a deduction in this item. The N=1 superspace expression is a field/action packaging; the full hypermultiplet transformations close only after imposing the physical field equations, and the finite N=1 auxiliary fields are eliminated in this on-shell description. Fields are smooth in local trivializations and admissible variations are smooth and compactly supported; actions are taken over relatively compact regions or when the spacetime integral converges. No path-integral measure, regulator, quantum theory, or continuum existence claim is included. In mass-dimension notation $[x]=-1$, $[\theta]=-\frac12$, $[\Phi]=[Q]=[\widetilde Q]=1$, $[\mathcal W_\alpha]=3/2$, $[m]=1$, and $[g]=0$; equivalently scalar fields and mass parameters have units $\mathrm m^{-1}$.

declaration.design_state: Step 1 ready; current N=1/N=2/Yang–Mills interfaces match the adopted action; sixteen-supercharge invariance remains an adopted premise.
declaration.statement:
Use the physical action brackets $[U]_D=-I_D(U)/4$ and $[Y]_F=I_F(Y)/2$ from [[def-qftx-physical-superspace-normalization]], with raw mathematical coefficient integrals $I_D,I_F$ unchanged. Physical chiral components obey $\psi_{\mathrm{raw}}=\sqrt2\psi$ and $F_{\mathrm{raw}}=2F$. All physical action and coupling formulas below use these brackets and physical component names; adding Hermitian conjugation applies only to the F action and occurs once.

Use the oriented, time-oriented Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb{R}^{1,3}$ with coordinates $x^\mu$ of length, orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, time orientation of increasing $x^0$, and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Let $P\to M$ be one smooth right-principal $SU(2)$ bundle in the selected sector $\{[P]\}$; $[P]$ is its smooth bundle-isomorphism class and the global group is $SU(2)$, not $SO(3)$. The adjoint action is $\operatorname{Ad}_uX=uXu^{-1}$. Use $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$, $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$ with $\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$, $c=\hbar=1$, and dimensionless coupling $g=g_{\mathrm{YM}}>0$. The Pauli matrices are $\sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix}$, and $\sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$. Use $\sigma^0=I_2$, $\sigma^j$ for these spatial matrices, $\bar\sigma^0=I_2$, $\bar\sigma^j=-\sigma^j$, and $\epsilon_{12}=1$, so $\sigma^\mu\bar\sigma^\nu+\sigma^\nu\bar\sigma^\mu=-2\eta^{\mu\nu}I_2$. In the N=1 decomposition, $V_{\mathrm{ad}}$ is the dimensionless real adjoint vector prepotential with $e^{2gV_{\mathrm{ad}}}\mapsto e^{i\Lambda^\dagger}e^{2gV_{\mathrm{ad}}}e^{-i\Lambda}$, where $\Lambda$ is a chiral gauge-parameter superfield, and $\Phi_1,\Phi_2,\Phi_3$ are adjoint chiral superfields in connection normalization. Each $\Phi_i$ obeys $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}\Phi_i=0$ and has one complex adjoint scalar, one adjoint Weyl fermion, and an algebraic auxiliary field. The canonical chiral fields are $\Phi_{i,\mathrm{can}}=\Phi_i/g$.


Write $\mathfrak{su}(2)_{\mathbb C}=\mathfrak{su}(2)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$, let $\kappa_{\mathbb C}$ be the complex-bilinear extension of $\kappa$, set $\kappa_H(\bar X,Y)=\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\bar X,Y)$, and write $[X,Y]$ for the complexified Lie bracket. The complexified form is nondegenerate and adjoint-invariant. For $U=e^{i\Lambda}$, each adjoint chiral field transforms by $\Phi_i\mapsto U\Phi_iU^{-1}$, so the adjoint cubic in the action is gauge invariant under this law. Use $D_\alpha=\partial^L_{\theta^\alpha}+i\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}\bar\theta^{\dot\beta}\partial_\mu$ and $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}=-\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}}-i\theta^\beta\sigma^\mu_{\beta\dot\alpha}\partial_\mu$. Each $\Phi_i$ is an even chiral superfield satisfying $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}\Phi_i=0$, and the represented adjoint matrix curvature is $\mathscr C_{\alpha,\mathrm{ad}}=-\tfrac14\bar D^{\dot\beta}\bar D_{\dot\beta}(e^{-2gV_{\mathrm{ad}}}D_\alpha e^{2gV_{\mathrm{ad}}})$. The abstract connection-normalized chiral curvature in the action is $\mathcal W_\alpha$, defined by $\rho_{R*}(\mathcal W_\alpha)=\mathscr C_{\alpha,R}/(2i)$ for every representation $R$. Thus $\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal W^\alpha,\mathcal W_\alpha)/(4g^2)=\operatorname{Tr}_2(\mathscr C^\alpha\mathscr C_\alpha)/(8g^2)$ in the defining representation, before adding its Hermitian conjugate. The adopted connection-normalized N=1 action is

$$\mathcal L_{N=4}=\frac{1}{g^2}\left\{\frac14\left([\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal W^\alpha,\mathcal W_\alpha)]_F+\mathrm{h.c.}\right)+\sum_{i=1}^3[\kappa_H(\bar\Phi_i,e^{2gV_{\mathrm{ad}}}\Phi_i)]_D+\left([\sqrt2\,\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\Phi_1,[\Phi_2,\Phi_3])]_F+\mathrm{h.c.}\right)\right\}.$$

Here $[Y]_F=I_F(Y)/2$ and $[Z]_D=-I_D(Z)/4$ are the normalized physical brackets; the raw mathematical measures retain their coefficient-extraction meaning. In canonical fields, the cubic superpotential coefficient is $\sqrt2g$, so its Yukawa coupling equals the gauge coupling. On shell, meaning after eliminating algebraic auxiliary fields and imposing the field equations, the physical content is one gauge connection, six real adjoint scalars $X^I$ ($I=1,\ldots,6$), and four adjoint Weyl fermions $\lambda^A$ ($A=1,\ldots,4$). The scalar potential in connection normalization is

$$V_{\mathrm{scalar}}=\frac{1}{2g^2}\sum_{1\le I<J\le6}\kappa([X^I,X^J],[X^I,X^J]);$$

for canonical fields $X^I_{\mathrm{can}}=X^I/g$ this is $\frac{g^2}{2}\sum_{I<J}\kappa([X^I_{\mathrm{can}},X^J_{\mathrm{can}}],[X^I_{\mathrm{can}},X^J_{\mathrm{can}}])$. With the N=2 model's N=1 decomposition, this is the $R=\mathrm{ad}$, $m=0$ hypermultiplet specialization after rescaling its two canonical hypermultiplet chiral fields by $g$ to the connection normalization of $\Phi_2$ and $\Phi_3$.

Adopt rigid four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ supersymmetry, with four independent left-Weyl supercharges and sixteen real components, as part of this physical model postulate. The action's extended invariance and on-shell closure are not proved in this item. This is a classical action with smooth fields in local bundle trivializations and compactly supported admissible variations; no path-integral measure, regulator, quantum continuum theory, or empirical result is asserted. Use $c=\hbar=1$: $g$ is dimensionless, connection-normalized scalar fields have units $\mathrm m^{-1}$, and canonical fields have mass dimension one.

declaration.statement:
Use the physical action brackets $[U]_D=-I_D(U)/4$ and $[Y]_F=I_F(Y)/2$ from [[def-qftx-physical-superspace-normalization]], with raw mathematical coefficient integrals $I_D,I_F$ unchanged. declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ in four-dimensional rigid, global
$\mathcal N=1$ gauge-model data. Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex
Hermitian vector space of scalar field values, let a compact Lie group $G$ act
unitarily on $V$, and fix an orthonormal complex basis
$(\phi^1,\ldots,\phi^n)$ of $V$. Choose Hermitian matrices
$T_a$ for the infinitesimal action of a basis of the Lie algebra of $G$, a
gauge coupling $g>0$, and a gauge-invariant holomorphic polynomial
$W:V\to\mathbb C$. Assume canonical scalar kinetic energy and no
Fayet--Iliopoulos term. Define the auxiliary-field maps

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{kin}}=-\sum_i\partial_\mu\overline{\phi^i}\,\partial^\mu\phi^i,\qquad [\phi^i]=\mathrm{mass},\quad [W]=\mathrm{mass}^3,\quad [g]=1.$$

$$F_i(\phi)=\frac{\partial W}{\partial\phi^i}(\phi),\qquad D_a(\phi)=-g\,\phi^\dagger T_a\phi.$$

The tree-level scalar potential is

$$V_{\mathrm{tree}}(\phi)=\sum_{i=1}^n|F_i(\phi)|^2+\frac12\sum_a D_a(\phi)^2.$$

Thus $F_i$ and $D_a$ have mass dimension two and $V_{\mathrm{tree}}$ has
mass dimension four.

A **classical supersymmetric vacuum configuration** is a constant scalar
configuration $\phi\in V$ for which every $F_i(\phi)$ and every
$D_a(\phi)$ is zero. Its **classical vacuum-moduli set** is the topological
orbit space

$$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}=\{\phi\in V:F_i(\phi)=0\text{ for all }i,\ D_a(\phi)=0\text{ for all }a\}/G.$$

where two configurations are identified exactly when they lie in the same
compact-$G$ orbit, and the set has the quotient topology. The stability
convention here retains every such compact-group orbit, including singular
orbits. No quotient by the complexified group, geometric-invariant-theory
stability criterion, or smooth-manifold structure is included in this
definition.

For a **specified, already constructed quantum theory** $\mathcal T$, suppose
there is a Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, a unitary translation representation
$U(a)$, and densely defined supercharges $Q^I$ and their Hilbert adjoints on a
common domain $\mathcal D$. A **quantum supersymmetric vacuum ray** is the
phase-equivalence class $[\Omega]$ of a normalized vector $\Omega\in\mathcal D$
satisfying
$U(a)\Omega=\Omega$ for every spacetime translation $a$ and
$Q^I\Omega=(Q^I)^*\Omega=0$ for every supercharge $I$. The **quantum
vacuum-moduli set** $\mathcal M_{\mathrm q}(\mathcal T)$ is the set of these
rays, with the topology, if any, supplied by the constructed theory. This
definition is conditional on normalizable invariant vacuum vectors and a
specified quantum Hilbert-space model. It asserts no path-integral measure,
continuum limit, nonperturbative existence, or equality between
$\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}$ and $\mathcal M_{\mathrm q}(\mathcal T)$.

declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$, spacetime $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and a selected pure four-dimensional
rigid $\mathcal N=2$ Yang--Mills model whose global gauge group is $SU(2)$.
The microscopic matter-hypermultiplet index set is empty, as explicitly adopted in the independent pure-model postulate. In $\mathcal N=1$ language the gauge sector is one vector superfield and one adjoint chiral superfield with scalar $\phi\in\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$, connection normalization $\phi_{\mathrm{can}}=\phi/g$, positive dimensionless gauge coupling $g$, zero chiral superpotential and no ultraviolet matter mass. The low-energy charged monopole fields introduced later are emergent infrared fields, not an ultraviolet hypermultiplet. This is the selected physical datum, not a specialization inferred from the different one-hypermultiplet postulate.

A **classical Coulomb-branch configuration** is a constant adjoint scalar
configuration satisfying the model's zero auxiliary-field conditions, taken
modulo the compact $SU(2)$ gauge action. This uses the compact-group orbit
quotient in the preceding vacuum-moduli definition; it does not replace that
quotient by a complexified-group stability construction. In the
weak-coupling semiclassical frame, let $a$ be the eigenvalue coordinate fixed
by $\phi=\tfrac12\operatorname{diag}(a,-a)$, of mass dimension one. When a quantum
theory with a vacuum-moduli set has actually been constructed, the **quantum
Coulomb-branch coordinate** $u$ denotes the chosen gauge-invariant chiral
quadratic-operator expectation value in the source trace normalization for
which the weak-coupling relation is $u=a^2/2$. Its mass dimension is two.
This definition does not assert that $u$ globally parameterizes the quantum
vacua.

On an open patch $U$ of the $u$-plane where the period functions are
holomorphic and the local gauge-coupling matrix has positive imaginary part,
an **electric/magnetic frame** means a chosen ordered basis of the formal
charge lattice that fixes local cycle representatives. Their period
functions are the complex electric coordinate $a:U\to\mathbb C$ and complex
dual coordinate $a_D:U\to\mathbb C$, both of mass dimension one. The local
two-derivative abelian gauge action is encoded by a holomorphic
**prepotential** $\mathcal F_U(a)$ of mass dimension two, defined on that
patch by

$$a_D=\frac{\partial\mathcal F_U}{\partial a},\qquad \tau=\frac{\partial a_D}{\partial a}=\frac{\partial^2\mathcal F_U}{\partial a^2},\qquad \operatorname{Im}\tau>0.$$

The dimensionless $\tau$ is the local complexified gauge coupling; changing
the electric/magnetic frame changes the pair $(a_D,a)$ by the corresponding
integral linear transformation and may require a different local
prepotential. Thus neither period is asserted to be a single-valued global
function on a punctured branch.

For this source-normalized data, define the **formal electric/magnetic charge
label lattice** to be $\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}=\mathbb Z^2$, with a label
$(n_e,n_m)$ and period pairing
$\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW}}(u;n_e,n_m)=n_ea(u)+n_ma_D(u)$. The pair labels
the central-charge formula; the lattice definition does not assert that every
label is an allowed line operator, a dynamical particle, a stable state, or a
state in any constructed Hilbert space. Those are separate model data.

The word **exact** in this page refers only to the adopted source-proposed
Wilsonian two-derivative low-energy data on a regular patch of the selected
pure SU(2) model. It does not mean a proof of a nonperturbative continuum
path integral, a global single-valued prepotential, or an exact statement
about arbitrary $\mathcal N=2$ theories.
