declaration.title: Local dual U(1) monopole-Higgs effective data
declaration.design_state: Owner reviewed source/model boundary repair; remaining vortex prerequisite and native recertification recorded separately.
declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$, metric
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and the local duality frame near one
monopole singularity of the selected pure $SU(2)$, four-dimensional rigid
$\mathcal N=2$ model. Let $A_D$ be the complex scalar coordinate in the
local dual $U(1)_D$ vector multiplet, and let $M,\widetilde M$ be complex
scalar fields of dual electric charges $+1$ and $-1$ in two $\mathcal N=1$
chiral multiplets. These are emergent infrared monopole fields in a dual frame of the independent pure ultraviolet model, not microscopic matter hypermultiplets. The dual gauge group acts by

$$A_D\mapsto A_D,\qquad M\mapsto e^{i\alpha}M,\qquad \widetilde M\mapsto e^{-i\alpha}\widetilde M,\qquad \alpha\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z).$$

Let $u(A_D)$ be the supplied holomorphic coordinate function on an open
patch $|A_D|<r$ about $A_D=0$, with $u(0)=u_m$ and
$c:=u'(0)\ne0$. Let $\mu\ne0$ be the coefficient of the small adjoint
mass perturbation, let $g_D>0$ be the dimensionless dual gauge coupling,
and use connection normalization for $A_D$, canonical kinetic terms for $M,\widetilde M$, and zero microscopic D-type Fayet--Iliopoulos parameter. Freeze the positive local vector-multiplet metric at $b=g_D^{-2}$; this is a specified constant-coupling two-derivative approximation within the patch, not the full field-dependent Wilsonian metric.
Define

$$W_\mu(A_D,M,\widetilde M)=\sqrt2 A_D M\widetilde M+\mu u(A_D),\qquad D=g_D\bigl(|M|^2-|\widetilde M|^2\bigr).$$

$$V_\mu=g_D^2|\partial_{A_D}W_\mu|^2+|\partial_M W_\mu|^2+|\partial_{\widetilde M}W_\mu|^2+\frac12D^2.$$

Let $\widetilde F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu\widetilde A_\nu-
\partial_\nu\widetilde A_\mu$ and
$\widetilde D_\mu A_D=\partial_\mu A_D$,
$\widetilde D_\mu M=(\partial_\mu-i\widetilde A_\mu)M$, and
$\widetilde D_\mu\widetilde M=(\partial_\mu+i\widetilde A_\mu)
\widetilde M$. In metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, the
connection-normalized bosonic kinetic Lagrangian is

$$\mathcal L_{\mathrm{kin}}=-\eta^{\mu\nu}\left(g_D^{-2}\partial_\mu\overline{A_D}\,\partial_\nu A_D+\overline{\widetilde D_\mu M}\,\widetilde D_\nu M+\overline{\widetilde D_\mu\widetilde M}\,\widetilde D_\nu\widetilde M\right)-\frac{1}{4g_D^2}\widetilde F_{\mu\nu}\widetilde F^{\mu\nu}.$$

The mass dimensions are
$[A_D]=[M]=[\widetilde M]=[\mu]=\mathrm{mass}$,
$[u]=\mathrm{mass}^2$, $[W_\mu]=\mathrm{mass}^3$,
$[F_{A_D}]=[F_M]=[F_{\widetilde M}]=[D]=[\widetilde F_{\mu\nu}]=\mathrm{mass}^2$,
$[\widetilde A_\mu]=\mathrm{mass}$,
$[c]=\mathrm{mass}$, and $[g_D]=1$. The allowed regime is restricted to
field values within this patch and energies below its stated effective
cutoff; “small $\mu$” means that the induced scale
$(|\mu c|/\sqrt2)^{1/2}$ lies well below that cutoff.

For a controlled leading linear-superpotential truncation, explicitly replace $u(A_D)$ by $u_m+cA_D$ in this constant-metric model. Then the perturbation is an $F$-type FI deformation of the local $\mathcal N=2$ abelian theory, related to a D-type FI deformation by rotation of its auxiliary triplet. This extra truncation admits the critical BPS square completion. The generic holomorphic $u(A_D)$ model above is softly broken to $\mathcal N=1$ and is not asserted to have exact BPS vortices; the full physical solution and a globally valid metric are separate inputs. Neither a small $\mu$ nor a holomorphic superpotential theorem alone controls all non-holomorphic metric or higher-derivative corrections.

This is a one-singularity effective data package. It includes neither a
simultaneously local electric description of mutually nonlocal dyons nor a
claim that the local action extends over the full moduli space. A finite-energy
vortex is not part of this Definition; its existence, when needed, is a
separate hypothesis.

declaration.title: Finite-energy dual-Higgs flux-tube sector
declaration.design_state: Owner reviewed source/model boundary repair; remaining vortex prerequisite and native recertification recorded separately.
declaration.statement:
Use the dual $U(1)_D$ fields and potential of the preceding local
monopole-Higgs model. Let $x^1,x^2$ be coordinates on the transverse plane
$\mathbb R^2$ and let $x^3$ be the coordinate along a straight static tube.
Write $\widetilde A_i$ for the spatial dual gauge potential,
$\widetilde F_{12}=\partial_1\widetilde A_2-\partial_2\widetilde A_1$,
$D_iM=(\partial_i-i\widetilde A_i)M$, and
$D_i\widetilde M=(\partial_i+i\widetilde A_i)\widetilde M$.

A **finite-energy dual vortex profile of winding $n$** is a smooth static
configuration $(A_D,M,\widetilde M,\widetilde A_1,\widetilde A_2)$ on
$\mathbb R^2$ for which the transverse energy

$$\sigma=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(\frac{\widetilde F_{12}^2}{2g_D^2}+g_D^{-2}|\partial_i A_D|^2+|D_iM|^2+|D_i\widetilde M|^2+V_\mu-V_{\mathrm{vac}}\right)\,d^2x$$

is finite. The fields approach a supersymmetric vacuum at infinity satisfying
$A_D=0$, $|M|=|\widetilde M|=v>0$,
$\sqrt2 M\widetilde M+\mu u'(0)=0$, and
$V_{\mathrm{vac}}=0$. The phase map $M/|M|$ restricted to a sufficiently
large circle has degree $n\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$ as a map to the unit
circle; the phase map $\widetilde M/|\widetilde M|$ has degree $-n$.
Require also that $D_iM$ and $D_i\widetilde M$ tend to zero on that circle,
that the coefficient of $d\theta$ in the pulled-back one-form $\widetilde A-d\arg M$ tends uniformly in
$\theta$ to zero as the circle radius tends to infinity, and that the
limiting flux exists. The profile is a translation-invariant
tube along $x^3$; its tension is the transverse integral $\sigma$. This
Definition includes no assertion that such a configuration exists or is a
stationary solution of the field equations.

In the adopted electric/magnetic frame, the **original electric flux** of
this sector means the dual magnetic flux
$\Phi_D=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{|x|\le R}\widetilde F_{12}\,d^2x$.
The flux dictionary is part of the selected duality model; this Definition
does not state that every electric line charge is represented by a vortex.
In natural units, $[\widetilde A_i]=\mathrm{mass}$,
$[\widetilde F_{12}]=\mathrm{mass}^2$, and
$[\sigma]=\mathrm{mass}^2$.

declaration.statement:
Adopt the source-proposed low-energy solution data for pure four-dimensional
rigid $\mathcal N=2$ Yang--Mills with global gauge group $SU(2)$, one
adjoint vector multiplet, rank one, no matter hypermultiplets, and the coupling, units, connection-normalized scalar, and prepotential convention of the independent pure ultraviolet vector-multiplet datum. Use natural units
$c=\hbar=1$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and a positive
dynamical scale $\Lambda$ of mass dimension one. The gauge-invariant
coordinate $u$ has mass dimension two; set $w=u/\Lambda^2$.

The absence of microscopic hypermultiplets is an explicit model input in that independent ultraviolet postulate. The charged monopole hypermultiplet in a local infrared frame below is emergent; it does not change the ultraviolet matter content.

On the regular $w$-plane with singular values $w=1,-1,\infty$ removed,
adopt the family of genus-one curves, where $x,y,w$ are dimensionless:

$$\Sigma_w:\quad y^2=(x-1)(x+1)(x-w).$$

and the meromorphic period differential

$$\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}=\frac{\sqrt2\Lambda}{2\pi}\frac{y\,dx}{x^2-1}.$$

Within this proposed solution, take the quantum vacuum-moduli data to be the
entire $u$-plane, with a $\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry $u\mapsto-u$ and singular
values $u=\Lambda^2,-\Lambda^2,\infty$. This is part of the adopted
solution ansatz, not a consequence of a constructed continuum theory.

For a chosen local cycle basis $\gamma_m,\gamma_e$ on $\Sigma_w$ with
intersection number $\gamma_m\cdot\gamma_e=1$, define
$a_D=\oint_{\gamma_m}\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}$ and
$a=\oint_{\gamma_e}\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}$. These periods have mass
dimension one, are multivalued under continuation around the punctures, and
are used in the local prepotential convention
$a_D=\partial\mathcal F/\partial a$ and
$\tau=\partial^2\mathcal F/\partial a^2$ with
$\operatorname{Im}\tau>0$. In the source's counterclockwise-loop
convention, the period column $(a_D,a)^T$ has monodromy matrices

$$M_\infty=\begin{pmatrix}-1&2\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad M_+=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-2&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad M_-=\begin{pmatrix}-1&2\\-2&3\end{pmatrix}.$$

$\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW}}=n_ea+n_ma_D$ for labels
$(n_e,n_m)\in\mathbb Z^2$. In the supersymmetry convention of this page,
the scalar central charge is normalized as
$z=\sqrt2\,\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW}}$. The mass inequality and its
saturation statement are separate theorem deductions. No claim is made that
every lattice label is an allowed line operator or is represented by a stable
particle.

Adopt the singularity interpretation that the $w=1$ point has a light
monopole with $a_D=0$, while the $w=-1$ point has a light dyon with
$a-a_D=0$ in the chosen frame. These are source-proposed physical inputs
tested by their monodromies; they are not deduced here from a constructed
continuum theory.
In the local monopole patch, adopt the dual $U(1)_D$ field content and superpotential described in the preceding effective-model definition. The source two-derivative vector metric is positive and generally field dependent, determined by the local dual coupling; a regulated matching scale is part of any effective action with the light monopole retained. mass dimension one adds the local superpotential term $\mu u(A_D)$ to

singularity, below its effective cutoff, and does not simultaneously describe

not mean a proof of a nonperturbative UV path integral, a global

declaration.statement:
Use the local monopole fields, charges and superpotential with $a=A_D$, $c=u'(0)\ne0$, $\mu\ne0$, $v^2=|\mu c|/\sqrt2$ and $\xi=2v^2$. Keep the holomorphic function $u$ nonlinear. Choose a closed disk $K_\delta=\{|a|\le\delta\}$ contained in its open valid patch with $u'(a)\ne0$ throughout. Define

$$m_*=\min_{a\in K_\delta}|\mu u'(a)|>0,\qquad K=\sup_{a\in K_\delta}|\mu u''(a)|<\infty.$$

Continuity, compactness and the nonzero $c$ allow such a disk. No linear Taylor replacement of $u$ is made. In the already adopted constant-metric model put $b(a)=b_0=g_D^{-2}$. More generally, the same classical energy problem may be specified with a supplied smooth real function $b$ on a neighborhood of $K_\delta$ and constants $0<b_-\le b(a)\le b_+<\infty$. This is additional explicit local Wilsonian metric data, not the vector-only logarithmically singular period metric inferred at a massless-monopole point. Let $b_0=b(0)$ and $g_0^2=b_0^{-1}$. Define

$$H=\sqrt2M\widetilde M+\mu u'(a),\qquad d=|M|^2-|\widetilde M|^2,\qquad s=|M|^2+|\widetilde M|^2,$$

$$V_b=b(a)^{-1}|H|^2+\frac{d^2}{2b(a)}+2|a|^2s.$$

Charged kinetic terms are canonical. The gauge kinetic coefficient is $b(a)$ and the neutral kinetic coefficient is $b(a)$. Work in the classical magnetostatic model with omitted or **constant** theta angle, no dynamical dual magnetic sources in the interior, static fields and $A_0=0$. No field-dependent-theta Gauss-law conclusion is included.

Fix $n\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$ and $e^{i\beta}=-\mu c/(\sqrt2v^2)$. A planar admissible profile is a smooth real one-form $A=A_1dx^1+A_2dx^2$ and smooth complex fields $a,M,\widetilde M$ on $\mathbb R^2$, with $a(x)\in K_\delta$, finite energy

$$E_b=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left\{\frac{b(a)}2B^2+b(a)|\partial_i a|^2+|D_iM|^2+|\widetilde D_i\widetilde M|^2+V_b\right\}d^2x,$$

where $i=1,2$, $B=\partial_1A_2-\partial_2A_1$, $D_i=\partial_i-iA_i$ and $\widetilde D_i=\partial_i+iA_i$. Require **uniform** approach to the vacuum orbit at transverse infinity:

$$a\to0,\qquad |M|,|\widetilde M|\to v,\qquad M\widetilde M\to e^{i\beta}v^2.$$

This is an independent boundary hypothesis, not inferred from finite energy. Outside a compact set $M$ is nonzero and its phase has winding $n$ on each sufficiently large circle; the phase of $\widetilde M$ has winding $-n$. In the angular coordinate $\theta$, require the coefficient of $d\theta$ in $A-d\arg M$ to tend uniformly to zero, and the limiting flux to exist. Require also $D_iM,\widetilde D_i\widetilde M\to0$ uniformly, as in the admitted flux-sector data. These conditions define the gauge-invariant class $\mathcal P_n$. Gauge transformations are arbitrary smooth maps $U:\mathbb R^2\to U(1)$ acting by $M\mapsto UM$, $\widetilde M\mapsto U^{-1}\widetilde M$ and $A\mapsto A-iU^{-1}dU$; there is no added asymptotic-constant gauge restriction. A **canonical exterior representative** has $M=m e^{in\theta}$ with $m>0$ real outside a compact set.

Write

$$\tau_n=\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}E_b(P).$$

This notation alone asserts neither nonemptiness nor attainment. The adopted electric/magnetic dictionary identifies the dual magnetic flux with the original electric flux only for the specified test-charge/flux boundary sector.

For fixed canonical exterior representatives $P_0,P_1\in\mathcal P_n$ and $L>0$, let $\mathcal C_n(L;P_0,P_1)$ be the smooth static fields on $\mathbb R^2\times[0,L]$ with these tangential end traces, $a\in K_\delta$, and a planar admissible winding-$n$ profile on almost every slice. $$E_{b,3}=\int_0^L\!\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left\{\frac{b(a)}2\sum_{i<j}F_{ij}^2+b(a)\sum_{i=1}^3|\partial_i a|^2+\sum_{i=1}^3\bigl(|D_iM|^2+|\widetilde D_i\widetilde M|^2\bigr)+V_b\right\}d^2x\,dx^3,$$

and $I_n(L;P_0,P_1)=\inf_{\mathcal C_n(L;P_0,P_1)}E_{b,3}$. Competitors have finite displayed energy and the stated flux/boundary data; no stationary solution or minimizer is assumed. Any further hard field cutoff is part of a different admissible class and must be checked to admit the profiles and interpolation paths used here. In particular the neutral scalar lies in the specified small closed disk, the positive smooth **light-hyper-retaining** metric has the explicit bounds $b_-,b_+$, the vacuum approach is uniform, and theta is omitted or constant. Let

$$t_*=\min\{\xi/2,m_*/\sqrt2\}>0,\qquad C_V=\max\left\{\frac{4b_+\xi^2}{m_*^2},\;6b_++\frac{2K^2}{t_*}\right\},\qquad c_V=C_V^{-1},\qquad \gamma=\min\left\{1,\frac{b_-}{b_0},2b_0c_V\right\}>0.$$

Then the full nonlinear potential and every planar profile obey

$$V_b\ge c_V(s-\xi)^2,\qquad E_b\ge\gamma\,2\pi\xi|n|.$$

The class $\mathcal P_n$ is nonempty for **every** nonzero integer winding: a smooth compact-core radial test suffices, with no field equation, exact BPS profile or Taubes existence theorem assumed. Consequently

$$0<\gamma\,2\pi\xi|n|\le\tau_n<\infty.$$

Every admissible profile has a globally smooth gauge transform to a canonical exterior representative. Any two such canonical representatives admit a smooth fixed-width finite-energy interpolation collar in the same winding class; the collar keeps the neutral scalar in its convex disk. In particular, for fixed end traces $P_0,P_1$ and any $\varepsilon>0$, there are finite constants $C_\varepsilon$, $\ell>0$, independent of $L$, such that for $L\ge2\ell$

$$\tau_nL\le I_n(L;P_0,P_1)\le(\tau_n+\varepsilon)(L-2\ell)+C_\varepsilon.$$

Therefore

$$\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{I_n(L;P_0,P_1)}{L}=\tau_n>0.$$

It does not assert that the planar infimum or finite-cylinder infimum is attained, that a nonlinear stationary profile is BPS, or that $I_n(L)=\tau_nL+O(1)$. declaration.statement:
Let integers $N_c\ge2$ and $N_f$ satisfy
$\frac32N_c<N_f<3N_c$, and put $\widetilde N_c=N_f-N_c$. Consider the
following proposed four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ SQCD field data, in
natural units. In the electric $SU(N_c)$ theory, there are $N_f$ quark
chiral multiplets $Q$ in the fundamental of the flavor group
$SU(N_f)_L$, with $N_c$ color copies; the antiquark multiplets are singlets
under $SU(N_f)_L$. In the proposed magnetic $SU(\widetilde N_c)$ theory,
the quark multiplets $q$ are in the antifundamental of $SU(N_f)_L$, with
$\widetilde N_c$ color copies, and the meson multiplet $M$ transforms in
$(\mathbf N_f,\overline{\mathbf N_f})$ under
$SU(N_f)_L\times SU(N_f)_R$, giving $N_f$ copies of the fundamental of
$SU(N_f)_L$. The magnetic antiquarks and both gauginos are
$SU(N_f)_L$ singlets. Normalize the cubic-anomaly coefficient of a
left-handed Weyl fermion to $+1$ in $\mathbf N_f$ and $-1$ in
$\overline{\mathbf N_f}$, and add coefficients over independent copies.
Then the electric and proposed magnetic $SU(N_f)_L^3$ coefficients are

$$\mathcal A_{\mathrm{electric}}=N_c,\qquad \mathcal A_{\mathrm{magnetic}}=-(N_f-N_c)+N_f=N_c.$$

This equality is one anomaly-matching consistency check of the proposed
field data; it is not a proof of Seiberg duality or of equality of the
infrared continuum theories.

declaration.statement:
In the local dual $U(1)_D$ model, let $u(A_D)$ be holomorphic near
$A_D=0$, let $c=u'(0)\ne0$, and choose a neighborhood small enough that
$u'(A_D)\ne0$ throughout. Choose a nonzero small perturbation
$\mu$ for which $(|\mu c|/\sqrt2)^{1/2}$ is below the effective cutoff.
The supersymmetric vacuum equations have the gauge orbit represented by

$$A_D=0,\qquad M=v>0,\qquad \widetilde M=-\frac{\mu c}{\sqrt2v},\qquad v=\left(\frac{|\mu c|}{\sqrt2}\right)^{1/2}.$$

At this representative $|M|=|\widetilde M|=v$, so the D equation vanishes.
The dual $U(1)_D$ is fully Higgsed and the canonical dual vector mass is
$m_D^2=4g_D^2v^2>0$. This is a symbolic local effective-model calculation.
The example does not assert existence of a finite-energy vortex or linear
confinement; the zero-perturbation case $\mu=0$ is outside its scope.

declaration.design_state: Vacuum-state definition authored; two independent full-text treatments stamped; focused dependency and rendering checks pass.
declaration.statement:
Let a positive unitary representation of the four-dimensional extended super-Poincare algebra act on a complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, with common invariant product domain $\mathcal D$, translation generators $P^\mu$, supercharges $Q^I_\alpha$, and actual Hilbert adjoints $(Q^I_\alpha)^*$, using metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $\sigma^0=I_2$, and natural units $\hbar=c=1$. A **rest-frame ground-state vector** is a vector $\Omega\in\mathcal D$ such that $\|\Omega\|=1$, there is a real number $E_\Omega$ with $P^0\Omega=E_\Omega\Omega$ and $P^j\Omega=0$ for $j=1,2,3$, and

$$\langle P^0\psi,\psi\rangle\ge E_\Omega\|\psi\|^2\qquad(\psi\in D(P^0)).$$

Such a vector is called a **global supersymmetry vacuum state** in the representation. Its vacuum energy is the eigenvalue $E_\Omega$, with units of mass in natural units; it is not an energy density. The vector is **boundary-neutral** when $Z^{IJ}\Omega=0$ and $\bar Z_{IJ}\Omega=0$ for every central generator, **supersymmetry-invariant** when $Q^I_\alpha\Omega=(Q^I_\alpha)^*\Omega=0$ for every $I,\alpha$, and **supersymmetry-noninvariant** when at least one of these vectors is nonzero. These are separate predicates: boundary neutrality does not define supersymmetry invariance. The definition does not assert that any such vector exists or that a constant field configuration is allowed by a separate field-model boundary condition.

declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and a positive unitary representation of the four-dimensional extended super-Poincare algebra with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $\sigma^0=I_2$, natural units $\hbar=c=1$, common invariant product domain $\mathcal D$, and actual Hilbert adjoints $(Q^I_\alpha)^*$. Let $N\ge1$, and let $\Omega\in\mathcal D$ satisfy $\|\Omega\|=1$, $P^0\Omega=E_\Omega\Omega$ for a real number $E_\Omega$, $P^j\Omega=0$ for $j=1,2,3$, and $\langle P^0\psi,\psi\rangle\ge E_\Omega\|\psi\|^2$ for every $\psi\in D(P^0)$. Say that $\Omega$ is supersymmetry-invariant when $Q^I_\alpha\Omega=(Q^I_\alpha)^*\Omega=0$ for every $I,\alpha$, and supersymmetry-noninvariant when at least one of these vectors is nonzero; say it is boundary-neutral when $Z^{IJ}\Omega=\bar Z_{IJ}\Omega=0$ for every central generator. Then

$$4N E_\Omega=\sum_{I=1}^N\sum_{\alpha=1}^2\left(\|Q^I_\alpha\Omega\|^2+\|(Q^I_\alpha)^*\Omega\|^2\right)\ge0.$$

Consequently, $E_\Omega=0$ if and only if $\Omega$ is supersymmetry-invariant, and every supersymmetry-noninvariant such state has $E_\Omega>0$. The identity holds whether or not the state is boundary-neutral. The energy is an eigenvalue, not an energy density. The theorem is conditional on the representation and state data; it proves neither existence of a vacuum state nor existence of a quantum field theory realizing that representation.

declaration.statement:
In the classical rigid N=1 Wess–Zumino model with three chiral scalar coordinates $(\phi_1,\phi_2,\phi_3)\in\mathbb C^3$, canonical Kähler metric, no gauge D-term, and natural units $\hbar=c=1$, adopt the holomorphic superpotential

$$W(\Phi_1,\Phi_2,\Phi_3)=-k\Phi_1+m\Phi_2\Phi_3+\frac y2\Phi_1\Phi_3^2,$$

where $k,m\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$, $y\in\mathbb C$ is arbitrary, and $[\phi_i]=[m]=M$, $[k]=M^2$, and $[y]=1$. The classical zero-derivative F-term potential on pointwise field values is

$$V(\phi_1,\phi_2,\phi_3)=\left|-k+\frac y2\phi_3^2\right|^2+|m\phi_3|^2+|m\phi_2+y\phi_1\phi_3|^2.$$

Here “tree-level” means this classical potential before quantum-loop corrections. At a field value, F-term supersymmetry is unbroken exactly when all eliminated auxiliary fields $F^i=-\overline{\partial_iW}$ vanish; otherwise it is F-term broken.

Put $a=|k|>0$, $b=|m|^2>0$, and $c=|y|$. If $b\ge ac$, including $y=0$, the global minimum is $V_{\min}=a^2=|k|^2$, and all minimizing field values are $\phi_3=\phi_2=0$ with arbitrary $\phi_1\in\mathbb C$. If $0<b<ac$, then $c>0$ and

$$V_{\min}=a^2-\frac{(ac-b)^2}{c^2}=\frac bc\left(2a-\frac bc\right)>0,$$

with all minimizing field values given by arbitrary $\phi_1\in\mathbb C$, one of the two distinct square roots $\phi_3$ of

$$\phi_3^2=\frac{2k}{y}\left(1-\frac{b}{ac}\right),$$

and $\phi_2=-y\phi_1\phi_3/m$. In both regimes every minimizing field value has at least one nonzero auxiliary F term, so the pointwise classical minimum breaks F-term supersymmetry. Thus the stronger bound $V\ge |k|^2$ holds for all field values exactly when $|m|^2\ge |k||y|$; in the other regime the exact minimum is smaller but remains positive. The set of minima has a flat complex $\phi_1$ direction and is not an isolated point. The adopted field-model postulate restricts spacetime fields to compact support, so this pointwise minimization alone does not establish that nonzero constant minimizing values are allowed homogeneous vacuum configurations. No quantum vacuum, stability against radiative corrections, goldstino conclusion, or continuum-QFT existence is asserted.

declaration.title: Four-Dimensional SCFT and Protected Observable Data
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored definition; exact sources, hypotheses, and local status are recorded in batch notes.
declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. The selected classical model is the rigid four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ Yang--Mills model with spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and global gauge group $G=SU(2)$ rather than $SO(3)$. Its field data are one $SU(2)$ connection, six real adjoint scalars, and four adjoint Weyl fermions, with the coupling and action normalization fixed by the selected model data. The gauge coupling $g>0$ is dimensionless in four dimensions. The model's sixteen-supercharge invariance is adopted as part of that classical model; this definition does not add a proof of invariance, a quantum measure, or a continuum construction.

A four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ superconformal field theory (SCFT) is, by definition here, a unitary positive-energy quantum field theory whose local-operator state space carries the four-dimensional conformal algebra $\mathfrak{so}(4,2)$ together with its $\mathcal N=4$ superconformal extension. The real Lie superalgebra for the selected maximally supersymmetric case is $\mathfrak{psu}(2,2|4)$: it is the real form of the supertrace-zero $4|4$ matrix Lie superalgebra preserving a Hermitian form with signature $(2,2)$ on the even block and positive signature on the odd block, modulo its central real line $\mathbb R\,iI_{4|4}$; for a block-diagonal matrix $A\oplus D$, the supertrace is $\operatorname{tr}A-\operatorname{tr}D$. Its even part is $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)\oplus\mathfrak{su}(4)_R$, with $\mathfrak{su}(2,2)\cong\mathfrak{so}(4,2)$; its odd generators are the Poincar\'e supercharges $Q,\bar Q$ and the special superconformal charges $S,\bar S$. The conformal generators include translations $P_\mu$, Lorentz transformations $M_{\mu\nu}$, dilations $D$, and special conformal transformations $K_\mu$. A superconformal primary is a state annihilated by all $K_\mu$ and all special superconformal charges; its descendants are obtained by applying $P_\mu$ and Poincar\'e supercharges. A unitary representation means that these generators act on a common invariant dense domain, the indicated adjoints are Hilbert adjoints, translations and radial Hamiltonian are self-adjoint, and the inner product is positive.

For the scalar-primary sector, use the selected $\mathcal N=1$ subalgebra and normalize its $U(1)_R$ generator $R$ so that the three adjoint chiral superfields have scalar charge $2/3$. Write $d_{\mathcal O}$ for the eigenvalue of the dilation generator on a scalar superconformal primary $|\mathcal O\rangle$ and $r_{\mathcal O}$ for its $R$ charge. The scalar unitarity bound in this convention is $d_{\mathcal O}\geq 3|r_{\mathcal O}|/2$; equality in the positive-charge branch is the chiral-primary shortening condition. The local conditional norm argument is given by the chiral-primary unitarity item on this page; no classification of all $\mathfrak{psu}(2,2|4)$ representations is asserted here.

For the superconformal index, use Euclidean radial quantization on a unit three-sphere, defined by writing the punctured Euclidean space as $(t,\Omega)=(\log |x|,x/|x|)\in\mathbb R\times S^3$. Let $\mathcal H(S^3)$ be the resulting graded Hilbert space, $E$ its dimensionless radial Hamiltonian, $J_1$ one chosen Lorentz $SU(2)$ Cartan generator, $F$ fermion parity, and $Q$ the selected supercharge with radial Hilbert adjoint $S=Q^\dagger$. In this normalization the superconformal algebra gives the nonnegative operator

$$\delta=2\{S,Q\}=E-2J_1-\frac32R.$$

Use the convention in which $Q$ is the component whose scalar chiral-primary branch has $d_{\mathcal O}-3r_{\mathcal O}/2$ as its anticommutator eigenvalue. For its conjugate component $\bar Q$ with radial adjoint $\bar S=\bar Q^\dagger$, write $J_2$ for the other Lorentz $SU(2)$ Cartan; its conjugate anticommutator is $2\{\bar S,\bar Q\}=E-2J_2+3R/2$. On a scalar superconformal primary both Cartan eigenvalues are zero, so these are the two scalar-primary positivity bounds used on this page.

For the index sector require the closed odd operator $D_Q=\sqrt2(Q+S)$ to be self-adjoint with $D_Q^2=\delta$ as a closed composition equality. Require also $\delta=2(SQ+QS)$ as an equality on the full intersection of the two composition domains, not merely as an extension of an identity on test vectors. Supply a simultaneous orthonormal energy/charge/parity eigenbasis for $\delta,J_1',\ldots,J_k'$ and $(-1)^F$, with real eigenlabels $(\lambda,\mathbf j)$ and maximal diagonal self-adjoint domains. Here $\lambda\ge0$, the joint labels form a supplied countable set, and entire gap eigenspaces, including the protected kernel, may be infinite-dimensional. For every joint projection $P$, require $P D(T)\subset D(T)$ and $TP\psi=PT\psi$ for $T=Q,S,D_Q$ on $D(T)$. These reducing-domain conditions specify the actual spectral compatibility; common-domain commutators alone are insufficient. The grading preserves the joint subspaces and anticommutes with the odd operators on their domains.

For $\beta>0$ and finite real or complex chemical potentials $\boldsymbol\mu$, define the weighted exponential first on the finite joint-eigenvector span by the eigenvalues $\exp(-\beta\lambda+\sum_a\mu_a j_a)$. Require its closure to be bounded trace class for every $\beta>0$ at the chosen $\boldsymbol\mu$. This is the meaning of the exponential in the index observable, not an unspecified product of unbounded operators. Every joint block then has finite dimension: its weight is nonzero and infinitely many equal singular values would violate trace class. Infinite total gap multiplicities are permitted through infinitely many joint blocks. Define

$$\mathcal I(\beta,\boldsymbol\mu)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H(S^3)}\left((-1)^F\exp\left[-\beta\delta+\sum_{a=1}^k\mu_aJ_a'\right]\right).$$

If the trace is not trace class, the same symbol may be used only for a specified formal series whose coefficients are defined; it does not denote a convergent partition function. The index is called protected against $\beta$-variation when the stated operator and trace hypotheses imply that positive-$\delta$ states cancel in the graded trace, as proved by the index-pair theorem on this page. A source's further claim of invariance under changing a coupling requires its own stated deformation hypotheses. A protected local operator means a named primary whose dimension is fixed by a specified shortening relation; the word alone asserts no deformation invariance.

For the quantum coupling family, use the source normalization

$$\tau=\frac{\theta}{2\pi}+\frac{4\pi i}{g^2},\qquad \operatorname{Im}\tau>0,$$

This is the physical component coupling family, not the formal Wilsonian coordinate $\tau_{\mathrm h}$ of the earlier zero-theta density bridge; no equality of the two parameter symbols is inferred. Here, on a closed oriented Euclidean four-manifold $X$ with an $SU(2)$ bundle, $k=-\frac1{8\pi^2}\int_X\operatorname{Tr}_2(F_A\wedge F_A)\in\mathbb Z$ is the instanton number in the selected trace convention and $\theta$ weights its sectors by $e^{i\theta k}$. For the opposite, positive-ASD counting convention $k_{\mathrm A}=+\int_X\operatorname{Tr}_2(F_A\wedge F_A)/(8\pi^2)$ on the same oriented manifold, one has $k_{\mathrm A}=-k$ by definition. The fixed physical gauge coefficient gives weight $q^k$ for a positive self-dual sector and $\bar q^{k_{\mathrm A}}$ for a positive anti-self-dual sector on the real coupling slice, where $q=e^{2\pi i\tau}$. A local ADHM/Nekrasov pole orientation and weight identification is separate data; it is not obtained by equating these signed charge symbols. The corresponding source-reported $S$ and $T$ parameter maps are $S:\tau\mapsto-1/\tau$ and $T:\tau\mapsto\tau+1$. The global form and line-operator spectrum are part of the theory data, not determined by the Lie algebra alone. In the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ center-charge sector define $\mathcal C=\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ with charge $(e,m)$ and mutual-locality pairing

$$\langle(e,m),(e',m')\rangle=em'-me'\pmod 2.$$

An electric Wilson line is parallel transport traced in a representation of the global gauge group; a magnetic 't Hooft line is specified by a magnetic singularity around the support curve; a dyonic line carries both charges. Their center-charge classes are $(e,m)\in\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$. An allowed center-charge set is a subgroup $L\subseteq\mathcal C$ on which the displayed pairing vanishes; the three maximal such subgroups are the line-spectrum data for $SU(2)$, $SO(3)_+$, and $SO(3)_-$. The source-reported charge maps are $S:(e,m)\mapsto(m,-e)$ and $T:(e,m)\mapsto(e+m,m)$, so these transformations may change the global form. The 2007 and 2013 sources read for this item describe the quantum $S$-duality as a conjecture and refine it by global form and line data. This dated source status is recorded as such; this item does not assert an exhaustive literature-status review, an open-problem classification, or a proof of equivalence between the theories.

declaration.title: Positive-Supercharge Pair Cancellation in the Superconformal Index
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored physics-theorem; exact sources, hypotheses, and local status are recorded in batch notes.
declaration.statement:
Let $\mathcal H=\mathcal H^{\bar 0}\oplus\mathcal H^{\bar 1}$ be a $\mathbb Z_2$-graded Hilbert space in a unitary representation of the selected four-dimensional superconformal algebra. Let $Q$ be the selected odd supercharge and $S=Q^\dagger$ its Hilbert adjoint. Assume a common invariant dense domain $D$ on which $Q^2=S^2=0$ and

$$\delta=2(SQ+QS)$$

is positive and extends to a self-adjoint operator. Assume that $D_Q=\sqrt2(Q+S)$ is self-adjoint with $D_Q^2=\delta$ as a closed equality. Require also $\delta=2(SQ+QS)$ as an equality on the full intersection of the two composition domains, not merely as an extension of an identity on test vectors. Supply an orthogonal countable direct sum of finite-dimensional reducing parity blocks $\mathcal H_b$, each contained in the common product domain, on which $\delta=\lambda_b I$ with $\lambda_b\ge0$. Repeated values of $\lambda_b$ are allowed, so total gap eigenspaces and the protected kernel may be infinite. Let $U$ be an even block-diagonal operator, on the maximal direct-sum domain containing the finite block span, whose finite restrictions commute with $Q,S$. Require the block operator $e^{-\beta\delta}U$ to extend to a trace-class operator for every $\beta>0$. This includes the original bounded-insertion finite-gap-eigenspace case. It also includes the full chemical-potential character in the earlier definition: its joint blocks reduce the charges, and their finite dimension follows from the nonzero exponential weights and trace class. Define

$$\mathcal I(\beta)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H}\!\left((-1)^F e^{-\beta\delta}U\right),$$

where $(-1)^F$ acts as $+1$ on $\mathcal H^{\bar 0}$ and $-1$ on $\mathcal H^{\bar 1}$. Then

$$\mathcal I(\beta)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\ker\delta}\!\left((-1)^F U\right)$$

for every $\beta>0$. In particular, this trace is independent of $\beta$, and $\ker\delta=\ker Q\cap\ker S$. The conclusion applies to the superconformal index only when its Hilbert-space, operator-domain, spectral, commuting-charge, and trace hypotheses above hold; it makes no conclusion for continuous spectrum or a non-trace-class formal path integral.

declaration.title: Topological defect insertion in a specified model
declaration.design_state: Assigned A-page definition authored from the exact future item contract.
declaration.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$ and a smooth $d$-manifold $M$, possibly with boundary. Fix the metric and signature, orientation and any time orientation, the geometric background bundles or lifts required by the model, and the boundary conditions. A **selected model** $\mathcal T$ on $M$ consists of a specified configuration space $\mathcal C_{\mathcal T}(M)$ of fields, including each field bundle, regularity class, and admissible boundary behavior; a specified collection of local observables and their supports; a set $\mathcal A_{\mathcal T}$ of admissible finite observable lists with boundary data; a declared value space $\mathcal V_{\mathcal T}$ (for example, $\mathbb C$ or a specified distribution space); and a normalized correlation functional $C_{\mathcal T}:\mathcal A_{\mathcal T}\to\mathcal V_{\mathcal T}$. The model also fixes its unit system, action and charge normalizations, and any regulator, measure, or renormalization prescription used to define $C_{\mathcal T}$. These are model inputs: this definition does not construct them or assume a general interacting continuum theory exists.

A **defect insertion** in $\mathcal T$ is data $(j,\lambda)$ where $j:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M^\circ$ is a smooth embedding of a manifold $\Sigma$ without boundary whose image is closed in the interior $M^\circ=M\setminus\partial M$, and $\lambda$ is the model-specified local field, operator, or boundary-condition data supported on $j(\Sigma)$. Its codimension is $d-\dim\Sigma$. The model must define the modified correlator $C_{\mathcal T}(D_{j,\lambda};O_1,\ldots,O_n)$ for every allowed list of other insertions $O_j$. An orientation, coorientation, or framing is included in $\lambda$ whenever the model needs it. A defect network is a finite list of such strata with a specified incidence relation; each allowed meeting stratum has a stated order of incident labels and a local junction operator inserted by the model. A list of strata or a picture without this field and junction data is not a defect insertion.

An **isotopy** of this insertion is a smooth family of embeddings $j_t:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M^\circ$, $t\in[0,1]$, that transports all included orientation, coorientation, framing, and junction data, leaves the boundary conditions fixed, and keeps every support disjoint from every other insertion throughout the deformation. The insertion is **topological in $\mathcal T$** if, for every admissible list of other insertions and boundary data and every such isotopy, the model-defined correlators satisfy

$$C_{\mathcal T}(D_{j_0,\lambda_0};O_1,\ldots,O_n)=C_{\mathcal T}(D_{j_1,\lambda_1};O_1,\ldots,O_n).$$

This is a property to verify for the specified model and insertion, not an automatic consequence of assigning a defect label or drawing a crossing. No physical quantity with units is introduced here; all dimensional quantities and normalizations remain those declared by $\mathcal T$.
declaration.physical_scope: A definition for a named field-theory or quantum model whose admissible configurations and correlation functionals are specified; it asserts neither existence of a general continuum QFT nor realization of any proposed defect.

declaration.title: Topological interface between specified models
declaration.design_state: Assigned A-page definition authored from the exact future item contract.
declaration.statement:
Use the selected-model and defect-insertion data from the preceding defect definition: a model specifies its manifold, background and boundary data, fields with regularity conditions, unit conventions, and correlator functional; an insertion is a model-defined local modification supported on an embedded submanifold. Let $\mathcal T_-$ and $\mathcal T_+$ be two such models in the same spacetime dimension $d$ on the same smooth manifold $M$. Their metric or signature, background bundles, boundary conditions, field normalizations, and units must either agree or be related by an explicitly supplied identification. No such identification is inferred from names or equal dimensions.

A **codimension-one interface** from $\mathcal T_-$ to $\mathcal T_+$ is data $(\mathcal W,\mathcal I)$ where $\mathcal W\hookrightarrow M^\circ$ is a closed smooth embedded hypersurface with a chosen coorientation and a specified collar $\mathcal W\times(-\epsilon,\epsilon)$, $\epsilon>0$. The negative side uses $\mathcal T_-$ and the positive side uses $\mathcal T_+$. The interface data $\mathcal I$ is a specified local transmission condition, operator map, or boundary condition relating the one-sided field data in that collar, together with any orientation, framing, or junction labels required by the models. The combined model must assign a correlator $C_{\mathcal T_-,\mathcal T_+}(\mathcal I(\mathcal W);O_1,\ldots,O_n)$ to every stated admissible list of insertions. The interface is **topological** when this correlator obeys the isotopy-invariance criterion of the preceding defect definition, with the two side labels and all interface data transported and no other insertion crossed.

For interfaces $\mathcal I_{01}:\mathcal T_0\to\mathcal T_1$ and $\mathcal I_{12}:\mathcal T_1\to\mathcal T_2$, define their **fusion** only when the model supplies a product collar containing two parallel interfaces at separation $\delta>0$ and, as $\delta\downarrow0$, every declared correlator with the pair converges to the correlator of a single interface. The limiting insertion, its normalization, and its junction data are the fused interface $\mathcal I_{12}\star\mathcal I_{01}:\mathcal T_0\to\mathcal T_2$. If this limit is not part of the model or does not exist, no single fused interface is asserted.

An **endodefect** has $\mathcal T_- = \mathcal T_+$ as the same complete model data, not merely models with similarly named fields. The **transparent identity interface** $\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}$ is the model-supplied transmission condition that identifies the two sides without changing any correlator. An endodefect is an **invertible symmetry interface** only if a two-sided inverse exists under the stated fusion operation, both composites equal $\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}$ in all declared correlators, and the induced map is an automorphism of the model's observable and background data preserving its correlators. A topological interface between distinct source and target models is an interface, not an internal symmetry of either model. No supersymmetry or BPS condition is implicit; claiming one requires additional model data and a separate check of the specified supercharges and their domains.

No dimensional quantity is added by this definition. Each model and interface must retain its declared unit system and normalization, and this definition does not assert that a continuum fusion limit exists.

declaration.title: A nontrivial Z2 topological defect in finite quantum mechanics
declaration.design_state: Owner-directed B-page finite-model example or counterexample, proved locally; no empirical or continuum claim.
declaration.statement:
Let $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^2$ with its standard positive inner product, and let the Hamiltonian be the zero matrix $H=0$. This defines a finite-dimensional $0+1$-dimensional quantum-mechanical transfer model: propagation through an interval of length $s\ge0$ is $e^{-sH}=I$, where $s$ is Euclidean time in units with $\hbar=1$. The local observables are all matrices in $\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H)$, and a correlator with fixed boundary vectors is the matrix element of their time-ordered product with the propagation matrices between insertions.

Let $G=\mathbb Z_2=\{0,1\}$ with addition modulo $2$, and define $U_0=I$ and $U_1=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$. Insert $U_g$ at an interior point $\tau\in(0,T)$ of the time interval $[0,T]$. For any finite ordered list of other fixed observable insertions, moving $\tau$ within a gap that contains no other insertion leaves their order relative to $U_g$ unchanged. The insertion is a nontrivial invertible $\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry defect of this model.

declaration.title: An invertible interface between two finite quantum-mechanical models
declaration.design_state: Owner-directed B-page finite-model example or counterexample, proved locally; no empirical or continuum claim.
declaration.statement:
Use natural units $\hbar=1$. Let the source model $\mathcal T_-$ and target model $\mathcal T_+$ each have Hilbert space $\mathbb C^2$ with its standard positive inner product and all complex $2\times2$ matrices as local observables. Their Hamiltonian matrices are

$$H_- = \begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&\Delta\end{pmatrix},\qquad H_+ = \begin{pmatrix}\Delta&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \Delta>0.$$

Here $\Delta$ has units of energy and a Euclidean time interval $s$ has units of inverse energy; propagation is $e^{-sH_\pm}$. Define the interface map

$$V=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}:\mathcal H_-\longrightarrow\mathcal H_+.$$

The target observable corresponding to $O_-\in\operatorname{End}(\mathbb C^2)$ is $O_+=VO_-V^\dagger$. For a single interface at time $\tau\in(0,T)$, its transfer amplitude between boundary vectors $\psi_-\in\mathcal H_-$ and $\psi_+\in\mathcal H_+$ is

$$C_\tau=\langle\psi_+,e^{-(T-\tau)H_+}V e^{-\tau H_-}\psi_-\rangle.$$

This is an invertible topological interface between two specified models. It is an internal symmetry only if the source and target models are subsequently identified as one complete model.

declaration.title: Group-like p-form global symmetry and backgrounds
declaration.design_state: Codimension-general topological-defect prerequisite is current and ready. Direct dependency corrected from the supplier codimension-one interface definition; owner escalation is recorded for this cross-batch edge change.
declaration.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$, an integer $p$ with $0\le p<d$, and a smooth $d$-dimensional spacetime manifold $M$, possibly with boundary. A selected model $\mathcal T$ specifies its spacetime structure and boundary conditions; field configuration space, field bundles, regularity and admitted sectors; observables and their supports; normalized correlation functionals; and, when present, its action, regulator, measure, unit system and charge normalization. No such data are inferred from a familiar theory name.

Use the preceding topological-defect definition with its exact content: a defect is model-specified field, operator or boundary-condition data on a closed embedded support, and it is topological when every declared correlator is invariant under each admissible isotopy that transports its data, avoids other insertions and preserves boundary data. For this symmetry, each defect is an endodefect insertion in the same selected model; the model supplies parallel fusion and the induced action on its admitted observables and backgrounds. A support $\Sigma$ is the image of a smooth embedding $\iota:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M^\circ$ from a manifold without boundary, with closed image in the interior $M^\circ$.

A **group-like $p$-form global symmetry** of $\mathcal T$ consists of a locally compact Hausdorff topological group $G$ and an assignment $g\mapsto U_g(\Sigma)$ of invertible topological symmetry defects to the allowed closed supports $\Sigma$ of dimension $d-p-1$ and codimension $p+1$. The model must define the parallel fusion operation and a transparent identity defect, with $U_e(\Sigma)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal T}$ and $U_g(\Sigma)\star U_h(\Sigma)=U_{gh}(\Sigma)$ whenever that fusion is defined. Each $U_g$ has a two-sided inverse $U_{g^{-1}}$ under the supplied fusion law, and crossing it induces an automorphism preserving the declared observables, backgrounds and correlators. The group $G$ is **effective**: elements inducing identical actions in every admitted correlator and on every admitted observable and background are identified. A group element labels a transformation, not the charge of an observable.

A **genuine $p$-dimensional observable** is an observable supported on a closed embedded $p$-dimensional submanifold whose definition is independent of an attached higher-dimensional support. Its symmetry action is defined by moving a symmetry defect across it, with the model specifying the resulting junction or operator action. For $p>0$, if crossing by every $U_g$ preserves the one-dimensional space $\mathbb C O$ for a nonzero genuine observable $O$, write the scalar action as $\chi_O(g)O$. If the resulting map $\chi_O:G\to U(1)$ is a continuous homomorphism in a model where $G$ is Abelian, call $\chi_O$ the character charge of $O$; it is an element of $\widehat G$. This definition does not assert scalarity, continuity or multiplicativity for every observable. For $p=0$, local observables may carry higher-dimensional representations of a non-Abelian group; the representation label is distinct from the group element implementing a transformation. For a locally compact Hausdorff Abelian group $A$, write its character group as $\widehat A=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(A,U(1))$, with pointwise multiplication. Here $U(1)=\{e^{i\alpha}:\alpha\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z\}$, so every character value and its argument are dimensionless.

A **background** for a symmetry is nondynamical model data, not summed over. For a finite Abelian group $A$, fix a triangulation $K$ of $M$ and let $C^k(K;A)$ be the group of functions from oriented $k$-simplices to $A$, with orientation reversal acting by negation. Its coboundary is the alternating sum over faces,

$$
(\delta c)([v_0,\ldots,v_{k+1}])=\sum_{j=0}^{k+1}(-1)^j c([v_0,\ldots,\widehat v_j,\ldots,v_{k+1}]).
$$

Since $\delta^2=0$ by pairwise cancellation of twice-deleted faces, a discrete $(p+1)$-form background with no higher-group mixing is a cocycle $B\in C^{p+1}(K;A)$ modulo $B\mapsto B+\delta\Lambda$ for $\Lambda\in C^p(K;A)$. Relative cochains or boundary-fixed gauge transformations are used when required by the model's boundary conditions. If other backgrounds mix with $B$, the model must give the modified cocycle and gauge-transformation laws.

For a continuous $U(1)^r$ $p$-form symmetry, a background consists of model-supplied local $(p+1)$-form potentials, their overlap and lower-overlap transition data, a globally specified curvature locally given by $H=dB$, and the small and large gauge transformations with their holonomy and integral-flux normalization. Small transformations have the local form $B\mapsto B+d\Lambda$ for a $p$-form $\Lambda$. The unit system and all coefficients in background couplings remain model inputs. The model must define its correlators in these backgrounds; this definition asserts neither that every symmetry admits such a coupling nor that the symmetry can be gauged.

declaration.title: Exchangeability makes p-form symmetry groups Abelian and simple charges characters
declaration.design_state: Complete conditional proof authored; its p-form definition prerequisite is current and ready.
declaration.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, $1\le p<d$, and let $\mathcal T$ have a group-like $p$-form global symmetry $G$ as defined above. Assume the selected model has a unitary Hilbert-space realization and, for every $g,h\in G$, admits two parallel copies of their codimension-$(p+1)$ symmetry supports inside a contractible neighborhood with a disk spanned by two independent normal directions, together with an isotopy exchanging their order without intersecting any other insertion or changing boundary data. Then $G$ is Abelian.

Let $O(C)$ be a nonzero genuine $p$-dimensional operator bounded in the operator norm of the selected Hilbert-space representation. Call it **simple for this result** when each topological local junction endomorphism on $O$ produced by passing a symmetry defect across it is a scalar multiple of $O$. Assume the induced action on the one-dimensional space spanned by $O$ is continuous and unitary. There is a continuous character $\chi_O:G\to U(1)$ such that passing $U_g$ across $O$ multiplies it by $\chi_O(g)$. Thus the charge of $O$ belongs to the Pontryagin dual $\widehat G=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,U(1))$. This theorem makes no claim for $p=0$ or for operators with nonscalar crossing endomorphisms.

declaration.title: Magnetic one-form charge of an external U(1) line
declaration.design_state: The field-configuration proof derives the U(1) character directly from the integer flux data, so it does not import the abstract theorem or assume that the line satisfies its Hilbert-space simplicity hypotheses.
declaration.statement:
Use natural units $\hbar=c=1$ and $M=\mathbb R^4$ with its standard orientation and Euclidean metric. The selected field model is pure compact Maxwell theory with actual gauge group $U(1)=\{e^{i\alpha}:\alpha\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z\}$, no dynamical electric or magnetic matter, and a smooth right principal $U(1)$-bundle with connection on the complement of admitted external line insertions. A principal connection is a smooth $\mathfrak u(1)$-valued one-form reproducing each fundamental vertical vector and equivariant under the right group action. Identify $\mathfrak u(1)=i\mathbb R$ with $\mathbb R$ so its local potentials $A_i$ have holonomy $\exp(i\int A_i)$ and the real curvature $F$ obeys $F|_{U_i}=dA_i$, since the Abelian Lie bracket vanishes. The model fixes the action convention $S[A]=(2e^2)^{-1}\int F\wedge *F$ with dimensionless $e>0$, integrating outside any prescribed line-core tube with its declared boundary condition. It also fixes the allowed bundle sectors, boundary behavior at infinity, and any regulator or measure; no continuum measure is constructed here. With this normalization $[A_i]=\mathrm{length}^{-1}$, $[F]=\mathrm{length}^{-2}$, and $\int_\Sigma F$ is dimensionless.

Let $C$ be a closed smooth oriented curve carrying an admitted genuine external magnetic line $T_m(C)$, where genuine means that no auxiliary surface is attached to define the insertion. Its integer charge $m\in\mathbb Z$ is specified by $\int_{S^2_{\mathrm{link}}}F=2\pi m$ on every sufficiently small oriented normal two-sphere linking $C$. The model has no other magnetic sources, and its normalized correlation functional is assumed to be defined for these insertions.

For a closed smooth oriented surface $\Sigma$ disjoint from the line, and $\alpha\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$, define the magnetic surface operator

$$
U_\alpha(\Sigma)=\exp\!\left(\frac{i\alpha}{2\pi}\int_\Sigma F\right).
$$

For this example, a smooth singular three-chain is a finite real linear combination of smooth maps from the standard 3-simplex, with boundary the alternating sum of its face maps. For a source-free move, the model supplies a compact smooth singular three-chain $V$ in $M\setminus C$ with $\partial V=\Sigma_1-\Sigma_0$. For a move across the line, the model supplies a compact oriented smooth three-dimensional track $W$ in $M$, represented as a finite smooth singular chain, with endpoint boundary $\partial W=\Sigma_1-\Sigma_0$; its support is a smooth embedded three-manifold near each of its finitely many intersections with $C$, and the intersections are transverse interior points. Transverse means that the tangent space of this three-manifold and the tangent line of $C$ span $T_xM$. Excise a small open three-ball in each such regular neighborhood. The model supplies a source-free collar in the punctured tubular neighborhood identifying each resulting boundary sphere with a small oriented normal two-sphere $S_j^2$ linking $C$. The resulting punctured chain $V$ lies in $M\setminus C$ and has $\partial V=\Sigma_1-\Sigma_0-\sum_j\epsilon_jS_j^2$, where $\epsilon_j$ is the oriented intersection sign of $W$ with $C$. Define the algebraic intersection number $I(W,C)=\sum_j\epsilon_j$. The claimed action is that a source-free move leaves $U_\alpha$ unchanged, while a move across the line multiplies it by $e^{i\alpha m I(W,C)}$. In particular, the line carries the character $\chi_m(e^{i\alpha})=e^{i\alpha m}$ of the magnetic one-form $U(1)$ symmetry.
declaration.physical_scope: A conditional field-configuration example for a pure compact U(1) Maxwell model in four Euclidean dimensions with an external genuine magnetic line; it makes no continuum-measure, empirical, or general interacting-QFT claim.

declaration.design_state: Complete finite-model verification authored; the p-form and character-theorem suppliers are current and ready.
declaration.statement:
Let $M=S^1_\beta$ be Euclidean time of circumference $\beta>0$, let $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^3$ with orthonormal basis $e_1,e_2,e_3$, and let the Hamiltonian be $H_0=0$. Use natural units $\hbar=1$. The finite model's normalized correlation functional for time-ordered operator insertions is $C(O_1,\ldots,O_n)=\frac13\operatorname{Tr}(O_1\cdots O_n)$. Let $S_3$ be the group of permutations of $\{1,2,3\}$, with composition $(\sigma\tau)(j)=\sigma(\tau(j))$, and define the unitary action $\rho(\sigma)e_j=e_{\sigma(j)}$. A symmetry defect at time $t$ is $U_\sigma(t)=\rho(\sigma)$.

The state space decomposes as $\mathcal H=\mathbb C(e_1+e_2+e_3)\oplus V_2$, where $V_2=\{(z_1,z_2,z_3)\in\mathbb C^3:z_1+z_2+z_3=0\}$. The first summand is the trivial representation and $V_2$ is the two-dimensional standard irreducible representation. The representation label of a state sector is therefore either the trivial representation or the standard two-dimensional representation; a permutation $\sigma\in S_3$ is instead a group element implementing a symmetry transformation. This is an ordinary $p=0$ example and does not conflict with the exchange theorem for $p\ge1$.

declaration.title: Finite 2-group symmetry realization and background coupling
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; the statement, complete argument, placement, proof contract and exact dependencies are recorded. All direct suppliers are current-ready and their interfaces have been checked.
declaration.statement:
Fix an integer $d\geq2$, a closed compact oriented smooth $d$-manifold $M$, and a finite ordered triangulation $K$ of $M$, meaning a finite vertex-ordered simplicial complex whose geometric realization is $M$. The model fixes an orientation and any additional spin or related lifting data required by its fields; these choices are its tangential structure. A **selected finite-regulator Euclidean model** on $K$ specifies its exact symmetry groups, field representations, finite field-value sets $X_\sigma$ for cells $\sigma\in K$, constraints, and configuration spaces $\Phi_x\subseteq\prod_{\sigma\in K}X_\sigma$ for each background $x$. It also specifies a dimensionless Euclidean action $S_x:\Phi_x\to\mathbb R$, finite measure weights $\mu_x:\Phi_x\to\mathbb C$, and a unital algebra $\mathcal O_x$ of model-defined observables, represented as functions on $\Phi_x$. An observable is **local** when its function depends only on field variables on a specified subcomplex of $K$; a line observable has support on a one-dimensional subcomplex. Write $W_x(\phi):=\mu_x(\phi)e^{-S_x(\phi)}$. For local insertion functions $o_{j,x}:\Phi_x\to\mathbb C$, define the unnormalized correlator by $C_x(O_1,\ldots,O_n):=\sum_{\phi\in\Phi_x}W_x(\phi)\prod_{j=1}^n o_{j,x}(\phi)$; the empty tuple has value $Z_x=C_x()$. Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$; cochain labels, action phases, and the partition weight are dimensionless. The model separately assigns dimensions to any continuous field quantities or observables it includes. No continuum limit or Lorentzian continuation is part of this definition.

Let $G$ be the selected finite discrete internal $0$-form symmetry group. Its action on the model's local field and observable data is specified by group homomorphisms into the corresponding automorphism groups. Let $A$ be the selected finite discrete abelian $1$-form symmetry group, written additively, with the exact support, charge, and background conventions of the selected p-form symmetry model. Choosing a finite Abelian $A$ is part of this 2-group model's input; no claim is made that every p-form symmetry group is Abelian without further hypotheses. The group is effective in the selected model: elements inducing identical actions in every admitted correlator, observable, and background are identified. Each generator $U_a(\Sigma)$ is a defect insertion with support $j(\Sigma)$, where $\Sigma$ is a smooth manifold without boundary and $j:\Sigma\hookrightarrow M$ is a smooth embedding with closed codimension-two image represented by a subcomplex of $K$; the insertion includes the model-specified local field or operator data and any required orientation, coorientation, framing, or junction data on that image. It is topological when the model's correlators are invariant under permitted isotopies of that support avoiding other insertions; an allowed isotopy is a piecewise-smooth family of such embeddings in $M$ with disjoint supports and transported defect data. The generators fuse by $U_aU_{a'}=U_{a+a'}$. A genuine line observable is a line-supported insertion defined without an attached surface or other defect. For a nonzero genuine line observable $O_\gamma$ whose one-dimensional span is preserved by every $U_a$, its scalar $A$-action is a character $\chi_\gamma\in\widehat A:=\operatorname{Hom}(A,U(1))$; sweeping $U_a(\Sigma)$ once across that line in the chosen positive orientation multiplies the correlator by $\chi_\gamma(a)$. Other line observables need not carry a scalar character. The selected $0$-form symmetry acts on these defect labels through a specified left action $\rho:G\to\operatorname{Aut}(A)$.

Choose a normalized inhomogeneous $3$-cocycle $\beta:G^3\to A$ for this left action; normalized means it vanishes if any argument is the identity, and the cocycle equation is

$$
\rho_g\beta(h,k,l)-\beta(gh,k,l)+\beta(g,hk,l)-\beta(g,h,kl)+\beta(g,h,k)=0.
$$

For a normalized $2$-cochain $c:G^2\to A$, set

$$
(\delta_\rho c)(g,h,k):=\rho_g c(h,k)-c(gh,k)+c(g,hk)-c(g,h).
$$

Two normalized $3$-cocycles represent the same Postnikov class when their difference is $\delta_\rho c$ for such a normalized $c$; $[\beta]$ denotes this equivalence class. The skeletal associator convention is directed from $(gh)k$ to $g(hk)$. A discrete background is nondynamical model data and is not summed over. It is an object $x=(a,B)$ of the finite background gauge $2$-groupoid on $K$: $a_{ij}\in G$ is a flat edge cochain, $a_{ij}a_{jk}=a_{ik}$ on every ordered triangle; $B_{ijk}\in A$ is a face cochain at its first vertex; and on every ordered tetrahedron

$$
(\delta_a B)_{ijkl}:=\rho_{a_{ij}}B_{jkl}-B_{ikl}+B_{ijl}-B_{ijk}=\beta(a_{ij},a_{jk},a_{kl})=(a^*\beta)_{ijkl}.
$$

Thus the two background fields are constrained and are not independent. A $1$-gauge arrow is given by vertex labels $g_i\in G$ and edge labels $\lambda_{ij}\in A$, with

$$
a'_{ij}=g_i a_{ij}g_j^{-1},\qquad \zeta^g_{ijk}=-\beta(g_i,a_{ij},a_{jk})+\beta(a'_{ij},g_j,a_{jk})-\beta(a'_{ij},a'_{jk},g_k),
$$

$$
B'_{ijk}=\rho_{g_i}B_{ijk}+\zeta^g_{ijk}+\rho_{a'_{ij}}\lambda_{jk}-\lambda_{ik}+\lambda_{ij}.
$$

A $2$-arrow between $1$-arrows with the same vertex labels $g$ and edge labels $\lambda,\lambda'$ is a vertex $A$-cochain $t$ satisfying $\lambda'-\lambda=\delta_{a'}t$, where $(\delta_{a'}t)_{ij}=\rho_{a'_{ij}}t_j-t_i$; vertical composition adds these cochains. For consecutive $1$-arrows $(g,\lambda)$ then $(h,\mu)$, their composite has vertex labels $hg$ and edge labels $\nu_{ij}=\rho_{h_i}\lambda_{ij}+\mu_{ij}+\tau_{ij}$, where $\tau_{ij}=\beta(h_i,g_i,a_{ij})-\beta(h_i,a'_{ij},g_j)+\beta(a''_{ij},h_j,g_j)$ and $a''_{ij}=h_i a'_{ij}h_j^{-1}$. Horizontal composition sends $2$-arrow cochains $t,s$ to $s+\rho_h t$. For three consecutive arrows with vertex labels $g,h,k$, the associator is the vertex cochain $\sigma_i=\beta(k_i,h_i,g_i)$; identity arrows have vertex labels $e$ and edge labels $0$, and unit constraints are identity $2$-arrows. The pentagon and triangle coherence equations are those of this finite background gauge $2$-groupoid.

A **finite 2-group background coupling** in the selected model assigns to each finite 2-group background its configuration space, local observable algebra, action, measure, and partition function $Z_x=C_x()$, and assigns to every $1$-gauge arrow $f:x\to y$ a specified bijection $T_f:\Phi_x\to\Phi_y$ and observable-algebra isomorphism $\alpha_f:\mathcal O_x\to\mathcal O_y$. Every $2$-arrow is assigned its specified intertwiner, and all assignments must obey the identity, composition, associator, and unit coherence laws of the background gauge $2$-groupoid. The action and measure are model inputs; the finite 2-group data alone do not choose them or determine their transformation phase.

A permitted background counterterm is a model-declared dimensionless functional $L_x\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$ that is a finite sum of functions, each depending only on cochain labels in one simplex or a specified finite cluster of simplices; it reweights the model by $e^{iL_x}$. If under a gauge arrow $f:x\to y$ all unnormalized correlators transform by a common phase $\chi_f(x)\in U(1)$, coherence requires $\chi_{\mathrm{id}_x}(x)=1$, $\chi_{g\circ f}(x)=\chi_g(y)\chi_f(x)$ for composable arrows, and equal phases for $2$-isomorphic arrows. The residual background anomaly is the class of these phases under $\chi_f(x)\mapsto e^{iL_y}\chi_f(x)e^{-iL_x}$ for the permitted counterterms. The anomaly is absent in the selected scheme exactly when an allowed counterterm makes every such phase $1$. The Postnikov class specifies the background constraint and gauge transformations; it is not itself the model's transformation phase or anomaly. It may enter an anomaly calculation for a specified action and measure.

For each background object $x$, let the selected Euclidean finite-regulator model have a finite configuration set $\Phi_x$, dimensionless action $S_x:\Phi_x\to\mathbb R$, measure weight $\mu_x:\Phi_x\to\mathbb C$, and total weight $W_x(\phi):=\mu_x(\phi)e^{-S_x(\phi)}$, in natural units $c=\hbar=1$. $$
C_x(O_1,\ldots,O_n):=\sum_{\phi\in\Phi_x}W_x(\phi)\prod_{j=1}^n o_{j,x}(\phi),
$$

$$
W_y(T_f\phi)=\chi_f(x)W_x(\phi),
$$

with a model-specified phase $\chi_f(x)\in U(1)$ independent of $\phi$. Assume these phases are $1$ on identity arrows, multiply under composition, and agree on $2$-isomorphic arrows. Then for every such arrow and observable tuple,

$$
C_y(\alpha_fO_1,\ldots,\alpha_fO_n)=\chi_f(x)C_x(O_1,\ldots,O_n),\qquad Z_y=\chi_f(x)Z_x.

Give the simple-label fusion product by

$$
\mathbf 1\otimes a=a\otimes\mathbf 1=a,\qquad \psi\otimes\psi=\mathbf 1,\qquad \psi\otimes\sigma=\sigma\otimes\psi=\sigma,\qquad \sigma\otimes\sigma=\mathbf 1\oplus\psi.
$$

Extend the product bilinearly to direct sums and on morphisms by the induced tensor product of scalar maps. The unit is $\mathbf 1$ and the unitors are strict. Fusion spaces are $V_{ab}^c=\operatorname{Hom}(a\otimes b,c)$; each is one-dimensional when the displayed fusion rule allows $c$ and is zero otherwise. In every allowed one-dimensional fusion space choose its displayed basis vector. On three simple labels, define the associator in these bases by the matrix $[F^{abc}_d]_{xy}$, where $x$ is the intermediate label in $(a\otimes b)\otimes c\to d$ and $y$ is the intermediate label in $a\otimes(b\otimes c)\to d$. $$
\left[F^{\sigma\sigma\sigma}_{\sigma}\right]_{xy}=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}_{xy},\qquad x,y\in\{\mathbf 1,\psi\},
$$

$$
\left[F^{\psi\sigma\psi}_{\sigma}\right]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1,\qquad \left[F^{\sigma\psi\sigma}_{\psi}\right]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1.
$$

Every other coefficient is $1$ when all four fusion vertices are allowed and $0$ when any required fusion vertex is forbidden. Extend each associator linearly over direct sums. The candidate dual of each simple label is itself. For $\mathbf 1$ and $\psi$, take evaluation and coevaluation to be the unit-channel basis maps with coefficient $1$. declaration.title: Finite-lattice realization of the Ising non-invertible defect
declaration.design_state: Assigned conditional finite-lattice physical theorem with explicit Hamiltonian, defect operator, fusion and junction data.
declaration.statement:
Fix an integer $L\ge2$ and the periodic site set $\mathbb Z/L\mathbb Z$. Let $\mathcal H_L=\ell^2(\mathbb Z_2^L)$ with orthonormal basis $|h_1,\ldots,h_L\rangle$, where every $h_j\in\mathbb Z_2$ and $h_0=h_L$. Define Pauli operators by $Z_j|\mathbf h\rangle=(-1)^{h_j}|\mathbf h\rangle$ and $X_j|\mathbf h\rangle=|\mathbf h+\mathbf e_j\rangle$. Adopt the finite quantum Ising model with Hamiltonian

$$
H_L=-J\sum_{j=1}^{L}(Z_jZ_{j+1}+X_j),\qquad J>0,
$$

where $Z_{L+1}=Z_1$, $J$ has units of energy, and $\hbar=1$. Euclidean propagation through a time interval $s\ge0$ is the exact finite matrix $e^{-sH_L}$, with $s$ in inverse-energy units. Correlators are matrix elements between arbitrary boundary vectors of finite ordered lists of observable matrices and these propagation factors.

Let $\widehat{\mathcal H}_L=\ell^2(\mathbb Z_2^L)$ have basis $|\widehat h_{1/2},\ldots,\widehat h_{L-1/2}\rangle$, with dual Pauli operators $\widehat Z$ and $\widehat X$ defined by the same formulas on half-integer sites. Define the Kramers–Wannier defect map $D_L:\mathcal H_L\to\widehat{\mathcal H}_L$ by

$$
\langle\widehat{\mathbf h}|D_L|\mathbf h\rangle=2^{-L/2}(-1)^{\sum_{j=1}^{L}\widehat h_{j-1/2}(h_{j-1}+h_j)}.
$$

Identify the dual chain with the original chain by the half-site shift $j+1/2\mapsto j$; under this identification $D_L$ is an endodefect. A defect line is a wrapping insertion of $D_L$ on a Euclidean time slice. Its allowed position changes are slides within gaps between fixed observable insertions. In this finite lattice model, topologicality means invariance under the declared local line slides and re-association moves; no smooth continuum isotopy claim is made. A finite defect network has labels $\mathbf 1,\psi,\sigma$, represented on the chain by $I,P_L,D_L$, where $P_L=\prod_jX_j$. Its fusion spaces are one-dimensional precisely for

$$
\mathbf 1\otimes a=a\otimes\mathbf 1=a,\qquad \psi\otimes\psi=\mathbf 1,\qquad \psi\otimes\sigma=\sigma\otimes\psi=\sigma,\qquad \sigma\otimes\sigma=\mathbf 1\oplus\psi,
$$

and zero otherwise. Fix the Ising junction bases and associator as follows. Write $\epsilon(\mathbf 1)=0$ and $\epsilon(\psi)=1$; then

$$
[F^{\sigma\sigma\sigma}_{\sigma}]_{ab}=2^{-1/2}(-1)^{\epsilon(a)\epsilon(b)},\qquad a,b\in\{\mathbf 1,\psi\},
$$

$$
[F^{\psi\sigma\psi}_{\sigma}]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1,\qquad [F^{\sigma\psi\sigma}_{\psi}]_{\sigma\sigma}=-1,
$$

and every other allowed associator coefficient is $1$. In the local height basis, the nontrivial trivalent tensors with cyclic labels $(\sigma,\sigma,\psi)$ and $(\sigma,\psi,\sigma)$ are $2^{-1/4}(-1)^h$ and $(X)_{hh'}=\delta_{h',h+1}$, respectively; reversed orientations use adjoint tensors. Together with the unit-channel maps specified above, these are the adopted local junction and re-association data of this finite network model; they are not inferred from fusion multiplicities alone.

For this selected finite model, $D_L$ is topological under the declared defect slides, its exact operator fusion is $D_L^2=I+P_L$, $P_L^2=I$, and $D_LP_L=P_LD_L=D_L$, and the junction spaces and associators are the finite semisimple unitary Ising fusion data above. In particular $D_L$ is non-invertible. The claim is confined to this finite lattice model and asserts no continuum limit or empirical fact.

declaration.title: Finite-Jet Non-Abelian BRST Complex
declaration.statement:
Let $n\geq 1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty open set with coordinates $x^1,\ldots,x^n$, and let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra with bilinear alternating bracket $[\ ,\ ]_{\mathfrak g}$ satisfying the Jacobi identity. Let $V=V_{\bar 0}\oplus V_{\bar 1}$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Z_2$-graded complex vector space, and let $\rho:\mathfrak g\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ be an even representation, meaning $\rho([X,Y]_{\mathfrak g})=\rho(X)\rho(Y)-\rho(Y)\rho(X)$ for all $X,Y\in\mathfrak g$ and each $\rho(X)$ preserves the grading of $V$. This is local Lie-algebra data; no global group, principal bundle, action functional, or quantum theory is selected here.

Choose a basis $T_a$ of $\mathfrak g$ and write $[T_b,T_c]_{\mathfrak g}=f^a{}_{bc}T_a$. A local gauge potential is a $\mathfrak g$-valued one-form $A=A_\mu^aT_a\,dx^\mu$ whose component jet generators $A_{\mu,I}^a$ are even and have ghost number zero. A matter field is a $V$-valued local field $\psi$ with each component jet generator $\psi_I^\alpha$ assigned the parity of its graded component and ghost number zero. The ghost is $c=c^aT_a$, with odd component jet generators $c_I^a$ of ghost number one. The coefficient bracket of homogeneous $\mathfrak g$-valued fields is $[X,Y]^a=f^a{}_{bc}X^bY^c$, using multiplication in the graded-commutative coefficient algebra; in particular $[c,c]^a=f^a{}_{bc}c^bc^c$ has no factor of $1/2$.

For a multi-index $I=(I_1,\ldots,I_n)\in\mathbb N^n$, let $\Phi_I$ denote the corresponding formal jet generator of a field component $\Phi$. The finite-jet local algebra $\mathcal F_U$ is $C^\infty(U)$ tensored with the polynomial algebra in its even jet generators and the exterior algebra in its odd jet generators, where each element uses only finitely many jet generators. The total derivatives $D_\mu$ act by $D_\mu f=\partial_\mu f$ on $f\in C^\infty(U)$ and $D_\mu\Phi_I=\Phi_{I+e_\mu}$ on every jet generator; the multi-index derivatives commute.

Define the degree-one BRST operator candidate $s$ on the fields by

$$sA_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c],\qquad sc=-\frac12[c,c],\qquad s\psi=-\rho(c)\psi.$$

On coefficient functions set $sf=0$, and on every jet generator set $s(\Phi_I)=D_I(s\Phi)$; extend $s$ to $\mathcal F_U$ by the odd left-derivation rule $s(FG)=(sF)G+(-1)^{|F|}F(sG)$ for homogeneous $F$, where $|F|$ is total parity. The minimal sector here contains only $A,\psi,c$ and their jets. Antighosts and Nakanishi–Lautrup variables are not included; adjoining such a nonminimal pair requires separate definitions and a proof before any cohomological triviality claim. The specified data are a BRST complex once $s^2=0$, which is established for these formulas in the following nilpotence lemma.

declaration.title: Local BRST Cohomology Modulo Total Derivatives
declaration.statement:
Let $n\geq1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be nonempty and open, let $\mathcal F_U$ be the finite-jet local algebra with nilpotent BRST derivation $s$ and commuting total derivatives $D_\mu$, and let $dx^1,\ldots,dx^n$ be anticommuting coordinate one-forms. For $g\in\mathbb Z$ and $0\leq p\leq n$, let $\mathcal A_U^{g,p}$ be the space of local horizontal $p$-forms of ghost number $g$, namely finite sums of $dx^{\mu_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{\mu_p}$ with coefficients in the ghost-number-$g$ part of $\mathcal F_U$. Define the horizontal differential $d_H:=dx^\mu D_\mu$; its square is $d_H^2a=dx^\mu\wedge dx^\nu D_\mu D_\nu a=\tfrac12dx^\mu\wedge dx^\nu[D_\mu,D_\nu]a=0$. Extend $s$ to horizontal forms by $s(dx^\mu\wedge a)=-dx^\mu\wedge sa$. Since $sD_\mu=D_\mu s$, one has $s(d_Ha)=-dx^\mu\wedge D_\mu(sa)=-d_H(sa)$, hence $sd_H+d_Hs=0$.

For $p=0$, set $\mathcal A_U^{g,-1}=\{0\}$. The local BRST cohomology modulo total derivatives in bidegree $(g,p)$ is

$$H^{g,p}(s\mid d_H):=\frac{\{a\in\mathcal A_U^{g,p}:\text{there is }b\in\mathcal A_U^{g+1,p-1}\text{ with }sa+d_Hb=0\}}{\{sm+d_Hn:m\in\mathcal A_U^{g-1,p},\ n\in\mathcal A_U^{g,p-1}\}}.$$

The denominator is a subspace of the numerator: for $a=sm+d_Hn$, choose $b=sn$ and compute $sa+d_Hb=s^2m+sd_Hn+d_Hsn=0$. For $p=0$, $n=b=0$ and the same verification reduces to $s^2m=0$. This is cohomology of the specified local jet algebra and horizontal differential; it is not cohomology of a physical state space or Hilbert space. Interpreting $d_H$-exact top forms as equal local functionals additionally assumes compact support or boundary conditions that make the corresponding surface term vanish.

declaration.title: Classical BV Antibracket and Yang–Mills Master-Action Data
declaration.statement:
Use the local field data and BRST convention on an open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ given by a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a graded representation space $V$, an even $\mathfrak g$-valued gauge potential $A_\mu$, an odd ghost $c$ of ghost number $1$, and matter components $\psi^\alpha$ of parity $\epsilon_\alpha$ and ghost number $0$. For every field or ghost coordinate $\Phi^A$ of parity $\epsilon_A$ and ghost number $g_A$, introduce an antifield $\Phi_A^*$ of parity $\epsilon_A+1\pmod 2$ and ghost number $-1-g_A$. Thus $A^*$ and the antifields of even matter are odd of ghost number $-1$, while $c^*$ is even of ghost number $-2$. The minimal sector consists of $A,\psi,c$ and these antifields.

For a finite-dimensional canonical coordinate algebra, take the polynomial algebra in the even coordinates tensor the exterior algebra in the odd coordinates. In the local-field notation, use finite-jet local functionals with variational derivatives only when the chosen domain makes those derivatives and integrations by parts well-defined; compact support or boundary conditions that kill surface terms are part of that domain. For homogeneous functionals $F,G$, define the canonical antibracket by

$$
(F,G):=\sum_A\left(\frac{\partial_r F}{\partial\Phi^A}\frac{\partial_lG}{\partial\Phi_A^*}-\frac{\partial_rF}{\partial\Phi_A^*}\frac{\partial_lG}{\partial\Phi^A}\right),
$$

with an integral over $U$ replacing the sum in a local-field expression. Left and right derivatives are the graded derivatives acting from the indicated side. This convention has odd parity, ghost number $+1$, the shifted graded-skew identity, the shifted Jacobi identity, and the graded Leibniz identity. A regular finite-dimensional canonical domain has no nonzero central element of ghost number $1$: an element central against every coordinate has all coordinate derivatives zero and is a numerical constant. A formal local-functional domain used below must separately satisfy this same no-ghost-number-one-center condition.

Let a local gauge parameter be a smooth map $\lambda:U\to\mathfrak g$, and define its infinitesimal action on the fields by $\delta_\lambda A_\mu=\partial_\mu\lambda+[A_\mu,\lambda]$ and $\delta_\lambda\psi=-\rho(\lambda)\psi$. Write these variations as $\delta_\lambda\Phi^i=R^i_\alpha[\Phi]\lambda^\alpha$, where $R$ is the resulting linear differential operator in $\lambda$. Assume this declared gauge action is irreducible: if $\delta_\lambda\Phi^i\equiv0$ for every field configuration, then $\lambda\equiv0$. Assume also that its Lie-algebra action closes off shell, meaning its commutator closes without using equations of motion, and that no additional gauge symmetry is included. Let $S_0[A,\psi]$ be a specified local classical action invariant under these transformations. Write $s_0$ for the BRST operator on the minimal fields given by $s_0A_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$, $s_0c=-\tfrac12[c,c]$, and $s_0\psi=-\rho(c)\psi$. The minimal BV functional candidate is

$$S_{\mathrm{BV}}:=S_0+\int_U d^nx\,\sum_A(-1)^{\epsilon_A}\Phi_A^*\,s_0\Phi^A,$$

where each product is in the displayed order and the same left/right derivative convention is used in the antibracket. It is a **classical master action** exactly when it satisfies the classical master equation $(S_{\mathrm{BV}},S_{\mathrm{BV}})=0$; the displayed formula alone does not assert that a particular $S_0$ satisfies that equation.

The optional nonminimal sector adds an odd antighost $\bar c^a$ of ghost number $-1$, an even auxiliary field $b^a$ of ghost number $0$, and their antifields, with the BV functional term $-\bar c_a^*b^a$ giving $s\bar c=b$ and $sb=0$. This definition makes no cohomological contractibility claim for that pair. The formal local-field notation does not define an infinite-dimensional measure, a BV Laplacian $\Delta$, a path integral, or the quantum master equation.
