declaration.title: Canonical Antibracket Generates the Declared BRST Field Variations
declaration.statement:
Let $\mathcal B$ be the finite-dimensional algebra that is polynomial in even canonical coordinates and exterior in odd canonical coordinates $\Phi^A,\Phi_A^*$. Give each homogeneous minimal coordinate $\Phi^A$ parity $\epsilon_A\in\{0,1\}$ and ghost number $g_A$, and give its antifield parity $\epsilon_A+1\pmod 2$ and ghost number $-1-g_A$. Use the canonical antibracket

$$ (F,G)=\sum_A\left(\frac{\partial_rF}{\partial\Phi^A}\frac{\partial_lG}{\partial\Phi_A^*}-\frac{\partial_rF}{\partial\Phi_A^*}\frac{\partial_lG}{\partial\Phi^A}\right). $$

Suppose each $s_0\Phi^A$ is independent of all antifields, has parity $\epsilon_A+1\pmod 2$ and ghost number $g_A+1$, and let $S_0$ be even of ghost number zero and independent of antifields. Define $S:=S_0+\sum_A(-1)^{\epsilon_A}\Phi_A^*s_0\Phi^A$, with the displayed product order. Then $(S,\Phi^A)=s_0\Phi^A$ for each minimal coordinate. For a local-field version on a nonempty open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, use fields $\Phi^A(x)$ and antifields $\Phi_A^*(x)$ with the same parity and ghost-number assignments, replace coordinate derivatives in the bracket by variational derivatives and the sum by $\int_U d^nx$, and set $S_U:=S_{0,U}+\int_U d^nx\,\sum_A(-1)^{\epsilon_A}\Phi_A^*(x)s_0\Phi^A(x)$. If this domain makes the variational derivatives and integrations by parts well-defined and its boundary term vanishes, then $(S_U,\Phi^A(x))=s_0\Phi^A(x)$ pointwise.

declaration.statement: Let $\mathcal B$ be a graded-commutative canonical BV algebra with an odd antibracket $(\ ,\ )$ of ghost number $+1$ satisfying shifted graded skew-symmetry and the shifted Jacobi identity. declaration.title: Finite two-group lattice spin state-sum model
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; dependency and source evidence is recorded in the batch notes and current readiness record.
declaration.statement:
A finite ordered simplicial complex $K$ has a finite vertex set with a total order and a collection of nonempty finite vertex subsets, called simplices, closed under taking nonempty subsets. Its dimension is the maximum of $|\sigma|-1$ over its simplices. A closed physical regulator is a finite ordered triangulation of a closed compact oriented smooth three-manifold; relative amplitudes are also defined on its finite ordered subcomplexes. The increasing vertex order orients every simplex.

Choose $G=\mathbb Z/2$, the trivial Abelian group $A=\{0\}$, the unique action $\rho:G\to\operatorname{Aut}(A)$, and the zero normalized Postnikov cocycle $\beta=0$. A background on $K$ is a flat edge cochain $a_{ij}\in G$, satisfying $a_{ij}+a_{jk}-a_{ik}=0$ on each ordered triangle; its face cochain $B$ is uniquely zero. A raw $1$-gauge arrow has vertex labels $g_i\in G$ and sends $a_{ij}$ to $a'_{ij}=g_i+a_{ij}-g_j$. The edge label $\lambda$ and vertex $2$-gauge label $t$ are necessarily zero, so this selected two-group is the ordinary finite $G$ symmetry regarded as a two-group with trivial $A$.

For each background $x=(a,0)$, the model's cell-value sets are $X_v=G$ at each vertex and a singleton at every positive-dimensional simplex. The configuration set is $\Phi_x=C^0(K;G)$, the set of spin assignments $\sigma=(\sigma_v)_{v\in K^{(0)}}$. There are no further constraints. Set the dimensionless action $S_x(\sigma)=0$, the finite measure weight $\mu_x(\sigma)=2^{-V_K}$, where $V_K$ is the number of vertices, and the observable algebra $\mathcal O_x=\operatorname{Fun}(\Phi_x,\mathbb C)$. A function is local when it depends on spins in a specified subcomplex. The local spin observable $m_v(\sigma)=(-1)^{\sigma_v}$ transforms nontrivially under the constant global $G$ action, so this $0$-form symmetry is effective. For a closed one-dimensional subcomplex $\gamma$, the product $\prod_{v\in\gamma^{(0)}}m_v(\sigma)$ is a line-supported observable defined without an attached surface. The selected $1$-form group is trivial: its only defect is $U_0(\Sigma)=1$, and the line observable has only the trivial $A$-character.

For a background gauge arrow with vertex labels $g$, the configuration bijection is $T_g(\sigma)_v=\sigma_v+g_v$ and the observable-algebra isomorphism is $\alpha_g(O)=O\circ T_g^{-1}$. These assignments respect identity and composition. The per-background partition weight is

$$
W_K(x)=Z_x=\sum_{\sigma\in\Phi_x}2^{-V_K}=1.
$$

The boundary state space on a subcomplex $L$ is the finite-dimensional space $\mathcal H(L)=\operatorname{Fun}(\pi_0\mathcal B(L),\mathbb C)$. For a fixed background $s$ on $L$, the relative convention fixes only this background restriction and sums over all spins on $K$ with weight $2^{-V_K}$; it does not fix boundary spin values. Thus the spin sector contributes $1$ for each extending background and introduces no additional seam factor. The relative background amplitude then uses the relative higher-gauge sum. All fields, action phases, measures, and amplitudes are dimensionless in the convention $\hbar=1$.

The closed-manifold data instantiate the finite-regulator two-group model interface. The relative subcomplex amplitudes and the background-only boundary state space are the additional boundary convention adopted here; they are not inferred from the closed-manifold interface. No continuum limit or empirical conclusion is part of this definition.

declaration.title: Gauge invariance and gluing in the finite symmetry model
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; dependency and source evidence is recorded in the batch notes and current readiness record.
declaration.statement:
Let $K$ be a finite ordered oriented simplicial complex of dimension at most three in the relative extension of the selected model, with $V_K$ vertices and $E_K$ edges. For a closed physical regulator, $K$ is a finite ordered triangulation of a closed compact oriented smooth three-manifold. Use $G=\mathbb Z/2$, the trivial group $A=\{0\}$, the unique action $\rho$, the zero normalized Postnikov cocycle $\beta$, and the unit background response $W_K(x)=1$. The dynamical spin configurations for each background are $\Phi_x=C^0(K;G)$, with action $S_x=0$ and normalized measure $\mu_x(\sigma)=2^{-V_K}$. A background gauge arrow with vertex labels $g$ transports spins by $T_g(\sigma)=\sigma+g$ and transports observables by pullback.

For every background $x$, its spin partition weight is $Z_x=1$. The normalized background-gauging amplitude is
$$ Z_K^{(2)}=\sum_{[x]\in\pi_0\mathcal B(K)}\frac{|\pi_2(\mathcal B(K),x)|}{|\pi_1(\mathcal B(K),x)|}=\frac{1}{2^{V_K}}|\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal B(K)|. $$
For a subcomplex $L\subseteq K$ and fixed background $s$ on $L$, the relative background amplitude is
$$
Z_{K,L}^{(2)}(s)=2^{-(V_K-V_L)}|\{x\in\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal B(K):x|_L=s\}|.
$$
If $K=K_1\cup_\Sigma K_2$ is a union of ordered subcomplexes with compatible restrictions and opposite induced seam orientations, the relative boundary amplitudes are gauge-invariant and obey
$$ Z_K^{(2)}=\sum_{[s]\in\pi_0\mathcal B(\Sigma)} Z_{K_2,\Sigma}^{(2)}(s)Z_{K_1,\Sigma}^{(2)}(s)\frac{|\pi_2(\mathcal B(\Sigma),s)|}{|\pi_1(\mathcal B(\Sigma),s)|}. $$
For a one-vertex boundary complex the amplitude is $1/2$. These conclusions concern only the specified finite model; they do not establish a continuum quantum field theory or empirical behavior.

declaration.title: Degree-six cubic trace polynomial for a chiral representation
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
declaration.statement:
Let $H=SU(3)\times U(1)$, where $SU(3)=\{g\in M_3(\mathbb C):g^\dagger g=I_3,\det g=1\}$ and $U(1)=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$. For a finite-dimensional unitary representation $\rho:H\to U(V_\rho)$, let $A_\rho$ be a smooth anti-Hermitian matrix-valued one-form on a smooth manifold $X$, representing a connection in a local trivialization, and set $F_\rho=dA_\rho+A_\rho\wedge A_\rho$. Define the degree-six invariant polynomial

$$\mathcal I_6(\rho,A_\rho):=2\pi\left[\operatorname{tr}_{V_\rho}\exp\!\left(-\frac{iF_\rho}{2\pi}\right)\right]_6=\frac{i}{24\pi^2}\operatorname{tr}_{V_\rho}(F_\rho\wedge F_\rho\wedge F_\rho),$$

where the exponential is its formal power series and $[\,\cdot\,]_6$ selects the differential-form component of degree six. This is a homogeneous polynomial in the formal curvature; on a four-dimensional physical spacetime it is interpreted on the formal six-dimensional extension used for descent, not integrated as a six-form over spacetime. The normalization fixes anti-Hermitian generators, the fundamental trace, and the overall coefficient once and for all.

For the defining representation $E=\mathbb C^3$ with $\rho_E(g,z)=zg$, a background connection is $A_E=A+iB I_3$, where $A$ is an $\mathfrak{su}(3)$-valued one-form and $B$ is a real $U(1)$ connection one-form. The dual representation is $E^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(E,\mathbb C)$ with $\rho_{E^*}(g,z)=\rho_E(g,z)^{-T}$; its induced connection and curvature are $A_{E^*}=-A_E^T$ and $F_{E^*}=-F_E^T$.

declaration.title: Local perturbative ’t Hooft anomaly modulo counterterms
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
declaration.statement:
Fix a four-dimensional smooth spacetime region $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with a stated orientation, spin structure, boundary conditions, and unit system. A selected model specifies a continuous global symmetry group $H$, its action on the fields and observables, the nondynamical background connections, the field and jet domains, a regulator and measure or formal perturbative generating functional, and the admissible local counterterms. A background connection is nondynamical model data: it transforms under local changes of background trivialization but is not integrated over.

Let $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{g,p}$ be the finite-jet horizontal $p$-forms of ghost number $g$ generated by the nondynamical background connections and their BRST ghost jets, without matter-field jets, and restrict the model’s nilpotent BRST differential $s$ and horizontal exterior derivative $d_H$ to this background subalgebra. An infinitesimal local anomaly representative is a local horizontal four-form $a_4\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{1,4}$ such that $sa_4+d_Hb_3=0$ for some $b_3\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{2,3}$. The **local perturbative ’t Hooft anomaly** of the specified global symmetry is the class $[a_4]$ in the relative cohomology $H^{1,4}(s\mid d_H)$ of this background subalgebra, with the quotient taken using exactly the model’s admissible four-dimensional background counterterms and total-derivative boundary convention. Its class is zero exactly when an admissible local counterterm removes the infinitesimal background variation modulo a boundary term.

Any prescribed noninvariance of the classical action or selected couplings is an explicit-symmetry-breaking insertion and is separated before assigning this quantum anomaly class. It is not, by itself, a measure anomaly. A claim of anomaly matching therefore assumes the stated classical symmetry, or carries such breaking insertions separately.

This definition applies to a global symmetry whose background is nondynamical. If the same local class concerns a field integrated over as a gauge redundancy, it is a local gauge anomaly, not a ’t Hooft anomaly; an uncancelled gauge anomaly obstructs the proposed gauging unless a separately specified cancellation mechanism is included. The definition addresses only infinitesimal transformations and makes no claim about large or disconnected transformations, determinant-line holonomy, torsion phases, or a physical continuum limit.

declaration.title: Flat-space chiral anomaly-matching data and regulator convention
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and flat oriented Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-,+,+,+)$ and its standard spin structure. Fix Dirac matrices by $\{\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu\}=2\eta^{\mu\nu}I$ and $\gamma_5=i\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3$; set $P_+=(I+\gamma_5)/2$ and $P_-=I-P_+$. The global symmetry group is the fixed global form $H=SU(3)\times U(1)_V$, acting on a finite multiset $S$ of massless positive-chirality Weyl fields. Each field is a Grassmann-odd smooth compactly supported section of $\operatorname{im}(P_+)\otimes V_i$, where $V_i$ carries a specified finite-dimensional unitary representation $R_i$ of $H$. The chiral kinetic operator is $\mathcal D_{+,i}=P_-i\gamma^\mu D_{\mu,i}P_+$ from positive to negative chirality; its regulated determinant phase is a formal perturbative input. The matter field has mass dimension $3/2$; the background potentials have mass dimension one, their curvature two-forms dimension two, and all $U(1)_V$ charges and trace coefficients are dimensionless. The backgrounds are global one-forms on the trivial bundles over $M$, vary smoothly, and have compact support; the global symmetry is not integrated over as a dynamical gauge redundancy.

For each species, the background covariant derivative is $D_{\mu,i}=\partial_\mu+\rho_{i*}(A_\mu,iB_\mu)$ in its representation, where $A$ is an anti-Hermitian $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ connection, $B$ is a real $U(1)_V$ connection, and $\rho_{i*}:\mathfrak{su}(3)\oplus i\mathbb R\to\mathfrak u(V_i)$ is the derived Lie-algebra representation. Set $F_A=dA+A\wedge A$ and $f=dB$, and write $A_i:=\rho_{i*}(A,iB)$ and $F_i:=dA_i+A_i\wedge A_i$; thus $D_{\mu,i}=\partial_\mu+(A_i)_\mu$. For $E=(\mathbf3,+1)$, $A_E=A+iB I_3$ and $F_E=F_A+ifI_3$; for $E^*=(\bar{\mathbf3},-1)$, $A_{E^*}=-A^T-iB I_3$ and $F_{E^*}=-F_A^T-ifI_3$. Local transformations are $A\mapsto g^{-1}Ag+g^{-1}dg$ and $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$ for compactly supported $g: M\to SU(3)$ and $\alpha:M\to\mathbb R$; the $U(1)$ group element is $e^{i\alpha}$. Let $c$ be the ghost-number-one odd $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ ghost and $\eta$ the ghost-number-one odd real $U(1)_V$ ghost. The finite-jet BRST differential for $\mathfrak h=\mathfrak{su}(3)\oplus i\mathbb R$ is specified on components by $sA_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$, $sc=-[c,c]/2$, $sB_\mu=\partial_\mu\eta$, $s\eta=0$, and $s\psi_i=-\rho_{i*}(c,i\eta)\psi_i$; it acts on jets by commuting with total derivatives. The $U(1)_V$ factor is central. On horizontal forms use the supplier's extension $s(dx^\mu\wedge a)=-dx^\mu\wedge s(a)$, so $sd_H+d_Hs=0$. In particular the whole one-form obeys $sB=-d_H\eta$; the positive component rule is not a whole-form equation.

For an ordinary compactly supported infinitesimal parameter $\epsilon=\epsilon^aT_a:M\to\mathfrak{su}(3)$ and $\alpha:M\to\mathbb R$, define a linear map $\mathcal E^p_{\epsilon,\alpha}$ from ghost-number-one background horizontal $p$-forms to ordinary $p$-forms. In the unique normal form with all $dx$ factors to the left and the single ghost jet to the right, replace $c_I^a$ by $\partial_I\epsilon^a$ and $\eta_I$ by $\partial_I\alpha$, leaving background jets unchanged. Every such form has precisely one ghost factor because the background algebra has no negative-ghost generators. This is a linear map on that homogeneous component, not an algebra homomorphism on the exterior ghost algebra. It commutes with $d_H$. If $C_p$ is ghost-free, the finite-jet chain rule gives $\mathcal E^p_{\epsilon,\alpha}(sC_p)=(-1)^p\delta_{\epsilon,\alpha}C_p$: the sign moves $s$ past the $p$ coordinate one-forms, and the component rules give the ordinary infinitesimal field variation. Thus in physical degree four $\mathcal E^4(sC_4)=\delta C_4$, and $d_H$-exact terms evaluate to ordinary total derivatives. The degree-five descent is first formed on the formal auxiliary extension used for the degree-six polynomial, before restriction to $M$; there $\mathcal E^5(sI_5)=-\delta I_5$. Consequently $sI_5+d_HI_4^{(1)}=0$ yields the physical convention $\delta I_5=d_H\mathcal E^4(I_4^{(1)})$.

The anomaly-matching data include one common Pauli–Villars subtraction prescription for the chiral triangle graphs, with opposite-statistics regulator fields and regulator masses taken to the large-mass limit, together with the consistent effective-action variation convention and compact-support boundary conditions. The local anomaly complex is the finite-jet background subalgebra generated by $A,B$ and their BRST ghosts, with no matter-field jets, so its ghost-number-zero four-forms are precisely the admitted local counterterms. We quotient by all such finite-jet local counterterms and by compactly supported total derivatives; no background-gauge-invariance condition is imposed on an individual counterterm. In particular, for real dimensionless $\lambda$, the four-form $C_4=\lambda B\wedge K_3(A)$ is admitted, where $K_3(A):=\operatorname{tr}(A\wedge dA+\tfrac23A\wedge A\wedge A)$. As an explicit source-backed one-loop input, after the regulator masses are taken to infinity this selected prescription assigns to each positive-chirality species $R_i$ the consistent local anomaly obtained by descent from $\mathcal I_6(R_i,A_i)$ of the preceding cubic-polynomial definition. The fixed linear descent map is normalized by $\mathcal I_6=dI^{(0)}_5$, $sI^{(0)}_5+d_HI^{(1)}_4=0$, and $sI^{(1)}_4+d_HI^{(2)}_3=0$, with $\delta_{\epsilon,\alpha}\Gamma=\sum_{i\in S}\int_M\mathcal E^4_{\epsilon,\alpha}(I^{(1)}_4(R_i,A_i))$. This determinant law is an adopted regulator input in the data, not a locally derived theorem about every regulator. The total polynomial is $\mathcal I_6^{\mathrm{tot}}=\sum_{i\in S}\mathcal I_6(R_i,A_i)$, and its local anomaly class is interpreted using the preceding local ’t Hooft-anomaly definition. No large-transformation test, torsion calculation, mixed gravitational term, dynamical gauge quantization, or continuum-existence result is included.

declaration.title: Local anomaly cancellation for a conjugate chiral pair
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
declaration.statement:
Use the selected flat-space anomaly-matching model on oriented $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-,+,+,+)$ and natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Its nondynamical global-symmetry backgrounds are a smooth compactly supported anti-Hermitian $SU(3)$ connection $A$ and a smooth compactly supported real $U(1)_V$ connection $B$ on the trivial bundles. The finite field spectrum consists of two massless positive-chirality Weyl species, one in $E=(\mathbf3,+1)$ and one in its dual $E^*=(\bar{\mathbf3},-1)$. The background is not integrated over. Use one common large-mass Pauli–Villars subtraction scheme and the consistent effective-action convention fixed in the model data.

Adopt the source-backed one-loop input that each positive-chirality species in this regulator has consistent local variation given by descent from $\mathcal I_6(R)=2\pi[\operatorname{tr}_R\exp(-iF_R/(2\pi))]_6$, with the same linear descent for every species: $\mathcal I_6=dI_5^{(0)}$, $sI_5^{(0)}+d_HI_4^{(1)}=0$, and $sI_4^{(1)}+d_HI_3^{(2)}=0$, and $\delta_{\epsilon,\alpha}\Gamma=\sum_R\int_M\mathcal E^4_{\epsilon,\alpha}(I_4^{(1)}(R))$. Here $s$ is the component BRST differential extended with $s(dx^\mu\wedge a)=-dx^\mu\wedge s(a)$. The linear map $\mathcal E^4_{\epsilon,\alpha}$ writes each ghost-number-one form with its four $dx$ factors on the left, then replaces its single $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ or real $U(1)_V$ ghost jet by the corresponding ordinary parameter jet; it is not an algebra substitution on products of ghosts. The local anomaly class is the class of $I_4^{(1)}$ in $H^{1,4}(s\mid d_H)$: local ghost-number-one four-forms satisfying the second descent equation, modulo $s$-variations of admitted local counterterms and total derivatives.

Then the total perturbative local anomaly class of this conjugate pair vanishes. This conclusion concerns only the identity component of the background-transformation group in the adopted one-loop convention; it asserts no absence of large-transformation or torsion anomalies and no consistency result for a dynamical gauge redundancy.

declaration.title: A single chiral fundamental has a nonzero local polynomial
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
declaration.statement:
Use the same flat-space background convention but take the spectrum to contain only one positive-chirality species $E=(\mathbf3,+1)$. Its polynomial is

$$\mathcal I_6(E)=\frac{i}{24\pi^2}\left(\operatorname{tr}F_A^3+3i f\wedge\operatorname{tr}F_A^2+3(if)^3\right),$$

where $F_A$ is the anti-Hermitian $SU(3)$ curvature, $f=dB$ is the $U(1)_V$ curvature, and the expression is evaluated as a degree-six polynomial on the formal extension used for descent. The mixed $U(1)_V$–$SU(3)^2$ term and the pure $U(1)_V^3$ term have nonzero coefficients. This example verifies that the one-field polynomial is not the zero invariant polynomial; it does not claim that the associated relative BRST class is nontrivial modulo every admissible counterterm or that a global anomaly has been evaluated.

declaration.title: A mixed-background counterterm shifts the local representative
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
declaration.statement:
Let $A$ be a smooth compactly supported anti-Hermitian $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ connection one-form on trivial $\mathbb R^{1,3}$, with curvature $F_A=dA+A\wedge A$, and let $B$ be a smooth real $U(1)_V$ background one-form with compactly supported gauge parameter $\alpha$. In natural units, $[A]=[B]=\text{mass}$ and $[F_A]=\text{mass}^2$. Define the local three-form

$$K_3(A):=\operatorname{tr}\left(A\wedge dA+\frac23A\wedge A\wedge A\right)$$

and add the four-dimensional local counterterm $C_4=\lambda B\wedge K_3(A)$ to the effective action, with dimensionless coefficient $\lambda$. Under the $U(1)_V$ background transformation $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$ with $A$ fixed, its local variation is

$$\delta_\alpha C_4=\lambda\,d(\alpha K_3(A))-\lambda\,\alpha\operatorname{tr}(F_A\wedge F_A).$$

The first term integrates to a boundary term and vanishes for compactly supported $\alpha$. Thus this counterterm shifts the $U(1)_V$ component of the local anomaly representative by $-\lambda\alpha\operatorname{tr}(F_A\wedge F_A)$ while the full relative class is unchanged modulo the admitted counterterm space. This calculation does not assert that the full $SU(3)\times U(1)_V$ anomaly vanishes or that the $SU(3)$ component of the representative is unchanged.

declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
declaration.statement:
Use the flat four-dimensional background data with global group $SU(3)\times U(1)_V$ and the common consistent regulator fixed above. Take the finite spectrum to consist of positive-chirality Weyl species $E=(\mathbf3,+1)$ and $E^*=(\bar{\mathbf3},-1)$. On a formal six-dimensional extension, write the anti-Hermitian $SU(3)$ curvature as $F_A$ and the $U(1)_V$ curvature as $f=dB$. The defining-representation curvature is $F_E=F_A+i f I_3$, with $\operatorname{tr}F_A=0$, so

$$\mathcal I_6(E)=\frac{i}{24\pi^2}\left(\operatorname{tr}F_A^3+3i f\wedge\operatorname{tr}F_A^2+3(if)^3\right).$$

The dual species has the opposite polynomial. The total polynomial and its common linear consistent descent therefore vanish, so this example has zero perturbative local anomaly class in the selected scheme. The six-dimensional extension is only the formal degree-six polynomial domain; the physical model remains four-dimensional.

declaration.title: Determinant-line holonomy for a global anomaly test
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; current batch-41 local-anomaly Definition inspected and used only to distinguish its infinitesimal class from determinant-line holonomy. Its Step 1 readiness record is missing; effective dependency level recomputed as 4 from the current supplier graph.
declaration.statement:
Fix an even integer $d\ge2$, a compact smooth oriented Riemannian $d$-manifold $M$ without boundary with a specified spin structure, a smooth principal right $G$-bundle $P\to M$ with connection $A$, and a unitary finite-dimensional complex representation $R:G\to U(V_R)$. Let $E_R=P\times_R V_R$ be the associated Hermitian bundle. Let $S^+$ and $S^-$ be the associated bundles of the two half-spin representations of $\operatorname{Spin}(d)$. The chiral Dirac operator is the first-order operator

$$D^+_{A,R}:H^1(M;S^+\otimes E_R)\longrightarrow L^2(M;S^-\otimes E_R),$$

where $H^1$ and $L^2$ are the first Sobolev and square-integrable completions for the fixed Riemannian metric. Assume the operator is Fredholm. Its inverse determinant line is

$$\mathcal L_A=\left(\det_{\mathbb C}\ker D^+_{A,R}\right)^*\otimes\det_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}D^+_{A,R},$$

Here $\det_{\mathbb C}W=\bigwedge^{\dim_{\mathbb C}W}_{\mathbb C}W$, including $\det0=\mathbb C$. Our phrase **inverse determinant line** means the dual of $\Delta_A=\det\ker D^+\otimes(\det\operatorname{coker}D^+)^*$; the displayed $\mathcal L$ is the line called $\mathrm{Det}$, not $\mathrm{Det}^{-1}$, in Dai–Freed §2. This explicit formula fixes the convention throughout.

The named regularized geometry means the following supplied **admissible analytic data**, rather than an arbitrary Hermitian line relabeled by a name. Test smooth dependence on each finite-dimensional smooth parameter manifold $T$ of connections on the fixed $M,P,R$. Write $\mathscr H^\pm=T\times L^2(M;S^\pm\otimes E_R)$ with common first-Sobolev domains. Supply unitary parameter connections $\widetilde\nabla^\pm$ on these Hilbert bundles, preserving smooth sections and the Sobolev domains; for the fixed product identification one may take the ordinary derivative in $T$. Fix a positive inverse-length scale $\mu$ and put $\mathscr D=D^+/\mu$, with Hilbert adjoint $\mathscr D^*$. These choices and the local-counterterm convention are fixed before phases are compared.

Require $Q^+=\mathscr D^*\mathscr D$ and $Q^-=\mathscr D\mathscr D^*$ to have the supplied nonnegative self-adjoint realizations with discrete spectrum, finite multiplicities and smooth eigensections, and the same positive spectrum with multiplicity. A spectral cut is a number $a>0$ not in either spectrum on an open parameter patch $U_a\subseteq T$. The orthogonal projections onto eigenvalues $\lambda<a$, including zero modes, must form smooth finite-rank bundles $V_a^\pm\subset\mathscr H^\pm$; their complements are denoted $\mathscr H^\pm_{>a}$. The finite cut line is $L_a=(\det V_a^+)^*\otimes\det V_a^-$. For $a<b$, the operator $\mathscr D$ is invertible between the eigenbundles $V_{(a,b)}^+$ and $V_{(a,b)}^-$. Glue $L_a$ to $L_b$ by tensoring with its top exterior power $\det\mathscr D_{(a,b)}$. Finite-dimensional cancellation of these invertible modes identifies each fiber with the displayed kernel/cokernel line, even where kernel dimensions jump. Tensor factors are kept in increasing cut order; parity is $\operatorname{ind}D^+\bmod2$ if graded lines are used.

For each cut, define the scalar function $\zeta_a(z)=\sum_{\lambda>a}\lambda^{-z}$ using the positive $Q^+$ eigenvalues with multiplicity and real $\log\lambda$. Admissibility requires convergence on an initial right half-plane, a specified meromorphic continuation to a connected domain reaching $z=0$, regularity there, and smooth parameter dependence of $\zeta'_a(0)$. The **Quillen squared norm** is $\|\ell\|_Q^2=\exp(-\zeta'_a(0))\|\ell_a\|_{L^2}^2$. Finite bands satisfy $\zeta_a-\zeta_b=\sum_{a<\lambda<b}\lambda^{-z}$ and $\|\ell_b\|_{L^2}^2=(\prod_{a<\lambda<b}\lambda)\|\ell_a\|_{L^2}^2$, which give cut independence of this norm. No existence of that continuation for an arbitrary Fredholm family is inferred.

Project $\widetilde\nabla^\pm$ to the cut subbundles and their complements. They induce a connection $\nabla^a$ on $L_a$. On the invertible complement let $\widetilde\nabla\mathscr D_{>a}=\widetilde\nabla^-_{>a}\mathscr D_{>a}-\mathscr D_{>a}\widetilde\nabla^+_{>a}$. For $t>0$ define the complex one-form $h_a(t)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathscr H^+_{>a}}(\mathscr D_{>a}^{-1}(\widetilde\nabla\mathscr D_{>a})e^{-tQ^+_{>a}})$; the trace is the absolutely convergent sum of diagonal matrix coefficients in an orthonormal eigenbasis, independent of choices within each eigenspace. Require this convergence and the smooth coefficient expansion $h_a(t)=\sum_{j=-d/2}^{-1}b_jt^j+b_0+b_{\log}\log t+o(1)$ as dimensionless $t\downarrow0$. The finite-part convention is $\operatorname{FP}h_a=b_0+\gamma_1b_{\log}$, where $\gamma_1=\int_0^\infty e^{-r}\log r\,dr=\Gamma'(1)$; the equality names the usual gamma-function derivative and fixes the log-term subtraction. The **Bismut–Freed connection** in this convention is the local formula $\nabla^{\mathrm{BF}}=\nabla^a+\operatorname{FP}h_a$, as in Dai–Freed (3.6)–(3.7).

Admissibility further requires that these forms are smooth, intertwine the specified cut transitions, and are compatible with the Quillen norm: $d\|s\|_Q^2=\langle\nabla^{\mathrm{BF}}s,s\rangle_Q+\langle s,\nabla^{\mathrm{BF}}s\rangle_Q$ for every local section $s$. Thus in a unit frame the connection form is purely imaginary. Gauge identifications must intertwine all cut data, preserve this norm and preserve the connection after the corresponding parameter pullback. These are explicit mathematical conditions on the supplied regularization. Cut gluing reduces on a finite band to the determinant derivative $(\det\mathscr D)^{-1}\nabla(\det\mathscr D)=\operatorname{Tr}(\mathscr D^{-1}\widetilde\nabla\mathscr D)$ with the induced finite-dimensional connections; analytic existence, smooth heat expansions and naturality for all geometric families are not asserted here. In particular a Hermitian line alone does not supply this connection. Parallel transport means the solution of $\nabla^{\mathrm{BF}}_{\dot A_t}s(t)=0$ with a specified initial value; in a unit frame with connection $i\beta$, it is multiplication by $\exp(-i\int\beta)$.

When the supplied real or pseudoreal fermion structure instead yields a skew-Fredholm quadratic form, include its actual **Pfaffian data**. Smooth gluing, the square identification, spectral continuations, metric compatibility and gauge naturality are required Pfaffian admissibility data, not an arbitrary choice of a square root or an existence assertion for every real/pseudoreal theory.

declaration.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$. Let $Y$ be a compact oriented smooth spin $(d+1)$-manifold with boundary $M=\partial Y$, using the outward-normal-first boundary orientation. A background $b$ consists of the metric, spin structure, and any specified principal-bundle connections and associated fields on $Y$; its restriction to $M$ is the boundary background. A $d$-dimensional boundary theory is **relative to an invertible bulk theory** when its partition value is a vector $Z_\partial(M,b|_M)$ in a specified one-dimensional Hermitian line $\mathcal L_\partial(M,b|_M)$, and the bulk assigns the dual line $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}}(M,b|_M)\cong\mathcal L_\partial(M,b|_M)^*$ together with a vector $Z_{\mathrm{bulk}}(Y,b)$ in that line. The canonical evaluation

$$\mathrm{ev}:\mathcal L_\partial(M,b|_M)\otimes\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}}(M,b|_M)\longrightarrow\mathbb C$$

then defines the combined scalar amplitude. Invertibility means that the bulk assigns a one-dimensional line to each closed $d$-dimensional boundary background and an isomorphism to each bordism map; orientation reversal replaces the assigned line by its dual. For a loop $\gamma$ of compatible background fields and endpoint gauge identifications, the boundary/bulk pair cancels that anomaly along $\gamma$ exactly when

$$\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(\mathcal L_\partial)\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}})=1.$$

The diagram records this condition: the vertical maps are the line evaluation at the two endpoints, and the top map is parallel transport on both lines.

~~~tikzcd
\mathcal L_{\partial,0}\otimes\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk},0}
  \arrow[r,"\mathrm{PT}^{\partial}_{\gamma}\otimes\mathrm{PT}^{\mathrm{bulk}}_{\gamma}"]
  \arrow[d,"\mathrm{ev}_0"'] &
\mathcal L_{\partial,1}\otimes\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk},1}
  \arrow[d,"\mathrm{ev}_1"] \\
\mathbb C \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb C}"'] & \mathbb C
~~~

declaration.statement: Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Let $M=S^4$ with its boundary orientation, a specified smooth Riemannian metric and standard spin structure, and let $E\to M$ be a smooth rank-two Hermitian bundle with structure group $SU(2)$ and smooth unitary connection $A$. Treat $SU(2)$ as a nondynamical background global symmetry and consider one massless left-handed Weyl fermion in the fundamental representation. Use the inverse determinant/Pfaffian line and the index-density normalization $I_6=[\widehat A(TM)\operatorname{ch}(E)]_6$ for its universal local anomaly polynomial, with $F_A$ anti-Hermitian and $\operatorname{ch}(E)=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf 2}\exp(-F_A/(2\pi i))$. Assume the selected background is in the index-one sector, meaning the coupled chiral Dirac operator $D_A^+$ is Fredholm and $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}D_A^+=1$. For a proved concrete instance, assume full AC and take the unit round metric, $E=S^+$ and the positive-spin Levi-Civita connection: its complex chiral kernel has dimension $1$, its cokernel dimension $0$, and $\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=-1$ in the convention $c(E)=\det(I-F_A/(2\pi i))$. The conditional conclusion below still applies to every stipulated index-one background; this concrete instance supplies that index by proof rather than as a physical postulate. Let $z=-I\in SU(2)$ act on the fermion fibers and form the corresponding order-two loop $\gamma_z$ of the background/gauge-field groupoid. Since $z$ acts as $-1$ in the fundamental representation, its action on this fermion is the same twist as $(-1)^F$; use the fermion-parity mapping-torus convention represented by $Y_z=S^4\times S^1$ with pulled-back gauge connection and periodic spinors around $S^1$. Equivalently, a central $z$ gauge clutch combined with an antiperiodic spin clutch has this periodic total fermion boundary condition. A periodic spin clutch combined with the same $z$ gauge clutch would instead give antiperiodic total fermions; the two conventions must not be conflated in an eta-holonomy formula. For $N\ge1$ independent identical Weyl doublets, the local polynomial vanishes and the boundary holonomy on this loop is $(-1)^N$. Adopt, for this test, a five-dimensional invertible bulk response with phase $Z_{\mathrm{bulk}}(Y_z,A)=(-1)^{N\operatorname{ind}_2D_{Y_z}}$, where $\operatorname{ind}_2D_{Y_z}=\dim_{\mathbb R}\ker D_{Y_z}\bmod2$ for the real Dirac realization; then the bulk phase is $(-1)^N$ and the combined boundary/bulk holonomy is $+1$. For the finite normalization check take $K$ to be a single-vertex ordered simplicial complex and the ordinary field groupoid $\mathcal F(K)=BC_2$, with one object and automorphism group $C_2=\{1,z\}$. The boundary line alone has no invariant scalar gauging weight when $N$ is odd, while the boundary line tensored with the inverse bulk line has the normalized finite groupoid sum $1/2$. Even $N$ cancels this tested anomaly; this statement does not exclude other global or local anomalies outside the stated model and loop.

declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Fix an integer $d\geq1$, a compact smooth oriented Euclidean $d$-manifold $M$ with no boundary, its tangential structure (including a spin structure when the fields require one), and the model's boundary conditions. Let $\Gamma$ be its chosen finite regulator graph. Fix a compact internal symmetry group $G$ with its actual global form and its action on every retained and integrated field multiplet. The symmetry is global, not a dynamical gauge redundancy. A **background groupoid** $\mathscr B$ is a category in which every arrow is invertible; its objects are the admitted nondynamical $G$-background data and its arrows are exactly the permitted background gauge transformations, including large transformations when the model admits them. The background data, groupoid objects and arrows are part of the model input.

At each positive Wilsonian scale $\mu$ in a fixed interval $0<\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}<\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}$, a regulated model supplies its actual finite-dimensional field configuration space $\Phi_\mu$, Borel measure $\nu_\mu$, dimensionless action $S_\mu(\phi;b)$ for $\phi\in\Phi_\mu$ and $b\in\mathscr B$, and finite nonzero background partition functional

$$
Z_\mu[b]=\int_{\Phi_\mu}e^{-S_\mu(\phi;b)}\,d\nu_\mu(\phi).
$$

All field representations, the regulator, measure normalizations, and background boundary conditions are fixed data. The local effective functional is $W_\mu[b]=-\log Z_\mu[b]$ on each common nonzero background patch; its transition phases on overlaps are retained.

An **exact background-coupled RG comparison** from $\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}$ to $\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}$ consists of exact Wilsonian high-coordinate integrations as in the supplied finite-regulator Wilsonian-action definition, equivariant under every arrow of $\mathscr B$, with all surviving low-energy fields and topological sectors included at the infrared endpoint. It also specifies one single-valued, admissible, dimensionless local background counterterm $C[b]$ for which

$$
W_{\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}}[b]-W_{\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}}[b]=C[b]
$$

in each common local branch and compatibly on overlaps. Here local means an integral or finite-regulator sum of densities depending on background data and finitely many derivatives or neighboring cochains; the allowed counterterm space is fixed as part of the model. This definition records a finite-regulator flow interface and its locality hypothesis. It does not assert that such a flow exists for an arbitrary continuum QFT or that any continuum limit exists.

Different boundaries realizing an equivalent abstract symmetry category are not silently identified.

Consider marked diagrams $\mathcal N\xrightarrow{I}\mathcal C\xrightarrow{P}\mathcal S$ of finite semisimple monoidal 2-categories and linear monoidal 2-functors, together with chosen symmetry boundaries $B_{\mathcal N},B_{\mathcal S}$, gapped interfaces $\mathcal I_I,\mathcal I_P$ between their SymTFTs, and specified identifications of each transported source symmetry boundary with the corresponding target symmetry boundary (the source's Matching Equation). The marking includes the object, junction and point-junction transport, their composition and tensor coherences, and all endpoint spaces and composition maps of bulk defects on the boundaries and interfaces. An endpoint is an allowed boundary or interface junction terminating a bulk topological defect. Two such marked diagrams are equivalent when monoidal 2-equivalences of $\mathcal N$ and $\mathcal S$, the identity of the fixed marked $\mathcal C$, invertible monoidal transformations of the two functors, and equivalences of the interfaces and endpoint data intertwine all these markings and coherences. This is not equality merely of lists of defect labels.

declaration.statement:

$$
C_k[A_1,A_2,A_3]=\frac{ik}{2\pi}\int_{T^4} A_1\wedge A_2\wedge F_3,

$$

and therefore define the same local anomaly class modulo the declared counterterms.

declaration.statement:
Let $\Lambda_a=(a\mathbb Z/Na\mathbb Z)^4$ be the periodic four-dimensional lattice with $N\geq2$ sites in each direction and spacing $a>0$; each coordinate is taken modulo $Na$. $$

A dimensionless nonzero Yukawa parameter $y$ gives the mass term $-y\Phi\bar\psi_+\psi_-+\mathrm{h.c.}$, where h.c. denotes Hermitian conjugation, and heavy mass $M_H=|y|v>0$. The fermion fields have mass dimension $3/2$, $v$ and $M_H$ have mass dimension one, $B_\mu$ has mass dimension one, $G_{\mu\nu}$ has mass dimension two, and $\theta$ is dimensionless.

For $\alpha\in C_c^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$, use $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$, $\psi_+\mapsto e^{-i\alpha}\psi_+$, $\psi_-\mapsto\psi_-$, and $\Phi\mapsto e^{-i\alpha}\Phi$, hence $\theta\mapsto\theta-\alpha$. Adopt the source-derived consistent-anomaly formula for a positive-chirality Weyl field in representation $R$, written in Bilal's Hermitian convention,

$$\delta_{\epsilon}\Gamma_R=-\frac{1}{24\pi^2}\int_M\operatorname{tr}_R\!\left(\epsilon\,d\left(\mathscr A\wedge d\mathscr A-\frac{i}{2}\mathscr A\wedge\mathscr A\wedge\mathscr A\right)\right).$$

Since $R=(\mathbf1,+1)$ is one-dimensional, $\operatorname{tr}_R(1)=1$; since $\mathscr A$ is Abelian, its cubic wedge term vanishes. The heavy-sector local variation is therefore $\mathcal A_H(\alpha,B)=+\frac{1}{24\pi^2}\int_M\alpha G\wedge G$. If $\Gamma_L$ is any specified remaining-light-sector functional with infinitesimal variation $\mathcal A_L$, and the low-energy theory retains $\theta$ and is required to match this perturbative background anomaly, then

$$\Gamma_{\mathrm{WZ}}[B,\theta]=-\frac{1}{24\pi^2}\int_M\theta G\wedge G$$

satisfies $\delta_\alpha\Gamma_{\mathrm{WZ}}=\mathcal A_H$ and hence $\delta_\alpha(\Gamma_L+\Gamma_{\mathrm{WZ}})=\mathcal A_L+\mathcal A_H=\delta_\alpha(\Gamma_L+\Gamma_H)$. Its coefficient has no $M_H^{-1}$ factor. This is a local perturbative anomaly-matching statement in the fixed representative; it asserts no global determinant phase, dynamical-gauge consistency, gravitational contribution, non-Abelian generalization, convergence of the EFT expansion, or continuum interacting QFT.

declaration.title: Leading Wilsonian Superpotential Match at a Supersymmetric Chiral Threshold
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; planned item contract; readiness recorded separately.
declaration.statement:
Assume full Axiom of Choice for the selected finite operator-equivalence data. Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and the rigid four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ Wilsonian EFT data in the action definition. Let $\Phi$ be a finite collection of light chiral superfields and let $X$ be one heavy gauge-singlet chiral superfield with canonical physical D-term $[X^\dagger X]_D$. Suppose the derivative-free holomorphic high-energy superpotential is

$$W_+(\Phi,X)=W_L(\Phi)+\frac12 M X^2+XJ(\Phi),$$

where $M>0$ has mass dimension one, $[\Phi_i]=[X]=1$, $W_L$ is a gauge-invariant holomorphic function of mass dimension three, and $J$ is a gauge-singlet holomorphic function of mass dimension two. The model identifies the physical heavy threshold mass with this positive coefficient $M$. Let $\Pi_0$ denote the projection in the supplied formal superspace-derivative expansion onto degree zero in $\partial_\mu,D_\alpha,\bar D_{\dot\alpha}$, with each $D$ and $\bar D$ assigned degree $1/2$; this is a formal truncation and gives no numerical remainder bound. Assume the declared tree-level threshold prescription uses the $\Pi_0$ projection of the full chiral equation obtained by varying the canonical $X^\dagger X$ term and $W_+$, at external energies $E_{\mathrm{ext}}\ll M$, with a fixed finite operator basis and truncation. Then the holomorphic coefficient component of this tree-level Wilsonian threshold map is

$$W_-^{(0)}(\Phi)=W_L(\Phi)-\frac{J(\Phi)^2}{2M}.$$

The Wilsonian scale $\mu_W$, renormalization scale $\mu$, $M$, $E_{\mathrm{ext}}$, regulator cutoff $\Lambda_{\mathrm{reg}}$, and operator-suppression scale $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$ remain distinct inputs; no equality among them is inferred. This result gives the leading derivative-free F-term coordinate only. declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; planned item contract; readiness recorded separately.
declaration.statement:
Take one light gauge-singlet chiral superfield $\Phi$ and one heavy gauge-singlet chiral superfield $X$, with canonical quadratic D-terms, in the rigid flat-space $\mathcal N=1$ convention of the Wilsonian action definition. Let $M>0$ be the heavy threshold mass, let $g,y,\kappa\in\mathbb C$ be dimensionless, and choose

$$W_+(\Phi,X)=\frac12MX^2+\frac g2X\Phi^2+\frac y6\Phi^3.$$

Use the tree-level zero-supercovariant-derivative matching prescription at external energies $E_{\mathrm{ext}}\ll M$. The matched holomorphic Wilsonian superpotential coefficient is

$$W_-(\Phi)=\frac y6\Phi^3-\frac{g^2}{8M}\Phi^4.$$

In the low-energy EFT, choose a fixed nondynamical chiral spurion background $\mathcal X=2\theta^1\theta^2 F_{\mathcal X}$ with $[\mathcal X]=1$ and constant $[F_{\mathcal X}]=2$, and add the single local operator

$$\Delta W=\frac{\kappa}{6\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}}\mathcal X\Phi^3,$$

where $\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}>0$ is an operator-suppression scale distinct from $M$. After fixing this background, the added component term is $\frac{A_{\mathrm{soft}}}{6}\phi^3+\mathrm{h.c.}$ with $A_{\mathrm{soft}}=\kappa F_{\mathcal X}/\Lambda_{\mathrm{op}}$ and mass dimension one. Here a soft scalar trilinear means a scalar cubic interaction with a positive-mass-dimension coefficient. This is an explicit spurion insertion, not an observed value or a consequence of the supersymmetric threshold theorem. No numerical smallness bound on $A_{\mathrm{soft}}$ is asserted; omitting additional spurion insertions requires separate power-counting input.

declaration.title: Profile likelihood ratios with nuisance parameters
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
declaration.statement:
Let $(S,\mathcal S)$ be a measurable data space, let $\nu$ be a measure on it, and let $\Psi$ and $H$ be nonempty parameter sets. For each $(\psi,\eta)\in\Psi\times H$, let $p_{\psi,\eta}:S\to[0,+\infty]$ be a specified measurable density with $\int_S p_{\psi,\eta}\,d\nu=1$. A specified pointwise version of each density is part of the model because an observed-data likelihood can depend on the representative chosen within an almost-everywhere equivalence class. The coordinate $\psi$ is the parameter of interest; $\eta$ is a nuisance coordinate, meaning that it is retained in the probability model but is not the parameter whose value is tested or reported. The common dominating measure $\nu$ and the full density family are part of the model.

For observed data $s\in S$, define the likelihood $L_s(\psi,\eta)=p_{\psi,\eta}(s)$. Take both suprema below in the extended real line and suppose the global supremum
$$M_s:=\sup_{(\psi',\eta')\in\Psi\times H}L_s(\psi',\eta')$$
satisfies $0<M_s<+\infty$. For each $\psi\in\Psi$, define the profile likelihood $M_s(\psi)=\sup_{\eta\in H}L_s(\psi,\eta)$ and the profile likelihood ratio
$$\lambda_s(\psi):=\frac{M_s(\psi)}{M_s}\in[0,1].$$
The associated likelihood-ratio statistic is
$$q_s(\psi):=\begin{cases}-2\log\lambda_s(\psi),&\lambda_s(\psi)>0,\\ +\infty,&\lambda_s(\psi)=0,\end{cases}$$
where $\log$ is the real natural logarithm on $(0,\infty)$. These definitions use suprema and do not require a maximizing parameter value to exist. The distribution of $q_s$, a p-value calibration, and the coverage of a confidence set require additional model and sampling assumptions; none follows from this definition.

declaration.title: Upper-tail p-values under an explicit null calibration
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
declaration.statement:
Let $(S,\mathcal S,\{\mathbb P_\theta\}_{\theta\in\Theta})$ be a statistical model, let $\Theta_0\subseteq\Theta$ be a nonempty null set, and let $T:S\to\mathbb R$ be a statistic whose upper-tail sets are measurable. Fix an explicit calibration probability measure $Q_0$ on $(\mathbb R,\mathcal B(\mathbb R))$ for the statistic under the null procedure. For a simple null $\Theta_0=\{\theta_0\}$, the exact calibration is $Q_0=\mathbb P_{\theta_0}\circ T^{-1}$. For a composite null or an asymptotic analysis, $Q_0$ is supplied by the specified calibration procedure, whose nuisance-parameter treatment and approximation assumptions are part of the data.

For an observed datum $s\in S$, with the convention that larger $T$ values are more extreme, the upper-tail p-value is
$$p_0(s):=Q_0\bigl(\{t\in\mathbb R:t\ge T(s)\}\bigr).$$
It is a probability under the stated null calibration for a test statistic at least as extreme as the observed one. It is not a probability assigned to the null hypothesis conditional on the data; no probability distribution on $\Theta$ is supplied by this definition. The definition alone establishes neither type-I error control nor super-uniformity; any such validity claim requires a separate argument for the specified sampling model and calibration. A lower-tail or two-sided procedure must specify its own measurable extremeness set instead of using the displayed upper-tail convention.

declaration.title: CLs ratio for source-specified signal exclusions
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
declaration.statement:
Let $(S,\mathcal S)$ be a data space with two supplied probability laws $\mathbb P_b$ and $\mathbb P_{s+b}$ for the background-only and signal-plus-background hypotheses. Fix a statistic $T:S\to\mathbb R$ for which larger values are more incompatible with the signal-plus-background hypothesis and for which every upper-tail set is measurable. For observed datum $x\in S$, set $R_x:=\{y\in S:T(y)\ge T(x)\}$ and define
$$\mathrm{CL}_b(x):=\mathbb P_b(R_x),\qquad \mathrm{CL}_{s+b}(x):=\mathbb P_{s+b}(R_x).$$
When $\mathrm{CL}_b(x)>0$, the modified-frequentist exclusion ratio is
$$\mathrm{CL}_s(x):=\frac{\mathrm{CL}_{s+b}(x)}{\mathrm{CL}_b(x)}.$$
A reported exclusion rule at threshold $\alpha\in(0,1)$ excludes a specified signal-plus-background hypothesis when its supplied analysis has $\mathrm{CL}_s(x)<\alpha$. The likelihood ratio, test statistic, nuisance treatment, and sampling laws are part of the specified analysis. The ratio is not itself a probability or a frequentist coverage level; in the cited method it is a conservative, frequentist-motivated approximation used to present exclusion results. It does not give the probability that a signal model is true or false.

declaration.title: Complex structure on an associated bundle by realification
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
declaration.statement:
Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional real Lie group, let $\pi:P\to M$ be a smooth
right principal $H$-bundle, let $W$ be a finite-dimensional complex vector
space, and let $\rho:H\to\mathrm{GL}_{\mathbb C}(W)$ be a smooth complex
representation. Regard $W$ as the underlying real vector space $W_{\mathbb R}$
and $\rho$ as the real representation $\rho_{\mathbb R}$. The associated
quotient $P\times_{H,\rho_{\mathbb R}}W_{\mathbb R}$ has the smooth real
vector-bundle structure supplied by the associated-vector-bundle theorem. The
map $J[p,w]=[p,iw]$ is well-defined and smooth and satisfies $J^2=-\mathrm{id}$.
It therefore gives this real bundle a complex vector-bundle structure of rank
$\dim_{\mathbb C}W$, with transition maps $\rho(g_{ji})$ in any local principal
trivializations $s_i=s_jg_{ji}$. This assertion specifies the complex structure
induced by $J$ and makes no uniqueness claim about other possible complex
structures on the same real bundle.

declaration.title: Rigid supersymmetric background and localization data
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Let $M$ be a nonempty Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold without boundary, let $g$ be a smooth positive-definite metric on $TM$, and choose an orientation $o$. Coordinates $x^\mu$ have units of length, the metric components in length coordinates are dimensionless, and the scalar curvature has units of inverse length squared. A concrete background may instead have a boundary, but then its boundary conditions and the vanishing or treatment of every boundary term are additional data.

Write $SO(4)=\{R\in M_4(\mathbb R):R^{\mathsf T}R=I,\ \det R=1\}$. For $x\in M$, an oriented $g$-orthonormal frame is an orientation-preserving linear isometry $e:\mathbb R^4\to T_xM$. The oriented orthonormal frame bundle $F_g^+(M)$ is the set of these frames, with projection to $M$ and right action $e\cdot R=e\circ R$. Its smooth principal $SO(4)$-bundle structure is part of the supplied geometry. A Euclidean spin structure is a smooth right principal $\operatorname{Spin}(4)$-bundle $\widetilde F\to M$ and a smooth equivariant map $\lambda:\widetilde F\to F_g^+(M)$ whose restriction to every fibre is a two-sheeted cover. Use $\operatorname{Spin}(4)=SU(2)_+\times SU(2)_-$, where $SU(2)=\left\{\begin{pmatrix}z&w\\-\bar w&\bar z\end{pmatrix}:z,w\in\mathbb C,\ |z|^2+|w|^2=1\right\}$ and the two factors act by their defining matrix representations on $\mathbb C^2$. Identify each factor with the unit quaternions by $\begin{pmatrix}z&w\\-\bar w&\bar z\end{pmatrix}\leftrightarrow z+w\mathbf j$, with $\mathbf j^2=-1$ and $\mathbf j z=\bar z\mathbf j$; write $\mathbb H=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{1,i,\mathbf j,i\mathbf j\}\cong\mathbb R^4$. The fixed standard double-covering homomorphism $\rho:\operatorname{Spin}(4)\to SO(4)$ is $\rho(u_+,u_-)q=u_+qu_-^{-1}$; it is surjective with kernel $\{(1,1),(-1,-1)\}$. The chiral spinor bundles are the associated bundles $S_\pm=\widetilde F\times_{\pi_\pm}\mathbb C^2$, where $\pi_\pm$ are the defining representations of the two $SU(2)$ factors and the quotient convention is $(ps,z)\sim(p,\pi_\pm(s)z)$. Equip each real associated bundle with the complex structure $[p,z]\mapsto[p,iz]$, so $S_\pm$ has complex rank two. A spin connection is a principal connection on $\widetilde F$ projecting to the Levi-Civita connection of $g$; it induces covariant derivatives on $S_\pm$. A spin structure and its connection are supplied data, not conclusions that follow from the metric.

An R-symmetry background consists of a specified finite-dimensional Lie group $K_R$, a smooth right principal $K_R$-bundle $P_R\to M$, a principal connection $A_R$, and a declared smooth representation of $K_R$ on each field bundle. Gauge data consist of a specified compact Lie group $G$, a smooth right principal $G$-bundle $P_G\to M$, its gauge group of smooth bundle automorphisms over $\operatorname{id}_M$, and a principal connection $A$. Matter and auxiliary fields are smooth sections of explicitly declared vector bundles associated to $\widetilde F$, $P_R$, and $P_G$; bosonic and fermionic fields are assigned even and odd parity, respectively. The curvature, global form of $G$, representations, bundle sectors, and reality contours are part of the model data.

A rigid supersymmetric background datum is a fixed Riemannian metric, spin structure and spin connection, R-symmetry background, supergravity auxiliary background fields, and a nonzero smooth spinor section $\epsilon$ in a declared spinor/R-symmetry representation. It also supplies the exact first-order linear system $\mathscr K(\nabla^S,A_R,\mathcal B)(\epsilon)=0$ imposed on $\epsilon$, where $\mathcal B$ denotes the named auxiliary background fields and $\mathscr K$ is the operator obtained by setting the chosen supergravity fermion variation to zero. The equation, its signature, gamma-matrix convention, spinor reality conditions, and boundary conditions must be specified separately for each model; no universal Killing-spinor equation or existence statement is built into this definition. “Rigid” means the metric and supergravity fields are fixed external data and are not integrated over.

An off-shell multiplet is a specified $\mathbb Z_2$-graded collection of bosonic, fermionic, and auxiliary fields together with an odd transformation $Q$ on all of them. An isometry is a diffeomorphism preserving $g$ and $o$; its action on associated bundles must also be supplied. A flavor transformation is the action of a separately named global internal group on the declared field representations. The multiplet closes off shell when $Q^2$ equals an explicitly declared combination of lifted spacetime isometries, gauge transformations, R-symmetry transformations, and flavor transformations on every field, without using Euler–Lagrange equations. A localization package additionally specifies its field configuration space $\mathcal F$, action $S$, gauge group $\mathcal G$, a gauge-fixing slice (a locally transverse condition on gauge orbits), the associated Faddeev–Popov operator and determinant, and a ghost complex (graded ghost, antighost, and multiplier fields with an odd BRST differential). A Faddeev–Popov zero mode is a vector in the kernel of the specified gauge-fixing operator; stabilizer modes are infinitesimal gauge transformations that fix the chosen connection. The package also specifies its integration contour $\mathcal C$, boundary conditions, and either an actual measure or a regulator map from field configurations to regulated spaces $\mathcal F_\Lambda$ with measures $\mu_\Lambda$. If a measure is only written formally as $[D\Phi]$, this notation is not a constructed measure. Applying a $Q$-exact deformation $S_t=S+tQV$ further requires an explicit assumption or proof of $Q$-invariance of the regulated measure and contour, absence or treatment of anomalies, justified differentiation under the integral, and vanishing or controlled boundary terms. This definition supplies no such proof.

For a four-dimensional gauge model in these units, $g_{\mathrm{YM}}$ is dimensionless, $[A_\mu]=[\Phi]=\mathrm{length}^{-1}$, $[F_{\mu\nu}]=\mathrm{length}^{-2}$, and a fermion field has mass dimension $3/2$; the supercharge has mass dimension $1/2$ and its spinor parameter has mass dimension $-1/2$. Every additional mass, radius, equivariant parameter, and suppressed constant must be assigned dimensions in the concrete item. No metric is asserted to admit this data, and finite-dimensional equivariant identities alone do not construct a continuum field-space measure.

declaration.title: Adopted rigid N=4 Yang–Mills localization background on the round four-sphere
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
declaration.statement:
Adopt the following Euclidean source model in the conventions stated here. Let $r>0$ have units of length and let
$$S^4_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^5:\sum_{j=1}^5 y_j^2=r^2\}$$
have its round metric, standard orientation, and scalar curvature $12/r^2$. In stereographic coordinates $x^\mu$ of length, $\mu=1,\dots,4$, the metric is
$$ds^2=\frac{\sum_{\mu=1}^4(dx^\mu)^2}{(1+x^2/(4r^2))^2},\qquad x^2=\sum_{\mu=1}^4(x^\mu)^2.$$
Use the standard spin structure, a trivial $SU(2)_R$ background bundle with zero connection, and the $SU(2)_R$ generator selected below. The global gauge group is $G=SU(2)$, not $SO(3)$; its Lie algebra consists of anti-Hermitian $2\times2$ traceless matrices and has positive invariant form $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$, normalized by $\kappa(-i\sigma_a/2,-i\sigma_b/2)=\delta_{ab}$. Let $\Sigma$ be the declared set of isomorphism classes of smooth right principal $SU(2)$-bundles over $S^4_r$; each $P\in\Sigma$ is a separate gauge sector. The sector set and any sum over it are formal model inputs, not a classification or measure construction.

The matter content is the massless four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ vector multiplet: one gauge connection $A_\mu$, six real adjoint scalar fields $\Phi_A$ with $A\in\{0,5,6,7,8,9\}$, and four adjoint Weyl fermions. Equivalently, its flat-space component content is one $\mathcal N=1$ vector multiplet and three adjoint $\mathcal N=1$ chiral multiplets. Set the topological $\theta$-term to zero in this selected model. Use the ordinary trace $\operatorname{Tr}_2$ in the defining representation of $SU(2)$ and a positive dimensionless coupling $g_{\mathrm{YM}}$. The current N=4 model carrier uses the same global group, $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$, the same dimensionless coupling, and connection-normalized adjoint chiral fields, with one vector and three adjoint chiral multiplets; this is an interface match for flat-space component content and normalization. This postulate separately adopts the source’s curved $S^4$ action, curvature coupling, selected-spinor algebra, gauge fixing, contour, and formal regulator inputs; it does not identify that curved action with the supplier’s flat Minkowski superspace action. For the dimensional-reduction notation, in a local gauge trivialization define the Lie-algebra-valued components $F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu+[A_\mu,A_\nu]$, $F_{\mu A}=D_\mu\Phi_A$, and $F_{AB}=[\Phi_A,\Phi_B]$, extended antisymmetrically to $F_{MN}$. Here $D_\mu X=\nabla_\mu^{\mathrm{LC}}X+[A_\mu,X]$ on adjoint tensor fields, with the supplied spin connection on spinor indices, and $D_A X=[\Phi_A,X]$; in the fermion term $D_\mu\Psi$ includes the spin and gauge connections. These $F_{MN}$ are Lie-algebra-valued matrices, so $\operatorname{Tr}_2$ is taken in the defining representation. Use $\eta_{MN}=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,\dots,1)$ for $M,N=0,\dots,9$. With the seven localization auxiliaries included, the adopted classical action input is
$$S_{\mathrm{off}}=-\frac{1}{g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}\int_{S^4_r}d^4x\,\sqrt g\,\operatorname{Tr}_2\left(\frac12\sum_{M,N}F_{MN}F^{MN}-\Psi\Gamma^M D_M\Psi+\frac{2}{r^2}\sum_A\Phi_A\Phi^A-\sum_{i=1}^7K_iK_i\right).$$
Here $\Psi$ is the adjoint ten-dimensional Majorana–Weyl fermion used to package the four-dimensional fields; after Euclidean continuation it is complex and has no independent conjugate field. The chiral gamma matrices obey $\Gamma_M\widetilde\Gamma_N+\Gamma_N\widetilde\Gamma_M=2\eta_{MN}I_{16}$, with $\widetilde\Gamma_0=-\Gamma_0$ and $\widetilde\Gamma_M=\Gamma_M$ for $M=1,\dots,9$; $\Gamma_{MN}:=\widetilde\Gamma_{[M}\Gamma_{N]}$. The four sphere directions have positive metric. The term with $2/r^2$ is the conformal curvature coupling of the six scalars. The Yang–Mills coupling is dimensionless, $[A_\mu]=[\Phi_A]=\mathrm{length}^{-1}$, $[K_i]=[F_{MN}]=\mathrm{length}^{-2}$, and $[\Psi]=\mathrm{length}^{-3/2}$.

Let $\widehat\epsilon_s=(0_8,1,0_7)^{\mathsf T}$ be the normalized sixteen-component chiral spinor in the source gamma convention, with $\Gamma_{5678}\widehat\epsilon_s=\widehat\epsilon_s$ and $\Gamma_{1234}\widehat\epsilon_s=-\widehat\epsilon_s$, and set $\widehat\epsilon_c=(2r)^{-1}\Gamma_{012}\widehat\epsilon_s$. With $\Omega(x)=1+x^2/(4r^2)$, adopt
$$\epsilon(x)=\Omega(x)^{-1/2}\bigl(\widehat\epsilon_s+x^i\widetilde\Gamma_i\widehat\epsilon_c\bigr),\qquad \widetilde\epsilon(x)=\Omega(x)^{-1/2}\left(\widehat\epsilon_c-\frac{x^i}{4r^2}\Gamma_i\widehat\epsilon_s\right),\quad i=1,\dots,4.$$
They solve the conformal Killing-spinor system
$$\nabla_\mu\epsilon=\widetilde\Gamma_\mu\widetilde\epsilon,\qquad \nabla_\mu\widetilde\epsilon=-\frac{1}{4r^2}\Gamma_\mu\epsilon.$$
The selected spinors obey the source's same-chirality conditions, in particular $\widetilde\epsilon\epsilon=0$, so the dilation term in the supercharge square vanishes. Their bilinear $v^\mu=\epsilon\Gamma^\mu\epsilon$ generates the $U(1)$ isometry rotating the $(x^1,x^2)$ and $(x^3,x^4)$ planes equally. The corresponding internal R-symmetry generator is $R_{AB}=2\widetilde\epsilon\Gamma_{AB}\epsilon$ on scalar fields and its induced spin representation on fermions.

For this single supercharge, introduce seven adjoint auxiliary scalars $K_i$, $i=1,\dots,7$, and seven spinors $\nu_i$ satisfying
$$\epsilon\Gamma_M\nu_i=0,\qquad \frac12(\epsilon\Gamma^N\epsilon)\widetilde\Gamma_{N,\alpha\beta}=\sum_{i=1}^7\nu_{i,\alpha}\nu_{i,\beta}+\epsilon_\alpha\epsilon_\beta,\qquad \nu_i\Gamma_M\nu_j=\delta_{ij}\epsilon\Gamma_M\epsilon.$$
Adopt the off-shell transformations
$$Q_\epsilon A_M=\Psi\Gamma_M\epsilon,\qquad Q_\epsilon\Psi=\frac12\Gamma^{MN}F_{MN}\epsilon+\frac12\Gamma^\mu\Gamma^A\Phi_A\nabla_\mu\epsilon+\sum_iK_i\nu_i,\qquad Q_\epsilon K_i=-\nu_i\Gamma^M D_M\Psi.$$
With $v^M=\epsilon\Gamma^M\epsilon$, their square is the source's off-shell symmetry
$$Q_\epsilon^2=-\mathcal L_v-\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(v^M A_M)-\delta_R-\delta_\Omega,$$
where $\mathcal L_v$ is the lifted Lie derivative along the spacetime part $v^\mu$, $\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(u)$ acts on an adjoint field $X$ by $[u,X]$ and on a connection by $-D_\mu u$, $\delta_R$ is the internal transformation generated by $R_{AB}$, and $\delta_\Omega$ is the dilation with parameter $2\widetilde\epsilon\epsilon=0$. This off-shell closure is for the selected generator; it is not a claim that the full hypermultiplet algebra closes with finitely many auxiliary fields.

In a trivialization chart use the Faddeev–Popov gauge slice $d^*A=0$, where $d^*$ is the metric adjoint of the exterior derivative. In a nontrivial bundle sector $P$, choose a background connection $A_*$ and fluctuations $a=A-A_*$ in $\Omega^1(S^4,\operatorname{ad}P)$; the supplied local slice is $d_{A_*}^*a=0$ and its Faddeev–Popov operator is $d_{A_*}^*D_A$ with stabilizer modes omitted. Introduce odd ghost and antighost fields $c,\widetilde c$, an even multiplier $b$, and the constant zero-mode fields $a_0,\widetilde a_0,b_0,c_0,\widetilde c_0$. In the trivialization chart the Faddeev–Popov operator is $d^*D_{A_{\mathrm{gauge}}}$ with its zero modes omitted; its determinant is denoted $\det'(d^*D_{A_{\mathrm{gauge}}})$. Take dimensionless gauge-fixing parameters $\xi_1,\xi_2>0$ and the BRST gauge-fixing functional
$$\delta\left((\widetilde c,\,i d^*A+\tfrac{\xi_1}{2}b+i b_0)-(c,\,\widetilde a_0-\tfrac{\xi_2}{2}a_0)\right).$$
The brackets are the integrated invariant pairing on adjoint-valued fields, and the prime removes the stabilizer/constant zero modes treated by the displayed auxiliary fields. Let $S^\delta_{\mathrm{gf}}$ denote the BRST variation of this functional. If $\psi$ is the fermionic one-form superpartner of $A$ and $\rho_{\mathrm{gh}}(\omega)$ is the infinitesimal action of the selected circle generator on ghosts, the source's $Q$-closed completion is
$$S^Q_{\mathrm{gf}}=S^\delta_{\mathrm{gf}}-(\widetilde c,d^*\psi+\tfrac{\xi_1}{2}\rho_{\mathrm{gh}}(\omega)\widetilde c)-(\phi,\widetilde a_0-\tfrac{\xi_2}{2}a_0).$$
The gauge-fixed functional integral is the formal expression
$$Z_{\mathrm{formal}}=\sum_{[P]\in\Sigma}\frac{1}{\operatorname{vol}(\mathcal G(P),g_{\mathrm{YM}})} \int_{\mathcal C_P}[D\Phi\,Dc\,D\widetilde c\,Db\,D(\text{zero modes})]\, e^{-S_{\mathrm{off}}[P]-S_{\mathrm{gf}}^Q[P]}.$$
Here $\mathcal G(P)$ is the smooth gauge-automorphism group of $P$, $\mathcal C_P$ is the declared contour in that sector, and $\operatorname{vol}(\mathcal G(P),g_{\mathrm{YM}})$ is the source's formal gauge-group volume with its invariant measure scaled by the gauge coupling; it is not an actual infinite-dimensional Haar measure. In the Euclidean contour, gauge fields and $\Phi_{5},\dots,\Phi_9$ lie in the real Lie algebra, $\Phi_0=i\Phi_0^E$ with $\Phi_0^E$ real, the seven localization auxiliaries satisfy $K_i=iK_i^E$ with $K_i^E$ real, and $a_0=i a_0^E$ with $a_0^E$ real.

Let $\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(u)$ denote the infinitesimal gauge action with parameter $u$, and let $\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)$ denote the lifted infinitesimal circle action. The supersymmetry differential acts by $sX=X'$, $sX'=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(\phi)X+\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)X$, $sc=\phi$, $s\phi=0$, $sa_0=0$, $s\widetilde c=s\widetilde a_0=sb_0=s\widetilde c_0=sc_0=0$, and $sb=\rho_{\mathrm{gh}}(\omega)\widetilde c$. The Faddeev–Popov differential acts on an adjoint-valued tensor field $X$ by $\delta X=-[c,X]$ and on its odd superpartner by $\delta X'=-[c,X']$. On the gauge connection it acts by $\delta A_\mu=D_\mu c=-\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(c)A_\mu$, using the earlier convention $\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(u)A_\mu=-D_\mu u$; the connection's one-form superpartner $\psi$ transforms as $\delta\psi=-[c,\psi]$. The remaining rules are $\delta c=-a_0-\tfrac12[c,c]$, $\delta a_0=0$, $\delta\phi=-[c,\phi]-\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)\phi$, $\delta\widetilde c=b$, $\delta b=[a_0,\widetilde c]$, $\delta\widetilde a_0=\widetilde c_0$, $\delta\widetilde c_0=[a_0,\widetilde a_0]$, $\delta b_0=c_0$, and $\delta c_0=[a_0,b_0]$. Here $X$ ranges over adjoint-valued physical and auxiliary tensor fields other than the connection, $X'$ is its odd superpartner, $c,\widetilde c,c_0,\widetilde c_0$ are odd, and $a_0,\widetilde a_0,b,b_0,\phi$ are even. The total localization differential is $Q=s+\delta$, with $s$ the supersymmetry differential and $\delta$ the Faddeev–Popov differential. These rules give, on adjoint-valued tensor fields and their superpartners,
$$s^2X'=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(\phi)X'+\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)X',\qquad \delta^2X=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(a_0)X,\qquad \{s,\delta\}X=-\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(\phi)X,$$
and the same graded algebra on the connection and its one-form superpartner when the gauge action on the connection is interpreted as $\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(u)A_\mu=-D_\mu u$. On ghosts, $\{s,\delta\}=\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)$ and $s^2=0$; the displayed ghost transformations give $\delta^2=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(a_0)$. Thus $Q^2=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(a_0)+\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)$ on fields and ghosts: a constant gauge transformation plus the $U(1)$ spacetime rotation. These are the finite-dimensional geometric symmetry data of the background; this assertion does not identify the infinite-dimensional field space with a smooth finite-dimensional manifold.

Adopt as a formal regulator the supersymmetry-compatible noncommutative deformation used by the source for gauge-field regularization on $\mathbb R^4$. Its $\Omega$-background is the $U(1)^2$ action rotating the two coordinate planes in $\mathbb R^4\cong\mathbb C^2$, with angular parameters $\varepsilon_1=\varepsilon_2=r^{-1}$, each of mass dimension one. For the four-sphere, assume an extension exists and agrees near the north and south poles with the stated $\mathbb R^4$ regulator. This extension is not explicitly constructed in the source and is an additional unresolved model assumption. The regulated measure, contour, and gauge-fixed action are likewise formal inputs; any use of $S_t=S+tQV$ is conditional on measure and contour invariance, no anomalous Jacobian, justified differentiation under the integral, and no uncontrolled boundary contribution. This postulate is a source-qualified modeling choice, not a proof of a continuum path integral or a result about nature.

declaration.statement: Take the adopted massless $\mathcal N=4$ model on the round $S^4_r$ with its specified conformal Killing spinors, seven auxiliary scalars, and combined gauge-fixed differential $Q=s+\delta$. For every adjoint-valued tensor field $X$ and its odd superpartner $X'$, the source algebra gives $sX=X'$, $sX'=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(\phi)X+\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)X$, $\delta X=-[c,X]$, and $\delta X'=-[c,X']$, with $\delta^2X=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(a_0)X$ and $\{s,\delta\}X=-\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(\phi)X$. For the connection, $sA=\psi$, its superpartner transforms by $s\psi=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(\phi)A+\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)A$, and the Faddeev–Popov rule is $\delta A_\mu=D_\mu c=-\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(c)A_\mu$; the same square and mixed-square identities hold with the gauge action $\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(u)A_\mu=-D_\mu u$. On the ghost fields, $s^2=0$, $\delta^2=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(a_0)$, and $\{s,\delta\}=\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)$. Thus the combined square is $Q^2=\delta_{\mathrm{gauge}}(a_0)+\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)$: a constant gauge transformation and the selected $U(1)$ isometry. The $U(1)$ factor acts smoothly on the finite-dimensional base $S^4_r$; its ordinary Cartan complex is the invariant polynomial-valued differential-form complex for that circle action. This finite Cartan complex concerns forms on $S^4_r$, not the infinite-dimensional field configuration space. The measure and noncommutative regulator extension remain formal assumptions of the adopted model.

declaration.physical_scope: A definition of gauge-fixed fluctuation and finite-regulator data for Euclidean rigid supersymmetry. It asserts no arbitrary-background existence, ellipticity, determinant evaluation, finite-dimensional regulator existence, continuum measure, regulator-removal theorem, or empirical conclusion.
declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Let $M$ be a compact oriented smooth four-manifold with a Riemannian metric and with the spin, gauge, matter, auxiliary, and R-symmetry bundles supplied as part of a rigid-background package. For each declared field species $a$, let $E_a\to M$ be its specified vector bundle. Put $E^{\bar 0}=\bigoplus_{a\ {\rm bosonic}}E_a$ for bosonic and auxiliary fields and $E^{\bar 1}=\bigoplus_{a\ {\rm fermionic\ or\ ghost}}E_a$ for fermion and ghost fields. The grading is parity modulo two. Write $\Gamma^\infty(M,E)$ for the space of smooth sections of a bundle $E\to M$. The space of smooth field configurations is a specified subset of $\Gamma^\infty(M,E^{\bar 0}\oplus E^{\bar 1})$ satisfying the declared reality, contour, gauge, and boundary conditions; the smooth sections are the common classical domain unless a different domain is stated.

A gauge-fixed supersymmetry fluctuation datum at a smooth $Q$-fixed configuration $\Phi_*$, meaning a configuration with $Q\Phi_*=0$ after the declared gauge fixing, consists of the field bundles, the declared gauge-fixing condition, its Faddeev–Popov operator, the ghost and auxiliary fields, and the odd gauge-fixed transformation $Q$ on every field. Here $Q$ is the sum of the selected off-shell supersymmetry transformation and the specified gauge-fixing or BRST differential. Its square $H=Q^2$ is part of the data and must be given on every field; it may be a nonzero combination of gauge, spacetime, R-symmetry, and flavor transformations. For the round-sphere model used in this page, the total gauge-fixed convention is $Q=s+\delta$ and $H=\delta_{\rm gauge}(a_0)+\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)$ on fields and ghosts, with $\delta_{\rm gauge}(u)A_\mu=-D_\mu u$ on the connection and $\delta_{\rm gauge}(u)X=[u,X]$ on adjoint tensors. Thus $Q$ is not called nilpotent unless $H$ acts as zero on the specified sector.

The linearized fluctuation operator is the derivative $\mathcal D_{\Phi_*}=(dQ)_{\Phi_*}$ acting on tangent fluctuations, which are sections of $E^{\bar 0}\oplus E^{\bar 1}$ obeying the linearized gauge and boundary conditions. If $Q$ is a finite-order differential transformation, $\mathcal D_{\Phi_*}$ is a matrix of finite-order differential operators. The relation $Q^2=H$ implies $\mathcal D_{\Phi_*}^2=(dH)_{\Phi_*}$ at a $Q$-fixed configuration; it is a cochain differential on the subspace on which this linearized symmetry acts as zero. For operator domains on a compact manifold, one may choose Sobolev completions $W^{k,2}(M,E_a)$ defined by requiring all weak covariant derivatives through order $k$ to be square-integrable with respect to the chosen metric and bundle metric. An operator of order $m$ then has the stated domain $W^{k,2}$ and codomain $W^{k-m,2}$ for a declared integer $k\ge m$; the bundle metrics, connections, boundary conditions, and closed-operator realization are additional data.

For a differential operator $D$ of order $m$, its principal symbol $\sigma_m(D)(x,\xi)$ is the homogeneous degree-$m$ part obtained in local coordinates by replacing each highest-order derivative $\partial_\mu$ by $i\xi_\mu$. A differential sequence is elliptic when its symbol sequence is exact for every nonzero cotangent vector $\xi$. For a specified smooth compact-group action on $M$, it is transversely elliptic when the symbol sequence is exact for every nonzero cotangent vector that annihilates the tangent space to the action orbit. Any claim of either property must identify the operators, symbols, domains, and symmetry directions; this definition asserts neither. A zero mode of $D$ is a vector in its specified domain that lies in $\ker D$. A Faddeev–Popov zero mode is a vector in the kernel of the specified Faddeev–Popov operator, and an infinitesimal gauge stabilizer is a gauge transformation that fixes the background connection. A one-loop determinant is a regularized determinant or ratio of determinants of specified fluctuation operators with their domains, spectra, phases, and zero-mode conventions fixed. A primed determinant omits only the stated kernel; the omitted modes require separate treatment. No determinant follows from the symbol or from a formal supercharge algebra alone.

A finite-dimensional regulator is extra data, not a consequence of the continuum fluctuation datum. It consists of a finite-dimensional oriented smooth field-parameter manifold $\mathfrak F_\rho$, a smooth positive volume form, an integration cycle and boundary conditions, a graded algebra identified with $\Omega^\bullet(\mathfrak F_\rho;\mathbb C)$, a graded integral of its top-degree part, and an odd derivation $Q_\rho$ induced by the declared field transformation. Its square is the induced symmetry $H_\rho$. In this page the finite-dimensional integration and deformation data use the exact conventions of the finite-dimensional Q-exact localization definition: $Q_\rho$-invariance means the integral of $Q_\rho F$ vanishes on the admissible integrands, including the zero-boundary-flux condition. This data does not identify the formal noncommutative S4 regulator with a finite-dimensional regulator, and it does not construct an infinite-dimensional field-space measure.
