declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and fix one bundle sector of the adopted massless $\mathcal N=4$ $SU(2)$ Yang–Mills model on the round Euclidean four-sphere $S^4_r$, with $r>0$ a length. The adopted background fixes the action, contour, field content, and total gauge-fixed odd transformation $Q=s+\delta$; on its fields and ghosts the square is $Q^2=\delta_{\rm gauge}(a_0)+\delta_{U(1)}(\omega)$, where the first term is the declared infinitesimal gauge transformation and the second is the selected circle action. This is a physical model assumption, not a deduction that the formal continuum functional integral exists.

For a fixed regulator label $\rho$, assume that a finite-dimensional regulator of this model is supplied by an oriented smooth field-parameter manifold $\mathfrak F_\rho$ of finite dimension $n$, a smooth positive volume form $\mu_\rho$, and integration over the whole cycle $\mathfrak F_\rho$. Let $\mathcal A_\rho=\Omega^\bullet(\mathfrak F_\rho;\mathbb C)$, let $I_\rho(F)=\int_{\mathfrak F_\rho}F_{[n]}$ be the integral of the degree-$n$ part, and let $Q_\rho$ be the induced smooth odd derivation. The regulator must preserve the stated total $Q$ action and its square; no regulator existence or regulator-preservation claim is assumed. Let $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval of dimensionless deformation parameters. Let $S_\rho,O_\rho\in\mathcal A_\rho$ be even, let $V_\rho\in\mathcal A_\rho$ be odd, and define $E_{\rho,t}=e^{-S_\rho-tQ_\rho V_\rho}$. In units with $\hbar=1$, assume the regulated action $S_\rho$ and deformation $tQ_\rho V_\rho$ are dimensionless. Assume $Q_\rho S_\rho=Q_\rho O_\rho=0$ and $(Q_\rho^2V_\rho)E_{\rho,t}=0$ for every $t\in J$. Assume the regulated measure and cycle are Q-invariant on the admissible integrands, in the exact sense that $I_\rho(Q_\rho(O_\rho V_\rho E_{\rho,t}))=0$ for every $t\in J$, with no anomaly or boundary contribution. Write $(O_\rho E_{\rho,t})_{[n]}=f_{\rho,t}\mu_\rho$ and assume $f_{\rho,t}$ is integrable for each $t$, has a measurable parameter derivative almost everywhere, and for every compact $K\subset J$ one $g_K\in L^1(\mathfrak F_\rho,\mu_\rho)$ bounds both $|f_{\rho,t}|$ and $|\partial_t f_{\rho,t}|$ for every $t\in K$ outside one null set. Then

$$Z_\rho(t):=I_\rho(O_\rho E_{\rho,t})$$

is constant on $J$, and for every $t\in J$,

$$Z_\rho'(t)=-I_\rho(O_\rho(Q_\rho V_\rho)E_{\rho,t})=-I_\rho(Q_\rho(O_\rho V_\rho E_{\rho,t}))=0.$$

The conclusion applies only to this fixed finite-dimensional regulator and fixed bundle sector at finite $t$. The adopted S4 postulate does not construct the finite-dimensional data above, and this result supplies no infinite-dimensional continuum identity, $t\to\infty$ localization limit, or regulator-removal theorem.

declaration.title: Adopted ABJM localization model on the round three-sphere
declaration.design_state: A-page adopted source-specific ABJM N=2 model on round S3, with exact global form, levels, field content, R-charges, zero deformations, contour, gauge fixing, and formal measure limit.
declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Fix $r>0$ with units of length and the round oriented sphere
$$
\mathbb S^3_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^4:\textstyle\sum_{\alpha=1}^4 y_\alpha^2=r^2\}
$$
with its induced Riemannian metric, no boundary, and its unique spin structure. Adopt the source-specific ABJM model on this background, viewed through one chosen three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ subalgebra. Its gauge group is $G=U(N)\times U(N)$ with $N\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}$ and supersymmetric Chern–Simons levels $k$ and $-k$, where $k\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$. The global group includes both central $U(1)$ factors. Write $\operatorname{tr}_N$ for the trace in the defining representation of either factor; in the Kapustin–Willett–Yaakov convention the level multiplies $\operatorname{tr}_N/(4\pi)$ in the supersymmetric Chern–Simons action.

Each $\mathcal N=2$ vector multiplet has a Hermitian matrix-valued connection $A_\mu$ (or $\widehat A_\mu$), a real Hermitian adjoint scalar $\sigma$ (or $\widehat\sigma$), a two-component complex gaugino $\lambda$ (or $\widehat\lambda$), and a real auxiliary scalar $D$ (or $\widehat D$). In an oriented coordinate chart the first factor's source-normalized action is
$$
S_{\mathrm{CS},k}=\frac{k}{4\pi}\int d^3x\,\operatorname{tr}_N\!\left(\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho}\left(A_\mu\partial_\nu A_\rho+\frac{2i}{3}A_\mu A_\nu A_\rho\right)-\lambda^\dagger\lambda+2D\sigma\right);
$$
the second factor uses the same expression with $(A,\lambda,D,\sigma,k)$ replaced by $(\widehat A,\widehat\lambda,\widehat D,\widehat\sigma,-k)$. Here $\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho}$ is the oriented Levi-Civita density.

The matter consists of two chiral multiplets $A_a$, $a=1,2$, in $(\mathbf N,\overline{\mathbf N})$ and two $B_{\dot a}$, $\dot a=1,2$, in $(\overline{\mathbf N},\mathbf N)$. A chiral multiplet means a complex scalar, a two-component complex spinor, and a complex auxiliary scalar in its stated representation. For $A_a$, for example, a gauge transformation $(U,\widehat U)\in G$ acts by $A_a\mapsto U A_a\widehat U^{-1}$; the $B_{\dot a}$ action is the reversed one. The covariant derivative on a bifundamental scalar is $D_\mu A_a=\partial_\mu A_a+iA_\mu A_a-iA_a\widehat A_\mu$; spinors also carry the Levi-Civita spin connection. The vector-multiplet fields act in that representation by left multiplication from the first factor minus right multiplication from the second.

The round-sphere component action for one chiral multiplet $(\phi,\psi,F)$ of $R$-charge $\Delta=\tfrac12$, in the representation determined by its bifundamental type, is
$$
S_{\mathrm{chiral}}=\int_{\mathbb S^3_r}d^3x\,\sqrt g\left((D_\mu\phi)^\dagger D^\mu\phi+\frac{3}{4r^2}\phi^\dagger\phi+i\psi^\dagger\gamma^\mu D_\mu\psi+F^\dagger F-\phi^\dagger\sigma^2\phi+\phi^\dagger D\phi-\psi^\dagger\sigma\psi+i\phi^\dagger\lambda^\dagger\psi-i\psi^\dagger\lambda\phi\right).
$$
The representation-valued $\sigma,D,\lambda$ in this expression act by the first-factor action minus the second-factor action. Sum this action over the four chiral multiplets.

The adopted $\mathcal N=2$ superpotential is
$$
W=\frac{2\pi}{k}\epsilon^{ab}\epsilon^{\dot a\dot b}\operatorname{tr}_N(A_aB_{\dot a}A_bB_{\dot b})=\frac{4\pi}{k}\operatorname{tr}_N(A_1B_1A_2B_2-A_1B_2A_2B_1),
$$
where $\epsilon^{12}=1=-\epsilon^{21}$ and all other components vanish. The superpotential is the holomorphic interaction that supplies the chiral auxiliary-field and Yukawa terms. This is the ABJM quartic interaction; the adopted quantum model has the enhanced $\mathcal N=6$ superconformal symmetry, while localization uses only the selected $\mathcal N=2$ subalgebra. The scalar component of each chiral multiplet has $U(1)_R$ charge and superconformal dimension $\Delta=\tfrac12$; its fermion and auxiliary component have charges $\Delta-1$ and $\Delta-2$. Set all real masses and Fayet–Iliopoulos parameters to zero. A real mass here is the constant scalar in a background flavor vector multiplet; a Fayet–Iliopoulos parameter is the coefficient of the auxiliary $D$ field for an abelian vector multiplet. The level $k$ is dimensionless, $r$ has units of length, $[A_\mu]=[\sigma]=[\lambda]=r^{-1}$, $[D]=r^{-2}$, $[\phi]=r^{-1/2}$, $[\psi]=r^{-1}$, and $[F]=r^{-3/2}$.

The smooth field domain consists of pairs of smooth connections and the listed smooth associated matter and auxiliary fields on the trivial $U(N)\times U(N)$ bundles. The smooth gauge group $C^\infty(\mathbb S^3_r,U(N)\times U(N))$ acts by the transformations just specified. The source gauge-fixes this quotient by the covariant Lorenz conditions $\nabla^\mu A_\mu=\nabla^\mu\widehat A_\mu=0$. Its Faddeev–Popov ghosts are anticommuting scalar fields representing the determinant of the derivative of these gauge conditions along gauge orbits. The Euclidean contour takes the vector connections and real scalars on their Hermitian/real slices, pairs each matter scalar with its Hermitian conjugate, and integrates the fermions as independent Grassmann variables. The diagonal Hermitian matrices form the Cartan subalgebras; the residual Weyl group $S_N\times S_N$, with $S_N$ the permutation group on $N$ entries, permutes their eigenvalues. The Cartan eigenvalues lie on real lines.

Choose a normalized conformal Killing spinor $\epsilon$ satisfying $\nabla_\mu\epsilon=\frac{i}{2r}\gamma_\mu\epsilon$ in an orthonormal frame, where $\gamma_\mu$ are Hermitian two-dimensional gamma matrices. Let $Q$ be its off-shell supersymmetry transformation and let $\delta_{\mathrm{FP}}$ be the Faddeev–Popov differential. In the source gauge-fixed complex, $Q_{\mathrm{gf}}=Q+\delta_{\mathrm{FP}}$ is odd and squares to zero on the gauge-fixed fields and ghosts. The source localization calculation adds a dimensionless parameter $t$ times a $Q_{\mathrm{gf}}$-exact Yang–Mills deformation. Its one-loop determinants are zeta-regularized, with $\log\det L=-\zeta_L'(0)$ when the source's spectral hypotheses apply; they are the Gaussian boson/fermion/ghost determinant ratios about the constant-Cartan locus.

The corresponding gauge-fixed functional integral is only the formal expression
$$
Z_{\mathrm{formal}}=\frac{1}{\operatorname{vol}(\mathcal G)}\int_{\mathcal C/\mathcal G}[D\Phi]\,e^{-S_E[\Phi]},
$$
where $\mathcal G=C^\infty(\mathbb S^3_r,U(N)\times U(N))$, $\mathcal C$ is the source Euclidean contour, and $S_E$ is the supersymmetric Chern–Simons, chiral-matter, and superpotential action specified above. The source calculation assumes that its gauge-fixed measure and contour are $Q_{\mathrm{gf}}$-invariant and that the deformation introduces no anomalous Jacobian (a multiplicative change of the formal measure under $Q_{\mathrm{gf}}$) or surface contribution at the boundary of field space. These are adopted formal field-theory inputs: this postulate does not construct an infinite-dimensional measure, prove convergence of the localization limit, or assert a theorem for arbitrary three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ models.

declaration.design_state: B-page source-reported ABJM matrix integral with exact one-loop factors, Weyl measure, level sign, real contour, and formal-source limits.
declaration.statement:
Fix the adopted zero-mass, zero-Fayet–Iliopoulos ABJM model on the round sphere of radius $r>0$, with $N\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}$ and nonzero integer level $k$. Let $s_i,\widehat s_i\in\mathbb R$ be the eigenvalues of the two constant Hermitian Cartan scalars, each of physical dimension $r^{-1}$, and put $\lambda_i=rs_i$ and $\widehat\lambda_i=r\widehat s_i$. declaration.title: Hodge decomposition of two-forms in four dimensions
declaration.design_state: Step 1 ready; current prerequisites, placement, proof contract, and scoped checks recorded.
declaration.statement:
Let $V$ be a four-dimensional real vector space with an orientation and inner product $g$, and let $W$ be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space. Define the Hodge operator $*_g$ on $\Lambda^2V^*$ by $\alpha\wedge *_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,\mathrm{vol}_g$, and extend it $W$-linearly to $\Lambda^2V^*\otimes W$. Give this tensor product the inner product induced by those on $\Lambda^2V^*$ and $W$. Then $*_g^2=I$, $*_g$ is an isometry, and its $+1$ and $-1$ eigenspaces are orthogonal. Every $\Phi\in\Lambda^2V^*\otimes W$ has the unique decomposition

$$
\Phi=\Phi^++\Phi^-,\qquad \Phi^\pm:=\frac{\Phi\pm *_g\Phi}{2},\qquad *_g\Phi^\pm=\pm\Phi^\pm.
$$

If the inner product on $V$ is rescaled to $\widehat g=\lambda^2g$ for any $\lambda>0$, then the Hodge operator on two-forms is unchanged: $*_{\widehat g}=*_g$.

declaration.title: Smooth principal bundle from two-chart gluing data

declaration.statement:
Let $X$ be a Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold covered by open sets $U$ and $V$. Let $G$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable real Lie group, and let $\tau:U\cap V\to G$ be smooth. On the disjoint union $Q=(U\times G)_U\sqcup(V\times G)_V$, impose the equivalence relation generated, for $x\in U\cap V$ and $h\in G$, by

$$ (x,h)_V\sim (x,\tau(x)h)_U. $$

Let $P:=Q/{\sim}$ with the quotient topology, write $[x,h]_U$ and $[x,h]_V$ for its classes, and define $\pi:P\to X$ by $\pi([x,h]_U)=\pi([x,h]_V)=x$. Define the right action by $[x,h]_i\cdot k=[x,hk]_i$ for $k\in G$ and $i\in\{U,V\}$. Then $P$ is a smooth right principal $G$-bundle over $X$. Its local sections $s_U(x)=[x,e]_U$ and $s_V(x)=[x,e]_V$ satisfy $s_V(x)=s_U(x)\tau(x)$ on $U\cap V$.

declaration.title: Trace-normalized instanton number and self-dual sectors
declaration.design_state: Step 1 ready; current prerequisites, placement, proof contract, and scoped checks recorded.
declaration.statement:
Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a nonempty, connected, compact, oriented, finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold without boundary, with a supplied Riemannian metric. Let $G\subseteq U(V,h)$ be a compact non-Abelian matrix Lie group in its specified global form, let $\pi:P\to X$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle in a specified bundle sector (an isomorphism class of smooth principal bundles under isomorphisms over $X$), and let $\omega$ be a supplied smooth principal connection. Let $B:\mathfrak g\times\mathfrak g\to\mathbb R$ be a positive-definite symmetric bilinear form invariant under $\operatorname{Ad}(G)$. For local sections $s_i:U_i\to P$, set $A_i=s_i^*\omega$ and $F_i=dA_i+\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i]$. If $F_i=\sum_a e_a F_i^a$ in a finite basis of $\mathfrak g$, define $B(F_i\wedge F_i):=\sum_{a,b}B(e_a,e_b)F_i^a\wedge F_i^b$; this expression is independent of the basis. Invariance of $B$ makes the local expressions $\beta_B|_{U_i}:=(8\pi^2)^{-1}B(F_i\wedge F_i)$ restrictions of a global four-form $\beta_B$. The **trace-normalized topological charge** is

$$
q_B(P,\omega):=\int_X\beta_B.
$$

The number $q_B(P,\omega)$ is independent of the supplied connection. For a general compact matrix group and invariant $B$, it is a real characteristic number; no integrality is asserted. In the special case $G=SU(2)$ in its defining representation on $\mathbb C^2$, with $h(v,w)=v^*w$ and $B(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_2(XY)$, the associated Hermitian bundle $E=P\times_{SU(2)}\mathbb C^2$ has

$$
q_B(P,\omega)=-\langle c_2(E),[X]\rangle\in\mathbb Z,
$$

where $c_2(E)\in H^4(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the integral second Chern class and $[X]\in H_4(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the orientation fundamental class. This sign is fixed by the library convention $c(E,\nabla)=\det(I-\Omega_\nabla/(2\pi i))$.

The Hodge operator $*_g$ on two-forms is characterized by $\alpha\wedge *_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,d\operatorname{vol}_g$ and acts componentwise on $\mathfrak g$-valued forms. Set $F_i^+=(F_i+*_gF_i)/2$ and $F_i^-=(F_i-*_gF_i)/2$. The self-dual sector consists of connections with $F_i^-=0$, equivalently $F_i=*_gF_i$; the anti-self-dual (ASD) sector consists of connections with $F_i^+=0$, equivalently $F_i=-*_gF_i$. These conditions are independent of the local section.

declaration.design_state: Step 1 ready; current prerequisites, placement, proof contract, and scoped checks recorded.
declaration.statement:
Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a nonempty, connected, compact, oriented, finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth four-manifold without boundary, with Riemannian metric $g_X$. Let $G\subseteq U(V,h)$ be a compact non-Abelian matrix Lie group in its specified global form, let $P\to X$ be a smooth right principal $G$-bundle, and let $\omega$ be a supplied smooth principal connection. Let $B$ be a positive-definite, symmetric, $\operatorname{Ad}(G)$-invariant bilinear form on $\mathfrak g$. For any local section $s_i$, set $A_i=s_i^*\omega$ and $F_i=dA_i+\tfrac12[A_i\wedge A_i]$. Invariance of $B$ makes the local four-forms $\beta_B|_{U_i}=\frac{1}{8\pi^2}B(F_i\wedge F_i)$ and $\gamma_B|_{U_i}=B(F_i\wedge *_{g_X}F_i)$ restrictions of global forms. Define $q_B=\int_X\beta_B$. For a real scalar $g>0$, define the Euclidean Yang–Mills functional by

$$
S_B(P,\omega):=\frac{1}{g^2}\int_X\gamma_B,
$$

where the Hodge operator is characterized by $\alpha\wedge *_{g_X}\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_{g_X}\,d\operatorname{vol}_{g_X}$ and acts componentwise on $\mathfrak g$-valued forms. Then

$$
S_B(P,\omega)\geq \frac{8\pi^2}{g^2}\,|q_B(P,\omega)|.
$$

Equality holds exactly in these cases: if $q_B>0$, then $F_i=*_{g_X}F_i$; if $q_B<0$, then $F_i=-*_{g_X}F_i$; if $q_B=0$, then $F_i=0$. Every self-dual or anti-self-dual supplied connection satisfies the source-free Euclidean Yang–Mills equation $D_{A_i}(*_{g_X}F_i)=0$, where $D_{A_i}\eta=d\eta+[A_i\wedge\eta]$. The statement asserts neither existence nor uniqueness of a connection in any charge sector.

declaration.title: Explicit charge-one BPST connection on the round four-sphere
declaration.design_state: Owner supplier repair: full source-backed mathematical construction promoted to A-page proposition; proof preserved.
declaration.statement:
Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $S^4=\{z\in\mathbb R^5:|z|=1\}$ have its unit round metric $g_X$. Denote by $p_\infty$ the point omitted by the north stereographic chart and by $p_0$ the point with north-chart coordinates $x=0$. Orient $S^4$ so that north-chart coordinates $x=(x^1,x^2,x^3,x^4)$ satisfy $dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\wedge dx^4>0$. Set $r^2=\sum_{\mu=1}^4(x^\mu)^2$. The metric in the north chart is $4(1+r^2)^{-2}\sum_{\mu=1}^4(dx^\mu)^2$. Let $U_N=S^4\setminus\{p_\infty\}$ carry coordinate $x$, and $U_S=S^4\setminus\{p_0\}$ carry coordinate $y=x/r^2$; the metric in the south chart is $4(1+|y|^2)^{-2}\sum_{\mu=1}^4(dy^\mu)^2$.

Define $SU(2)=\{U\in M_2(\mathbb C):U^*U=I,\det U=1\}$. Write $\epsilon_{123}=1$ and let

$$ \sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad T_a=-\frac{i}{2}\sigma_a. $$

The $T_a$ are traceless anti-Hermitian generators. Set $B(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_2(XY)$. Define antisymmetric symbols by $\eta_{aij}=\epsilon_{aij}$, $\eta_{ai4}=\delta_{ai}$, $\bar\eta_{aij}=-\epsilon_{aij}$, and $\bar\eta_{ai4}=\delta_{ai}$ for spatial indices $i,j\in\{1,2,3\}$, where $\delta_{ai}$ is the Kronecker delta; extend them antisymmetrically in the last two indices. For a scale parameter $\rho>0$, define $u(x)=(x^4I-i x^j\sigma_j)/r\in SU(2)$ on $U_N\cap U_S$. Form the quotient of the two trivial right $SU(2)$-bundles by identifying $(x,h)_S\sim(x,u(x)^{-1}h)_N$ for each $x\in U_N\cap U_S$ and $h\in SU(2)$, so its local sections satisfy $s_S=s_Nu^{-1}$. Take the set of admitted bundle sectors to be the singleton containing the isomorphism class of this glued bundle, and take the representation family to be the singleton defining representation on $\mathbb C^2$. Define the local connection potentials by

$$ A_N=\frac{2\eta_{a\mu\nu}x^\nu}{r^2+\rho^2}T_a\,dx^\mu,\qquad A_S=-\frac{2\rho^2\bar\eta_{a\mu\nu}y^\nu}{1+\rho^2|y|^2}T_a\,dy^\mu. $$

On the overlap these obey $A_S=\operatorname{Ad}_u A_N+u\,d(u^{-1})$, so they define a smooth principal connection on the glued bundle. Let $F$ be its global curvature, with chart representatives $F_N$ and $F_S$. In the north chart its curvature, written $F_N=\tfrac12F^N_{\mu\nu}dx^\mu\wedge dx^\nu$, has components

$$ F^N_{\mu\nu}=-\frac{4\rho^2}{(r^2+\rho^2)^2}\eta_{a\mu\nu}T_a. $$

Let $*_{g_X}$ be the Hodge star characterized on two-forms by $\alpha\wedge *_{g_X}\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_{g_X}\,d\operatorname{vol}_X$, acting componentwise on the Lie-algebra coefficients. This curvature is self-dual, meaning $F_N=*_{g_X}F_N$. With $B$ as fixed above, define the charge by $q_B=(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}B(F\wedge F)$ and, for any real $g>0$, define the action by $S_B(g)=g^{-2}\int_{S^4}B(F\wedge *_{g_X}F)$. Then $q_B=1$, $S_B(g)=8\pi^2/g^2<\infty$, and the action saturates the self-dual bound. This is one explicit Belavin–Polyakov–Schwartz–Tyupkin (BPST) charge-one connection; no uniqueness or moduli classification is asserted.

declaration.statement:
Assume full AC. Give the unit sphere $S^4\subset\mathbb R^5$ its boundary orientation, round metric and standard spin structure induced from the Euclidean ball. Let $S=S^+\oplus S^-$ be its complex spinor bundle, with skew-Hermitian Clifford action $c(v)c(w)+c(w)c(v)=-2\langle v,w\rangle$ and positive chirality the $+1$ eigenspace of $\Gamma=-c(e_1)c(e_2)c(e_3)c(e_4)$ in an oriented orthonormal frame. A spin lift here is a principal $\operatorname{Spin}(4)$ bundle double-covering the oriented orthonormal frame bundle; explicitly $\operatorname{Spin}(4)=Sp(1)\times Sp(1)$ covers $SO(4)$ by $(a,b):q\mapsto aqb^{-1}$ on $\mathbb H\cong\mathbb R^4$, where $Sp(1)$ is the unit-quaternion group, identified with $SU(2)$. The connection on spinors is the lift of the Levi-Civita connection. Set $E=S^+$ with its rank-two Hermitian $SU(2)$ connection $A_+$.

The twisted chiral Dirac operator $D^+_{A_+}=\sum_i c(e_i)\nabla_{e_i}:H^1(S^4;S^+\otimes E)\to L^2(S^4;S^-\otimes E)$ is Fredholm, with complex kernel dimension $1$, cokernel dimension $0$ and index $1$. In the anti-Hermitian Chern convention,

$$
\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=\frac1{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}(F_{A_+}\wedge F_{A_+})=-1.
$$

Its positive trace-form instanton charge $q=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int\operatorname{tr}(F\wedge F)$ is $1$; its connection is the scale-one self-dual BPST connection. More precisely there are parallel unitary identifications $F:\Lambda^0_{\mathbb C}\oplus\Lambda^2_{+,\mathbb C}\to S^+\otimes S^+$ and $G:\Lambda^1_{\mathbb C}\to S^-\otimes S^+$ under which

$$
G^{-1}D^+_{A_+}F(f,\omega)=df+\sqrt2\,d^*\omega.
$$

Here $\Lambda^2_+$ is the $+1$ Hodge-star subbundle, $d^*$ is the Riemannian formal adjoint, and all Sobolev spaces and adjoints use the specified bundle metrics. In the complete twisted spinor bundle the full Dirac operator is selfadjoint with domain $H^1$ and its square has domain $H^2$. This is a direct operator calculation for this explicit bundle, not an application of a general index formula.

$$ \sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad T_a=-\frac{i}{2}\sigma_a. $$

The $T_a$ are traceless anti-Hermitian generators. Set $B(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_2(XY)$. Define antisymmetric symbols by $\eta_{aij}=\epsilon_{aij}$, $\eta_{ai4}=\delta_{ai}$, $\bar\eta_{aij}=-\epsilon_{aij}$, and $\bar\eta_{ai4}=\delta_{ai}$ for spatial indices $i,j\in\{1,2,3\}$, where $\delta_{ai}$ is the Kronecker delta; extend them antisymmetrically in the last two indices. For a scale parameter $\rho>0$, define $u(x)=(x^4I-i x^j\sigma_j)/r\in SU(2)$ on $U_N\cap U_S$. Form the quotient of the two trivial right $SU(2)$-bundles by identifying $(x,h)_S\sim(x,u(x)^{-1}h)_N$ for each $x\in U_N\cap U_S$ and $h\in SU(2)$, so its local sections satisfy $s_S=s_Nu^{-1}$. Take the set of admitted bundle sectors to be the singleton containing the isomorphism class of this glued bundle, and take the representation family to be the singleton defining representation on $\mathbb C^2$. Define the local connection potentials by

$$ A_N=\frac{2\eta_{a\mu\nu}x^\nu}{r^2+\rho^2}T_a\,dx^\mu,\qquad A_S=-\frac{2\rho^2\bar\eta_{a\mu\nu}y^\nu}{1+\rho^2|y|^2}T_a\,dy^\mu. $$

On the overlap these obey $A_S=\operatorname{Ad}_u A_N+u\,d(u^{-1})$, so they define a smooth principal connection on the glued bundle. Let $F$ be its global curvature, with chart representatives $F_N$ and $F_S$. In the north chart its curvature, written $F_N=\tfrac12F^N_{\mu\nu}dx^\mu\wedge dx^\nu$, has components

$$ F^N_{\mu\nu}=-\frac{4\rho^2}{(r^2+\rho^2)^2}\eta_{a\mu\nu}T_a. $$

Let $*_{g_X}$ be the Hodge star characterized on two-forms by $\alpha\wedge *_{g_X}\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_{g_X}\,d\operatorname{vol}_X$, acting componentwise on the Lie-algebra coefficients. This curvature is self-dual, meaning $F_N=*_{g_X}F_N$. With $B$ as fixed above, define the charge by $q_B=(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}B(F\wedge F)$ and, for any real $g>0$, define the action by $S_B(g)=g^{-2}\int_{S^4}B(F\wedge *_{g_X}F)$. Then $q_B=1$, $S_B(g)=8\pi^2/g^2<\infty$, and the action saturates the self-dual bound. This is one explicit Belavin–Polyakov–Schwartz–Tyupkin (BPST) charge-one connection; no uniqueness or moduli classification is asserted.

Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. For $r>0$, let

$$S^4_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^5:\sum_{j=1}^5 y_j^2=r^2\}$$

with its standard orientation, round metric, scalar curvature $12/r^2$, and standard spin structure. In stereographic length coordinates $x^\mu$, $\mu=1,\ldots,4$, use

$$ds^2=\frac{\sum_{\mu=1}^4 (dx^\mu)^2}{(1+x^2/(4r^2))^2},\qquad x^2=\sum_{\mu=1}^4(x^\mu)^2.$$

Let $G=U(2)$, with Lie algebra $\mathfrak u(2)=\{X\in M_2(\mathbb C):X^\dagger=-X\}$ and positive invariant form $(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_{\mathbf 2}(XY)$. A gauge sector is a smooth right principal $U(2)$ bundle $P\to S^4_r$ up to smooth bundle isomorphism, with a smooth connection $A$ and curvature $F_A=dA+A\wedge A$ in a local trivialization. Fields in the adjoint representation are sections of the associated adjoint bundle. This postulate does not classify the bundle sectors. 

The microscopic field content is one four-dimensional rigid $\mathcal N=2$ vector multiplet and one adjoint hypermultiplet: the vector multiplet has the connection, one complex adjoint scalar, two adjoint Weyl fermions, and an $SU(2)_R$ auxiliary triplet; the hypermultiplet has two complex adjoint scalars and one adjoint Dirac fermion. There is no other matter. 

The hypermultiplet has real Euclidean mass $m_E$ of mass dimension one, supplied by a background flavor-vector multiplet. 

In the source's orthonormal basis for its four scalar directions, write its mass matrix as $M_{ij}=i m_EJ_{ij}$, where $J$ is the fixed real antisymmetric self-dual complex structure with $J^2=-I$ and source normalization $J_{ij}J^{ij}=4$. This is the $\mathcal N=2^*$ model; $m_E=0$ is its $\mathcal N=4$ limit. 

Adopt the source's Euclidean curvature-coupled action and Scherk–Schwarz mass deformation, with gauge kinetic normalization

$$S_{\mathrm{YM}}=\frac{1}{2g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2} \int_{S^4_r}d^4x\sqrt g\,(F_{\mu\nu},F^{\mu\nu}),$$

where $g_{\mathrm{YM}}>0$ is dimensionless and the trace is in the defining representation. 

The theta angle $\theta$ is real and dimensionless. Set

$$\tau=\frac{4\pi i}{g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}+\frac{\theta}{2\pi},\qquad q=e^{2\pi i\tau}.$$

The rigid background data are a fixed metric, spin structure and connection, trivial $SU(2)_R$ background bundle with zero connection, the mass background, and a nonzero conformal Killing-spinor pair $(\epsilon,\widetilde\epsilon)$ in the source's gamma-matrix convention satisfying

$$\nabla_\mu\epsilon=\widetilde\Gamma_\mu\widetilde\epsilon,\qquad \nabla_\mu\widetilde\epsilon=-\frac{1}{4r^2}\Gamma_\mu\epsilon.$$

The vector $v$ is the round-sphere isometry rotating the two orthogonal coordinate planes with equal angular magnitudes $r^{-1}$, so the pole equivariant parameters are $\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=r^{-1}$. 

Adopt the source's formal gauge-fixing and ghost complex. On its gauge-fixing slice $d^*A=0$, the Faddeev–Popov operator is $d^*\nabla_A$ and the determinant $\det'(d^*\nabla_A)$ omits its zero modes; constant gauge transformations are factored by the gauge-group volume. The BRST-like differential $\delta$ acts by $\delta X=-[c,X]$, $\delta c=-a_0-\tfrac12[c,c]$, $\delta\widetilde c=b$, and $\delta a_0=0$, where $c,\widetilde c$ are the ghost and antighost, $b$ is the multiplier, and $a_0$ is the constant ghost for ghost. The source adds constant variables $\widetilde a_0,b_0,c_0,\widetilde c_0$ to handle the zero-mode sector and uses $Q=s+\delta$; its square is the constant gauge transformation together with the selected $U(1)$ rotation. In the Euclidean contour, gauge and hypermultiplet fields take values in the real Lie algebra; the scalar descending from the time component is continued as $\Phi_0=i\Phi_0^E$, the seven localization auxiliaries as $K_i=iK_i^E$, and $\Phi_0^E,K_i^E$ are real Lie-algebra-valued fields. The positive-FI stable complex ADHM quotient $X_{k,N}^\zeta$ is the geometric quotient by $GL(V)$ of quadruples $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$, satisfying $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$ and the condition that the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$ span $V$ for all words of length $m\geq0$ and $w\in W$. This is the positive stability chamber; it is not, by definition, the zero-FI regular quotient or the moduli space of anti-self-dual connections.

Let $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^\times)^2\times(\mathbb C^\times)^N$ act algebraically, and let $K=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ be its maximal compact subgroup. Thus $\mathbf W=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha^{-1}$ and $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha$. Write $\epsilon_i=c_1^K(t_i)$ and $a_\alpha=c_1^K(e_\alpha)$; each has mass dimension one in units $c=\hbar=1$. Let $q$ be a dimensionless formal charge-counting variable.

Assume the complexification of this action gives each $X_{k,N}^\zeta$ a smooth separated finite-type complex structure of dimension $2kN$, a finite invariant affine atlas, and a finite proper fixed locus $F_{k,N}$. Write $\epsilon_i=c_1^T(t_i)$ and $a_\alpha=c_1^T(e_\alpha)$, and assume these weights are algebraically independent. Let $q$ be dimensionless and formal. For an $N$-tuple of partitions $\vec Y=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_N)$, each $Y_\alpha$ a finite downward-closed subset of $\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^2$, put $|\vec Y|=\sum_\alpha|Y_\alpha|$, $\mathbf V_{\vec Y}=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha\sum_{(i,j)\in Y_\alpha}t_1^it_2^j$, and $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$. Assume the complexified torus acts algebraically on a smooth separated finite-type variety of complex dimension $2kN$, with a finite invariant affine atlas and finite proper fixed locus. Assume the fixed points and tangent characters are exactly those of the positive-FI ADHM theorem. Extend $T$ by a flavor circle acting trivially on the quotient, with additive character $\widetilde m$, and let $\mathcal E_{\widetilde m}=c_{2kN}^{T_m}(TX_{k,N}^\zeta\otimes L_{-1})$ be the top Chern insertion for the inverse flavor line. Assume its localized Borel–Moore pushforward is defined by the proper-fixed-locus construction and satisfies the noncompact localization formula. For the source-reported N=2* convention, set $m=i m_E$ for real Euclidean mass $m_E$ and $\widetilde m=m+(\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2)/2$.

At a fixed point $\vec Y$, the tangent character is
$$\operatorname{ch}_T(T_{\vec Y}X_{k,N}^\zeta)=\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf V_{\vec Y}(t_1+t_2-1-t_1t_2)+\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf W^\vee+t_1t_2\mathbf W\mathbf V_{\vec Y}.$$
For each tangent character $\chi$, write $w_\chi=c_1^T(\chi)$ and let $E_{\vec Y}=\prod_\chi w_\chi$ and $N_{\vec Y}(\widetilde m)=\prod_\chi(w_\chi-\widetilde m)$, with multiplicities. Then the mass-inserted coefficient and formal series are
$$I_{k,N}^{\mathrm{adj}}(\widetilde m)=\sum_{|\vec Y|=k}\frac{N_{\vec Y}(\widetilde m)}{E_{\vec Y}},\qquad Z_{N,\mathrm{adj}}^{\mathrm{loc}}(q;\widetilde m)=\sum_{k\geq0}q^k\sum_{|\vec Y|=k}\frac{N_{\vec Y}(\widetilde m)}{E_{\vec Y}}\in\mathbb Q(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,a_1,\ldots,a_N,\widetilde m)\langle\!\langle q\rangle\!\rangle.$$

declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Use natural units $\hbar=c=1$ on Minkowski spacetime $\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, orientation $dt\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, and spatial orientation $\epsilon_{123}=1$. Fix the global gauge group $SU(2)$, not $SO(3)$, and the trivial right principal $SU(2)$-bundle over each spatial slice. Let

$$T_a=-\frac{i}{2}\sigma_a\quad(a=1,2,3),\qquad \kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY),$$

where $\sigma_a$ are the Pauli matrices and $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ has basis $T_1,T_2,T_3$. Thus $[T_a,T_b]=\epsilon_{abc}T_c$ and $\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$. The positive coupling $g$ is dimensionless. The scalar field is one real adjoint Higgs field: a smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued map $\Phi$ on $\mathbb R^3$, viewed as the real form in the complexified adjoint representation. A gauge connection is a smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued one-form $A=A_i dx^i$. In a local section change $s_j=s_i h_{ij}$, use the right-action convention $A_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{h_{ij}^{-1}}A_i+h_{ij}^{-1}dh_{ij}$ and $\Phi_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{h_{ij}^{-1}}\Phi_i$. Define

$$F_{ij}=\partial_iA_j-\partial_jA_i+[A_i,A_j],\qquad D_i\Phi=\partial_i\Phi+[A_i,\Phi],\qquad B_i=\frac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}.$$

The static Prasad–Sommerfield sector has $\partial_tA_i=\partial_t\Phi=0$, $A_0=0$, no other dynamical fields, and identically zero Higgs potential. Its adopted energy functional is

$$E[A,\Phi]=\frac{1}{2g^2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\sum_{i=1}^3\bigl(\kappa(B_i,B_i)+\kappa(D_i\Phi,D_i\Phi)\bigr)\,d^3x.$$

The field dimensions are $[A_i]=[\Phi]=\mathrm{length}^{-1}$ and $[F_{ij}]=[B_i]=[D_i\Phi]=\mathrm{length}^{-2}$, so $E$ has dimension $\mathrm{length}^{-1}$. A configuration is finite-energy when this integral is finite.

The boundary data fix a number $v>0$ of dimension $\mathrm{length}^{-1}$ and require $|\Phi|_\kappa\to v$ and $n_\infty(\omega):=\lim_{R\to\infty}\Phi(R\omega)/v$ to exist smoothly on the unit sphere $S^2$ of spatial directions. Here $|X|_\kappa^2:=\kappa(X,X)$. The limiting tangential covariant derivative of $n_\infty$ vanishes, and the limiting magnetic field lies in the pointwise stabilizer Lie algebra $\{X\in\mathfrak{su}(2):[X,n_\infty(\omega)]=0\}$. The stabilizer subgroup of $T_3$ is $U(1)=\{\exp(\theta T_3):\theta\in\mathbb R/(4\pi\mathbb Z)\}$. On closed northern and southern hemispheres choose smooth local lifts $u_N,u_S$ with $\operatorname{Ad}_{u_\alpha}T_3=n_\infty$; their equatorial transition is $u_S=u_N h$ with $h(\varphi)=\exp(\theta(\varphi)T_3)$, where $\varphi\in[0,2\pi]$ parametrizes the equator and $\theta:[0,2\pi]\to\mathbb R$ is a smooth lift. The local adapted frames, connection forms, and curvature forms extend smoothly, respectively $C^1$, to open neighborhoods of the closed hemispheres. The surface limit below exists. The admissible external Wilson probes include the fundamental doublet, on which $T_3$ has weights $\pm\tfrac12$; this specifies the electric probe lattice without adding a propagating fundamental matter field. Define the classical magnetic surface charge and its energy normalization by

$$m:=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{S_R^2}\kappa(\Phi,B_i)\,\hat x_i\,dS,\qquad T:=g^{-2}m,$$

where $\hat x=x/|x|$ is the outward unit normal and $dS$ is Euclidean area. The transition increment $\theta(2\pi)-\theta(0)$ is not assumed to be quantized in this definition. These are adopted classical model data; they assert no empirical law, quantum continuum construction, supersymmetry representation, or quantum BPS state.

$$m=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{S_R^2}\kappa(\Phi,B_i)\hat x_i\,dS$$

$$m=4\pi v\nu,\qquad T=\frac{m}{g^2}=\frac{4\pi v}{g^2}\nu.$$

Suppose the energy

$$E=\frac{1}{2g^2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\sum_i\bigl(\kappa(B_i,B_i)+\kappa(D_i\Phi,D_i\Phi)\bigr)\,d^3x$$

is finite and the model's asymptotic reduction and surface limit

$$m=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{S_R^2}\kappa(\Phi,B_i)\hat x_i\,dS$$

exist. Put $T=m/g^2$. Then both identities hold:

$$E=\frac{1}{2g^2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\sum_i\kappa(B_i-D_i\Phi,B_i-D_i\Phi)\,d^3x+T,$$

$$E=\frac{1}{2g^2}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\sum_i\kappa(B_i+D_i\Phi,B_i+D_i\Phi)\,d^3x-T.$$

Consequently $E\ge |T|$. If $T>0$, equality holds exactly when $B_i=D_i\Phi$ for every $i$ and every $x$; if $T<0$, equality holds exactly when $B_i=-D_i\Phi$ everywhere. If $T=0$, equality holds exactly when $B_i=0$ and $D_i\Phi=0$ everywhere. A **pure-point physical index datum** consists of a specified physical model record and its operator data. The model record identifies the spacetime and spatial domain, metric and orientation, global gauge group including its global form, field bundles and representations, adopted action or other postulates, and boundary conditions; it also states whether the Hilbert-space operators are constructed directly or obtained from a named regulator and measure. These are supplied model inputs, not conclusions of this definition. When curved spacetime is used, the record includes fixed Riemannian spin geometry, spin and R-symmetry data, and the model-specific spinor equation as in the earlier background definition; no claim is made that arbitrary geometry admits such data. The operator data include a complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H=\mathcal H^+\oplus\mathcal H^-$ as an orthogonal sum of closed subspaces, and the grading operator $\Gamma$ equal to $+I$ on $\mathcal H^+$ and $-I$ on $\mathcal H^-$. They supply a densely defined self-adjoint operator $\mathcal Q$ with domain invariant under $\Gamma$ and $\mathcal Q\Gamma\psi=-\Gamma\mathcal Q\psi$ on that domain. Set $K=\mathcal Q^2$ on $D(K)=\{\psi\in D(\mathcal Q):\mathcal Q\psi\in D(\mathcal Q)\}$ and require that $K$ is nonnegative and self-adjoint. The grading is dimensionless; if $K$ has energy units, $\mathcal Q$ has energy dimension $1/2$.

Require an orthogonal pure-point decomposition

$$\mathcal H=\mathcal H_0^+\oplus\mathcal H_0^-\oplus\widehat{\bigoplus}_{\lambda\in\Sigma}(\mathcal H_\lambda^+\oplus\mathcal H_\lambda^-),$$

where $\Sigma\subset(0,\infty)$ is a supplied countable set of distinct eigenvalues, $\mathcal H_0^\pm=\ker K\cap\mathcal H^\pm$ are finite-dimensional, and each $\mathcal H_\lambda^\pm=\ker(K-\lambda I)\cap\mathcal H^\pm$ is finite-dimensional and contained in $D(K)$. A compatible orthonormal basis $E=E^+\sqcup E^-$ of these subspaces is supplied as part of the data. For each $\beta>0$, also supply a bounded diagonal operator $T_\beta$ with eigenvalue $1$ on $E\cap\ker K$ and $e^{-\beta\lambda}$ on $E\cap(\mathcal H_\lambda^+\oplus\mathcal H_\lambda^-)$, and require $T_\beta$ to be trace class. The parameter $\beta$ has units of inverse energy when $K$ has energy units; in dimensionless radial-quantization conventions it is dimensionless.

The **Witten index** of this datum is the absolutely convergent graded heat supertrace, defined by the supplied basis rather than by an unproved basis-independence claim,

$$W_E(\beta)=\sum_{e\in E^+}\langle T_\beta e,e\rangle-\sum_{e\in E^-}\langle T_\beta e,e\rangle,\qquad \beta>0,$$

where each heat operator is trace class, meaning compact with summable singular values, and the supplied-basis diagonal sums are absolutely convergent; the sums are taken over finite subsets and then their absolutely convergent limits. This signed supertrace is not a raw state degeneracy. The zero-gap subspace singled out by the selected supercharge is $\ker K=\mathcal H_0^+\oplus\mathcal H_0^-$. Equality of the full heat supertrace with the even-minus-odd dimension of this subspace is a separate conditional theorem under the exact hypotheses. A physical model may call this a **BPS index** only when its own supercharge algebra identifies this kernel with a specified BPS-saturated sector. Here a BPS-saturated state means a domain vector in a specified massive rest fiber satisfying the mass/central-charge equality in the earlier BPS definition. The present definition does not identify every BPS state with $\ker K$ and asserts no such state exists.

The model record names its gauge group and global form, matter representations, action or other adopted postulates, and the Hilbert-space construction or regulator and measure; the spatial sphere has no boundary, and any other boundary or domain conditions are stated as input. The rotation group is $\operatorname{Spin}(4)=SU(2)_1\times SU(2)_2$. Normalize $R$ so that the chosen right-handed Poincare supercharge $Q=\widetilde Q_{\dot -}$ has $R$-charge $+1$ and $J_2$-weight $-\tfrac12$; it has $J_1$-weight zero. Its actual Hilbert adjoint in radial quantization is the conformal supercharge $Q^\dagger=\widetilde S^{\dot -}$. The model supplies a common invariant dense product domain, an even grading $\Gamma=(-1)^F$ with $Q$ and $Q^\dagger$ odd, $Q^2=(Q^\dagger)^2=0$, and the exact positive self-adjoint operator relation

$$\Delta=\frac12\{Q,Q^\dagger\}=E-2J_2-\frac32R\ge0.$$

The protected sector is $\ker\Delta=\ker Q\cap\ker Q^\dagger$, since on the common domain $\langle\Delta\psi,\psi\rangle=\tfrac12(\|Q\psi\|^2+\|Q^\dagger\psi\|^2)$. Define the two dimensionless commuting charges

$$J_+=J_1+J_2+\frac12R,\qquad J_-=J_2-J_1+\frac12R.$$

Also require the odd operator $\mathsf Q=(Q+Q^\dagger)/\sqrt2$ on its stated domain to be self-adjoint and to satisfy $\mathsf Q^2=\Delta$ as a closed-operator equality. Supply a simultaneous pure-point decomposition for $\Delta,J_+,J_-$ and $\Gamma$, with a compatible orthonormal Hilbert basis $E=E^+\sqcup E^-$. More explicitly, the basis vectors have real charge eigenvalues $(\lambda,a,b)$, with $\lambda\ge0$, and span the joint subspaces $\mathcal H_{\lambda,a,b}^\pm$; the distinct joint labels form a supplied countable set. Each closed self-adjoint charge has its maximal diagonal domain: for eigenvalues $d_e$ its domain consists of the coefficient sequences $\psi=\sum_e c_e e$ with $\sum_e|d_e c_e|^2<\infty$. This specifies the joint spectral calculus, not merely formal commutators on test vectors. The total eigenspaces of $\Delta$, including positive ones, may be infinite-dimensional.

For every joint charge projection $P_{\lambda,a,b}$, require reducing-domain commutation with the closed supercharges: $P_{\lambda,a,b}D(T)\subset D(T)$ and $TP_{\lambda,a,b}\psi=P_{\lambda,a,b}T\psi$ for $T=Q,Q^\dagger,\mathsf Q$ and $\psi\in D(T)$. The grading preserves these subspaces and anticommutes with the odd operators on their domains. Thus the given commuting fugacity charges preserve the actual closed supercharge domains and the finite-span joint eigenvector domain; no integrated spectral conclusion is inferred from a common-domain commutator alone.

For positive real fugacities $p,q\in(0,1)$, define $\Xi_{p,q}=p^{J_+}q^{J_-}$ by the supplied joint diagonal calculus, with eigenvalue $p^a q^b$ and its maximal diagonal domain. Define $T_{\beta,p,q}$ first on the finite span of $E$ by $T_{\beta,p,q}e=p^a q^b e^{-\beta\lambda}e$. An admissible pair is one for which this positive diagonal operator extends to a bounded trace-class operator for every dimensionless $\beta>0$; denote that extension by $\Xi_{p,q}e^{-\beta\Delta}$. This notation specifies the closed diagonal product, without assuming that an arbitrary product of unbounded operators is everywhere defined. Its supplied-basis diagonal sum is then absolutely convergent. Every joint charge block is finite-dimensional for an admissible pair: its common eigenvalue $p^a q^b e^{-\beta\lambda}$ is strictly positive, so infinitely many orthonormal vectors of that weight would contradict trace-class summability. Infinitely many joint blocks, an infinite protected kernel, and infinite total multiplicity at fixed $\lambda$ are allowed. The **right-handed four-dimensional N=1 superconformal index** is

$$\mathcal I_R(p,q;\beta)=\sum_{e\in E^+}\langle\Xi_{p,q}e^{-\beta\Delta}e,e\rangle-\sum_{e\in E^-}\langle\Xi_{p,q}e^{-\beta\Delta}e,e\rangle,$$

where $E=E^+\sqcup E^-$ is the supplied joint energy/charge/parity eigenbasis. The positive supercharge gap singles out $\ker\Delta$ as the protected sector, with signed fugacity weight $\Xi_{p,q}$; equality of the full heat supertrace with a trace over that sector is a separate conditional theorem. Other supercharges or central-charge sectors are not silently included. If the weighted trace-class or absolute-convergence condition fails, the expression is only a formal series until a separate regularization and its validity are supplied. No analytic convergence is asserted for all $p,q\in(0,1)$.

declaration.title: Pure SU(2) physical BPS charge and index data
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; exact proof/source contract and readiness disposition are recorded in batch 54 evidence.
declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and the selected pure four-dimensional rigid $\mathcal N=2$ Yang–Mills model with global gauge group $SU(2)$ and no microscopic matter hypermultiplets. Let $U$ be a simply connected regular patch of its source-proposed Seiberg–Witten Coulomb branch on which the local periods $a,a_D:U\to\mathbb C$ are holomorphic and $\operatorname{Im}(\partial a_D/\partial a)>0$. The earlier Coulomb-branch data define the formal charge-label lattice $\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}=\mathbb Z^2$, with labels $\gamma=(n_e,n_m)$ and period pairing $\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW},u}(\gamma)=n_ea(u)+n_ma_D(u)$. The source-proposed model convention fixes the scalar central charge to be $z_u(\gamma)=\sqrt2\,\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{SW},u}(\gamma)$; $a,a_D,z_u$ have mass dimension one, $u$ has mass dimension two, and charge labels and pairings are dimensionless.

For the model-specific physical charge data used here, equip $\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}$ with the integral antisymmetric Dirac pairing

$$\langle(n_e,n_m),(n'_e,n'_m)\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}=2(n_m n'_e-n_e n'_m).$$

In particular the source-designated monopole label $\gamma_m=(0,1)$ and dyon label $\gamma_d=(1,-1)$ satisfy $\langle\gamma_m,\gamma_d\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}=2$, the convention matched by a two-arrow Kronecker quiver with both arrows directed from the dyon vertex to the monopole vertex. The lattice records formal charge labels only: it does not assert that every label is an allowed line operator or a realized particle.

For each $u\in U$, the selected model supplies a stable support $\Gamma^{\mathrm{st}}_u\subseteq\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}\setminus\{0\}$. For each $\gamma\in\Gamma^{\mathrm{st}}_u$, supply a one-particle massive rest-fiber Hilbert sector $\mathcal H^1_{u,\gamma}$ carrying the selected unitary four-dimensional rigid $\mathcal N=2$ super-Poincaré representation at rest momentum $P^\mu=(M_{u,\gamma},0,0,0)$ in metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, with conserved charge $\gamma$, positive scalar rest mass $M_{u,\gamma}$, and scalar central-charge block $Z^{12}=z_u(\gamma)$, $Z^{21}=-z_u(\gamma)$. Supply a nonzero closed Hilbert subspace $\mathcal H^{1,\mathrm{BPS}}_{u,\gamma}\subseteq\mathcal H^1_{u,\gamma}$ invariant under the chosen massive little-group rotations and identified as the selected BPS sector. Its vectors lie in the common supercharge domain, and every nonzero vector is BPS-saturated in the exact sense of the earlier BPS-state definition: $M_{u,\gamma}=|z_u(\gamma)|$, and the two N=2 annihilating supercharge combinations in that definition vanish on them. Stability is supplied model data: this sector is discrete and separated by a positive spectral gap from the multiparticle continuum at the same conserved charge. The sector and gap are inputs, not conclusions here. On this sector let $J_3$ be the self-adjoint generator of rotations about a fixed spatial axis in the restricted unitary representation of the massive little group, normalized so that $2J_3$ has integer spectrum. Require its spectral calculus to define a bounded trace-class operator $B_{u,\gamma}=(-1)^{2J_3}(2J_3)^2$, and supply a Hilbert basis $E_{u,\gamma}$ of $\mathcal H^{1,\mathrm{BPS}}_{u,\gamma}$.

Define the four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ second-helicity supertrace, also called the $B_2$ index here, by

$$\Omega_u(\gamma)=-\frac12\operatorname{tr}_{E_{u,\gamma}}(B_{u,\gamma}),$$

Here $\operatorname{tr}_{E_{u,\gamma}}$ is the absolutely convergent supplied-basis trace of a trace-class operator; basis independence is not needed here. Set $\Omega_u(\gamma)=0$ for $\gamma\notin\Gamma^{\mathrm{st}}_u$. The trace convention uses only $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ through the stated mathematical suppliers, not full Choice. No existence or local constancy of this support is asserted.

For a chosen locally finite set of nonzero charges whose central charges lie, after one fixed rotation by a real phase $\alpha$, in the open upper half-plane, define $\phi_u(\gamma)=\arg(e^{-i\alpha}z_u(\gamma))/\pi\in(0,1)$. For two charges with nonzero central charges, their marginal-stability wall is the locus in $U$ where $z_u(\gamma)/z_u(\delta)\in\mathbb R_{>0}$; a chamber is a connected component of the regular patch after removing the specified wall loci. A formal positive cone $\Gamma_+\subseteq\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}$ used for ordered products contains $0$, is closed under addition, and is pointed ($\Gamma_+\cap(-\Gamma_+)=\{0\}$). It is supplied with an additive degree $\ell:\Gamma_+\to\mathbb N$ that is positive on nonzero charges and has finite sublevel sets, meaning $\{\gamma\in\Gamma_+:\ell(\gamma)\le N\}$ is finite for every $N\in\mathbb N$. The definition is conditional on the existence of the Hilbert sectors, trace data, cone, and degree; it constructs no continuum theory and makes no Hall-index identification.

declaration.title: Conditional physical BPS wall crossing from an exact Hall bridge
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; exact proof/source contract and readiness disposition are recorded in batch 54 evidence.
declaration.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as required by the supplied trace-class BPS-index data. Use the physical charge datum on a regular pure-SU(2) Seiberg–Witten patch and let $u_-$ and $u_+$ be points in two chambers. Write $\Omega_u(\gamma)$ for its second-helicity supertrace and $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}$ for its integral antisymmetric pairing. The finite-field Hall input is a finite acyclic quiver $Q$ over $\mathbb F_q$, where $q>1$ is a prime power, with the subobject-first, total-dimension-completed skew Hall generator from the mathematical supplier. Let

$$\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)=\sum_{i\in Q_0}d_i e_i-\sum_{a:i\to j}d_i e_j,\qquad \langle\mathbf d,\mathbf e\rangle_Q=\chi_Q(\mathbf d,\mathbf e)-\chi_Q(\mathbf e,\mathbf d),\qquad t=\sqrt q>0.$$

Suppose an additive map $\rho:\mathbb Z^{Q_0}\to\Gamma_{\mathrm{SW}}$ and a physical charge cone $\Gamma_+$ are supplied, where $\Gamma_+$ contains $0$, is closed under addition and is pointed, such that $\rho(\mathbb N^{Q_0})\subseteq\Gamma_+$. Supply a positive additive degree $\ell:\Gamma_+\to\mathbb N$ with finite sublevel sets and $\ell(\rho(\mathbf d))=\sum_i d_i$, and assume

$$\langle\rho(\mathbf d),\rho(\mathbf e)\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}=\langle\mathbf d,\mathbf e\rangle_Q.$$

Choose one real phase rotation $\alpha$ such that for both $u\in\{u_-,u_+\}$ the vertex charges $Z_u(\mathbf e_i)=e^{-i\alpha}z_u(\rho(\mathbf e_i))$ lie in the upper half-plane, with the decreasing Hall phase order matching the chosen physical BPS-ray order. Assume the nonzero BPS-index support lies in $\Gamma_+$, is locally finite in the $\ell$-completion, and has $\Omega_u(\gamma)\in\mathbb Z$ on its support.

Let $K_{\mathrm{phys}}$ be a coefficient field containing a fixed $\hbar$ and a field embedding $\sigma:\mathbb Q(t)\to K_{\mathrm{phys}}$ with $\sigma(t)=\hbar$. Define the completed physical charge torus with basis $Y^\gamma$ and multiplication

$$Y^\gamma\star_\hbar Y^\delta=\hbar^{-\langle\delta,\gamma\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}}Y^{\gamma+\delta}.$$

The charge map and coefficient embedding define the degree-continuous torus map $\Phi(x^{\mathbf d})=Y^{\rho(\mathbf d)}$, $\Phi(c x^{\mathbf d})=\sigma(c)Y^{\rho(\mathbf d)}$. On the commutative completed charge series with basis $y^\delta$ for $\delta\in\Gamma_+$, supply a sign refinement $\varepsilon:\Gamma_+\to\{\pm1\}$ with $\varepsilon(0)=1$ and $\varepsilon(\gamma+\delta)=(-1)^{\langle\gamma,\delta\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}}\varepsilon(\gamma)\varepsilon(\delta)$. Define the physical KS factor at supported charge $\gamma$ by

$$\mathcal K_{\gamma,u}(y^\delta)=y^\delta\bigl(1-\varepsilon(\gamma)y^\gamma\bigr)^{\Omega_u(\gamma)\langle\delta,\gamma\rangle_{\mathrm{DSZ}}}.$$

The integer power is interpreted by its formal binomial series in the pointed degree completion. Let $\mathcal S_u$ be the composition of these factors over the stable BPS support in decreasing phase order, with the largest phase leftmost. Finally assume an exact model-specific bridge: there is a continuous group homomorphism $\Theta$ from units of the physical completed quantum torus to continuous automorphisms of the commutative charge series, and for every phase $\phi$ and either chamber it satisfies

$$\Theta\!\left(\Phi(J(S_{Z_u}(\phi)))\right)=\prod_{\substack{\gamma\in\Gamma_+\\\phi_u(\gamma)=\phi}}^{\searrow}\mathcal K_{\gamma,u}.$$

Here $S_{Z_u}(\phi)$ and $J$ are the semistable phase factor and skew integration from the finite-field Hall definition. Then

$$\mathcal S_{u_-}=\mathcal S_{u_+}.$$

This is a conditional transport theorem. The specified per-phase bridge is an additional physical input; neither the finite-field Hall identity nor this theorem asserts that the pure-SU(2) model supplies it, that the resulting index counts exist, or that the model has a continuum quantum-field-theory construction.

declaration.title: Spectral-network, framed BPS, and defect data in a specified class-S model
declaration.design_state: Assigned A-page definition authored from the exact future item contract; its only local item edge is the inspected model-bound defect-insertion definition.
declaration.statement:
Fix an integer $K\ge2$. A **Riemann surface** here is a connected complex one-manifold; assume $\overline C$ compact. A **selected class-S input of type $A_{K-1}$** consists of $\overline C$, a finite marked set $P\subset\overline C$, a collection $D$ of specified puncture defects at $P$, a Coulomb-branch datum $u=(\phi_2,\ldots,\phi_K)$, a selected global form with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{su}(K)$, and a four-dimensional rigid $\mathcal N=2$ model $\mathcal T$ on $M=\mathbb R^4$ with Minkowski metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,+1,+1,+1)$, a chosen orientation, and a chosen time orientation. The model is adopted data: its six-dimensional $\mathcal N=(2,0)$ construction compactifies on $\overline C$ with a specified twist, meaning a chosen background coupling of the six-dimensional internal R-symmetry bundle to the tangent-bundle connection on $\overline C$ for which the compactification is taken to preserve four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ supersymmetry. This definition does not construct a continuum quantum field theory. The selected model also supplies its field bundles, admissible configuration space and field regularity, boundary conditions, observables, normalized correlation functional, and any regulator or measure used; none is deduced here. Put $C=\overline C\setminus P$. The holomorphic cotangent line bundle of $\overline C$ is $K_{\overline C}$. The sections $\phi_r$ of $K_{\overline C}^{\otimes r}$, for $2\le r\le K$, are meromorphic, have poles only in $P$, and have pole orders and residues fixed by $D$. The selected global form and allowed line and surface operators are part of the model data. Thus the coefficients have the units of the corresponding powers of mass when the Seiberg–Witten one-form is assigned mass dimension one. Use $c=\hbar=1$ and retain the model's trace, charge, and central-charge normalizations. A four-dimensional **Bogomolny–Prasad–Sommerfield (BPS) state** is a state in a model-supplied one-particle sector annihilated by a nonzero subset of the model's supercharges; when the selected supersymmetry algebra supplies a massive rest-fiber mass operator $M$ and central charge $Z$, its BPS-saturation condition is $M=|Z|$. No such state or algebraic identification is implied by the geometric data below.

Let $p:T^*\overline C\to\overline C$ be the cotangent-bundle projection and let $\lambda$ be its tautological Liouville one-form. The **spectral curve** $\Sigma_u$ is the compactification of the degree-$K$ curve in $T^*\overline C$ defined by

$$\lambda^K+\sum_{r=2}^{K}p^*\phi_r\,\lambda^{K-r}=0,$$

Write $\pi=p|_{\Sigma_u}:\Sigma_u\to\overline C$ and also use $\lambda$ for the restriction of the tautological one-form. The curve is required to be reduced and to define a finite degree-$K$ branched cover. A **branch point** is a point of $\overline C$ over which at least one point of $\Sigma_u$ has local degree greater than one; the **branch locus** is the set of all such values. Away from the branch locus and $P$, the local roots are one-forms $\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(K)}$. Remove the poles of $\lambda$ and write $\widetilde\Sigma=\Sigma_u\setminus\operatorname{Pol}(\lambda)$. The geometric charge group is the first singular homology $\Gamma_{\rm geom}=H_1(\widetilde\Sigma;\mathbb Z)$, namely closed integral one-cycles modulo boundaries. For a marked subset $A\subseteq\widetilde\Sigma$, relative one-cycles are chains in $\widetilde\Sigma$ whose boundary lies in $A$, modulo boundaries of two-chains in $\widetilde\Sigma$ and one-chains contained in $A$; their classes form $H_1(\widetilde\Sigma,A;\mathbb Z)$.

For distinct sheets $i,j$, a regular **$ij$-trajectory of Wentzel–Kramers–Brillouin (WKB) phase** $\vartheta_{\rm W}\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$ is a $C^1$ immersed path $z:I\to C\setminus\operatorname{Branch}(\pi)$, for an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$, with $\dot z\ne0$ and

$$\operatorname{Im}\!\left(e^{-i\vartheta_{\rm W}}(\lambda^{(i)}-\lambda^{(j)})(\dot z)\right)=0.$$

Orient it so the real part inside this expression is positive. Reversing the orientation exchanges $ij$ with $ji$. A geometric WKB network is generated from the maximal such trajectories issuing from branch points and from the local junction rule: when compatible $ij$- and $jk$-trajectories meet, an $ik$-trajectory may issue from their joint. A simple branch point is one where exactly two sheets ramify and their local difference is proportional to $z^{1/2}$ in a local coordinate; this square-root form gives three outgoing trajectory directions. A physical **spectral network** also includes the model-supplied soliton data on its walls; in the usual class-S construction an $ij$ wall carries a soliton index $\mu$. A geometric trajectory with no supplied nonzero soliton data is not thereby a physical BPS state. The WKB phase $\vartheta_{\rm W}$ is independent data from the phase $\vartheta_{\rm fr}$ of a supersymmetric interface unless the selected model supplies a relation.

A **finite web** is a finite connected metric ribbon graph: each edge has positive finite length and a cyclic order at each vertex; each internal vertex is trivalent and maps to a network joint, and each external univalent vertex maps to a branch point. The metric is part of the declared convention. In the Gaiotto–Moore–Neitzke (GMN) string convention, an $ij$ edge has length $L_{ij}=\int_a^b |(\lambda^{(i)}-\lambda^{(j)})(\dot z(t))|\,dt$ along a regular parameterization $z:[a,b]\to C$, and its physical string mass is $L_{ij}/\pi$. In the geometric cubic-differential convention, a lifted T3 edge has flat length $L_{\rm KT}=\int |\lambda(\dot{\tilde z}(t))|\,dt$ on the canonical cover. For a local K=3 sheet pair with $\lambda^{(i)}-\lambda^{(j)}=(1-\omega)\lambda$, the GMN edge length is $\sqrt3 L_{\rm KT}$; these conventions are not silently identified. The graph's map is isometric in the explicitly selected edge metric, with its sheet-pair labels, to compatible network trajectories. Closed edges are permitted. An open web ending at a surface-defect parameter point is instead a relative web. For a closed web, the chosen sheet-lift rule joins its oriented sheetwise edge lifts into a cycle $\gamma_{\rm geom}\in\Gamma_{\rm geom}$. For an open web on a surface defect $\mathbb S_z$, put $A_z=\pi^{-1}(z)\subset\widetilde\Sigma$; its lifted chain is a class in $H_1(\widetilde\Sigma,A_z;\mathbb Z)$ with boundary $z^{(j)}-z^{(i)}$ for its outgoing $ij$ edge, where $z^{(i)}$ and $z^{(j)}$ are the corresponding preimages of $z$. For an interface path $\wp:z_1\to z_2$, put $A_{12}=\pi^{-1}(\{z_1,z_2\})\subset\widetilde\Sigma$; its framed charge $\bar a$ is a class in $H_1(\widetilde\Sigma,A_{12};\mathbb Z)$ with boundary $z_2^{(j)}-z_1^{(i)}$. These lifts depend on the stated local branch and junction rules. The physical charge group $\Gamma_{\mathcal T}$ is a model-specified quotient of a subgroup $\Gamma_0\le\Gamma_{\rm geom}$, supplied with a surjective quotient map $\rho:\Gamma_0\to\Gamma_{\mathcal T}$; it is not identified with all of $H_1(\widetilde\Sigma;\mathbb Z)$ by notation alone.

For geometric periods use $Z_{\rm geom}(\gamma)=\int_\gamma\lambda$. The physical central charge is a model-supplied function $Z_{\mathcal T}:\Gamma_{\mathcal T}\to\mathbb C$ of mass dimension one. The selected GMN normalization $Z_{\mathcal T}(\rho(\gamma))=\pi^{-1}\int_\gamma\lambda$ for $\gamma\in\Gamma_0$ is available only when $\int_\kappa\lambda=0$ for every $\kappa\in\ker\rho$, so the period formula is independent of the representative of $\rho(\gamma)$. If this descent condition is not supplied, the physical central charge remains a separate model datum and no equality with geometric periods is asserted. A cubic-differential T3 geometry may use $Z_{\rm geom}$; its geometric normalization is not a physical mass normalization.

For a generic point $z\in C$ outside the branch and puncture loci, the selected model may supply a canonical half-BPS surface defect $\mathbb S_z$ in the fundamental representation of the type-$A_{K-1}$ Lie algebra, whose $K$ isolated gapped vacua are labeled by $\pi^{-1}(z)$. It is a codimension-two insertion: model-specified local field, operator, or boundary data are supported on a smooth embedded two-dimensional submanifold of $M$ labeled by $z$; no topological invariance is assumed. In Cartesian coordinates $x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3$ one standard interface arrangement places $\mathbb S_{z_1}$ on $x^2=x^3=0$, $x^1<0$, places $\mathbb S_{z_2}$ on $x^2=x^3=0$, $x^1>0$, and places their interface along $x^1=x^2=x^3=0$. declaration.title: Smooth and Sobolev configuration and reduced gauge spaces
declaration.design_state: Draft authored for Sobolev and Smooth Gauge-Orbit Geometry; full statement, dependencies, and source qualifications are in the item carrier.
declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact, connected, oriented, boundaryless smooth manifold of dimension $d\in\{3,4\}$ with a smooth Riemannian metric, let $N\ge2$, and fix a smooth right principal $SU(N)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$, a smooth connection $A_0$, and a point $p_m\in P$ over $x_m\in M$. Use the standard unitary representation of $SU(N)$ on $\mathbb C^N$ and the invariant positive inner product $\langle X,Y\rangle=-\operatorname{tr}(XY)$ on $\mathfrak{su}(N)$. Define the adjoint vector bundle $\operatorname{ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}\mathfrak{su}(N)$ and the adjoint group bundle $\operatorname{Ad}P=P\times_{\operatorname{Ad}}SU(N)$ with associated-bundle relation $[pg,z]=[p,\operatorname{Ad}_g z]$.

Choose one finite smooth bundle atlas with relatively compact coordinate domains and a subordinate partition of unity. For each integer $k>d/2+1$, let $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$ be the Sobolev completions of smooth sections in the resulting finite-atlas norms. Define the affine configuration space $\mathcal A_k:=A_0+H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ and the set $\mathcal G_{k+1}:=H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ of Sobolev gauge sections. The next lemma proves that the pointwise product and inverse close on this set and make it a Hilbert Lie group. Its based subset is $\mathcal G_{k+1,m}:=\{u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}:u(p_m)=e\}$. Let $Z_N=\{zI_N:z^N=1\}$ be the center of $SU(N)$, viewed as constant gauge sections. Indeed, if $Z=(z_{ij})$ is central and $D=\operatorname{diag}(t_1,\ldots,t_N)\in SU(N)$, then $(t_j-t_i)z_{ij}=0$. For each $i\ne j$ one can choose such a diagonal matrix with $t_i\ne t_j$, so $Z$ is diagonal. Commuting with the determinant-one unitary rotation whose block on the $(i,j)$ coordinates is $\begin{psmallmatrix}\cos t&\sin t\\-\sin t&\cos t\end{psmallmatrix}$ for $t\notin\pi\mathbb Z$ forces the $i$th and $j$th diagonal entries equal. Hence $Z=zI_N$; determinant one gives $z^N=1$, and conversely every such scalar is central. Write $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}$ for the set of $Z_N$-cosets with quotient topology; the next lemma also verifies that the induced pointwise operation makes it a Hilbert Lie group.

Let $\mathcal A_\infty:=A_0+\Omega^1(M,\operatorname{ad}P)$ and let $\mathcal G_\infty$ be the smooth gauge group, with the $C^\infty$ section topology generated by all finite-atlas derivative seminorms. Define $\bar{\mathcal G}_\infty:=\mathcal G_\infty/Z_N$. In a local section of $P$, write a connection as a matrix-valued one-form $A$ and a gauge section as a map $u$ into $SU(N)$; the right gauge action is $A^u:=u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$, equivalently pullback by the gauge automorphism associated with $u$. The calculus lemma proves that this formula defines a smooth action on the Sobolev spaces above. For an adjoint section $\xi$, set $d_A\xi:=d\xi+[A,\xi]$ using the degree-one Lie-algebra-valued-form bracket. In local coordinates and an orthonormal adjoint frame, define the formal adjoint on an adjoint-valued one-form $a$ by $(d_A^*a)=-g^{ij}(\nabla_i^{\mathrm{LC}}a_j+[A_i,a_j])$, where $\nabla^{\mathrm{LC}}$ differentiates the covector index. This is the $L^2$ adjoint for the Riemannian volume and stated fiber metric; its local coefficient formula defines a distribution at Sobolev regularity.

For $A\in\mathcal A_k$, parallel transport of its $C^1$ connection form around piecewise smooth loops based at $p_m$ defines a subgroup $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)\subseteq SU(N)$. Call $A$ irreducible when this subgroup leaves no nonzero proper complex subspace of $\mathbb C^N$ invariant; changing the chosen frame conjugates the subgroup and leaves this condition unchanged. Write $\mathcal A_k^*$ and $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ for the irreducible loci. Once the calculus lemma verifies the group action, define orbit equivalence by $A\sim B$ exactly when $B=A^u$ for some gauge section $u$; all resulting quotients carry the quotient topology, whose open sets are those with open inverse image under the orbit projection.

declaration.title: Gauge stabilizers and properness of the Sobolev action
declaration.design_state: Draft authored for Sobolev and Smooth Gauge-Orbit Geometry; full statement, dependencies, and source qualifications are in the item carrier.
declaration.statement:
Assume the configuration data and integer $k>d/2+1$ from the preceding definition, and let $\mathcal A_k^*$ be the locus where the holonomy representation on $\mathbb C^N$ is irreducible. For any $A\in\mathcal A_k$, evaluation at $p_m$ identifies its stabilizer in $\mathcal G_{k+1}$ with the centralizer of $\operatorname{Hol}_{p_m}(A)$ in $SU(N)$. Thus an irreducible connection has stabilizer exactly $Z_N$, and the induced action of $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}=\mathcal G_{k+1}/Z_N$ on $\mathcal A_k^*$ is free. The subset $\mathcal A_k^*$ is open in $\mathcal A_k$.

The Sobolev action is proper: if $A_j\to A$ and $A_j^{u_j}\to B$ in $H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ for sequences $A_j,A,B\in\mathcal A_k$ and $u_j\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$, then some subsequence $u_{j_\ell}$ converges in $H^{k+1}(\operatorname{Ad}P)$ to $u\in\mathcal G_{k+1}$ and $B=A^u$. Equivalently, the action map $\bar{\mathcal G}_{k+1}\times\mathcal A_k^*\to\mathcal A_k^*\times\mathcal A_k^*$ is proper, meaning inverse images of compact sets are compact.

declaration.design_state: Draft authored for Sobolev and Smooth Gauge-Orbit Geometry — Examples; full statement, dependencies, and source qualifications are in the item carrier.
declaration.statement:
Let $A\in\mathcal A_k^*$ for the configuration data and integer $k>d/2+1$. The differential at $(0,0)$ of the Coulomb-gauge action map

$$\Phi_A:\ker(d_A^*:H^k(T^*M\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)\to H^{k-1}(\operatorname{ad}P))\times H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)\longrightarrow\mathcal A_k,\qquad (a,\xi)\longmapsto(A+a)^{\exp\xi},$$

$$L_A^{-1}v=\bigl(v-d_AG_Ad_A^*v,\ G_Ad_A^*v\bigr),$$

where $G_A=(d_A^*d_A)^{-1}:H^{k-1}(\operatorname{ad}P)\to H^{k+1}(\operatorname{ad}P)$. Thus the connection variation lies in $H^k$, the infinitesimal gauge parameter lies in $H^{k+1}$, and the gauge term $d_A\xi$ loses one derivative. This is a linearized chart statement and asserts no determinant or measure formula.

declaration.design_state: Step 1 argument and contract are complete; current direct and transitive inputs have ready records. This does not claim independent proof approval.
declaration.statement: Assume ZF together with the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be $S^3$ or $S^4$ with its compact, connected, oriented, boundaryless smooth structure and a smooth Riemannian metric. Let $N\ge2$, let $P\to M$ be a smooth principal right $SU(N)$-bundle, choose a smooth reference connection $A_0$, a basepoint $m\in M$, and a frame of the fiber $P_m$. Put $\mathcal A_\infty=A_0+\Omega^1(M;\operatorname{ad}P)$ with its $C^\infty$ section topology. For a smooth connection $A$, let $\operatorname{Hol}_A\subseteq SU(N)$ be the group generated by parallel transports along based piecewise-smooth loops at $m$, expressed in the chosen frame. Call $A$ irreducible when the standard action of $\operatorname{Hol}_A$ on $\mathbb C^N$ has no nonzero proper invariant complex subspace, and write $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ for this locus. For each integer $q>\dim(M)/2+1$, let $\mathcal G_{q+1}$ be the $H^{q+1}$ gauge group of sections of $\operatorname{Ad}P$, acting on $H^q$ connections by the local formula $A^u=u^{-1}Au+u^{-1}du$, and let $Z_N=\{\zeta I_N:\zeta^N=1\}$. Measure $C^1$ closeness by coefficient and first-derivative suprema in a fixed finite bundle atlas. For every $A\in\mathcal A_\infty^*$, a finite tuple of based piecewise-smooth loops has holonomies with no common nonzero proper invariant subspace; the same tuple continues to witness irreducibility on a $C^1$ neighborhood of $A$, so $\mathcal A_\infty^*$ is open in the $C^\infty$ topology. The stabilizer of $A$ in $\mathcal G_{q+1}$ is exactly $Z_N$. Irreducibility here does not assert $\operatorname{Hol}_A=SU(N)$.

declaration.statement: Assume ZF together with the Axiom of Choice. Let $M=S^3$ or $S^4$, let $N\ge2$, take the trivial principal right $SU(N)$-bundle $P=M\times SU(N)$, and use its zero connection as affine origin. For any integer $j\ge1$ and any continuous sphere family $f:S^j\to\mathcal A_\infty^*$ of smooth connections on $P$, the cone formula $F([r,x])=r f(x)$ extends $f$ continuously over $D^{j+1}$ in the full affine connection space. The apex is the zero connection, whose holonomy group is the identity and which preserves every complex line, so this affine filling is reducible and does not lie entirely in $\mathcal A_\infty^*$. Relative avoidance changes the filling while fixing its boundary and produces a filling in $\mathcal A_\infty^*$; contraction of the disk to any chosen boundary point gives a based nullhomotopy. The weak-contractibility theorem ensures that such families exist for the trivial bundle and that their based homotopy classes vanish.

declaration.statement:
Let $P\to S^r$ be a smooth principal $SU(N)$ bundle with $r\in\{3,4\}$, $N\ge2$, a chosen point $m\in S^r$, and a chosen frame $p_m$ in its fiber. Write $\mathcal G(P):=\mathcal G_\infty(P)$ for the smooth gauge group defined by the finite-atlas $C^\infty$ section topology, let $\mathcal G_m(P):=\{u\in\mathcal G_\infty(P):u(p_m)=e\}$, and put $\overline{\mathcal G}(P):=\overline{\mathcal G}_\infty(P)=\mathcal G_\infty(P)/Z_N$, where $Z_N$ is the finite subgroup of constant central gauge sections. Evaluation $ev_m(u)=u(p_m)$ gives a locally trivial bundle
$$\mathcal G_m(P)\longrightarrow\mathcal G(P)\xrightarrow{ev_m}SU(N),$$
and the quotient map $\mathcal G(P)\to\overline{\mathcal G}(P)$ is a finite covering. For a local section $s:U\to\mathcal G(P)$, the bundle chart has the commutative form
$$\begin{array}{ccc}\mathcal G_m(P)\times U&\xrightarrow{\Phi_s}&ev_m^{-1}(U)\\\downarrow{\operatorname{pr}_2}&&\downarrow{ev_m}\\U&\hookrightarrow&SU(N)\end{array}$$
where $\Phi_s(v,g)=v\,s(g)$; the square commutes because $ev_m(v)=e$ and $ev_m(s(g))=g$. The corresponding TikZ source is:
```tikz
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathcal G_m(P)\times U \arrow[r,"\Phi_s"] \arrow[d,"\operatorname{pr}_2"'] & ev_m^{-1}(U) \arrow[d,"ev_m"]\\
U \arrow[r,hook] & SU(N)
\end{tikzcd}
```
The evaluation bundle is numerable; both maps are Serre fibrations and have the homotopy long exact sequence.

declaration.title: ADHM linear data, stability, costability and FI levels
declaration.statement:
Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and standard Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$ and $J:V\to W$. Define the complex and real polynomial expressions

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

declaration.title: Stable ADHM quotient charts, properness and torus lifts
declaration.statement:
Assume AC. Fix $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard bases. Let $X$ be the stable locus in the complex ADHM equation $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$, where $B_i\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, $J:V\to W$, and stability means that the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$ span $V$. The action $g\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ of $GL(V)$ on $X$ is free and proper. Its orbit quotient with quotient topology is a Hausdorff second-countable complex manifold of complex dimension $2kN$, with tangent space $\ker d_1/\operatorname{im}d_0$ for the infinitesimal ADHM deformation maps.

For $k>0$, a word frame $C(x)$ is a matrix whose columns are $k$ fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard framing basis vectors. The opens $U_C=\{x:\det C(x)\ne0\}$ cover $X$; words of length at most $k-1$ suffice. Each slice $S_C=\{x\in U_C:C(x)=I_V\}$ gives quotient coordinates, with $GL(V)\times S_C\to U_C$ a biholomorphism. Slice changes are holomorphic, in fact given by matrix inversion and polynomial operations on their domains. The quotient is also a separated smooth finite-type complex algebraic variety with a finite $T$-invariant affine atlas of these slices, and the map from $X$ is a geometric quotient in the regular-function sense.

Let $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ act by $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$, with $h$ acting on the $\alpha$th standard framing vector by $e_\alpha^{-1}$. This descends to a smooth holomorphic action. At any fixed quotient point represented by $x$, there is a unique $g(t)\in GL(V)$ with $t\cdot x=g(t)\cdot x$. If column $\ell$ of $C(x)$ uses framing color $\alpha_\ell$ and contains $a_\ell,b_\ell$ letters $B_1,B_2$, then

$$g(t)=C(x)\operatorname{diag}(e_{\alpha_\ell}t_1^{a_\ell}t_2^{b_\ell})C(x)^{-1}.$$

Thus the lift is a smooth character representation, without assuming Zariski density or a GIT linearization theorem. For $k=0$ the quotient is a point and these matrices and tangent spaces have their empty-dimensional interpretations. No correspondence with a real moment-map quotient, sheaf moduli or ASD connections is asserted.

declaration.title: Real and complex ADHM quotients at positive and regular zero FI
declaration.statement:
Assume AC. Fix $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, standard Hermitian $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$ and ADHM data $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with the complex equation $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. Stability means that the $B_1,B_2$ words applied to $I(W)$ span $V$; costability means no nonzero common invariant subspace of $V$ lies in $\ker J$; regular means both. Set

$$\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

For every $\zeta>0$, each stable $GL(V)$ orbit meets $\mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta I_V$ in exactly one $U(V)$ orbit, and the inclusion induces a diffeomorphism of smooth real manifolds

$$\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta I_V,\ \mathrm{stable}\}/U(V)\ \cong\ X^s/GL(V).$$

At $\zeta=0$, every stable datum satisfying the real equation is automatically costable. Each regular complex orbit meets the zero real level in exactly one unitary orbit, giving instead

$$\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=0,\ \mathrm{stable}\}/U(V)\ \cong\ X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V).$$

Both identifications are equivariant for the compact rotation/framing torus in the raw-data convention. For $k=0$ all spaces are points. This theorem identifies the stated finite-dimensional quotients; it asserts no correspondence with sheaves or ASD connections, and no identification of the entire positive-FI quotient with the zero-FI regular locus.

It is an exact tensor-compatible equivalence from algebraic coherent sheaves (locally finitely presented $\mathcal O_X$-modules) to holomorphic coherent sheaves.
