declaration.title: The projective-plane Beilinson monad for a framed torsion-free sheaf
declaration.statement:
Assume AC. Let $L_\infty=\{z_0=0\}\subset\mathbb P^2_{\mathbb C}$ and let $\mathcal E$ be an algebraic coherent sheaf (a locally finitely presented module over the structure sheaf) of generic rank $N\ge1$. Torsion-free means that no nonzero stalk element is annihilated by a nonzero local function. Suppose it has a framing, namely an isomorphism $\phi:\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}\xrightarrow{\sim}W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty}$ for $W=\mathbb C^N$, and Hilbert polynomial $\chi(\mathcal E(m))=N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$ for $k\ge0$, where $\chi$ is the alternating sum of coherent-sheaf cohomology dimensions. Then $\mathcal E$ is locally free near $L_\infty$ and

$$H^0(\mathcal E(-1))=H^0(\mathcal E(-2))=H^2(\mathcal E(-1))=H^2(\mathcal E(-2))=0.$$

$$\dim H^1(\mathcal E(-1))=\dim H^1(\mathcal E(-2))=k,\qquad H^0(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)=H^2(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)=0,\qquad \dim H^1(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)=2k+N.$$
The diagonal on $\mathbb P^2\times\mathbb P^2$ has its length-two Koszul resolution from the regular rank-two section described in the proof. Its associated finite Beilinson hypercohomology complex, applied to $\mathcal E(-1)$ and twisted by $\mathcal O(1)$, is a monad

$$H^1(\mathcal E(-2))\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\longrightarrow H^1(\mathcal E\otimes\Omega^1)\otimes\mathcal O\longrightarrow H^1(\mathcal E(-1))\otimes\mathcal O(1)$$

whose only cohomology is $\mathcal E$ in the middle. For an algebraic family over a finite-type complex base, the same construction is a family of monads provided the sheaf is flat over the base, the displayed cohomology groups have the stated constant ranks, and the corresponding cohomology-and-base-change maps are isomorphisms.

declaration.title: Framed P² monads and stable ADHM data
declaration.statement:
Assume AC. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, and let $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ satisfy $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$ and be stable, meaning that the vectors obtained by applying all words in $B_1,B_2$ to $I(W)$ span $V$. Costable means that no nonzero common $B_1,B_2$-invariant subspace lies in $\ker J$, and regular means stable and costable. On $\mathbb P^2$ with coordinates $[z_0:z_1:z_2]$, define

$$\alpha=\begin{pmatrix}z_0B_1-z_1\\z_0B_2-z_2\\z_0J\end{pmatrix}:V\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to(V\oplus V\oplus W)\otimes\mathcal O,\qquad \beta=\begin{pmatrix}-z_0B_2+z_2&z_0B_1-z_1&z_0I\end{pmatrix}:(V\oplus V\oplus W)\otimes\mathcal O\to V\otimes\mathcal O(1).$$

Then $\beta\alpha=z_0^2([B_1,B_2]+IJ)=0$, $\alpha$ is injective as a sheaf map, and $\beta$ is surjective at every point. The three-term complex is a monad, meaning it is exact at its first and last terms; its middle cohomology $\mathcal E=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$ is torsion-free of rank $N$, has Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$, and has a canonical framing $\mathcal E|_{L_\infty}\cong W\otimes\mathcal O_{L_\infty}$. Every framed torsion-free sheaf with this rank, framing and Hilbert polynomial arises uniquely up to simultaneous change of basis in $V$ from this construction. For a finite-type complex scheme $S$, a family of ADHM data is a rank-$k$ vector bundle with endomorphisms and framing maps satisfying the equation and stable on every geometric fiber; its monad cohomology is flat over $S$, and the two constructions are inverse on those families for which the relative cohomology bundles and base-change maps in the preceding Beilinson lemma have the stated ranks and are isomorphisms. A first-order framed deformation means an isomorphism class of such a family over $\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with its special fiber identified; the correspondence induces inverse maps on those deformation spaces and their tangent vector spaces. The sheaf is locally free exactly when the ADHM datum is costable; hence the regular locus is the locally-free sheaf locus. Combined with the real/complex quotient theorem, positive-FI data correspond to all such framed torsion-free sheaves, while the zero-FI real quotient corresponds to the locally-free locus. The framing representation has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a^{-1}$ and the dual framing has character $\sum_{a=1}^N e_a$.

declaration.title: The positive-FI and zero-FI rank-one chambers
declaration.statement: Take $N=k=1$. For every $\zeta>0$, the positive real-FI ADHM quotient is $\mathbb C^2$, with arbitrary scalar coordinates $B_1,B_2$, $J=0$, and $|I|=\sqrt{\zeta}$. The stable zero-real-FI locus is empty. The positive-FI monad is therefore a rank-one framed torsion-free sheaf that is not locally free. On the round oriented $S^4$, let $f$ be the real curvature two-form of a smooth $U(1)$ connection, define anti-self-dual (ASD) by $f=-*f$, and define charge by $q=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}f\wedge f$. The ordinary smooth charge-one $U(1)$ ASD space is empty, so the positive-FI space cannot equal it.

declaration.title: Finite non-Abelian lattice gauge data
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
declaration.statement:
Assume the axiom of countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Fix the compact noncommutative finite-dimensional real Lie group $G$, its Lie algebra $\mathfrak g=T_eG$, and a specified smooth finite-dimensional complex unitary representation $\rho:G\to U(W,h)$ on a Hermitian vector space $(W,h)$ supplied by a non-Abelian gauge datum. Thus the group multiplication and inversion are smooth, $G$ is compact in its manifold topology, and $\rho(g)$ preserves $h$ for every $g\in G$. No connection, principal bundle sector, action functional, or continuum theory is part of the lattice data below.

A **finite oriented lattice two-complex** is a finite set $\mathcal V$ of vertices, a finite set $\mathcal E^+$ containing one chosen orientation of each edge, an endpoint map $s,t:\mathcal E^+\to\mathcal V$, and a finite set $\mathcal F$ of faces. Each face $p\in\mathcal F$ is supplied with a based closed edge word $(e_1,\ldots,e_k)$ in the oriented edges $\mathcal E^+\sqcup\overline{\mathcal E^+}$, where the endpoint of each edge is the starting point of the next and the last endpoint is the first starting point. For the reverse orientation $\bar e$ of $e\in\mathcal E^+$, set $s(\bar e)=t(e)$ and $t(\bar e)=s(e)$.

A **link configuration** is a tuple $U=(U_e)_{e\in\mathcal E^+}\in G^{\mathcal E^+}$, with $U_{\bar e}:=U_e^{-1}$. The **holonomy of a face** $p=(e_1,\ldots,e_k)$ is the ordered product $U_p:=U_{e_1}\cdots U_{e_k}$ in traversal order, with the first traversed edge on the left. The vertex gauge group is $G^{\mathcal V}$ with coordinatewise multiplication; write $\mathbf e=(e)_{v\in\mathcal V}$ for its identity tuple. It acts by

$$
(h\cdot U)_e=h_{s(e)}U_eh_{t(e)}^{-1},\qquad h=(h_v)_{v\in\mathcal V}\in G^{\mathcal V}.
$$

Choose a normalized bi-invariant Borel probability measure $\mu_G$ on $G$. The link measure is the finite product $\mu_G^{\mathcal E^+}$. For each face choose a continuous function $\Phi_p:G\to\mathbb R$ satisfying $\Phi_p(gzg^{-1})=\Phi_p(z)$ and $\Phi_p(z^{-1})=\Phi_p(z)$. Define the dimensionless lattice action and its normalized expectation by

$$
S_\Lambda(U):=\sum_{p\in\mathcal F}\Phi_p(U_p),\qquad Z_\Lambda:=\int_{G^{\mathcal E^+}}e^{-S_\Lambda(U)}\,d\mu_G^{\mathcal E^+}(U),\qquad \langle O\rangle_\Lambda:=Z_\Lambda^{-1}\int_{G^{\mathcal E^+}}O(U)e^{-S_\Lambda(U)}\,d\mu_G^{\mathcal E^+}(U)
$$

for bounded measurable $O:G^{\mathcal E^+}\to\mathbb C$. The finite-volume **Gauss sector** is the closed subspace of $L^2(G^{\mathcal E^+},\mathbb P_\Lambda)$ consisting of measurable functions with finite integral of $|f|^2$, modulo equality $\mathbb P_\Lambda$-almost everywhere, whose equivalence classes are invariant under each element of $G^{\mathcal V}$. Here $\mathbb P_\Lambda$ is the normalized probability with density $Z_\Lambda^{-1}e^{-S_\Lambda}$ relative to product link measure. For $v\in\mathcal V$ and $X\in\mathfrak g$, let $X^{(v)}$ be the tangent vector at the identity of $G^{\mathcal V}$ with component $X$ at $v$ and zero at other vertices. If $\alpha(h,U)=h\cdot U$, define the infinitesimal **Gauss generator** on $C^\infty(G^{\mathcal E^+})$ by

$$
(D_{v,X}f)(U):=df_U\!\left(d\alpha_{(\mathbf e,U)}(X^{(v)},0)\right).
$$

The full Gauss sector uses invariance under every vertex gauge transformation; the infinitesimal equations $D_{v,X}f=0$ alone are not asserted to impose invariance under disconnected components of $G$. Link variables and the action are dimensionless. This finite mathematical regulator makes no continuum-limit or empirical claim.

declaration.title: Finite lattice gauge data define an invariant probability
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; authorized inventory expansion recorded; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
declaration.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every finite oriented lattice two-complex with compact Lie group $G$, normalized bi-invariant link probability $\mu_G$, and continuous conjugation-invariant face actions $\Phi_p$, the vertex formulas $(h\cdot U)_e=h_{s(e)}U_eh_{t(e)}^{-1}$ define a smooth group action on $G^{\mathcal E^+}$. Each face holonomy transforms by conjugation at its base vertex. Consequently the product Haar measure and the Boltzmann weight $e^{-\sum_p\Phi_p(U_p)}$ are gauge invariant, and the partition function satisfies $0<Z_\Lambda<\infty$. Thus the normalized finite-lattice expectation is a well-defined gauge-invariant probability expectation. In $L^2$ of that probability, the subspace of classes invariant under each vertex gauge transformation is closed. The infinitesimal Gauss generators defined by differentiating this smooth action are well-defined as directional derivatives on smooth functions.

declaration.title: Wilson loop on a finite lattice
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
declaration.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and take finite oriented lattice data with compact group $G$, link variables $U_e$, and vertex action $U_e\mapsto h_{s(e)}U_eh_{t(e)}^{-1}$. Fix a positive-dimensional finite-dimensional complex Hermitian space $(W,h)$ and a smooth group homomorphism $\rho:G\to U(W,h)$, where $U(W,h)$ is the group of invertible complex-linear maps preserving $h$; put $d=\dim_{\mathbb C}W\geq1$. A **based closed lattice loop** is a finite edge word $C=(e_1,\ldots,e_\ell)$ of integer length $\ell\geq0$ with a chosen base vertex $v_0$, such that consecutive endpoints match and, when $\ell>0$, the first and last endpoints are $v_0$; when $\ell=0$, the loop consists only of $v_0$. Its ordered holonomy is $U_C:=U_{e_1}\cdots U_{e_\ell}$, in traversal order with the first edge on the left; for $\ell=0$, set $U_C=e$. The reversed word is $C^{-1}=(\bar e_\ell,\ldots,\bar e_1)$. The **normalized Wilson loop** is

$$
W_\rho(C;U):=\frac{1}{d}\operatorname{Tr}_W\!\big(\rho(U_C)\big).
$$

The loop is dimensionless. Changing the base vertex by a cyclic rebase conjugates $U_C$ and leaves $W_\rho$ unchanged; reversing the loop gives $W_\rho(C^{-1};U)=\overline{W_\rho(C;U)}$. On a fixed finite lattice with a specified finite product Haar probability and bounded action, $\langle W_\rho(C)\rangle_\Lambda$ is the ordinary normalized finite-dimensional integral. No renormalized continuum Wilson loop or continuum limit is defined here.

declaration.title: Wilson loop is invariant under vertex gauge transformations
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; authorized inventory expansion recorded; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
declaration.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $G$ be a group and let $(W,q)$ be a finite-dimensional complex Hermitian inner-product space. Define $U(W,q):=\{T\in\operatorname{GL}_{\mathbb C}(W):q(Tu,Tv)=q(u,v)\text{ for all }u,v\in W\}$, and let $\rho:G\to U(W,q)$ be a group homomorphism, with $d=\dim_{\mathbb C}W\geq1$. Let a finite oriented graph have vertices $\mathcal V$ and one chosen orientation $\mathcal E^+$ for each edge; for $e\in\mathcal E^+$ write $s(e),t(e)$ for its source and target. A link configuration assigns $U_e\in G$ to each $e\in\mathcal E^+$ and sets $U_{\bar e}=U_e^{-1}$. A based closed edge word $C=(e_1,\ldots,e_\ell)$ has length $\ell\geq0$, consecutive endpoints match, and when $\ell>0$ it starts and ends at a chosen vertex $v_0$; for $\ell=0$ it consists only of $v_0$. Put $U_C:=U_{e_1}\cdots U_{e_\ell}$ in traversal order, with the empty product equal to the identity, and put $W_\rho(C;U):=d^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}_W(\rho(U_C))$. For every vertex tuple $k\in G^{\mathcal V}$ acting by $(k\cdot U)_e=k_{s(e)}U_ek_{t(e)}^{-1}$, one has $U_C(k\cdot U)=k_{v_0}U_C(U)k_{v_0}^{-1}$. Thus the normalized trace is gauge invariant and unchanged when the based word is cyclically rotated; for $\ell>0$ reversal is $C^{-1}=(\bar e_\ell,\ldots,\bar e_1)$, while the empty word reverses to itself, and $W_\rho(C^{-1};U)=\overline{W_\rho(C;U)}$.

declaration.title: Finite SU(2) Wilson plaquette measure
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; authorized inventory expansion recorded; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
declaration.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Use the matrix group $G_2=SU(2)=\{U\in M_2(\mathbb C):U^*U=I_2,\ \det U=1\}$ with matrix multiplication and its standard real Lie-group structure. Its defining representation is $\rho_2(U)=U$ on $W=\mathbb C^2$ with Hermitian form $h(v,w)=v^*w$. In real coordinates every element has the form

$$
U(x)=\begin{pmatrix}x_0+ix_3&x_2+ix_1\\-x_2+ix_1&x_0-ix_3\end{pmatrix},\qquad x\in S^3:=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:\textstyle\sum_{j=0}^3x_j^2=1\}.
$$

Let $\mu_2$ be the pushforward of normalized round surface measure on $S^3$ under $x\mapsto U(x)$. In spherical coordinates $x_0=\cos\theta$, $(x_1,x_2,x_3)=\sin\theta\,n$, $0\leq\theta\leq\pi$, $n\in S^2$, its coordinate density is $d\mu_2=(2/\pi)\sin^2\theta\,d\theta\,d\omega_2(n)$, where $n=(\sin\varphi\cos\psi,\sin\varphi\sin\psi,\cos\varphi)$ and $d\omega_2=(1/(4\pi))\sin\varphi\,d\varphi\,d\psi$ for $0\leq\varphi\leq\pi$, $0\leq\psi<2\pi$. Define the real class function $\tau(U):=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}_2(U)=x_0$.

For dimensionless $\beta\geq0$, define the pure-gauge Wilson plaquette action on any finite oriented lattice by

$$
S_\beta(U):=\beta\sum_{p}\bigl(1-\tau(U_p)\bigr),\qquad \beta=\frac{4}{g_0^2}
$$

when a dimensionless bare coupling $g_0>0$ is used. The finite link measure is the product of $\mu_2$ over positively oriented edges, and its normalized expectation is the finite product integral with density proportional to $e^{-S_\beta}$. The one-plaquette normalizing factor and one-plaquette probability are

$$
z_\beta:=\int_{G_2}e^{\beta\tau(U)}\,d\mu_2(U),\qquad d\nu_\beta(U):=z_\beta^{-1}e^{\beta\tau(U)}d\mu_2(U).
$$

This defines only a finite-lattice mathematical measure; it does not define an infinite-volume or continuum expectation.

declaration.title: Independent plaquette variables on a finite planar rectangle
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; authorized inventory expansion recorded; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
declaration.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and let $G$ be a compact group with normalized bi-invariant Borel probability $\mu$. For positive integers $M,N$, let $\Lambda_{M,N}$ have vertices $(i,j)$ with $0\leq i\leq M$ and $0\leq j\leq N$, east-oriented horizontal edges $h_{i,j}:(i,j)\to(i+1,j)$ for $0\leq i<M$, $0\leq j\leq N$, north-oriented vertical edges $v_{i,j}:(i,j)\to(i,j+1)$ for $0\leq i\leq M$, $0\leq j<N$, and faces $p_{i,j}$ for $0\leq i<M$, $0\leq j<N$. The face $p_{i,j}$ has counterclockwise boundary word $(h_{i,j},v_{i+1,j},\bar h_{i,j+1},\bar v_{i,j})$, started at its lower-left vertex; multiply its link matrices in traversal order, with the first factor on the left. Let $G^{\mathcal V}$ act on positively oriented link variables by $(g\cdot U)_e=g_{s(e)}U_eg_{t(e)}^{-1}$. Use the product Haar measure $\mu^{\mathcal E^+}$ on links and free boundary edges. Give each face a positive continuous conjugation-invariant weight $w_{i,j}:G\to(0,\infty)$ with $w_{i,j}(g^{-1})=w_{i,j}(g)$, and normalize the density proportional to $\prod_{i,j}w_{i,j}(U_{p_{i,j}})$ relative to this link measure. For any chosen column $a\in\{0,\ldots,M\}$, fixing the gauge factor at $(a,0)$ to the identity gives a unique representative with every horizontal edge and every vertical edge in column $a$ equal to the identity. Write $V_{i,j}$ for the vertical link in this representative and set $P_{i,j}:=V_{i+1,j}V_{i,j}^{-1}$. The plaquette variables $(P_{i,j})$ are independent, and $P_{i,j}$ has probability

$$
d\nu_{i,j}(g)=\frac{w_{i,j}(g)}{\int_Gw_{i,j}(z)\,d\mu(z)}\,d\mu(g).
$$

This is a finite planar lattice statement with no periodic identifications or continuum limit.

declaration.title: SU(2) one-plaquette matrix average at strong coupling
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; authorized inventory expansion recorded; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
declaration.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ and use the finite $SU(2)$ Wilson plaquette measure with $\beta>0$ defined above. Put

$$
I_0(\beta):=\int_{SU(2)}e^{\beta\tau(U)}d\mu_2(U),\qquad I_1(\beta):=\int_{SU(2)}\tau(U)e^{\beta\tau(U)}d\mu_2(U),\qquad \lambda(\beta):=I_1(\beta)/I_0(\beta).
$$

Then $\mu_2$ is a normalized bi-invariant Borel probability, $I_0(\beta)>0$, $0<\lambda(\beta)<1$, and the defining-representation matrix expectation is

$$
\int_{SU(2)}U\,d\nu_\beta(U)=\lambda(\beta)I_2.
$$

As $\beta\downarrow0$, $\lambda(\beta)=\beta/4+O(\beta^3)$. The parameter $\beta$ and the one-plaquette expectation are dimensionless.

declaration.title: Exact finite-lattice SU(2) Wilson area law in two dimensions
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
declaration.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $M,N\geq1$ be integers and use the finite $M$-by-$N$ square lattice with free boundary (no periodic identifications and all boundary links retained), one $SU(2)$ link matrix per positively oriented edge, product normalized round measure, and only link variables (no matter variables), with the Wilson action $S_\beta(U)=\beta\sum_p(1-\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}_2 U_p)$. Use the defining two-dimensional representation and normalized Wilson loop $W(C)=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}_2 U_C$, with edge matrices multiplied in traversal order. Let $\beta=4/g_0^2$ for dimensionless $g_0>0$, and restrict to the explicit strong-coupling window $0<\beta\leq1$ (equivalently $g_0^2\geq4$). For any axis-aligned rectangle contained in the lattice with corners $(a,c)$ and $(b,d)$, where $0\leq a<b\leq M$ and $0\leq c<d\leq N$, let $C_{a,b;c,d}$ be its boundary traversed counterclockwise from $(a,c)$. Its area in plaquette units is $A=(b-a)(d-c)$. The defining representation has nontrivial $\mathbb Z_2$ center charge because $-I_2$ acts as $-I_2$. Put

$$
\lambda(\beta):=\frac{\int_{SU(2)}\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}_2(U)e^{\beta\operatorname{Tr}_2(U)/2}\,d\mu_2(U)}{\int_{SU(2)}e^{\beta\operatorname{Tr}_2(U)/2}\,d\mu_2(U)},
$$

where $\mu_2$ is normalized round measure on $SU(2)\cong S^3$. Then $0<\lambda(\beta)<1$ and the exact finite-lattice expectation is

$$
\langle W(C_{a,b;c,d})\rangle_\beta=\lambda(\beta)^A=\exp\!\bigl(-\sigma_{\rm lat}(\beta)A\bigr),\qquad \sigma_{\rm lat}(\beta):=-\log\lambda(\beta)>0.
$$

The parameter $\beta$ and the lattice string tension $\sigma_{\rm lat}$ are dimensionless. The identity holds for every finite container and every stated rectangle; no infinite-area, infinite-volume, or continuum limit is taken, and no continuum confinement or mass-gap claim follows.

declaration.title: One-plaquette SU(2) Wilson average
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; authorized inventory expansion recorded; readiness recording follows final scoped checks.
declaration.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For one square face with free boundary in the finite $SU(2)$ Wilson model at $0<\beta\leq1$, the normalized plaquette holonomy has law $d\nu_\beta(U)=z_\beta^{-1}e^{\beta\tau(U)}d\mu_2(U)$, where $\tau(U)=\tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}_2U$ and $z_\beta=\int e^{\beta\tau}d\mu_2$. The Wilson action partition factor is $Z_\square=e^{-\beta}z_\beta$, and the normalized fundamental Wilson loop around the square has expectation $\langle W(\partial\square)\rangle_\beta=\lambda(\beta)$, where $\lambda(\beta)=\int\tau e^{\beta\tau}d\mu_2/z_\beta=\beta/4+O(\beta^3)$ as $\beta\downarrow0$.

declaration.title: Donaldson's ADHM matrix equations in the source convention
declaration.statement:
Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian inner products. Write $\alpha_1,\alpha_2\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $P:W\to V$, and $Q:V\to W$. The Donaldson source convention for these four matrices is

$$[\alpha_1,\alpha_2]+PQ=0,\qquad [\alpha_1,\alpha_1^\dagger]+[\alpha_2,\alpha_2^\dagger]-PP^\dagger+Q^\dagger Q=0.$$

The second equality is an equality of Hermitian endomorphisms of $V$. It is an algebraic convention from the displayed source equations; it does not by itself assert the full-rank condition on the source's ADHM linear map or an identification with the run's raw moment maps.

declaration.statement: Assume AC. Let $E$ be a smooth finite-rank complex vector bundle on a finite-dimensional complex manifold, and let $D''$ be a smooth complex-linear operator from its smooth sections to smooth $E$-valued $(0,1)$-forms satisfying $D''(fs)=\bar\partial f\otimes s+fD''s$. Extend it to bundle-valued forms by the graded Leibniz rule and suppose $(D'')^2=0$. Near every point there is a smooth invertible frame matrix $G$ with $D''G=0$. The changes between these frames are holomorphic, defining a unique holomorphic vector-bundle structure with Dolbeault operator $D''$. A smooth bundle map intertwines two such operators exactly when it is holomorphic for these structures. The construction is local and requires no projective GAGA, coherence or global vanishing theorem.

declaration.title: Entrywise conjugation does not match the raw ADHM real moment map
declaration.statement:
Let $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,P,Q)$ obey the source equations stated in the following references section. Under the proposed substitution

$$B_i=\overline{\alpha_i},\qquad I=\overline P,\qquad J=\overline Q,$$

the raw complex moment map vanishes, but the raw real moment map is

$$\mu_{\mathbb R}=\overline C+\overline X-\overline Y,$$

where $C=[\alpha_1,\alpha_1^\dagger]+[\alpha_2,\alpha_2^\dagger]$, $X=PP^\dagger$, and $Y=Q^\dagger Q$. The conjugated source real equation gives $\overline C-\overline X+\overline Y=0$, so on source solutions the proposed raw real moment map equals $2\overline C$; the source equations alone therefore do not establish its vanishing. This failure occurs for the explicit $k=N=2$ source solution in the proof below.

declaration.title: Zero-FI regular ADHM and framed twistor data
declaration.statement:
Fix integers $N\geq2$ and $k\geq0$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian inner products. A raw framed ADHM datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$. Its complex and real moment expressions are

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable when the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, for $m\geq0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$, and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable when no nonzero subspace of $V$ is invariant under both $B_1,B_2$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular when it is both stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ and its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$. The regular zero-FI real quotient is the orbit set

$$\mathcal A^{\mathrm{reg}}_{k,N}=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable and costable}\}/U(V).$$

Let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and the orientation whose restriction to the stereographic coordinates $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$ on $\mathbb R^4=S^4\setminus\{\infty\}$ is $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. For a smooth right principal $U(N)$-bundle $P\to S^4$, let $E=P\times_{U(N)}\mathbb C^N$ be its Hermitian associated vector bundle, let $A$ be a smooth unitary connection, and let $\Phi:E|_{\infty}\to\mathbb C^N$ be a unitary framing. Write $F_A$ for the anti-Hermitian curvature matrix and define

$$q_N(P,A)=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A).$$

The anti-self-dual equation is $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2=0$. For integer $k\geq0$, the framed ASD sector $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ is the set of such framed connections satisfying $F_A^+=0$ and $q_N(P,A)=-k$, modulo smooth unitary gauge transformations whose value at $\infty$ is the identity in the framing. This definition alone does not assert that every sector exists or that $q_N$ is integral; the exact $U(N)$ charge normalization is a separate lemma below.

Identify $\mathbb H^2$ with $\mathbb C^4$ using a fixed right quaternionic structure $j$ with $j^2=-1$. The twistor space is $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)$, the projection $\pi:Z\to\mathbb H\mathbb P^1=S^4$ sends a complex line $\ell$ to the quaternionic line $\ell+j\ell$, and the antiholomorphic involution is $\sigma([v])=[jv]$. A real twistor line is a fibre $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$; $\sigma$ restricts to the antipodal map on each such line. Fix homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ so $\sigma$ is induced by $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)\mapsto(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$. The finite real line over $z$ has equations $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. These equations fix the quaternionic identification and its orientation. In the chart $\lambda_1=1,\lambda_2=0$, vertical complex orientation followed by the positive orientation of $(z_1,z_2)$ is the complex orientation of $Z$.


For the spinor convention, use the standard spin structure on $S^4$ and $\operatorname{Spin}(4)\cong SU(2)_+\times SU(2)_-$. Let $S^+,S^-$ be the associated rank-two complex spinor bundles, so $T_{\mathbb C}S^4\cong S^+\otimes S^-$. The twistor fibre at $x$ is $\mathbb P(S_x^+)$, and the complex two-plane associated with $\ell\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ is $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. Use the Levi-Civita connection of the round metric for the horizontal distribution of $\pi$; the horizontal $(0,1)$ subspace at $[\ell]\in L_x$ projects to this complex alpha-plane. The displayed orientation is the twistor orientation: the vertical complex orientation followed by the quotient orientation on $S^4$ agrees with the complex orientation on $Z$. It is chosen so the curvature component that vanishes on every such plane is precisely $F^+=(F+*_gF)/2$. In spinor components, $F_{AB}=F_{(AB)}$ denotes the symmetric spinor corresponding to $F^+$ under $\Lambda^2_+T_x^*S^4\otimes\mathbb C\cong\operatorname{Sym}^2(S_x^+)^*$; restriction to the plane is $F_{AB}\pi^A\pi^B$, which vanishes for every $[\pi]\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ exactly when $F^+=0$.

A linear monad on $Z$ is a complex of holomorphic bundles

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

where $U,U',K$ are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces, $b\circ a=0$, $a$ is injective as a sheaf map, $b$ is surjective, and the cohomology sheaf $\ker b/\operatorname{im}a$ is locally free. It is framed when that cohomology has a specified unitary trivialization on $L_\infty$. For a holomorphic bundle $\mathcal E$ on $Z$ that is holomorphically trivial on every real line, a positive Hermitian Ward reality datum is a holomorphic nondegenerate pairing $b:\mathcal E\otimes\sigma^*\overline{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal O_Z$ satisfying $b_{\sigma z}(v,u)=\overline{b_z(u,v)}$. Here $b_z$ is complex linear in $u\in\mathcal E_z$ and conjugate linear in $v\in\mathcal E_{\sigma z}$; the conjugate pullback is holomorphic because $\sigma$ is antiholomorphic. For holomorphic sections $s,t$ on $L_x$, the function $b_z(s(z),t(\sigma z))$ is holomorphic on the compact line, hence constant. It defines $h_x(s,t)$; require this Hermitian form to be positive definite for every $x$. The metric on each fibre of $\mathcal E|_{L_x}$ is transported from this form by holomorphic evaluation. Thus positive forms are induced by the pairing, not independent arbitrary choices. A framed Ward bundle includes a unitary framing on $L_\infty$ for this induced form. Smoothness and parallelness of the induced section-bundle metric are conclusions of the Ward construction.

The compact torus $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ acts on $\mathbb R^4\cong\mathbb C^2$ by $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(t_1z_1,t_2z_2)$ and on $W$ by $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its raw ADHM action is

$$ (t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ). $$

On the framed ASD sector, the same torus acts by inverse pullback under the indicated rotation of $S^4$ and by postcomposition of the framing with $h$. On $Z$, the rotations act by $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]\mapsto[\lambda_1:t_1t_2\lambda_2:t_1\mu_1:t_2\mu_2]$, equivalently the projective spin lift to $\mathbb P(S^+)$; the central sign in the spin double cover acts trivially after projectivization, and the induced action commutes with $\sigma$. The framing torus acts on the framed monad cohomology by the same diagonal representation.

declaration.title: Determinant flatness and charge normalization for framed U(N) ASD data
declaration.statement:
Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $E\to S^4$ be a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ vector bundle with $N\geq2$, a smooth unitary connection $A$, and a unitary framing at $\infty$. Give $S^4$ the round metric and the orientation specified in the definition of the framed ASD sector, and assume $F_A^+=0$. Then the induced determinant-line connection on $\det E=\Lambda^N E$ is flat. Its framing at $\infty$ determines a unique global unit parallel section, so the framed unitary bundle reduces to a framed $SU(N)$ bundle. With $q_N=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A)$ and the determinant Chern-form convention $c(A)=\det(I-F_A/(2\pi i))$, one has

$$q_N(E,A)=-\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle\in-\mathbb Z_{\geq0}.$$

Thus $k=-q_N=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$ is a nonnegative integer, with the sign corresponding to the anti-self-dual equation $F_A^+=0$.

declaration.title: Smooth framed bundle of sections over real twistor lines
declaration.statement: Assume full AC and DC. Let $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3$, let $G=\operatorname{Gr}(2,4)$ be the complex Grassmannian of projective lines in $Z$, and let $p:\mathscr L\to G$ be the universal line family with evaluation map $e:\mathscr L\to Z$. Let $\mathcal E\to Z$ be a holomorphic rank-$N$ bundle, $N\geq2$, with a positive Hermitian real structure and a unitary framing on the twistor line at $\infty$. Assume its restriction to every real twistor line $L_x$ is holomorphically and unitarily trivial. The degree-zero base-change maps at every real line are isomorphisms. Then $(p_*e^*\mathcal E)|_{S^4}$ is a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ vector bundle, its fibre at $x$ is $H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$, and the evaluation morphism identifies its pullback to the real incidence family with $e^*\mathcal E$. More precisely, for every real line, there is a complex-open neighbourhood in $G$ on whose entire universal-line family the evaluation morphism is an isomorphism. The framing on $L_\infty$ induces a unitary framing of this bundle at $\infty$.

declaration.statement:
Assume AC. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, and let $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ satisfy the raw complex equation $\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. Put $K=V\oplus V\oplus W$. For $z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$ put

$$a_z=(B_1-z_1,B_2-z_2,J)^T,\qquad b_z=(-B_2^\dagger+\bar z_2,B_1^\dagger-\bar z_1,I^\dagger)^T,\qquad D_z=\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\dagger\\a_z^\dagger\end{pmatrix}.$$

Then

$$D_zD_z^\dagger=\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\dagger b_z&\mu_{\mathbb C}\\\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger&a_z^\dagger a_z\end{pmatrix},\qquad b_z^\dagger b_z-a_z^\dagger a_z=\mu_{\mathbb R}.$$

The maps $b_z^\dagger$ are onto for every $z$ exactly when the datum is stable; the maps $a_z$ are injective for every $z$ exactly when it is costable. Consequently, when both moments vanish, regularity is equivalent to $D_z$ being onto for every $z$. On this locus $f_z=a_z^\dagger a_z=b_z^\dagger b_z$ is positive definite and

$$P_z=1-D_z^\dagger\operatorname{diag}(f_z^{-1},f_z^{-1})D_z$$

is the smooth orthogonal projection onto a rank-$N$ bundle over $\mathbb R^4$. The projection connection $\nabla=P\,d$ is unitary and satisfies $F^+=0$ for the positive stereographic orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, where $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$.

In homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ on $\mathbb P^3$, put $A=B_1\lambda_1-B_2^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_1$, $C=B_2\lambda_1+B_1^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_2$ and

$$\alpha=(A,C,J\lambda_1+I^\dagger\lambda_2)^T,\qquad\beta=(-C,A,I\lambda_1-J^\dagger\lambda_2).$$

The polynomial identity is $\beta\alpha=\lambda_1^2\mu_{\mathbb C}+\lambda_1\lambda_2\mu_{\mathbb R}-\lambda_2^2\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger$. With $\sigma(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$, one has $\beta(v)=\alpha(\sigma v)^\dagger$. The real line over $z$ is $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. For regular zero-moment data these maps form a holomorphic bundle monad, trivial on each real line, with middle cohomology on the line over $z$ canonically $\ker D_z$. Its framing at infinity is $W$. The torus acts on the homogeneous coordinates by $(\lambda_1,t_1t_2\lambda_2,t_1\mu_1,t_2\mu_2)$ and on the raw data by $(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$; the monad isomorphism has source, middle and target factors $(t_1t_2)^{-1}$, $\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)$ and $1$, respectively. It preserves the framing representation $W$ with weights $e_\alpha^{-1}$.

This proves a forward raw block construction. It does not assert that every real Ward monad has this normal form, that its inverse extraction is unique, or that the connection extends with charge $k$; those global correspondence and charge assertions require their separate proofs.

declaration.title: Conditional framed Penrose–Ward correspondence on the round four-sphere
declaration.statement:
Assume full AC and the exact projective GAGA comparison used below. The local smooth integrable-Dolbeault frame theorem is supplied by the explicit local proof, rather than assumed as a new analytic input.

For $N\geq2$, let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ be the framed unitary ASD sector on the round oriented $S^4$ defined above. On the Ward side take a holomorphic rank-$N$ bundle $\mathcal E$ on $Z$, a positive Hermitian Ward reality datum, and a unitary framing on $L_\infty$. Require $\mathcal E|_{L_x}\cong\mathcal O_{L_x}^{\oplus N}$ for every real twistor line, and require $c_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$, where $H=c_1(\mathcal O_Z(1))$. Then $\widehat E_x=H^0(L_x,\mathcal E|_{L_x})$ forms a smooth rank-$N$ Hermitian bundle on $S^4$. For each section of $\widehat E_x$, extend it holomorphically and uniquely to the first infinitesimal neighbourhood of $L_x$ and differentiate this extension in the family of lines; this defines the Ward connection $\widehat\nabla$. The form induced by the positive holomorphic reality pairing is smooth and is preserved by $\widehat\nabla$; this is a conclusion, not an independent metric-compatibility assumption.

Under these hypotheses, the Ward construction gives a bijection between based unitary gauge classes in $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ and isomorphism classes of the specified framed Ward bundles. The reconstructed Ward connection satisfies $F^+=0$ and $q_N=-k$. The inverse sends a framed ASD connection to the holomorphic structure on $\pi^*E$ whose vertical part is the standard Dolbeault operator and whose horizontal $(0,1)$ part is the connection on the planes $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. Both maps preserve the framing, Hermitian form, charge, and compact torus action. Reducible bundles and flat summands are included; no irreducibility assumption is imposed.

declaration.title: Chern character and charge of the normalized twistor monad
declaration.statement:
Let $\pi:Z=\mathbb CP^3\to S^4$ be the oriented twistor fibration with the conventions stated in the following references section, let $H=c_1(\mathcal O_Z(1))$, and let $E\to S^4$ be a framed unitary ASD rank-$N$ bundle whose Ward bundle is $\mathcal E=\pi^*E$ as a smooth bundle. Suppose $\mathcal E$ is the cohomology of a linear monad

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)^{\oplus k}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus(2k+N)}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z(1)^{\oplus k}.$$

Then $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=N-kH^2$, $c_1(\mathcal E)=0$, and $c_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$. For the twistor orientation specified in the Definition, if $u\in H^4(S^4;\mathbb Z)$ satisfies $\langle u,[S^4]\rangle=1$, then $\pi^*u=H^2$. Consequently

$$k=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=-q_N(E,A).$$

declaration.title: Conditional Penrose vanishing from positive scalar curvature
declaration.statement:
Let $A$ be a smooth framed anti-self-dual unitary connection on the specified round oriented $S^4$, and let $\mathcal E$ be its holomorphic Ward bundle on $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3$. $$\mathcal P_{\mathcal E}:H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))\longrightarrow\{s\in\Gamma(E):(\nabla_A^*\nabla_A+R/6)s=0\},$$

and the analogous map for $\mathcal E^\vee$, where $R>0$ is the scalar curvature of the round metric and the target connection is the induced unitary connection. Then

$$H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))=H^1(Z,\mathcal E^\vee(-2))=0.$$

This is a conditional vanishing result; it does not assert or prove the Penrose-transform input.

declaration.title: Conditional twistor vanishing and normalized monad reconstruction
declaration.statement:
Let $A$ be a framed unitary ASD connection on the round oriented $S^4$, let $\mathcal E$ be its Ward bundle on $Z=\mathbb CP^3$, and let $k=-q_N(A)$. Use the exact coupled cohomology-vanishing input stated below for both $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal E^\vee$. Assume also the exact projective GAGA and line-family base-change inputs needed to regard $\mathcal E$ as an algebraic bundle, to make its restrictions trivial on a complex-open neighbourhood of at least one real twistor line, and to apply the diagonal resolution. Finally, use the Chern-character normalization $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=N-kH^2$ in $A^*(\mathbb CP^3)_\mathbb Q$, where $H=c_1(\mathcal O(1))$; this normalization is conditional on the twistor pullback class convention matching the framed charge.

Under these inputs,

$$H^1(Z,\mathcal E(-2))=H^1(Z,\mathcal E^\vee(-2))=0.$$

There is a canonical Beilinson three-term monad

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

whose middle cohomology is $\mathcal E$ and whose terms are

$$U=H^2(Z,\mathcal E(-3)),\qquad K=H^2(Z,\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^2),\qquad U'=H^2(Z,\mathcal E\otimes\Omega_Z^1(-1)),$$

with $\dim U=\dim U'=k$ and $\dim K=2k+N$. The construction is natural in framed bundle isomorphisms and unique up to changes of bases in $U,K,U'$. The values of all global parallel sections form its maximal trivial flat parallel summand, and the connection splits orthogonally into that summand and a summand with no nonzero parallel sections; arbitrary nonflat parallel summands are permitted. The monad construction is additive across this splitting and uses no hypothesis $H^0(Z,\mathcal E)=0$.

declaration.title: Real monad normalization, regularity, framing and charge
declaration.statement:
Let $N\geq2$, $k\geq0$, and let a framed real Ward bundle on $Z=\mathbb CP^3$ have the normalized linear monad with vector-space dimensions $k,2k+N,k$. Then the real monad is equivalent to a raw datum $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ on $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$ in exactly the convention

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=0.$$

The tuple is regular exactly when the associated quaternionic construction is pointwise nondegenerate. Its kernel projection connection extends over $\infty$, has the specified framing, and equals the Ward connection. Changes of normalized monad bases induce exactly the $U(k)$ action on raw data, and inverse matrix extraction recovers the same $U(k)$ orbit. The resulting charge is $k=-q_N=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$. The entrywise conjugation candidate is refuted by the recorded comparison lemma and is not used in the intrinsic real monad normalization.

declaration.title: Conditional zero-FI regular ADHM and framed ASD correspondence
declaration.statement:
Let $N\geq2$, $k\geq0$, and let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ADHM,reg}}_{k,N}$ be the quotient by $U(k)$ of the raw data satisfying both zero moment equations and stable-and-costable regularity in the conventions stated in the following references section. Let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ be the framed unitary ASD sector on the round oriented $S^4$ with $q_N=-k$ in those same conventions. Conditional on the real monad normalization and Ward inputs stated below, the construction gives a $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$-equivariant bijection

$$\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ADHM,reg}}_{k,N}\;\longleftrightarrow\;\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}.$$

The zero-FI real quotient is also diffeomorphic to the stable-and-costable complex $GL(k)$ quotient. Under the stated projective GAGA and family base-change hypotheses, the corresponding framed sheaves on $\mathbb P^2$ are exactly the locally free locus among the framed torsion-free sheaves with rank $N$ and Hilbert polynomial $N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$. The positive-FI stable quotient includes non-locally-free sheaves and is not identified with the ordinary framed ASD moduli. Under the same family and normal-form hypotheses, the correspondence is compatible with first-order framed deformations and their tangent spaces.

declaration.title: Rank-one regular zero-FI ADHM and ordinary ASD boundary
declaration.statement:
Assume AC and the exact rank-two regular zero-FI ADHM/ASD correspondence, with all its actual analytic and intrinsic normal-form prerequisites. Fix $k\ge0$, $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C$. Let $\mathcal A^{\mathrm{reg}}_{k,1}$ be the orbit set by $U(V)$ of $B_1,B_2\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, $J:V\to W$ with

$$[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0,\qquad [B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=0,$$

such that words in the $B_i$ applied to $I(W)$ span $V$ and no nonzero common invariant subspace lies in $\ker J$. On the positively stereographically oriented unit round $S^4$, let $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,1}$ be the set of smooth Hermitian line bundles $L$, smooth unitary connections $A$ with $F_A^+=0$, and unitary framings $\Phi:L_\infty\to\mathbb C$, with $q_1=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int F_A\wedge F_A=-k$, modulo framed unitary isomorphisms. After a fixed framed bundle is chosen, its gauge group consists of smooth unitary automorphisms equal to identity at infinity.

The regular complex $GL(V)$ quotient, defined by retaining the complex equation and the same stability and costability, has the same empty-or-point classification under the zero-FI real/complex quotient identification. For $k>0$ both ordinary sets are empty. For $k=0$ they are the single empty raw datum and the framed flat line, respectively, with no framed stabilizer. This identification is equivariant for $T=(S^1)^2\times S^1$, with $h=e^{-1}$, raw action $(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$ and connection action by inverse rotational pullback and postcomposition of the framing with $h$; on the resulting point these actions are trivial.

A first-order real Hermitian family here is over $D=\mathbb C[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)$ with involution $\varepsilon^\dagger=\varepsilon$. On the raw side use free $D$-modules of ranks $k,1$, the displayed equations over $D$, regular reduction, fixed framing module, and unitary $D$-linear changes of basis. On the connection side use locally free smooth Hermitian line-bundle deformations with framed special fiber and a unitary connection $A_0+\varepsilon a$, satisfying ASD coefficientwise, modulo unitary gauge transformations with framed reduction and value identity at infinity. For $k>0$ these groupoids are empty; for $k=0$ each is equivalent to the one-object groupoid with trivial automorphism group. The identification commutes with reduction, infinitesimal scalar base changes preserving the involution, and the compact action. In particular it identifies their zero tangent spaces and restricts to the exact locally-free/base-change family range in the rank-two correspondence. No positive-FI quotient, its non-locally-free rank-one boundary, or its fixed-point series is identified with ordinary ASD moduli.

declaration.title: A positive-FI point with a non-locally-free framed sheaf
declaration.statement:
Take $N=k=1$ and $\zeta>0$. The datum $B_1=B_2=0$, $I=\sqrt\zeta$, $J=0$ is a stable positive-FI solution but is not costable and does not lie in the zero-FI regular locus. Its stable complex orbit has the framed $\mathbb P^2$ monad

$$\mathcal O(-1)\xrightarrow{(-z_1,-z_2,0)^T}\mathcal O^{\oplus3}\xrightarrow{(z_2,-z_1,z_0)}\mathcal O(1),$$

whose middle cohomology is the ideal sheaf of $p=[1:0:0]$; it is torsion-free and not locally free at $p$. Thus this positive-FI point lies on the non-locally-free boundary excluded from the ordinary zero-FI framed ASD correspondence.

declaration.title: Localized torus-equivariant Borel–Moore classes
declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $r\geq 0$, let $T=(\mathbb C^\times)^r$ act algebraically on a separated finite-type complex variety $X$, and suppose $X$ has a finite cover by $T$-invariant affine open subvarieties. Use rational coefficients. Let $K=(S^1)^r$ be the maximal compact subgroup of $T$, and use the product right Milnor model $E_K=(E_{S^1})^r$, $B_K=E_K/K=(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r$. The inclusion $K\subset T$ gives the same topological Borel construction up to homotopy. For each algebraic character $\chi:T\to\mathbb C^\times$, let $L_\chi=E_K\times_K\mathbb C_{\chi|_K}\to B_K$, with right equivalence $(e,z)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,\chi(t)^{-1}z)$, and put $u_\chi=c_1(L_\chi)$. For the coordinate characters $\chi_i$ and $u_i=u_{\chi_i}$, the coefficient ring is $R_T=H^*(B_K;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q[u_1,\ldots,u_r]$, with $|u_i|=2$ and $u_\chi=\sum_i n_i u_i$ for $\chi(t_1,\ldots,t_r)=\prod_i t_i^{n_i}$. Let $S_T$ be the multiplicative set consisting of $1$ and finite products of $u_\chi$ for nontrivial $\chi$.

Let $H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X;\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D^b_{T,c}(X;\mathbb Q)}(\mathbb Q_X,\omega_X^T[-j])$, where $\omega_X^T$ is the normalized equivariant dualizing object whose restriction is the ordinary dualizing object $\omega_X$, without a quotient-stack dimension shift. Equivalently, this is the stable value in degree $j$ of $H^{\mathrm{BM}}_{j+2rm}(X_m;\mathbb Q)$, where $U_m=(\mathbb C^{m+1}\setminus\{0\})^r$ has the free right scalar $T$-action, $X_m=(U_m\times X)/T$ uses $(e,x)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,t^{-1}\cdot x)$, and the supplied bounded-Hom comparison is taken in its stable range. The ring $R_T$ acts by pullback from $B_K$ and cap product. For an $R_T$-module $M$, $S_T^{-1}M$ consists of fractions $m/s$ with $m\in M$, $s\in S_T$, and $m/s=m'/s'$ exactly when some $t\in S_T$ satisfies $t(s'm-sm')=0$; addition and scalar multiplication are the induced fraction operations. Proper equivariant maps induce degree-preserving pushforwards, invariant open inclusions induce Borel–Moore restrictions, and a smooth pure $d$-dimensional complex variety has its complex-oriented fundamental class $[X]_T$ in degree $2d$. For $r=0$, $R_T=\mathbb Q$ and $S_T=\{1\}$.

declaration.title: Nonzero eigenfunctions annihilate equivariant BM on their nonvanishing loci
declaration.statement: Let $T=(\mathbb C^\times)^r$ act algebraically on a separated finite-type complex variety $X$ with a finite invariant affine open cover. Let $U$ be one affine chart, let $f\in\mathcal O(U)$ be regular with a nontrivial character $\chi:T\to\mathbb C^\times$, and fix the convention $f(t\cdot x)=\chi(t)f(x)$. If $D(f)=\{x\in U:f(x)\neq0\}$ is nonempty, then the equivariant character class $u_\chi=c_1(L_{\chi|_K})$ acts by zero on every group $H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(D(f);\mathbb Q)$. It also acts by zero on every such group for a further $T$-invariant open subvariety $V\subseteq D(f)$. Consequently $S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(D(f);\mathbb Q)=S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(V;\mathbb Q)=0$ for all $j$.

declaration.statement:

$$
i_*:S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(F;\mathbb Q)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X;\mathbb Q).
$$
No compactness of $X$, normality hypothesis, or compact-orbit-type nilpotence hypothesis is required.

declaration.title: Fixed-embedding BM self-intersection and Euler units
declaration.statement:
Let $T=(\mathbb C^\times)^r$ act algebraically on a smooth separated finite-type complex variety $X$ with a finite invariant affine open cover. Let $F=X^T$, $i:F\hookrightarrow X$, and $\nu_F=TX|_F/TF$ be the complex normal bundle. Then $F$ is smooth, $T_xF=(T_xX)^T$ for every $x\in F$, and every normal fiber has only nontrivial $T$-weights. On each fiber the restriction of $e_T(\nu_F)$ to $BT$ is the product of the corresponding character classes with multiplicity. The closed regular embedding $i$ has an equivariant refined Gysin map $i^!:H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X;\mathbb Q)\to H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_{j-2c}(F;\mathbb Q)$ on each component of complex codimension $c$, normalized by $i^![X]_T=[F]_T$, with
$$
i^!i_*\beta=e_T(\nu_F)\mathbin{\cap}\beta
$$
for every $\beta\in H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_*(F;\mathbb Q)$, using the normalized Borel–Moore grading and complex orientation. If $F$ is proper, then $e_T(\nu_F)$ is a unit in $S_T^{-1}H_T^*(F;\mathbb Q)$. Empty components contribute no class, and a rank-zero normal bundle has Euler class $1$.

declaration.title: Intrinsic localized pushforward for a proper fixed locus
declaration.statement:
Let $T=(\mathbb C^\times)^r$ act on a smooth separated finite-type complex variety $X$ with a finite invariant affine open cover. Let $F=X^T$ be proper, $i:F\hookrightarrow X$, $p_F:F\to\mathrm{pt}$, and $S_T$ the character multiplicative set. By the finite-affine-atlas concentration isomorphism, $i_*:S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(F;\mathbb Q)\to S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X;\mathbb Q)$ is invertible. Define the intrinsic localized pushforward
$$
p^{\mathrm{loc}}_*:=p_{F*}\circ(i_*)^{-1}:S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(X;\mathbb Q)\longrightarrow S_T^{-1}H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_j(\mathrm{pt};\mathbb Q),
$$
where $p_{F*}$ is the genuine proper Borel–Moore pushforward. For a homogeneous $\alpha\in H_T^q(X;\mathbb Q)$ and smooth complex dimension $d$, an allowed insertion is $\alpha\cap[X]_T\in H^{\mathrm{BM},T}_{2d-q}(X;\mathbb Q)$; the fundamental class $[X]_T$ is the complex-oriented class, not the cohomological unit $1\in H_T^0(X;\mathbb Q)$. This construction does not define an ordinary pushforward along a nonproper map $X\to\mathrm{pt}$.

declaration.title: Why a nonproper fixed locus needs another theory
declaration.statement: Let $T=\mathbb C^\times$ act trivially on $X=\mathbb C^\times=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C[z,z^{-1}]$. Then the fixed locus is $F=X$, and $F\to\mathrm{pt}$ is not proper. Here proper means finite-type, separated, and universally closed; after base change to $\mathbb A^1$ with coordinate $s$, the closed subset $\{(z,s):zs=1\}\subseteq\mathbb C^\times\times\mathbb A^1$ projects to the nonclosed subset $\mathbb A^1\setminus\{0\}$. Consequently the intrinsic localized pushforward defined using a proper fixed-locus trace has no value on $[F]_T$; this example assigns no fixed-point integral or reciprocal-Euler sum.

declaration.title: Critical Abelian Higgs fields, winding and divisor data
declaration.statement:
Let $e>0$ and $\xi>0$ be real parameters, set $\kappa=2e^2\xi$, identify the oriented Euclidean plane $\mathbb R^2$ with $\mathbb C$ using coordinates $(x_1,x_2)$, and use the Hodge star convention $*dx_1=dx_2$, $*dx_2=-dx_1$. A field pair is a smooth real one-form $A=A_1dx_1+A_2dx_2$ on the trivial complex line over $\mathbb R^2$ and a smooth function $q:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb C$. Its unit-charge covariant derivative is $D_Aq=dq-iAq$, its curvature is $F_A=dA=B\,dx_1\wedge dx_2$ with $B=\partial_1A_2-\partial_2A_1$, and its transverse energy is
$$E(A,q)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(\frac{B^2}{2e^2}+|D_{A,1}q|^2+|D_{A,2}q|^2+\frac{e^2}{2}(|q|^2-\xi)^2\right)dx_1dx_2.$$
The pair has finite energy when this nonnegative Lebesgue integral is finite. An admissible boundary sector consists of an integer $n$, a radius $R_0$, and smooth functions $\rho>0$ and real $2\pi$-periodic $\phi$ on $r>R_0$ such that $q(r,\theta)=\rho(r,\theta)e^{i(n\theta+\phi(r,\theta))}$ and $\rho\to\sqrt\xi$, $\phi\to0$ uniformly as $r\to\infty$; $n$ is its winding. A gauge transformation is $(q,A)\mapsto(e^{i\chi}q,A+d\chi)$ for a smooth real-valued function $\chi$ on $\mathbb R^2$.

For $n\ge0$, the positive critical first-order equations are $(D_{A,1}+iD_{A,2})q=0$ and $B=e^2(\xi-|q|^2)$; for $n\le0$ the negative equations are $(D_{A,1}-iD_{A,2})q=0$ and $B=-e^2(\xi-|q|^2)$. The adjective critical refers to the displayed energy normalization and these square-saturating equations. For a positive-winding solution, its divisor is an effective finite divisor $D=\sum_{j=1}^Jm_j[z_j]$, where the $z_j\in\mathbb C$ are distinct, the multiplicities $m_j$ are positive integers, $q$ vanishes exactly at the $z_j$, and near each $z_j$ it has the local form $q(z)=(z-z_j)^{m_j}g_j(z)$ with $g_j$ smooth and nonzero there. The degree is $N=\sum_jm_j$; the empty divisor has degree zero. Negative winding uses the conjugate field and reversed orientation, with $N=|n|$.

On the complement of the divisor, define $h=\log(|q|^2/\xi)$. The associated scalar Taubes datum is a real function smooth away from the divisor such that $h-2m_j\log|z-z_j|$ extends smoothly across every $z_j$, $h\to0$ at infinity, and, as a distribution,
$$\Delta h+\kappa(1-e^h)=4\pi\sum_{j=1}^Jm_j\delta_{z_j},\qquad \langle\delta_z,\psi\rangle=\psi(z)\quad(\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)).$$
When the limit exists, the magnetic flux is $\Phi(A)=\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{|x|<R}B(x)\,dx_1dx_2$. These are mathematical configuration and normalization conventions; they make no assertion that a physical model describes nature.

declaration.title: Taubes disk barriers and monotone Dirichlet iteration
declaration.statement:
Let $\kappa>0$ and let $D=\sum_{j=1}^Jm_j[z_j]$ be a finite effective divisor in $\mathbb C$, where the centers $z_j$ are distinct and $m_j\in\mathbb N$; write $N=\sum_jm_j$. For any $a>0$ with $a\ge4N/\kappa$, the function
$$u_-(z)=\sum_{j=1}^Jm_j\log\frac{|z-z_j|^2}{|z-z_j|^2+a}$$
is a global distributional subsolution of $\Delta u+\kappa(1-e^u)=4\pi\sum_jm_j\delta_{z_j}$. For every $R>\max_j|z_j|$ (with the empty maximum interpreted as $0$), let $D_R=\{|z|<R\}$ and define
$$u_{s,R}(z)=\sum_jm_j\log\frac{R^2|z-z_j|^2}{|R^2-\overline z_jz|^2},\qquad \psi_R(z)=\frac{\kappa}{4}(R^2-|z|^2),\qquad A_R=e^{u_{s,R}}.$$
Then $u_{s,R}$ is the zero-boundary Dirichlet Green sum with $\Delta u_{s,R}=4\pi\sum_jm_j\delta_{z_j}$; $u_{s,R}+\psi_R$ is a supersolution and $u_-\le u_{s,R}+\psi_R$ on $D_R$. Write $H^1_0(D_R;\mathbb R)$ for the closure of $C_c^\infty(D_R;\mathbb R)$ in the real Sobolev space $W^{1,2}(D_R;\mathbb R)$. For any constant $L_R\ge\kappa\max_{\overline D_R}(A_Re^{\psi_R})$, the positive zero-Dirichlet resolver $(-\Delta+L_R)^{-1}$ on $H^1_0(D_R;\mathbb R)$ defines the monotone iteration
$$v_0=u_--u_{s,R},\qquad v_{k+1}=(-\Delta+L_R)^{-1}\bigl(\kappa+L_Rv_k-\kappa A_Re^{v_k}\bigr).$$
It converges pointwise and in $H^1(D_R)$ to a solution $v_R\in C^{2,\alpha}(\overline D_R)$ for every $0<\alpha<1$, with $v_0\le v_R\le\psi_R$ and zero boundary trace. Thus $u_R=u_{s,R}+v_R$ solves the distributional divisor equation, satisfies $u_-\le u_R\le0$, and has $u_R-2\sum_jm_j\log|z-z_j|$ smooth at the centers. For the fixed singular function $s(z)=2\sum_jm_j\log|z-z_j|$, every compact $K\subset\mathbb C$ and every $p>2$ admit constants independent of sufficiently large $R$ such that $u_R-s$ is uniformly bounded in $W^{2,p}(K)$. For each $0<\alpha<1$, choosing $p>2/(1-\alpha)$ also gives a uniform $C^{2,\alpha}(K)$ bound. These are the local compactness estimates for disk exhaustion.

declaration.title: Planar critical vortices for arbitrary finite divisors
declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix $e>0$, $\xi>0$, $\kappa=2e^2\xi$, and an effective finite divisor $D=\sum_{j=1}^Jm_j[z_j]$ on $\mathbb C$ with distinct centers and positive integer multiplicities; let $N=\sum_jm_j$. There is a unique real scalar function $h$, smooth on $\mathbb C\setminus\{z_j\}$, such that $h-2m_j\log|z-z_j|$ extends smoothly across each center, $h\to0$ as $|z|\to\infty$, and
$$\Delta h+\kappa(1-e^h)=4\pi\sum_{j=1}^Jm_j\delta_{z_j}$$
in distributions, where $\langle\delta_z,\psi\rangle=\psi(z)$ for $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$. For $N>0$, $h<0$ off the divisor; for the empty divisor, $h=0$. With $P(z)=\prod_j(z-z_j)^{m_j}$, $s=2\log|P|$, and the orientation $*dx_1=dx_2$, $*dx_2=-dx_1$, the fields
$$q(z)=\sqrt\xi\,e^{(h(z)-s(z))/2}P(z),\qquad A=-\tfrac12 *d(h-s)$$
extend smoothly across the centers and solve $(D_{A,1}+iD_{A,2})q=0$ and $B=e^2(\xi-|q|^2)$, where $D_A=d-iA$ and $B\,dx_1\wedge dx_2=dA$. They have finite energy
$$E(A,q)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(\frac{B^2}{2e^2}+|D_{A,1}q|^2+|D_{A,2}q|^2+\frac{e^2}{2}(|q|^2-\xi)^2\right)dx_1dx_2$$
and flux $\int_{\mathbb R^2}B\,dx_1dx_2=2\pi N$. For every $0<\alpha<\sqrt\kappa$ and every multi-index $\beta$, $|\partial^\beta h(z)|=O(e^{-\alpha|z|})$ as $|z|\to\infty$; the curvature $B$ and covariant gradient $D_Aq$ have the same exponential decay. On the exterior of a disk, the local gauge $e^{-i\arg P}$ gives $q_{\mathrm{ext}}=\sqrt\xi e^{h/2}$ and $A_{\mathrm{ext}}=-\tfrac12 *dh$, so the fields approach the vacuum exponentially in that exterior gauge; the raw global representative $q$ need not have an exponentially small phase correction. Negative winding $-N$ is obtained by complex conjugation and $A\mapsto-A$, with flux $-2\pi N$.

declaration.title: Global energy minima for critical Abelian Higgs vortices
declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix $e>0$ and $\xi>0$ and use the critical Abelian-Higgs energy and boundary-sector convention in which $D_A=d-iA$, $B=dA$, $q$ tends in modulus to $\sqrt\xi$, and its exterior phase has winding $n\in\mathbb Z$. For every smooth finite-energy field pair $(A,q)$ in that sector,
$$E(A,q)\ge 2\pi\xi|n|.$$
For $n\ge0$, the exact identity is
$$E(A,q)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(|(D_{A,1}+iD_{A,2})q|^2+\frac{(B-e^2(\xi-|q|^2))^2}{2e^2}\right)dx_1dx_2+2\pi\xi n;$$
for $n\le0$, replace $D_{A,1}+iD_{A,2}$ by $D_{A,1}-iD_{A,2}$ and $B-e^2(\xi-|q|^2)$ by $B+e^2(\xi-|q|^2)$, with topological term $-2\pi\xi n$. The boundary-current term in the disk identity vanishes along a radius sequence derived from the finite-energy hypotheses. The fields reconstructed for any fixed divisor by the arbitrary-divisor plane theorem attain equality, are absolute transverse energy minima in their winding sector, have zero first variation under smooth compactly supported variations, and have nonnegative second variation in those directions. This does not assert uniqueness of minimizing fields across distinct divisors of the same degree.

declaration.title: Fixed-flux cylinders and uniform end-collar energy
declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix $e>0$, $\xi>0$, $\kappa=2e^2\xi$, and $n\in\mathbb Z$. For transverse fields on the oriented Euclidean plane, let $A_\perp=A_1dx_1+A_2dx_2$ be a smooth real one-form, let $q:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb C$ be smooth, set $D_iq=(\partial_i-iA_i)q$ and $B_{12}=\partial_1A_2-\partial_2A_1$, and define
$$E_\perp(A_\perp,q)=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left(\frac{B_{12}^2}{2e^2}+|D_1q|^2+|D_2q|^2+\frac{e^2}{2}(|q|^2-\xi)^2\right)dx_1dx_2.$$
For $L>0$, write $\Omega_L=\mathbb R^2\times[0,L]$ with coordinates $(x_1,x_2,z)$, let $\mathcal A=A_1dx_1+A_2dx_2+A_3dz$ be a smooth real connection one-form, let $q:\Omega_L\to\mathbb C$ be smooth up to the ends, set $F=d\mathcal A$, $D_\mu q=(\partial_\mu-iA_\mu)q$, and define the full static energy
$$\mathcal E_L(\mathcal A,q)=\int_0^L\!\int_{\mathbb R^2}\left[\frac{B_{12}^2+F_{31}^2+F_{32}^2}{2e^2}+|D_1q|^2+|D_2q|^2+|D_3q|^2+\frac{e^2}{2}(|q|^2-\xi)^2\right]dx_1dx_2dz,$$
where $B_{12}=F_{12}$. Call such a pair admissible of winding $n$ if its energy is finite, every transverse slice has finite $E_\perp$, and there are $R_0>0$ and smooth $\rho>0$ and real $2\pi$-periodic $\phi$ on $\{|x|>R_0\}\times[0,L]$ such that $q=\rho e^{i(n\theta+\phi)}$, with $\rho\to\sqrt\xi$ and $\phi\to0$ uniformly in $z$ and $\theta$ as $|x|\to\infty$. Require that each slice has flux $\lim_{R\to\infty}\int_{D_R}B_{12}\,dx_1dx_2=2\pi n$, and require the angular one-form condition
$$\lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_{0\le z\le L}\left|\int_{\partial D_R}(A_1dx_1+A_2dx_2-n\,d\theta)\right|=0$$
and zero radial magnetic-flux leakage, meaning that the integral of $F$ over the side $\partial D_R\times[0,L]$ tends to zero as $R\to\infty$. The infimum below is over admissible pairs with fixed smooth finite-energy end traces $p_0=(A^0,q^0)$ and $p_1=(A^1,q^1)$ in winding $n$. If their exterior phase is $n\theta+\phi_j$, first apply the globally smooth degree-zero gauge cleanup proved below and prescribe the resulting representatives as the end values. The common canonical exterior gauge means $q^j=\rho_j e^{in\theta}$ and $A^j-n\,d\theta\in L^2$ outside a disk, with the angular one-form limit above.

For any two such fixed end traces, the cleaned differences $q^1-q^0$ and $A^1-A^0$ lie in $L^2(\mathbb R^2)$. declaration.statement:
Let $e,\xi>0$, $\kappa=2e^2\xi$, and let $z_0\ne z_1$ be any two points of $\mathbb C$. For the positive-winding divisor $D=2[z_0]+[z_1]$, whose degree is $3$, the unique scalar solution satisfies
$$\Delta h+\kappa(1-e^h)=8\pi\delta_{z_0}+4\pi\delta_{z_1},\qquad h-4\log|z-z_0|\text{ extends smoothly at }z_0,\qquad h-2\log|z-z_1|\text{ extends smoothly at }z_1,\qquad h\to0\text{ at infinity},$$
with $h<0$ off $\{z_0,z_1\}$. For $P(z)=(z-z_0)^2(z-z_1)$ and $s=2\log|P|$, the reconstructed fields $q=\sqrt\xi e^{(h-s)/2}P$ and $A=-\tfrac12*d(h-s)$ are smooth, have flux $6\pi$, and attain transverse energy $6\pi\xi$. Separately, for each $n\in\mathbb Z$ and each effective divisor of degree $|n|$, the corresponding planar minimizer has signed flux $2\pi n$ and transverse energy $T_n=2\pi\xi|n|$. For fixed smooth end traces in winding $n$ and the same canonical exterior gauge, its cylinder infimum satisfies
$$T_nL\le\inf\mathcal E_L\le T_n(L-2\ell)+C_0+C_1\quad(L\ge2\ell),$$
for a fixed collar width $\ell>0$ and finite constants $C_0,C_1$ independent of $L$; matching minimizing end traces give the exact value $T_nL$. This is the fixed-flux variational estimate for the stated cylinder class.

declaration.title: Coherent module sheaves on complex manifolds
declaration.statement:
Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, so $X$ is a topological space and $\mathcal O_X$ is a sheaf of commutative rings. An $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaf $\mathcal F$ is **locally of finite type** if for every $x\in X$ there are an open neighborhood $U$ of $x$, a finite integer $r\ge0$, and sections $s_1,\ldots,s_r\in\mathcal F(U)$ such that their germs generate $\mathcal F_y$ as an $\mathcal O_{X,y}$-module for every $y\in U$.

For an open $V\subseteq X$, a finite integer $p\ge0$, and an $\mathcal O_X$-module morphism $\phi:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus p}\to\mathcal F|_V$, its **relation sheaf** is the kernel sheaf $\ker\phi$. The module sheaf $\mathcal F$ is **coherent** if it is locally of finite type and, for every such $V$, $p$, and $\phi$, the relation sheaf $\ker\phi$ is locally of finite type. Here $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus0}$ is the zero module sheaf.

In particular, for a finite tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_p\in\mathcal O_X(U)$, its holomorphic relation sheaf is the kernel of the morphism $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus p}\to\mathcal O_U$ that sends $(a_1,\ldots,a_p)$ to $\sum_{j=1}^p a_jf_j$. The structure sheaf is coherent when it is coherent as a module over itself. If $M$ is a complex manifold, an **analytic coherent module on $M$** means a coherent module sheaf over its sheaf $\mathcal O_M$ of holomorphic functions.

declaration.title: Oka coherence and local coherent free resolutions
declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complex manifold and let $\mathcal O_M$ be its sheaf of holomorphic functions. For every open $U\subseteq M$ and every finite tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_q\in\mathcal O_M(U)$, the relation sheaf
$$
\ker\!\left(\mathcal O_U^{\oplus q}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_U,\quad(a_1,\ldots,a_q)\longmapsto\sum_{j=1}^q a_jf_j\right)
$$
is locally of finite type: every point has a neighborhood on which one finite family of relation sections generates the relation stalk at every point. Consequently $\mathcal O_M$ is coherent. Coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module sheaves are closed under kernels, cokernels, and finite extensions. For every coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module $\mathcal F$, point $x\in M$, and finite integer $\ell\ge0$, there are a chart neighborhood $W$ of $x$ and finite ranks $p_0,\ldots,p_\ell$ for which
$$
\mathcal O_W^{\oplus p_\ell}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow\mathcal O_W^{\oplus p_0}\longrightarrow\mathcal F|_W\longrightarrow0
$$
is exact at $\mathcal F|_W$ and at every free term except the leftmost one. No exactness at the leftmost free term and no global analytic free resolution are asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Fix an integer $n\ge1$, put

formal power-series ring. For any finitely generated ideal $I\subseteq

maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R$, define its completion by

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $X$ be a scheme of finite type over $\mathbb C$
and let $x\in X$ be a closed point with residue field $\mathbb C$. Choose an
affine neighborhood of $x$ presented as (adding a dummy coordinate if needed)
$\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb C[w_1,\ldots,w_n]/I)$, with $n\ge1$, $I$ a
finitely generated polynomial ideal contained in $(w_1,\ldots,w_n)$, and $x$
the origin. Write
$A=(\mathbb C[w_1,\ldots,w_n]_{(w_1,\ldots,w_n)})/I\mathbb C[w_1,\ldots,w_n]_{(w_1,\ldots,w_n)}$.
On this chart, define the analytic local ring by extending the same ideal to
holomorphic germs,
$B=\mathbb C\{w_1,\ldots,w_n\}/I\mathbb C\{w_1,\ldots,w_n\}$; this quotient
retains the given scheme structure, including nilpotents. For a local ring $R$
with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R$, let
$\widehat R=\varprojlim_{k\ge1}R/\mathfrak m_R^k$.

Its induced map $\widehat A\to\widehat B$ is an isomorphism, with both
completions canonically identified with

$A$-module $M$, the map $M\to M\otimes_A B$ is injective, and the quotient
$B/A$ is a flat $A$-module. These are local-ring conclusions; no relative
direct-image comparison is asserted.

declaration.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $N\ge0$, let $U$ be an open neighborhood
of $x\in\mathbb C^N$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent analytic
$\mathcal O_U$-module. A coordinate polydisc centered at $x$ means a set
$$W=\{z\in\mathbb C^N:|z_j-x_j|<r_j\ (1\le j\le N)\},\qquad r_j>0,$$
contained in $U$. There is such a $W$ for which the following hold.

For every nonempty coordinate polydisc $D\subseteq W$ and every integer
$q>0$, ordinary derived-functor sheaf cohomology satisfies
$$H^q(D,\mathcal F|_D)=0.$$
On each such $D$, scalar sheaf cohomology of $\mathcal O_D$ is computed by the
global smooth Dolbeault complex. Here $\mathcal A_D^{0,q}$ is the sheaf of
smooth complex-valued differential forms of type $(0,q)$ and $\bar\partial$ is
the Dolbeault differential:
$$\Gamma(D,\mathcal A_D^{0,0})\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\cdots \xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\Gamma(D,\mathcal A_D^{0,N}),$$
and in particular $H^q(D,\mathcal O_D)=0$ for $q>0$. The polydisc $W$ may be
chosen inside a neighborhood on which there is a partial finite-rank free resolution
$$\mathcal O_W^{p_\ell}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow \mathcal O_W^{p_0}\longrightarrow\mathcal F|_W\longrightarrow0$$
that is exact at $\mathcal F|_W$ and at every free term except possibly the
leftmost one, with $\ell=2N+1>2N$. No exactness at the leftmost term and no
global free resolution are asserted.

$$H_D=D\cap\{z_1=0\},\qquad i:H_D\hookrightarrow D,$$
and set $\mathcal Q=\mathcal O_D/(z_1)\mathcal O_D$. Then $\mathcal Q$ is
coherent and restriction to the hyperplane induces an isomorphism
$$\mathcal Q\cong i_*\mathcal O_{H_D}.$$
The multiplication sequence
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_D\xrightarrow{\ \cdot z_1\ }\mathcal O_D\longrightarrow\mathcal Q\longrightarrow0$$
is exact, and
$$\Gamma(D,\mathcal Q)\cong\mathcal O(H_D),\qquad H^q(D,\mathcal Q)=0\quad(q>0).$$
In particular the global sections are the actual quotient
$\mathcal O(D)/z_1\mathcal O(D)$, identified with holomorphic functions on
$H_D$. All cohomology here is ordinary derived global-sections cohomology;
no small-neighborhood restriction or general coherent Stein vanishing is assumed.

declaration.title: Fréchet spaces used in analytic coherent cohomology
declaration.statement:
A **Fréchet space** over $\mathbb C$ is a complex vector space $E$ with a Hausdorff locally convex vector-space topology generated by a separating countable family of seminorms $(p_n)_{n\ge1}$ and complete for its seminorm uniformity. Explicitly, use the translation-invariant compatible metric
$$d(x,y)=\sum_{n\ge1}2^{-n}\min\{1,p_n(x-y)\},$$
and require that this metric is complete. A seminorm is a function $p:E\to[0,\infty)$ satisfying $p(x+y)\le p(x)+p(y)$ and $p(cx)=|c|p(x)$ for $x,y\in E$ and $c\in\mathbb C$; separating means that for $x\ne0$ some $p_n(x)>0$. Locally convex means that every point has a neighborhood basis of convex sets. One may replace the defining family by the increasing family of its finite maxima.

Completeness here always refers to this vector-space uniformity. A sequence is Cauchy for the displayed metric exactly when it is Cauchy for every defining seminorm: each individual metric summand controls that seminorm at sufficiently small distances, and conversely the geometric tail of the metric series plus finitely many seminorm estimates controls the metric. Thus a seminorm-Cauchy series used in the accompanying proofs converges in $E$. The zero vector space is included, with its unique metric. This is the usual complete metrizable locally convex Fréchet convention.

declaration.title: Presentation and Čech quotient topologies for coherent analytic sections
declaration.statement:
Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complex manifold, let $\mathcal O_M$ be its sheaf of holomorphic functions, and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module sheaf. On an open set $V$ contained in a coordinate chart and in a neighborhood with a finite presentation $\mathcal O_V^{p_1}\to\mathcal O_V^{p_0}\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathcal F|_V\to0$, where $p_0,p_1$ are finite nonnegative ranks, require that the section map $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V^{p_0})\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)$ is surjective. Give $\mathcal O(V)^{p_0}$ the compact-convergence topology generated by the seminorms $f\mapsto\sup_{z\in K}\lVert f(z)\rVert$ for compact $K\subset V$, and give $\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)$ the quotient topology induced by that surjection. On any open subset covered by countably many such sets, use the topology of the closed subspace of the product of their local section spaces consisting of compatible families. For a finite ordered open cover $\mathcal U=(U_i)$ whose nonempty finite intersections have these section topologies, give each Čech cochain space

$$C^q(\mathcal U,\mathcal F):=\prod_{i_0<\cdots<i_q}\Gamma(U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_q},\mathcal F),\qquad (\delta c)_{i_0\cdots i_{q+1}}=\sum_{\nu=0}^{q+1}(-1)^\nu c_{i_0\cdots\widehat{i_\nu}\cdots i_{q+1}}\big|_{U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_{q+1}}}.$$

the finite-product topology, give its cocycle space the subspace topology, and give the quotient of cocycles by coboundaries the Čech quotient topology. The accompanying Fréchet-quotient lemma proves local chart and presentation independence; the compact projective-space finiteness theorem proves independence of its admissible finite acyclic cover topology.

declaration.title: Laurent decomposition of holomorphic functions on the punctured plane
declaration.statement:
Let $\mathbb C^*=\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$. For every holomorphic function $f\in\mathcal O(\mathbb C^*)$, there are unique entire functions $g,h\in\mathcal O(\mathbb C)$ and a unique scalar $a\in\mathbb C$ such that
$$
f(z)=g(z)+a z^{-1}+z^{-2}h(1/z)\qquad(z\in\mathbb C^*).
$$

declaration.title: Finite-dimensional coherent cohomology on compact projective space
declaration.statement:
Assume full AC. For $0\le r\le3$, let $P^r(\mathbb C)$ be the space of complex lines in $\mathbb C^{r+1}$ with its usual complex-manifold structure, and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent analytic module over its holomorphic structure sheaf. Write $H^q(P^r(\mathbb C),\mathcal F)$ for the $q$th right-derived global-sections group. Then every such group is finite-dimensional over $\mathbb C$ for every integer $q\ge0$.

For its topology, a coordinate polydisc means the image in a holomorphic chart of a product of open coordinate discs. Take any finite ordered cover $\mathcal U=(U_i)$ by relatively compact coordinate polydiscs such that each nonempty finite intersection $U_I$ has a finite presentation $\mathcal O_{U_I}^{p_1}\to\mathcal O_{U_I}^{p_0}\to\mathcal F|_{U_I}\to0$ whose global section map is surjective, and such that $H^q(U_I,\mathcal F|_{U_I})=0$ for every $q>0$. Give $\mathcal O(U_I)^{p_0}$ compact-convergence topology and $\Gamma(U_I,\mathcal F)$ the induced quotient topology. Set $C^k(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=\prod_{i_0<\cdots<i_k}\Gamma(U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_k},\mathcal F)$ with finite-product topology and differential
$$
(\delta c)_{i_0\cdots i_{k+1}}=\sum_{\nu=0}^{k+1}(-1)^\nu c_{i_0\cdots\widehat{i_\nu}\cdots i_{k+1}}\big|_{U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_{k+1}}}.
$$
Give the cocycle space its subspace topology and its quotient by coboundaries the Čech quotient topology. These cohomology groups are Hausdorff in that topology, which is independent of the chosen finite cover and local presentations.
declaration.strategy: Build a finite nested acyclic polydisc cover and apply the compact Fréchet-complex theorem.
declaration.axiom_base: ZF + full AC and the exact planned cross-batch suppliers as conditional inputs; no physical premise.

declaration.title: Finite-support coherent sheaves have only finitely many sections
declaration.statement: Assume full AC. Let $0\le r\le3$ and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent analytic module on $P^r(\mathbb C)$ whose support $S:=\{x\in P^r(\mathbb C):\mathcal F_x\ne0\}$ is finite. Assume each stalk $\mathcal F_x$ is finite-dimensional over $\mathbb C$, and put $\ell:=\sum_{x\in S}\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal F_x$. Then $H^0(P^r(\mathbb C),\mathcal F)\cong\bigoplus_{x\in S}\mathcal F_x$ has complex dimension $\ell$, and $H^q(P^r(\mathbb C),\mathcal F)=0$ for every $q>0$. Here $H^q$ is ordinary right-derived sheaf cohomology and $\ell$ is the total complex length of the finite-support sheaf.

declaration.title: Compact coherent cohomology can be finite and nonzero
declaration.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $P^1(\mathbb C)$ have standard charts $U_0=\{Z_0\ne0\}$ and $U_1=\{Z_1\ne0\}$, with coordinates $z=Z_1/Z_0$ on $U_0\cong\mathbb C$ and $w=Z_0/Z_1=1/z$ on $U_1\cong\mathbb C$. Let $\mathcal O(-2)$ be the projective twisting line bundle with local frames satisfying $e_1=z^{-2}e_0$ on $U_0\cap U_1\cong\mathbb C^*$. Then
$$
H^1(P^1(\mathbb C),\mathcal O(-2))\cong\mathbb C.
$$
Thus finite-dimensionality of compact coherent cohomology does not imply vanishing of positive-degree cohomology.

declaration.title: Projective twisting line bundles by coordinate transitions
declaration.statement:
For $r\ge1$, let $\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C)$ be the set of complex lines in
$\mathbb C^{r+1}$, with its quotient complex-manifold structure, and write
$[Z_0:\cdots:Z_r]$ for the line through a nonzero vector
$(Z_0,\ldots,Z_r)$. For $i\in\{0,\ldots,r\}$ set
$U_i=\{[Z_0:\cdots:Z_r]:Z_i\ne0\}$; its standard coordinates are the ratios
$Z_j/Z_i$ for $j\ne i$. For each integer $k$, the **projective twisting line
bundle** $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(k)$ is obtained by gluing the trivial
holomorphic line bundles $U_i\times\mathbb C$ with local frames $e_i^{(k)}$
and transition rule
$$e_j^{(k)}=\left(\frac{Z_j}{Z_i}\right)^k e_i^{(k)}\quad\text{on }U_i\cap U_j.$$
The transition factors are holomorphic and nowhere zero on the overlaps, with
$g_{ii}=1$, $g_{ij}=g_{ji}^{-1}$, and $g_{ij}g_{j\ell}=g_{i\ell}$ on every
triple overlap; hence they define a holomorphic line bundle. The sheaf
$\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(k)$ assigns to an open set the holomorphic sections of
this bundle, and $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}:=\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(0)$ is the
structure sheaf.
declaration.strategy: Direct transition-function gluing with a full cocycle check.
