declaration.title: Laurent–Čech cohomology of the projective coordinate cover
declaration.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. For $0\le r\le3$, let $P^r$ be the complex
projective space $(\mathbb C^{r+1}\setminus\{0\})/\mathbb C^\times$ with its
quotient complex-manifold structure; for $r=0$, $P^0$ is a point. For $r\ge1$ use the
standard homogeneous-coordinate cover $U_i=\{[Z_0:\cdots:Z_r]:Z_i\ne0\}$,
$0\le i\le r$. For nonempty $I\subseteq\{0,\ldots,r\}$ write
$U_I=\bigcap_{i\in I}U_i$. For $r\ge1$ and $k\in\mathbb Z$, let
$\mathcal O(k)$ be the line bundle with local frames satisfying
$e_j^{(k)}=(Z_j/Z_i)^k e_i^{(k)}$ on $U_i\cap U_j$; write
$\mathcal O=\mathcal O(0)$ and $\mathbb C^*=\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$. Analytic
sheaf cohomology $H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ is the $q$th right-derived
global-sections group of the abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$. For this ordered cover
and a sheaf $\mathcal G$, define
$$C^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal G)=\prod_{|I|=p+1}\mathcal G(U_I),\qquad (\delta c)_{i_0\cdots i_{p+1}}=\sum_{\nu=0}^{p+1}(-1)^\nu c_{i_0\cdots\widehat{i_\nu}\cdots i_{p+1}}|_{U_{i_0\cdots i_{p+1}}},$$
for $0\le p\le r$, with $C^p=0$ otherwise and increasing indices;
fixed-cover Čech cohomology is the cohomology of this complex. A mixed
Laurent–Taylor series is **normally convergent** when it
converges absolutely and uniformly on every compact product subset of its
domain. For $r\ge1$, every
$U_I$ is biholomorphic to
$\mathbb C^{r+1-|I|}\times(\mathbb C^*)^{|I|-1}$. For every integer $k$,
each section on $U_I$, in a standard local frame, has a unique normally
convergent mixed Laurent–Taylor expansion indexed by exponent tuples
$m=(m_0,\ldots,m_r)\in\mathbb Z^{r+1}$ with $\sum_i m_i=k$; its coefficient
occurs on $U_I$ exactly when $N(m):=\{i:m_i<0\}\subseteq I$. Restrictions
preserve each coefficient. In the ordered-cover Čech complex, every mode with
nonempty proper $N(m)$ has the cochain contraction, for $c\in C^p$ and an
output index $I$ of size $p$, given by $(h_mc)_I=0$ if $j\in I$ and
$(h_mc)_I=(-1)^{\#\{i\in I:i<j\}}c_{I\cup\{j\}}$ if $j\notin I$, where
$j$ is the least index outside $N(m)$; the resulting subseries converge
locally uniformly on the output intersections. The fixed-cover Čech cohomology
is canonically the analytic sheaf cohomology whenever that cover is acyclic for
the coefficient sheaf. For $k\in\{0,-1,-r-1\}$, the restricted sheaf
$\mathcal O(k)|_{U_I}$ has $H^q(U_I,\mathcal O(k)|_{U_I})=0$ for every integer
$q>0$, so the cover is acyclic for these three sheaves and the comparison
applies. Consequently, for $0\le r\le3$,
$$H^0(P^r,\mathcal O)=\mathbb C,\qquad H^q(P^r,\mathcal O)=0\quad(q>0),$$
and for $1\le r\le3$,
$$H^0(P^r,\mathcal O(-1))=0,\qquad H^r(P^r,\mathcal O(-r-1))\cong\mathbb C.$$
declaration.strategy: Prove acyclic projective intersections by the explicit Hartogs-pseudoconvex boundary function, then derive and contract the normally convergent Laurent–Čech modes.

declaration.title: Projective Dolbeault comparison and scalar structure-sheaf cohomology
declaration.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $r\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, let
$X=\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C)=(\mathbb C^{r+1}\setminus\{0\})/\mathbb C^\times$
with its standard quotient complex-manifold structure, and let $E\to X$ be a
holomorphic vector bundle of finite rank.
Write $\mathcal O(E)$ for its sheaf of holomorphic sections, and let
$H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ denote the $q$th right-derived global-sections group of an
abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$. For
$0\le q\le r$, let $\mathcal A^{0,q}(E)$ be the sheaf of smooth sections of
$\Lambda^{0,q}T^*X\otimes_{\mathbb C}E$, where $\Lambda^{0,q}T^*X$ is the
$q$th exterior power of the antiholomorphic cotangent subbundle. In a
holomorphic local frame of $E$,
define $\bar\partial_E$ by applying the scalar $\bar\partial$ to each
coefficient form; holomorphic transition matrices make this definition
independent of frame, and $\bar\partial_E^2=0$. Set
$\mathcal A^{0,q}(E)=0$ for $q>r$ and define
$$H^q_{\bar\partial}(X,E):=\frac{\ker\bigl(\bar\partial_E:\Gamma(X,\mathcal A^{0,q}(E))\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal A^{0,q+1}(E))\bigr)}{\operatorname{im}\bigl(\bar\partial_E:\Gamma(X,\mathcal A^{0,q-1}(E))\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal A^{0,q}(E))\bigr)},$$
where $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$ denotes the group of sections of $\mathcal F$ over
$X$ and the denominator is zero for $q=0$. For every $q\ge0$, the canonical
comparison induced by the smooth Dolbeault resolution is an isomorphism
$$H^q(X,\mathcal O(E))\cong H^q_{\bar\partial}(X,E).$$
For the trivial line bundle $E=\mathcal O_X$ and $0\le r\le3$, this gives
$$H^0(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O)=\mathbb C,\qquad H^q(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O)=0\quad(q>0).$$
The scalar cohomology conclusion is obtained by the direct Laurent–Čech
calculation on the standard projective cover; no GAGA theorem, Kähler Hodge
theorem in dimensions above one, or arbitrary-coherent projective vanishing is
assumed.
declaration.strategy: Resolve the holomorphic-section sheaf by smooth bundle-valued Dolbeault forms, apply the acyclic-resolution theorem, and use the local scalar Laurent–Čech supplier.

declaration.title: Scalar structure-sheaf cohomology of $\mathbb P^2$
declaration.statement:
Assume full AC and let $X$ be the complex lines in $\mathbb C^3$, equivalently
$X=\mathbb P^2(\mathbb C)=(\mathbb C^3\setminus\{0\})/\mathbb C^\times$.
Use the standard charts $U_i=\{[Z_0:Z_1:Z_2]:Z_i\ne0\}$ for $i=0,1,2$,
ordered $0<1<2$. Let $\mathcal O_X$ be the sheaf of holomorphic functions on
$X$. For each nonempty $I\subseteq\{0,1,2\}$ set
$U_I=\bigcap_{i\in I}U_i$ and define
$$C^p=\prod_{|I|=p+1}\mathcal O_X(U_I)\quad(0\le p\le2),\qquad (\delta c)_{i_0\cdots i_{p+1}}=\sum_{\nu=0}^{p+1}(-1)^\nu c_{i_0\cdots\widehat{i_\nu}\cdots i_{p+1}}|_{U_{i_0\cdots i_{p+1}}},$$
with increasing indices, and $C^p=0$ for $p<0$ or $p>2$; Čech cohomology
means the cohomology of this complex.
For $m=(m_0,m_1,m_2)\in\mathbb Z^3$ with
$m_0+m_1+m_2=0$, write $N(m)=\{i:m_i<0\}$ and call the degree-zero
homogeneous Laurent monomial the mode $m$; in frame $e_i^{(0)}$ its coefficient
is $\prod_{j\ne i}(Z_j/Z_i)^{m_j}$. A mode occurs in the Čech component on
$U_I$ exactly when $N(m)\subseteq I$. The zero mode contributes one copy of
$\mathbb C$ in degree zero, every nonzero mode contracts, and therefore
$$H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=\mathbb C,\qquad H^q(X,\mathcal O_X)=0\quad(q>0).$$
The contraction is the ordered three-chart Laurent calculation and its
subseries converge locally uniformly on every output intersection.
For $0\le q\le2$, let $\mathcal A_X^{0,q}$ be the sheaf of smooth
antiholomorphic $q$-forms, with differential the $\bar\partial$ part of the
exterior derivative, and set the terms to zero for $q>2$. The same groups are
the cohomology of the global complex $\Gamma(X,\mathcal A_X^{0,\bullet})$ by
the canonical projective Dolbeault comparison.
declaration.strategy: Display the three-chart degree-zero mode contraction and verify its finite zero-mode complex.

declaration.title: Negative twists obstruct untwisted projective A and B
declaration.statement:
Assume full AC. For each integer $1\le r\le3$, let $X$ be the set of complex
lines in $\mathbb C^{r+1}$, equivalently
$X=\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C)=(\mathbb C^{r+1}\setminus\{0\})/\mathbb C^\times$,
with standard cover $U_i=\{[Z_0:\cdots:Z_r]:Z_i\ne0\}$ and twisting line bundle
$\mathcal O(k)$ defined by $e_j^{(k)}=(Z_j/Z_i)^k e_i^{(k)}$.
For every nonempty $I\subseteq\{0,\ldots,r\}$ write $U_I=\bigcap_{i\in I}U_i$.
For $0\le p\le r$ set $C^p(k)=\prod_{|I|=p+1}\mathcal O(k)(U_I)$ and put
$C^p(k)=0$ outside this range. Use the increasing-index alternating
restriction differential; $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal O(k))$ denotes the
cohomology of this complex. For a degree-$k$
Laurent mode $m=(m_0,\ldots,m_r)\in\mathbb Z^{r+1}$, write
$N(m)=\{i:m_i<0\}$. A mode can represent a global section only if
$N(m)=\varnothing$, and it can survive in top Čech degree only if
$N(m)=\{0,\ldots,r\}$. The degree constraints $\sum_i m_i=-1$ and
$\sum_i m_i=-r-1$ therefore give, respectively,
$$H^0(X,\mathcal O(-1))=0,\qquad H^r(X,\mathcal O(-r-1))\cong\mathbb C.$$
For a holomorphic line bundle $L$, let $\mathcal A^{0,q}(L)$ for $0\le q\le r$
be the sheaf of smooth sections of $\Lambda^{0,q}T^*X\otimes L$, set the terms
to zero for $q>r$, and define $\bar\partial_L$ coefficientwise in holomorphic
local frames. Write $H^q_{\bar\partial}(X,L)$ for the cohomology of the global
complex. The canonical projective Dolbeault
comparison identifies the displayed sheaf groups with the corresponding
global Dolbeault groups.
Every fiber of the line bundle $\mathcal O(-1)$ is one-dimensional. A line
bundle is globally generated when its global sections evaluate surjectively
onto each fiber; since $H^0(X,\mathcal O(-1))=0$, its evaluation map is zero
and is not surjective. These are analytic cohomology calculations by
degree-weighted Laurent modes and the ordered-cover Čech comparison; no GAGA
identification is used.
declaration.strategy: Compute degree-weighted Laurent modes and show the negative twists obstruct global generation without GAGA.

declaration.title: Positive incidence geometry for the coupled Penrose transform
declaration.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.
declaration.statement:
Let $S^4={X\in\mathbb R^5:|X|=1}$ have its unit round metric and the orientation which, on the stereographic chart $S^4\setminus\{\infty\}\cong\mathbb R^4$, is $dx_0\wedge dx_1\wedge dx_2\wedge dx_3$. Put $z_1=x_0+ix_1$, $z_2=x_2+ix_3$, and $r^2=|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2$; in these coordinates the metric is $g=4(1+r^2)^{-2}\sum_{\mu=0}^3dx_\mu^2$. Identify $\mathbb H^2$ with $\mathbb C^4$ using a right quaternionic structure $j$ with $j^2=-1$, put $Z=\mathbb CP^3=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)$, and define $\pi:Z\to\mathbb HP^1=S^4$ by $\pi(\ell)=\ell+j\ell$ for a complex line $\ell\subset\mathbb H^2$. Its fibres are projective lines $L_x\cong\mathbb CP^1$. In homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$, the fibre over finite $z=(z_1,z_2)$ is the line

$$\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2,\qquad \mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2,$$

and the fibre over infinity is $L_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$. Give $Z$ the Fubini–Study metric induced by the standard Hermitian metric on $\mathbb C^4$ and give $\mathcal O_Z(-2)$ its induced Hermitian metric. On the incidence chart $\lambda_1\ne0$, set $t=\lambda_2/\lambda_1$, $\mu_1/\lambda_1=z_1-\bar z_2t$, and $\mu_2/\lambda_1=z_2+\bar z_1t$. The horizontal complex directions of type $(0,1)$ are spanned by

$$H_1=\partial_{\bar z_1}-t\partial_{z_2},\qquad H_2=\partial_{\bar z_2}+t\partial_{z_1};$$

They annihilate the displayed holomorphic coordinates. Together with $\partial_{\bar t}$ they form a direct local frame of $T^{0,1}Z$. Here $H_i$ are the constant-$t$ chart lifts; their projected complex alpha-plane is intrinsic, but this chart splitting is not asserted to be the global metric splitting. Globally let $V^{0,1}=\ker(d\pi)\cap T^{0,1}Z$, and let $H^{0,1}$ be its Fubini–Study orthogonal complement. Its lifts project to the same alpha-planes and may differ from the displayed $H_i$ by vertical components. All global horizontal/vertical form decompositions use this orthogonal splitting; local computations may use the displayed constant-$t$ splitting after retaining the resulting frame and normalization factors. The second projective chart supplies the same alpha-plane at $t=\infty$. The line bundle $\mathcal O_Z(-1)$ is the tautological holomorphic line bundle and $\mathcal O_Z(-2)=\mathcal O_Z(-1)^{\otimes2}$.
declaration.axiom_base: ZF

declaration.title: Injective fibre-harmonic edge for coupled Penrose cohomology
declaration.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.
declaration.statement:
Assume full AC and the following analytic comparison: for $r\in\{0,1,2,3\}$, every finite-rank holomorphic vector bundle $G$ on $X=\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C)$ has a canonical isomorphism $H^q(X,\mathcal O(G))\cong H^q_{\bar\partial}(X,G)$ for every $q\ge0$, and for $G=\mathcal O_X$ one has $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=\mathbb C$ and $H^q(X,\mathcal O_X)=0$ for $q>0$. Let $E\to S^4$ be a smooth finite-rank Hermitian bundle with smooth unitary connection $A$, and let $F$ be a holomorphic bundle on $Z=\mathbb CP^3$ smoothly identified with $\pi^*E$ so that its Dolbeault operator is the ordinary vertical Dolbeault operator and the connection-horizontal alpha-plane operator from the incidence definition. Fibrewise harmonic projection of a global Dolbeault representative defines a linear map

$$\mathcal P_A:H^1(Z,F\otimes\mathcal O_Z(-2))\longrightarrow\Gamma(S^4,E).$$

Every global closed representative $\alpha$ has a unique decomposition $\alpha=\alpha_H+s\sigma+\bar\partial_F\gamma$, where $s=\mathcal P_A[\alpha]$, $\alpha_H$ is horizontal, $\sigma$ is the normalized fibre-harmonic generator, and the vertical correction $\gamma$ is smooth and glues over the base. The map is well defined and injective. The comparison is supplied by the local analytic Dolbeault-resolution theorem; no algebraic-to-analytic comparison is assumed.

declaration.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.

declaration.title: First-order families of positive real linear monads
declaration.statement:
Use the dual-number scheme, relative projective-space charts, finite locally free sheaves and twisting sheaves in [[def-dual-numbers-scheme]], [[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]], [[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]] and [[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]], with the inherited AC convention for the twisting-sheaf construction. Let $A=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ and equip it with the conjugate-linear involution $\overline{a+b\epsilon}=\bar a+\bar b\epsilon$. Its reduction is the quotient map $A\to\mathbb C$ sending $\epsilon$ to zero. For every $r\in\mathbb R$, the map $\rho_r:A\to A$ fixing $\mathbb C$ and sending $\epsilon$ to $r\epsilon$ preserves this involution.

A **first-order family of positive real linear monads of dimensions $(k,2k+N,k)$** is a three-term complex of locally free sheaves on $\mathbb P^3_A=\operatorname{Proj}A[\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2]$,
$$\mathcal O(-1)\otimes_A U_A\xrightarrow{\alpha_A}\mathcal O\otimes_A S_A\xrightarrow{\beta_A}\mathcal O(1)\otimes_A U'_A,$$
where $U_A,S_A,U'_A$ are free $A$-modules of ranks $k,2k+N,k$, each map is homogeneous linear in $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)$, $\beta_A\alpha_A=0$, $\alpha_A$ is a locally split injection, $\beta_A$ is a locally split surjection, and $F_A=\ker\beta_A/\operatorname{im}\alpha_A$ is locally free of rank $N$. The two short exact sequences defined by the kernel and image split locally; hence their formation and the middle cohomology commute with reduction $A\to\mathbb C$. The reduced complex is therefore an ordinary linear monad on $\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C$.

The **first-order locally-free/base-change range** used here further requires that $H^0(\mathbb P^3_A,F_A)$ is a free $A$-module and reduction identifies it with $H^0(\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C,F_0)$, where $F_0=F_A\otimes_A\mathbb C$. The image in $S_A$ of the map from the four coefficient copies of $U_A$ under $\alpha_A$ is a direct summand and reduces to the corresponding coefficient-image subspace of $S_0$. For each real twistor line $\ell$ in the reduced projective space, the restriction of $F_A$ to $\ell_A=\ell\times_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Spec}A$ is trivial of rank $N$, and reduction identifies its global sections with $H^0(\ell,F_0|_\ell)$. These conditions state the precise global, coefficient-image, and line-section base-change range; no arbitrary analytic family or algebraization assertion is included.

Extend the coordinate map $j(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$ semilinearly using the involution of $A$; its projective action $\sigma$ is an involution and preserves each real twistor line. A **real twistor line** means the projectivization of a $j$-invariant complex two-plane in $\mathbb C^4$. Equivalently these are the finite lines
$$\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2,\qquad \mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2,\qquad (z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2,$$
together with $\ell_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$. Indeed a nonzero vector $v$ and $jv$ are complex-linearly independent because $j^2=-1$; they span the invariant plane. If its $\lambda$ projection is nonzero, that projection and its quaternionic conjugate give an invertible two-by-two matrix with determinant $|\lambda_1|^2+|\lambda_2|^2$, so it has exactly the displayed graph form; if the projection is zero the plane is the $\mu$ plane. Each fixed-line restriction above means the corresponding constant thickening $\ell_A$.

A first-order real structure on the monad is a nondegenerate holomorphic $\sigma$-Hermitian pairing on $F_A$, linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, whose reduction induces a positive-definite Hermitian form on the holomorphic section space of every real line. A unitary framing at infinity is an isometric isomorphism $F_A|_{\ell_\infty}\cong (A\otimes_\mathbb C W)\otimes_A\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}$, where $\ell_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ has its standard Hermitian form.

An isomorphism of such families is an $A$-linear chain isomorphism that intertwines the $\sigma$-Hermitian pairings and the framing. No order or positivity is assigned to elements of $A$ with nonzero nilpotent part: positivity is required only after reduction. The base-change scope in this definition consists exactly of reduction $\epsilon\mapsto0$ and the involution-preserving maps $\rho_r$ for real $r$.

declaration.title: Chern character and charge normalization of a linear twistor monad
declaration.axiom_base: ZF + full AC inherited from the named projective-cohomology and characteristic-class suppliers.
declaration.statement:
Let $\mathcal F$ be the locally free algebraic middle cohomology of a linear monad
$$
\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(-1)^{\oplus k}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}^{\oplus(2k+N)}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1)^{\oplus k}
$$
on $\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C$, with exactness at both ends. Let $H_{\rm alg}=c_1^{\rm alg}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1))$ in the Chow ring and let $H_{\rm top}=c_1^{\rm top}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1))$ in singular cohomology. The hyperplane cycle map identifies $H_{\rm alg}$ with $H_{\rm top}$; write $H$ for either class in the corresponding formula. The algebraic Chern character is $N-kH_{\rm alg}^2$, the algebraic first Chern class is zero, the algebraic second Chern class is $kH_{\rm alg}^2$, and the algebraic Euler characteristic is $N-2k$. The underlying topological bundle has total Chern class $1+kH_{\rm top}^2$ through degree six and topological Chern character $N-kH_{\rm top}^2$.

Identify $\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C$ with the twistor space of $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ by the quaternionic structure whose invariant lines are the real incidence lines in the positive stereographic coordinates. Let $\pi:\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C\to S^4$ be the resulting fibration, orient each fiber by its complex orientation, orient the base so the incidence chart followed by the fiber orientation gives the complex orientation of $\mathbb P^3$, and let $u\in H^4(S^4;\mathbb Z)$ be the positive point class. Then $\pi^*u=H^2$. Consequently, if the underlying topological bundle of $\mathcal F$ is $\pi^*E$ for a rank-$N$ complex bundle $E\to S^4$ with $c_1(E)=0$, then $c_2(E)=ku$ and $\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=k$.

declaration.title: Exact holomorphic hyperplane sequences for negative twists
declaration.statement:
For $r\ge1$, let $H=\{[Z_0:\cdots:Z_r]\in\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C):Z_0=0\}$ and
let $i:H\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C)$ be inclusion. For every
integer $m$, the homogeneous coordinate $Z_0$ defines an exact sequence of
holomorphic sheaves
$$
0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(m-1)
\xrightarrow{\ \cdot Z_0\ }\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(m)
\longrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_H(m)\longrightarrow0.
$$
Here $i_*\mathcal O_H(m)$ assigns to an open set $U$ the holomorphic
sections of $\mathcal O_H(m)$ on $U\cap H$. Twisting the sequence with
$m=0$ by $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(-1)$ gives, in particular,
$$
0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(-2)
\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(-1)
\longrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_H(-1)\longrightarrow0.
$$

declaration.title: Raw monad full rank and ADHM regularity
declaration.statement:
Let $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$, and let $B_1,B_2\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, $J:V\to W$ satisfy $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. Define for $z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$
$$
a_z=(B_1-z_1,\ B_2-z_2,\ J)^T:V\to V\oplus V\oplus W,\qquad
b_z^\dagger=(-B_2+z_2,\ B_1-z_1,\ I):V\oplus V\oplus W\to V.
$$
Then $a_z$ is injective for every $z$ if and only if the datum is costable, and $b_z^\dagger$ is surjective for every $z$ if and only if the datum is stable, where stability and costability have their word-span and invariant-subspace meanings. For the homogeneous linear maps
$$
\alpha=(B_1\lambda_1-B_2^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_1,\ B_2\lambda_1+B_1^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_2,\ J\lambda_1+I^\dagger\lambda_2)^T,
$$
$$
\beta=(-C,\ A,\ I\lambda_1-J^\dagger\lambda_2),\quad
A=B_1\lambda_1-B_2^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_1,\quad
C=B_2\lambda_1+B_1^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_2,
$$
fiberwise injectivity of $\alpha$ and surjectivity of $\beta$ on $\mathbb P^3$ imply regularity. Conversely, if the datum is regular and both raw moment maps vanish, then these homogeneous maps are fiberwise injective and surjective and form a linear bundle monad.

declaration.axiom_base: ZF + full AC inherited from the planned analytic scalar-cohomology supplier; the hyperplane-sequence deductions use no additional choice.
declaration.statement: Assume full AC. Then the analytic sheaf cohomology of $\mathcal O(-1)$ vanishes in every degree on $\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C)$ for $1\le r\le3$. The analytic cohomology of $\mathcal O(-2)$ vanishes in every degree on $\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C)$ for $r=2,3$. declaration.title: Unique chain lifting and sigma-Hermitian monad duality
declaration.axiom_base: ZF + full AC inherited through the analytic scalar-cohomology input; the finite matrix duality is choice-free.
declaration.statement:
Let $\mathbb P^3(\mathbb C)$ carry the antiholomorphic coordinate involution $\sigma([\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2])=[-\bar\lambda_2:\bar\lambda_1:-\bar\mu_2:\bar\mu_1]$. A linear monad is a locally split exact complex at its ends
$$
\mathcal O(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal O\otimes S\xrightarrow{\beta}\mathcal O(1)\otimes U'
$$
with locally free middle cohomology $F=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$, where $U,S,U'$ are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces. For a degree-one matrix $P(z)$ put $P^\#(z)=P(jz)^\dagger$ and define the signed dual monad $D(M):(U')^*\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\xrightarrow{-\beta^\#}S^*\otimes\mathcal O\xrightarrow{\alpha^\#}U^*\otimes\mathcal O(1)$; its cohomology is denoted $D(F)$, and dualizing twice uses $(P^\#)^\#=-P$ and $D^2(M)=M$. By a nondegenerate holomorphic $\sigma$-Hermitian self-pairing we mean an isomorphism $h_F:F\to D(F)$ that is linear in its first variable, conjugate-linear in its second, and fixed by this bidual operation. Assume $H^0(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O)=\mathbb C$, $H^q(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O(-1))=0$ for every $q\ge0$, and $H^q(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O(-2))=0$ for $q=0,1,2$. For any two such monads, every holomorphic morphism of their middle cohomology bundles lifts to a unique constant chain map between the monads. In particular, for a monad with a nondegenerate holomorphic $\sigma$-Hermitian self-pairing, the unique lift is a chain isomorphism with Hermitian middle map $H=H^\dagger$ and normalized identities
$$
\beta(z)=\alpha(jz)^\dagger H,\qquad \beta(jz)^\dagger=-H\alpha(z),
$$
where $j(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$ and the end spaces are identified by the lifted pairing.

Suppose a nondegenerate Hermitian form $H$ on $S$, linear in the first variable, satisfies $\beta(z)=\alpha(jz)^\dagger H$ for $j(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$. declaration.title: Positive real linear monad normal forms
declaration.axiom_base: ZF + full AC inherited through the named analytic cohomology and finite-dimensional suppliers.
declaration.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $k\ge0$ and
$N\ge2$. On $\mathbb P^3(\mathbb C)$ with homogeneous coordinates
$(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)$, set
$$j(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2) =(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1), \qquad \sigma([z])=[jz].$$
For each $(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$, let $\ell_z$ be the real twistor line
defined by
$$\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2,\qquad \mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2,$$
and let $\ell_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$. Suppose
$$\mathcal O(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{\alpha} \mathcal O\otimes S\xrightarrow{\beta} \mathcal O(1)\otimes U'$$
is a complex of holomorphic vector bundles with $\beta\alpha=0$, locally split
injective and surjective end maps, and locally free middle cohomology
$F=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$ of rank $N$, where
$\dim_\mathbb C U=\dim_\mathbb C U'=k$ and
$\dim_\mathbb C S=2k+N$. Suppose $F|_{\ell_z}$ is holomorphically trivial for
every $z$, and it has a nondegenerate holomorphic $\sigma$-Hermitian pairing
whose induced first-slot-linear Hermitian form on
$H^0(\ell_z,F|_{\ell_z})$ is positive definite for every $z$. Here the
pairing means an isomorphism $h:F\to D(F)$ fixed by $D$, where for a
homogeneous linear matrix $P$ one sets $P^\#(z)=P(jz)^\dagger$ and the signed
dual monad has differentials $-\beta^\#$ and $\alpha^\#$; thus $D^2$ is the
identity under the induced double-dual identifications. Suppose also that a
unitary framing identifies $F|_{\ell_\infty}$ isometrically with
$W\otimes\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}$ for a fixed Hermitian space $W$ of dimension
$N$.

Then there are Hermitian
spaces $V$ and $W$ of dimensions $k$ and $N$, with $W$ carrying the prescribed
framing, and maps
$$B_1,B_2\in\operatorname{End}(V),\qquad I:W\to V,\qquad J:V\to W$$
such that, after a pairing-preserving framed chain identification, the monad
maps are
$$\alpha= \begin{pmatrix} A\\ C\\ J\lambda_1+I^\dagger\lambda_2 \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \beta=(-C,\ A,\ I\lambda_1-J^\dagger\lambda_2),$$
where
$$A=B_1\lambda_1-B_2^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_1,\qquad C=B_2\lambda_1+B_1^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_2.$$
The extracted maps satisfy both zero-moment equations
$$\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=0.$$
They are stable, meaning the vectors
$B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$ span $V$, and costable, meaning no nonzero
subspace invariant under both $B_i$ is contained in $\ker J$. Conversely,
every such regular datum with both moments zero gives a locally split monad
with the stated real-line positivity and infinity framing.
Here $\dagger$ denotes adjoint in the indicated Hermitian spaces.

In the next assertion, a normalized framed isomorphism is a chain
isomorphism preserving the lifted pairing and the specified infinity frame.
Such isomorphisms correspond exactly to the simultaneous $U(V)$ action
$$(B_1,B_2,I,J)\longmapsto (gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1}),\qquad g\in U(V).$$
Thus inverse coefficient extraction recovers precisely one $U(V)$ orbit; when
$k=0$, $U(0)$ is trivial, and every constant flat summand is retained as an
unused orthogonal subspace of $W$.

For $t_1,t_2\in U(1)$, choose an orthonormal framed basis
$w_1,\ldots,w_N$ of $W$ and phases $e_1,\ldots,e_N\in U(1)$, and let
$h(w_a)=e_a^{-1}w_a$. The coordinate action
$(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)\mapsto
(\lambda_1,t_1t_2\lambda_2,t_1\mu_1,t_2\mu_2)$ acts on data by
$$(B_1,B_2,I,J)\mapsto (t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ).$$
The corresponding chain factors on the source, middle and target terms are,
respectively,
$(t_1t_2)^{-1}$, $\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)$, and $1$.

The same extraction and classification hold naturally for first-order
families over $A=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with
$\bar\epsilon=\epsilon$ in the following exact locally-free/base-change
range: the three modules are free of ranks $k,2k+N,k$, the end maps are
locally split, the middle cohomology is locally free and commutes with
reduction, its global section module is free and commutes with reduction, the
coefficient-image submodule in the middle term is a direct summand and
commutes with reduction, and each fixed real-line restriction is trivial
with its section module commuting with reduction. The framing and pairing
are defined over $A$, while positivity is required only on the reduced
complex; adjoints on these modules use the coefficient involution and the
induced $A$-Hermitian forms. Call an $A$-valued datum regular when its
reduction is stable and costable. The extracted matrices lie over $A$ and
obey the same moment equations. Conversely, every $A$-valued regular datum
whose raw
monad satisfies these same global-section, coefficient-image and real-line
base-change conditions gives a family in this range. Pairing-preserving
framed family isomorphisms correspond exactly to
$U(k,A)=\{g:g^\dagger g=1\}$. This assertion is restricted to reduction and
the involution-preserving base maps $\epsilon\mapsto r\epsilon$ with
$r\in\mathbb R$.

For the finite algebraic monad resolution, let
$H_{\rm alg}=c_1^{\rm alg}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1))$ and
$H_{\rm top}=c_1^{\rm top}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1))$. The hyperplane cycle
map identifies these classes in their respective theories. Then
$\operatorname{ch}(F)=N-kH_{\rm alg}^2$ and
$c_2^{\rm alg}(F)=kH_{\rm alg}^2$. Its topological line class is the same
$H_{\rm top}$ and $c_2^{\rm top}(F)=kH_{\rm top}^2$. Identify
$\mathbb P^3$ with the twistor space of $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ through
the quaternionic structure whose invariant lines are the $\ell_z$ and
$\ell_\infty$, and let $\pi:\mathbb P^3\to S^4$ be its projection. Give each
fiber its complex orientation, orient $S^4$ so that the positive incidence
chart followed by the fiber orientation is the complex orientation of
$\mathbb P^3$, and let $u\in H^4(S^4;\mathbb Z)$ be the positive point class.
For this positive twistor orientation, $\pi^*u=H_{\rm top}^2$; consequently, if the underlying
topological bundle is $\pi^*E$ for a bundle $E\to S^4$ with $c_1(E)=0$, then
$c_2(E)=ku$.

declaration.title: Zero-charge positive real monad
declaration.statement:
Let $N\ge2$, $k=0$, $V=\mathbb C^0$, and let $W=\mathbb C^N$ with its standard
Hermitian form and fixed unitary framing. The unique maps
$B_1,B_2\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$ are zero.
Their ADHM moments vanish, the stability and costability conditions are
vacuous, and the raw monad is
$$
0\longrightarrow W\otimes\mathcal O
\longrightarrow 0.
$$
Its middle cohomology is the framed trivial bundle $W\otimes\mathcal O$,
positive on every real-line section space. The normalized gauge group
$U(0)$ has one element, so no gauge or normal-form parameters remain. Its
algebraic and topological second Chern classes vanish and its Euler
characteristic is $N$.

declaration.title: An exact raw one-instanton block
declaration.statement:
Let $V=\mathbb C$, $W=\mathbb C^2$ with their standard Hermitian forms, and
let $\rho>0$. Take
$$
B_1=B_2=0,\qquad I=(\rho,0):W\to V,\qquad
J=(0,\rho)^T:V\to W.
$$
Both ADHM moments vanish. The associated homogeneous monad maps on
$\mathbb P^3$ are
$$
\alpha=
\begin{pmatrix}
-\mu_1\\-\mu_2\\\rho\lambda_2\\\rho\lambda_1
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\beta=(\mu_2,-\mu_1,\rho\lambda_1,-\rho\lambda_2).
$$
For $z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$, put
$$
D_z=
\begin{pmatrix}
z_2&-z_1&\rho&0\\
-\bar z_1&-\bar z_2&0&\rho
\end{pmatrix},\qquad
f_z=|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2+\rho^2.
$$
Then $D_zD_z^\dagger=f_z I_2$. The orthogonal projection
$P_z=I_4-D_z^\dagger f_z^{-1}D_z$ has image $\ker D_z$, a rank-two Hermitian
bundle over $\mathbb R^4$. Its projection connection is $\nabla=P\,d$.
With $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$, and positive orientation
$dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, its curvature satisfies
$F^+=\tfrac12(F+*F)=0$. The monad is trivial and positive on every real
line, and its infinity framing is the identity framing by $W$.

declaration.title: The standard product torus as a compact Lie group
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
declaration.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. For $r\geq0$, let
$T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ with the quotient topology and coordinatewise
addition. On each circle factor, for every open interval $I\subset\mathbb R$
of length less than $1$, use the chart
$q(I)\to I$ given by the unique lift through the quotient map
$q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$; give $T$ the product smooth structure.
Write $\mathfrak t=T_0T$. For $1\leq i\leq r$, let $e_i$ be the tangent vector
at $0$ to the one-parameter subgroup
$s\mapsto(0,\ldots,[s],\ldots,0)$ in the $i$th coordinate. These vectors form
the period-one basis of $\mathfrak t$, and $e_i^*$ denotes its dual basis.
The standard Lie exponential is normalized by
$\exp_T(s e_i)=(0,\ldots,[s],\ldots,0)$ for every $s\in\mathbb R$.
For $r=0$, use the one-point group and the empty basis. This convention makes
$T$ a compact connected abelian Lie group, hence a torus in the sense of the
standard compact-Lie-group definition; its identity inclusion is a cofibration,
so this based group is well-pointed.

right action to Milnor's countable-join model $E_{S^1}$; put

degree-two generator of $H^*(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty};\mathbb Z)$ defined by the
complex orientation of the real rank-two bundle underlying the tautological
complex line, and let $u_{\mathbb R}$ be its image under change of coefficients

and the chosen identification $e_i^*\mapsto u_i$ is a graded-algebra
isomorphism from $\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}(\mathfrak t^*)$, with its
linear generators assigned degree two. For $r=0$, both rings are $\mathbb R$.

declaration.title: Borel and Cartan equivariant cohomology for a compact torus
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
declaration.statement:
Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ be a compact torus with its standard product Lie-group smooth structure and period-one basis, and let $M$ be a smooth manifold without boundary, not assumed compact, with a smooth left action $a:T\times M\to M$. Work over $\mathbb R$ and use the chosen product Milnor model $ET=(E_{S^1})^r$ and $BT=ET/T$ from the preceding coefficient lemma. Give $ET\times M$ the right diagonal action $(e,p)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,t^{-1}\cdot p)$ and define
$$ET\times_T M:=(ET\times M)/T.$$
The **Borel equivariant cohomology** is the graded ring
$$H_T^*(M;\mathbb R):=H_{\mathrm{sing}}^*(ET\times_T M;\mathbb R).$$
For $M=\{\ast\}$ this gives $H_T^*(\ast;\mathbb R)=H^*(BT;\mathbb R)$; the selected degree-two normalization in $\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}(\mathfrak t^*)$ is the isomorphism established in the preceding coefficient lemma.

The quotient map $q:ET\times M\to ET\times_T M$ and projection
$\pi([e,p])=[e]$ give the associated-space square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}ET\times M&\xrightarrow{q}&ET\times_T M\\\downarrow\operatorname{pr}_1&&\downarrow\pi\\ET&\xrightarrow{q_T}&BT\end{array}$$
Its TikZ source is
```latex
\begin{tikzcd}
ET\times M \arrow[r,"q"] \arrow[d,"\operatorname{pr}_1"'] & ET\times_T M \arrow[d,"\pi"]\\
ET \arrow[r,"q_T"'] & BT
\end{tikzcd}
```
where $q_T:ET\to BT$ is the orbit quotient. The projection $\pi$ is
well-defined because $[e\cdot t]=[e]$ for every $t\in T$. The square
commutes because both composites send $(e,p)$ to $[e]$.

Let $\mathfrak t=T_eT$, with basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ and dual basis $u_1,\ldots,u_r$. Regard $\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}(\mathfrak t^*)$ as a polynomial algebra by assigning each linear generator degree two. Use the trivial $T$-action on this polynomial factor, and the induced left action $t\cdot\alpha=(a_{t^{-1}})^*\alpha$ on forms. It is a left action because pullback reverses composition: $a_{t^{-1}}^*a_{s^{-1}}^*=(a_{s^{-1}}\circ a_{t^{-1}})^*=a_{(ts)^{-1}}^*$. The **Cartan complex** is the graded-commutative algebra
$$C_T(M):=\bigl(\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}(\mathfrak t^*)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\Omega^*(M)\bigr)^T,$$
with multiplication $(P\otimes\alpha)(Q\otimes\beta)=PQ\otimes(\alpha\wedge\beta)$, where $\wedge$ is the differential-form wedge product and all tensor products are algebraic. The superscript denotes the fixed subspace for the diagonal action, and a polynomial of degree $j$ tensored with a $k$-form has total degree $2j+k$. For $\xi\in\mathfrak t$, use the library fundamental vector field
$$X_\xi(p)=\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}\exp_T(-s\xi)\cdot p.$$
On polynomial-valued forms define the degree-one Cartan operator
$$d_T(P\otimes\alpha)=P\otimes d\alpha-\sum_{i=1}^r(u_iP)\otimes\iota_{X_{e_i}}\alpha,$$
extended linearly. The tensor $\sum_i u_i\otimes X_{e_i}$ is basis-independent. The **Cartan equivariant cohomology** in this item means $H^*(C_T(M),d_T)$; the proof below establishes $d_T^2=0$ on $C_T(M)$.

This definition does not assert a general isomorphism between the Borel and Cartan cohomology rings. It defines neither equivariant Chow groups nor equivariant quotient-stack Borel–Moore homology, and no rational-coefficient comparison is being used in the real Cartan complex.

declaration.title: The free translation action of the circle on itself
declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored draft; current readiness is recorded separately.
declaration.statement: Assume AC. Let $T=M=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$, with $T$ acting on $M$ by left translation $t\cdot[x]=[t+x]$. Use the period-one tangent generator $e$, so the library convention gives $X_e=-\partial_x$, and let $\eta$ be the global one-form on $\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ descended from $-dx$ on $\mathbb R$. In the chosen Borel model the map $[v,x]\mapsto v\cdot x$ identifies $ET\times_TT$ with $ET$, hence $H_T^0(T;\mathbb R)=\mathbb R$ and $H_T^k(T;\mathbb R)=0$ for $k>0$. The invariant Cartan complex is $\mathbb R[u]\oplus\mathbb R[u]\eta$, with $|u|=2$, $|\eta|=1$, $d_TP(u)=0$, and $d_T(P(u)\eta)=-uP(u)$. Its cohomology is $\mathbb R$ in degree zero and zero in positive degrees, agreeing with the Borel calculation for this action.

declaration.title: Fixed loci and normal weights of compact torus actions
declaration.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let \(r\geq 0\), let \(T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r\) with its product Lie-group structure, and let \(M\) be a compact, finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. Let \(a:T\times M\to M\) be a jointly smooth left action. Then \(M\) admits a smooth Riemannian metric invariant under \(a\). Its fixed set
\[
F=M^T:=\{p\in M:a(t,p)=p\text{ for every }t\in T\}
\]
is a compact embedded smooth submanifold with finitely many connected components, and \(T_pF=(T_pM)^T\) for each \(p\in F\). The orthogonal normal bundle \(\nu_F=(TF)^\perp\subset TM|_F\) has no nonzero \(T\)-fixed vectors in any fiber. On each connected component of \(F\), its normal representation has a finite weight decomposition into nontrivial characters of \(T\), with constant multiplicities; equivalently, \(\nu_F\) admits a smooth \(T\)-invariant complex structure and orientation on each component.

declaration.title: Equivariant tubular and slice neighborhoods for compact torus actions
declaration.statement:
Assume countable choice. Let \(T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r\) act smoothly on a compact finite-dimensional smooth manifold \(M\) without boundary, and let \(g\) be a \(T\)-invariant Riemannian metric. If \(S\subseteq M\) is a compact embedded \(T\)-invariant submanifold, its orthogonal normal bundle \(
u(S)\) has a \(T\)-invariant open disk neighborhood \(D_\epsilon(
u(S))\) of the zero section, and the normal exponential map is a \(T\)-equivariant diffeomorphism from that disk bundle onto a \(T\)-invariant open neighborhood of \(S\). In particular, for \(x\in M\), with stabilizer \(H=T_x\), orbit \(O=T\cdot x\), and normal fiber \(V=
u_x(O)\), let \(H\) act on \(V\) by its differentials. There is an open \(H\)-invariant disk \(D_\epsilon(V)\) such that \([t,v]\), the equivalence class of \((t,v)\) under \((t,v)\sim(th,h^{-1}v)\) for \(h\in H\), maps by \([t,v]\mapsto t\cdot\exp_x(v)\) to a \(T\)-equivariant diffeomorphism from \(T	imes_H D_\epsilon(V)\) onto an open neighborhood \(U_x\) of \(O\). Every stabilizer of a point in \(U_x\) is a subgroup of \(H\).

declaration.title: A proper closed subgroup of a torus has a nonzero annihilating character
declaration.statement: Assume countable choice. Let \(T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r\) with \(r\geq1\), and let \(H\subsetneq T\) be a closed subgroup. A character means a smooth group homomorphism from \(T\) to the multiplicative unit circle \(S^1=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}\). Then there is a nontrivial character \(\chi:T\to S^1\) whose restriction to all of \(H\) is the trivial character.

declaration.title: Localization preserves exact sequences of modules
declaration.statement:
Let \(R\) be a commutative ring with identity, let \(S\subseteq R\) contain \(1\), be closed under multiplication, and not contain \(0\), and let \(0\to M'\xrightarrow{f}M\xrightarrow{g}M''\to0\) be an exact sequence of \(R\)-modules. The localization \(S^{-1}M\) is the module of fractions \(m/s\), with \((m,s)\sim(m',s')\) exactly when some \(t\in S\) satisfies \(t(s'm-sm')=0\). Then
\[
0\longrightarrow S^{-1}M'\xrightarrow{S^{-1}f}S^{-1}M\xrightarrow{S^{-1}g}S^{-1}M''\longrightarrow0
\]
is exact.

references.locator: Section 3, localization of equivariant-cohomology modules, printed pp. 5–7.

declaration.title: Rational coefficient ring and characters of a product torus classifying space
declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let \(r\geq0\), let \(T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r\), and use \(E_T=(E_{S^1})^r\), the product of the right Milnor join models, with \(BT=E_T/T\). For the \(i\)th coordinate character \(\chi_i([t_1,\ldots,t_r])=\exp(2\pi i t_i)\), let \(L_i=E_T\times_T\mathbb C_{\chi_i}\) be the associated complex line bundle over \(BT\), with the right diagonal equivalence \((e,z)\cdot t=(e\cdot t,\chi_i(t)^{-1}z)\), and put \(u_i=c_1(L_i)\in H^2(BT;\mathbb Q)\). Then
\[
BT\cong(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r,\qquad H^*(BT;\mathbb Q)\cong\mathbb Q[u_1,\ldots,u_r],\qquad |u_i|=2.
\]
Every smooth character \(\chi:T\to S^1\) is uniquely \(\chi_{\mathbf n}([t])=\exp(2\pi i\sum_i n_it_i)\) for \(\mathbf n=(n_1,\ldots,n_r)\in\mathbb Z^r\), and its associated line satisfies \(c_1(L_{\chi_{\mathbf n}})=\sum_i n_i u_i\). In particular a nontrivial character has a nonzero degree-two class. For each \(k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}\), \(H_q(BT;k)\) is finite-dimensional in every degree \(q\). For \(r=0\), \(BT\) is a point and its rational cohomology is \(\mathbb Q\).

references.locator: Section 3.2, Theorem 3.19, printed pp. 220–222.

declaration.title: Homotopy invariance of singular cohomology with field coefficients
declaration.statement: Let \(k\) be a field, let \(X,Y\) be topological spaces, and let \(f,g:X\to Y\) be continuous maps joined by a continuous homotopy \(H:X\times[0,1]\to Y\). Then \(f^*=g^*:H^n(Y;k)\to H^n(X;k)\) for every integer \(n\). Consequently every homotopy equivalence induces an isomorphism on singular cohomology with coefficients in \(k\).

declaration.title: A compact smooth manifold has a finite good-cover nerve model
declaration.statement: Assume AC. Let \(F\) be a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary and equip it with a Riemannian metric. An open set is strongly geodesically convex if every ordered pair of its points is joined by a unique affinely parametrized globally length-minimizing geodesic whose image stays in the set and whose connector depends smoothly on the endpoints. There are finitely many such open sets \(U_1,\ldots,U_N\) covering \(F\), every nonempty finite intersection of which is strongly geodesically convex. Let \(K\) be the finite simplicial complex whose nonempty faces are the index sets \(\sigma\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}\) for which \(U_\sigma=\bigcap_{i\in\sigma}U_i\) is nonempty. Then its usual geometric realization \(|K|\) is homotopy equivalent to \(F\). For \(F=\varnothing\), take \(N=0\) and \(K=\varnothing\).

declaration.title: Positive-degree cohomology of a compact manifold is nilpotent
declaration.statement: Assume AC. Let \(F\) be a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, equipped with a Riemannian metric, and let \(k\) be a field. There is a finite CW complex \(K\) homotopy equivalent to \(F\), and an integer \(N\geq1\) such that \(H^q(F;k)=0\) for every \(q\geq N\). Consequently the ideal \(J=\bigoplus_{q>0}H^q(F;k)\) in the graded cohomology ring satisfies \(J^N=0\). If \(F=\varnothing\), take \(K=\varnothing\), \(N=1\), and \(J=0\).

declaration.title: The fixed-locus Borel base is paracompact and of CW type
declaration.statement: Assume AC. Let \(r\geq0\), let \(T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r\) use the product Milnor model \(BT=(\mathbb{CP}^{\infty})^r\) with its ordinary product topology, and let \(F\) be a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold without boundary. declaration.title: Equivariant cohomology of the nonfixed locus vanishes after character localization
declaration.statement:
Assume AC. Let \(T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r\) act smoothly on a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable manifold \(M\) without boundary, let \(F=M^T\), and use the product Milnor Borel construction with coefficients \(k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}\). Let \(\mathscr S_T(k)\) be the multiplicative set generated by the first Chern classes of all nontrivial smooth characters of \(T\). Then
\[
\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(M\setminus F;k)=0.
\]
Equivalently, every class in the Borel equivariant cohomology of the nonfixed locus is annihilated by some finite product of nontrivial character classes.

declaration.title: Borel localization for compact torus actions
declaration.statement:
Assume AC. Let \(T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r\) act smoothly on a compact finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold \(M\) without boundary, and let \(F=M^T\). For \(k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}\), define \(H_T^*(X;k)=H^*(ET\times_T X;k)\) using the product of the right Milnor circle models, let \(A_T(k)=H^*(BT;k)\), and let \(\mathscr S_T(k)\) be the multiplicative set generated by the first Chern classes of all nontrivial smooth characters \(T\to S^1\). Then restriction along \(i:F\hookrightarrow M\) induces a graded-ring isomorphism
\[
i^*:\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(M;k)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(F;k).
\]
The conclusion concerns compact finite-dimensional smooth \(T\)-manifolds and ordinary Borel singular cohomology; it makes no noncompact or compact-support assertion.

declaration.title: Circle rotation on the complex projective line
declaration.statement:
Let \(T=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\) act on \(M=\mathbb{CP}^1\) by \(t\cdot[z_0:z_1]=[z_0:e^{2\pi it}z_1]\). For \(k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}\), use the product Milnor Borel model and let \(u=c_1(L_\chi)\in H^2(BT;k)\) for \(\chi(t)=e^{2\pi it}\). The fixed set is \(F=\{p_+,p_-\}\), where \(p_+=[1:0]\) and \(p_-=[0:1]\); the tangent weights are \(+1\) at \(p_+\) and \(-1\) at \(p_-\). If \(\mathscr S_T(k)\) is generated by nontrivial character classes and \(A_T(k)=H^*(BT;k)\), then restriction identifies
\[
\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(\mathbb{CP}^1;k)\cong
\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}A_T(k)\oplus\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}A_T(k),
\]
with the two summands given by evaluation at \(p_+\) and \(p_-\).

declaration.title: A free circle orbit has zero localized Borel cohomology
declaration.statement: Let \(T=M=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\) act on \(M\) by left translation \(t\cdot[x]=[t+x]\), and use the product Milnor Borel model with \(k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}\). Every positive-degree class in \(A_T(k)\) acts as zero, so localization at the nontrivial character classes gives \(\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(T;k)=0\), agreeing with restriction to the empty fixed set.

declaration.title: Rotation on one factor of a product with positive-dimensional fixed components
declaration.statement:
Let \(T=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\) act on \(M=\mathbb{CP}^1\times\mathbb{CP}^1\) by \(t\cdot([z_0:z_1],q)=([z_0:e^{2\pi it}z_1],q)\), and let \(k\in\{\mathbb Q,\mathbb R\}\). The fixed set is the disjoint union \(F=(\{p_+\}\times\mathbb{CP}^1)\amalg(\{p_-\}\times\mathbb{CP}^1)\), with \(p_+=[1:0]\) and \(p_-=[0:1]\); the normal weights are \(+1\) and \(-1\), respectively. Let \(u\in H^2(BT;k)\) be the weight-one character class and \(b\in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1;k)\) the generator with \(b^2=0\). Then localized restriction identifies
\[
\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}H_T^*(M;k)\cong
\bigl(\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}A_T(k)\otimes_k k[b]/(b^2)\bigr)\oplus
\bigl(\mathscr S_T(k)^{-1}A_T(k)\otimes_k k[b]/(b^2)\bigr),
\]
where the two summands are the Borel cohomology of the two positive-dimensional fixed components.

declaration.title: Borel Equivariant Integration Conventions for the ABBV Formula
declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^r$ have the standard product presentation, smooth structure, and period-one basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of the upstream torus definition. Use its selected product Milnor model $ET=(E_{S^1})^r$ with the right diagonal action and $BT=ET/T$. For a smooth left $T$-manifold $X$, define real Borel equivariant cohomology by $H_T^*(X;\mathbb R)=H^*(ET\times_T X;\mathbb R)$ using the quotient convention $(e\cdot t,x)\sim(e,t\cdot x)$. Its coefficient ring is $\mathcal R=H^*(BT;\mathbb R)\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathbb R}(\mathfrak t^*)=\mathbb R[u_1,\ldots,u_r]$, where $u_i$ is the class corresponding to the dual period-one basis vector $e_i^*$ and each $u_i$ has degree $2$.

For an integer vector $m=(m_1,\ldots,m_r)$, write the character as $\chi_m(t)=\exp(2\pi i\sum_i m_i t_i)$ and define its degree-two class by $u_{\chi_m}=\sum_i m_i u_i$. With the stated quotient convention, this is the Euler class of the Borel line $ET\times_T\mathbb C_{\chi_m}$, where $T$ acts on $\mathbb C_{\chi_m}$ by $\chi_m$. Use the complex-orientation convention $c_1(L)=e(L_{\mathbb R})$ for a complex line $L$; thus $u_\chi$ is also the first Chern class of its Borel character line. Let $S\subset\mathcal R$ be the multiplicative set generated by these classes for all nontrivial characters, together with $1$; thus $u_\chi\ne0$ exactly for nontrivial $\chi$. Write $S^{-1}H_T^*(X;\mathbb R)$ and $S^{-1}\mathcal R$ for the corresponding localizations. The coefficient-ring identification is used under AC: the upstream classifying-space cohomology proof invokes AC in its Künneth and coefficient arguments.

If $X$ is a compact oriented smooth $T$-manifold without boundary of dimension $n$ and the action preserves its orientation, the Borel projection $\pi_X:ET\times_T X\to BT$ has compact oriented $n$-dimensional fibers. Define equivariant integration $\int_X\alpha=(\pi_X)_!\alpha$, the cohomological pushforward along those fibers; it lowers degree by $n$ and has values in $\mathcal R$. For an oriented $T$-equivariant vector bundle $E\to X$ whose Borel-associated bundle has a normalized Thom class, define its equivariant Euler class $e_T(E)$ as the pullback of that Thom class by the zero section. The Thom class is normalized to restrict on each oriented fiber pair $(D^c,S^{c-1})$ to the positive generator of $H^c(D^c,S^{c-1};\mathbb R)$. For rank $c=0$, the Thom class and Euler class are $1$. For a complex representation line of character $\chi$, this convention gives Euler class $u_\chi$. For a fixed component $F$ of a $T$-action on $M$, the orientation convention is $o(TM|_F)=o(TF)\wedge o(\nu_F)$, where $\nu_F$ is its chosen equivariantly oriented normal bundle. This is the Borel convention; no identification with a Cartan, Chow, or quotient-stack cohomology model is assumed here.

declaration.title: Equivariant Thom-Gysin Identities for Fixed Submanifolds
declaration.statement:
Work in $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}$. Let $T$ be a compact torus acting smoothly on a compact oriented smooth manifold $M$ without boundary. Let $N\subseteq M^T$ be a compact closed embedded submanifold without boundary of codimension $c$, let $i:N\hookrightarrow M$ be inclusion, and let its normal bundle $
u$ have a $T$-invariant orientation. Orient $N$ by $o(TM|_N)=o(TN)\wedge o(
u)$. If $N=\varnothing$, the source groups and all asserted maps are zero. Otherwise, with the real Borel conventions of the preceding definition, there is a fiber-normalized equivariant Thom class $	au_
u\in H_T^c(
u,
u\setminus N;\mathbb R)$, and cup product with $	au_
u$ is an isomorphism $H_T^k(N;\mathbb R)	o H_T^{k+c}(
u,
u\setminus N;\mathbb R)$ for every $k$. A $T$-invariant tubular neighborhood and excision therefore define a cohomological Gysin map $i_*^T:H_T^k(N;\mathbb R)	o H_T^{k+c}(M;\mathbb R)$. It satisfies

$$i^*i_*^T( eta)=e_T(
u)\smile eta,\qquad \int_M i_*^T( eta)=\int_N eta.$$

If $N'$ is a different fixed component disjoint from $N$, then $i_{N'}^*i_{N*}^T( eta)=0$. These maps use the Thom normalization in which every oriented normal fiber integrates to $1$.

declaration.title: Fixed-Component Normal Euler Classes Become Invertible
declaration.statement:
Work in $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}$. Let a compact torus $T$ act smoothly on a compact smooth manifold $M$ without boundary, and let $F=M^T$. Then $F$ is a compact smooth embedded submanifold, its connected components $F_j$ are finite in number, and $T_pF=(T_pM)^T$ for every $p\in F$. If $F=\varnothing$, the component assertions are vacuous. The normal bundle $
u_j$ of each component has no trivial $T$-representation in any fiber. Give $
u_j$ a $T$-equivariant orientation, write $c_j=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb R}
u_j$, and choose an invariant complex structure on it; let $\epsilon_j\in\{+1,-1\}$ compare that complex orientation with the chosen orientation. If the nonzero characters of the normal representation on a fiber, counted with multiplicity, are $\chi_{j,1},\ldots,\chi_{j,c_j/2}$, then the component of $e_T(
u_j)$ in $H^0(F_j;\mathbb R)\otimes\mathcal R$ is

$$\epsilon_j\prod_{a=1}^{c_j/2}u_{\chi_{j,a}}.$$

Consequently $e_T(
u_j)$ is invertible in $S^{-1}H_T^*(F_j;\mathbb R)$. When $c_j=0$, the product is empty, equals $1$, and the Euler class is already a unit.

declaration.title: Atiyah–Bott–Berline–Vergne Integration Formula
declaration.statement:
Work in $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}$. Let $T$ be a compact torus acting smoothly on a compact oriented smooth $n$-manifold $M$ without boundary; use the standard Hausdorff, second-countable manifold convention, and assume the action preserves the orientation. Write $F=M^T=\coprod_{j=1}^{s}F_j$ for its fixed locus, with $s<\infty$, and $i_j:F_j\hookrightarrow M$ for each connected component. Give each normal bundle $\nu_j$ a $T$-equivariant orientation and orient $F_j$ by $o(TM|_{F_j})=o(TF_j)\wedge o(\nu_j)$. Use real Borel equivariant cohomology, $\mathcal R=H^*(BT;\mathbb R)$, the multiplicative set $S$ generated by nonzero character classes, and the degree-shifting fiber-integration convention of the preceding definition. For every homogeneous $\alpha\in H_T^k(M;\mathbb R)$,

$$\int_M\alpha=\sum_j\int_{F_j}\frac{i_j^*\alpha}{e_T(\nu_j)}\quad\text{in }S^{-1}H^{k-n}(BT;\mathbb R).$$

If the fixed locus is nonempty and consists of isolated points, necessarily $n=2m$. Use the ambient orientation on each normal space $\nu_p=T_pM$ and the positive orientation on each point $p$. Choose a $T$-invariant complex structure on each $T_pM$ and let $\chi_{p,1},\ldots,\chi_{p,m}$ be its nonzero character weights. Let $\epsilon_p=+1$ when its complex orientation agrees with the orientation of $M$ at $p$ and $-1$ otherwise. Then the same formula specializes to

$$\int_M\alpha=\sum_{p\in M^T}\frac{\epsilon_p\,i_p^*\alpha}{\prod_{a=1}^{m}u_{\chi_{p,a}}}\quad\text{in }S^{-1}\mathcal R.$$

If the fixed locus is empty, the fixed-component formula is the empty sum $0$ for every $n$; no parity condition or integer $m$ is needed in that case.

This is a finite-dimensional formula for compact manifolds; it does not assert a formula for arbitrary noncompact instanton spaces or infinite-dimensional field spaces.

declaration.title: ABBV on the Projective Line with the Standard Circle Action
declaration.statement:
Work in $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}$. Let $T=S^1=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ act on complex-oriented $M=\mathbb{CP}^1$ by $\lambda[z_0:z_1]=[z_0:\lambda z_1]$. Let $u\in H^2(BT;\mathbb R)$ be the class corresponding to the period-one weight-$+1$ character under the chosen tautological-Euler normalization, let $\mathcal O(1)$ be the dual tautological line with its induced equivariant structure, and put $x=e_T(\mathcal O(1))$. The fixed points are $p_0=[1:0]$ and $p_\infty=[0:1]$. Their tangent weights are $+1$ and $-1$, while $x|_{p_0}=0$ and $x|_{p_\infty}=-u$. The ABBV sum is

$$\frac{0}{u}+\frac{-u}{-u}=1,$$

which agrees with $\int_{\mathbb{CP}^1}x=1$.

declaration.title: ABBV with Positive-Dimensional Fixed Components
declaration.statement: Work in $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{AC}$. Let $T=S^1=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ act on complex-oriented $M=\mathbb{CP}^1\times\mathbb{CP}^1$ by $\lambda([z_0:z_1],[w_0:w_1])=([z_0:\lambda z_1],[w_0:w_1])$. Let $\eta\in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1;\mathbb R)$ be the positive generator with integral $1$, let $x_1$ be the pullback of the equivariant Euler class of the dual tautological line from the first factor, and set $\alpha=x_1\smile\operatorname{pr}_2^*\eta$. The fixed components are $F_0=\{[1:0]\}\times\mathbb{CP}^1$ and $F_\infty=\{[0:1]\}\times\mathbb{CP}^1$, with normal weights $+1$ and $-1$. The component formula gives a zero contribution from $F_0$ and $\int_{\mathbb{CP}^1}\eta=1$ from $F_\infty$, matching $\int_M\alpha=1$.
